title: Jaguars LB Foye Oluokun: We can't let wins mask stuff
summary: The Jaguars have taken two more steps toward the playoffs over the last two weeks and they've done it in impressive fashion.
full_text: The Jaguars have taken two more steps toward the playoffs over the last two weeks and they've done it in impressive fashion. They followed up a 42-7 humiliation of the Colts in Week 8 with Thursday night's 33-10 rout of the Ravens on the road. Blowouts are nothing new for the Jags as they have outscored their opponents by 108 points over their eight games this season and their 6-2 record has them well positioned to win the AFC South. Winning another division title is not the team's goal, however, and linebacker Foye Oluokun focused on that when he spoke to reporters on Thursday night. “You win and it feels great. We can’t let wins mask stuff ," Oluokun said. "You’ve always got stuff to improve. I've been here a while, went through winning, winning, winning, and one season, we let a lot slide because we were winning. So we got to keep learning in wins and stuff because it's all about who's playing the best in December and then we make that run [in] January and February. We got to keep improving all the way through the year, get the advantageous situation going into the playoffs." The Jaguars hosted a playoff game after winning 13 games in 2025, but they were bounced out of the postseason by the Bills. Oluokun was on the field during that game and avoiding a similar outcome will be front and center as he tries to keep the Jaguars' focus in the right place while they are running roughshod over weaker clubs.
author: Josh Alper

title: Trevor Lawrence is having by far the best season of his career
summary: Trevor Lawrence has so much talent for the quarterback position that if freshmen could declare for the NFL draft, Lawrence probably would have been the first overall pick in 2019, when he had just led Clemson to a national championship as a true freshman.
full_text: '' Trevor Lawrence has so much talent for the quarterback position that if freshmen could declare for the NFL draft, Lawrence probably would have been the first overall pick in 2019, when he had just led Clemson to a national championship as a true freshman. Instead, Lawrence stayed three years at Clemson and was the first pick in 2021, viewed as a sure-thing quarterback prospect. In Year 6, Lawrence finally looks like everything he was supposed to be. Lawrence is having by far the best year of his NFL career, with career-high stats across the board that are constrained only by the fact that the Jaguars win so many blowouts that Lawrence doesn't throw many passes in the fourth quarter. So far this season, Lawrence has completed 146 of 224 passes for 1,932 yards, with 18 touchdowns, four interceptions and an NFL-leading passer rating of 111.7. Project Lawrence's totals to a 17-game season, and he's on pace to finish with 4,106 yards, 38 touchdowns and nine interceptions. Those are MVP numbers. Lawrence's rookie year was a disaster, as he led the league in interceptions while playing on a chaotic Jaguars team coached by Urban Meyer, whose only foray into NFL coaching lasted less than one season. Lawrence and the Jaguars got a lot better once they kicked Meyer to the curb, but even in the next three years with Doug Pederson, an offensive coach with a Super Bowl-winning pedigree, Lawrence didn't live up to the pre-draft hype. Playing in Liam Coen's offense, something has changed. Last year the Jaguars went 13-4, winning double-digit games for the first time since drafting Lawrence, and this year Lawrence and the Jaguars are even better. Lawrence's average of 8.6 yards per pass is the best of his career by almost a yard and a half, a remarkable improvement for any quarterback to make in his sixth season. Lawrence has thrown touchdown passes on 8 percent of his attempts, the best in the NFL this season and by far the best mark of his career. And after getting sacked a career-high 41 times last year, Lawrence has gotten much more comfortable reading the pass rush in his second year in Coen's offense and has only been sacked 13 times this season. Lawrence's numbers would look even better if the Jaguars weren't so often taking their foot off the gas late in games because they're blowing opponents out. Lawrence has 1,196 yards and 12 touchdowns in the first halves of games this season, but he only has 736 yards and six touchdowns in the second halves of games. The Jaguars currently have the fourth-best odds to win the Super Bowl, and Lawrence has the fifth-best odds to win MVP. That might be underselling them, and him. The Jaguars may just be the best team, with the best quarterback, in the NFL right now.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Derrick Henry: I haven't mentioned going somewhere else, let's try to get better
summary: The Ravens got blown out for the third straight game on Thursday night and they lost their fourth straight overall, which led running back Derrick Henry to call it the "same story" after the Jaguars rolled to a 33-10 win in Baltimore.
full_text: The Ravens got blown out for the third straight game on Thursday night and they lost their fourth straight overall, which led running back Derrick Henry to call it the "same story" after the Jaguars rolled to a 33-10 win in Baltimore. Lamar Jackson only saw brief playing time in one of those losses, so the Ravens have been starting games in a hole throughout their losing streak. Jackson may not be back this season and that makes it hard to see any reason why the story that's frustrating Henry is going to change before the year is out. Given the stage Henry's at in his career, it wasn't unusual that he was asked after the game if he was reconsidering his plan to remain with the Ravens until he hangs up his cleats. Henry said that he isn't thinking about changing uniforms. "I have not mentioned me going anywhere else," Henry said, via a transcript from the team. "I'm saying, 'Let's go back to work. Let's try to get better and turn this thing around." The trade deadline is Tuesday and any team looking to bolster their backfield could do a lot worse than adding one of the most prolific backs in the history of the league. While a move may not be Henry's first choice, it could turn out to be the best course of action for the Ravens and he might find he likes being back on a team that can seriously talk about contending during the second half of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Derrick Henry's production has plummeted without Lamar Jackson this season
summary: Without quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Ravens want to be able to rely on running back Derrick Henry.
full_text: ' Without quarterback Lamar Jackson, the Ravens want to be able to rely on running back Derrick Henry. That plan isn't working. In Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars, Henry managed just 57 yards on 17 carries. That continues what has been happening all season, with Henry struggling to get anything going without Jackson on the field. It was a bad omen in Week 4 against the Titans, when Jackson left at halftime with an ankle injury and Henry was ineffective in the second half. In the first half of that game, with Jackson on the field, Henry had seven carries for 38 yards, an average of 5.4 yards per carry, and a touchdown. In the second half with Tyler Huntley, Henry had 16 carries for 35 yards, an average of 2.2 yards per carry, and no touchdowns. Jackson has played one snap since that Titans game, and the story has been the same, with Henry not able to do much of anything. Overall this season, in three and a half games playing with Jackson, Henry has 73 carries for 339 yards, an average of 4.6 yards per carry and 97 yards per game, and seven touchdowns. In five and a half games without Jackson, Henry has 102 carries for 350 yards, an average of 3.4 yards per carry and 64 yards per game, and one touchdown. At 4-5 and in last place in the AFC North, the Ravens, who entered the year with Super Bowl aspirations, are on the verge of their season collapsing. They need to turn things around, and they need Henry to turn things around.
author: Michael David Smith

author: Michael David Smith

title: Jaguars' point differential of +108 this season is 50 points better than any other team
summary: The Jaguars have won four games by more than 21 points this season; no other team has more than one win by more than 21 points.
full_text: '' No NFL team is dominating opponents like the Jacksonville Jaguars. After blowing out the Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night, the Jaguars have now outscored their opponents by a cumulative score of 229-121 this season. That's a point differential of +108, by far the best in the NFL. The team with the second-best point differential in the NFL is the 49ers, at +58. The Jaguars' point differential is 50 points better than the next-best team. At 6-2, the Jaguars do not have the best record in the league, as the Bills, 49ers and Vikings are all 6-1. The 49ers are favored to beat the Raiders and improve to 7-1, and the Bills and Vikings play each other on Monday night, so the winner will be 7-1. But at the midway point of the season, point differential is a better indication of a team's quality, and a better predictor of a team's future success, than win-loss record. That's because with as small a sample size as half a season, a few plays in a few close games can skew the won-loss record, but a few plays don't skew point differential. Historically, the teams that prove to be the best over the course of a season are the teams that win some blowouts, even if they also lose some close games. Winning blowouts and losing close games is exactly what the Jaguars do. Both of the Jaguars' losses were one-possession games that were tied in the fourth quarter, while the Jaguars' wins have included some massive blowouts: The Jaguars' 35-point win over the Colts was the biggest blowout of this NFL season, their 29-point win over the Patriots was the fourth-biggest blowout in the NFL this season, their 24-point win over the Browns was the seventh-biggest blowout in the NFL this season, and Thursday night's 23-point win over the Ravens was the 11th-biggest blowout in the NFL this season. The Jaguars have won four games by more than 21 points this season; no other team has more than one win by more than 21 points. Jacksonville has a 3.5-game lead in the AFC South, and six of the Jaguars' nine remaining games are against opponents with a losing record. They're poised to run away with their division, perhaps earn the No. 1 seed in the AFC, and maybe blow some teams out in the playoffs just like they have in the regular season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Justin Jefferson says his frustration came from "wanting to win"
summary: Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson engaged in a rare display of frustration late in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
full_text: Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson engaged in a rare display of frustration late in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions. He also didn't talk to reporters after the game, possibly to avoid saying things that would underscore what he was feeling in the moment. Four days later, Jefferson spoke to the media — and the No. 1 topic was his apparent mood during Minnesota's first loss of the season. "It was wanting to win ," Jefferson said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN, "and I felt like we had plenty of opportunities to win that game and we only hurt ourselves in multiple ways. It's just wanting better from the whole entire offense especially. And I feel like the potential and the guys that we have in that room is something very, very special. I feel like we're wasting that if not going out there executing the plays that we have called and just not living to that standard that we feel like we live up to every single day." Jefferson, who always says all the right things about his quarterbacks, said all the right things about Kyler Murray, whose performance against Detroit largely contributed to the failure to score more than 15 points. "I feel like Kyler has continued to grow," Jefferson said. "I feel like Kyler is continuing to get comfortable with this offense. And I feel like the plays that are there are plays that he's well capable of making. And those are plays that we've seen him make multiple times throughout the season, throughout practice and in training camp as well. So we definitely have faith in him. We have confidence in him to go out there and be that guy that we need him and want him to be. "But all in all, it's just executing our plays and just coming ready to play. And I feel like once he's back out there and he gets more comfortable with the system, more comfortable with just throwing to these different type of receivers, then I feel like he's going to look a lot better in [reporters'] eyes. But we see that every single day. We see that type of Kyler that we need out there on Sundays every single day. So just bringing that on Sundays. We're behind him. We're confident in him, so we just going to keep riding with him." For now, the Vikings will ride with Carson Wentz, while Murray is out with a hamstring injury. And Wentz has proven that, of all the quarterbacks who have played for the Vikings since Sam Darnold left for Seattle after the 2024 season, Wentz knows how to get the ball to Jefferson. Soft bench or not, Wentz has an opportunity to stay on the field if he makes the plays that Murray didn't on Sunday. Plays that, by the time the game was on the line, coach Kevin O'Connell didn't allow Murray to try to make. The one moment that resonates from Sunday's game wasn't anything Murray did or failed to do. It came from O'Connell's decision to punt from the Minnesota 33-yard line on fourth and five with 3:01 to play. Given the manner in which the Lions were running the ball, the likelihood of getting another opportunity to score a touchdown was slim. Put simply, if O'Connell didn't trust Murray to gain five yards with the game on the line, O'Connell shouldn't entrust the starting job to Murray. For now, Murray technically can't play due to injury. It's hard not to wonder whether, if Murray had made the plays needed to outscore the Lions on Sunday, he'd be playing on Monday night despite the injured hamstring.
author: Mike Florio

title: George Kittle is skeptical that Brandon Aiyuk will "get in" the team facility
summary: As 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk attempts to lay the foundation for a return to the NFL, at least one other 49ers player has expressed skepticism about Aiyuk's plan.
full_text: ' As 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk attempts to lay the foundation for a return to the NFL, at least one other 49ers player has expressed skepticism about Aiyuk's plan. His new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has said that Aiyuk will report to the 49ers' facility on Friday . Tight end George Kittle shared his views regarding that strategy on Thursday when asked whether he's looking forward to seeing Aiyuk. " Do you think he gets in the facility? " Kittle said, via Grant Cohn of SI.com. Kittle then was asked if he thinks Aiyuk gets into the facility. "Plead the fifth," Kittle said. "Yeah. You can ask [G.M.] John [Lynch]. Or [coach] Kyle [Shanahan]. Don't ask me. I'm a conspiracy guy." "Is there a conspiracy?" Kittle was asked. "Plead the fifth," he said. Kittle's skepticism is warranted. The entire situation is strange, and awkward. Aiyuk clearly hopes to trigger his outright release by reporting for work, after months of making it clear he had no intention to do so. The 49ers are tiptoeing around the situation, for now. Before the team has to do anything, Aiyuk needs to check the various boxes that put the 49ers in a posture that requires a decision. Of all potential outcomes, the least likely involves Aiyuk being welcomed back onto the roster. Especially since Aiyuk likely has no desire to be on the roster. He wants his freedom, and he finally — after months of stubbornness — has initiated the process aimed at making that happen. While it's possible that the 49ers will search for a hardball outcome that involves keeping him from becoming a free agent while avoiding putting him back on the team, the chances of Aiyuk wandering around the locker room and eventually wearing a 49ers' helmet again seem to be incredibly slim.
author: Mike Florio

title: Thursday Night Football: Jaguars blow out Ravens 33-10
summary: The Jaguars outgained the Ravens 319 to 227 and forced three Baltimore turnovers.
full_text: The Jaguars didn't eat the cheese. They didn't overlook the Ravens. Jacksonville cruised to a 33-10 victory, moving to 6-2. Baltimore lost its fourth consecutive game to fall to 4-5. Without starting quarterback Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley, and with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano making his first start, the Ravens' game plan was simple: Run the ball and shorten the game. They didn't stand a chance despite 34 runs and 19 passes and a slight edge in time of possession (30:45 to 29:15). The Jaguars won for the eighth time by 20-plus points since the start of last season. The Ravens didn't have a first down in the second half until Justice Hill ran for a 65-yard touhdown with 7:15 remaining. Baltimore ended with three first downs in the second half and 10 for the game. The Jaguars outgained the Ravens 319 to 227, and the visitors forced Baltimore into three turnovers. Jourdan Lewis and Montaric Brown each had an interception of Fagnano, and linebacker Jalen McLeod forced and recovered a fumble by LaJohntay Wester on a kickoff. Fagnano finished 10-of-18 for 60 yards and two interceptions. Hill had nine carries for 85 yards, and Henry moved up to seventh on the NFL's all-time rushing list with 57 yards on 17 carries. Lawrence went 16-of-26 for 242 yards and a touchdown. Jakobi Meyers had four catches for 65 yards; rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher caught two passes for 61 yards; and Parker Washington had two catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. Bhayshul Tuten had 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown, and Ameer Abdullah had seven carries for 30 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens rule out Kyle Hamilton with a hip injury
summary: Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton was injured in the second quarter and briefly returned after halftime.
full_text: Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton was injured in the second quarter and briefly returned after halftime. His night, though, is finished. The Ravens ruled out Hamilton with a hip injury. He has three tackles, including a tackle for loss, and a pass defensed. The Jaguars lead 23-3 in the fourth quarter after Cam Little's second-half field goals of 45 and 47 yards. The Ravens had 25 yards and no first downs in the third quarter and have only 126 yards and seven first downs for the game.
author: Charean Williams

title: Derrick Henry moves to seventh on the NFL's all-time rushing list
summary: The Ravens running back passed Jerome Bettis (13,662) and LaDainian Tomlinson (13,684).
full_text: The Ravens haven't had much to celebrate Thursday night, but Derrick Henry gave the home fans something to cheer. Henry had 51 first-half rushing yards, which was enough to move him into seventh on the all-time rushing list. He passed Jerome Bettis (13,662) and LaDainian Tomlinson (13,684) in moving from ninth to seventh. Curtis Martin is next on the list, with his 14,101 career rushing yards ranking sixth all time. Henry entered the night with 632 yards for the season and 13,650 in his career. Over the past four seasons, Henry has averaged 1,578 yards. He has averaged 85 yards per game in his career. Henry will need to play another three to four years to break Emmitt Smith's record of 18,355 yards. Smith was 35 years old in his final season of 2004. Henry turns 33 in January. Smith said earlier this year that he believes Henry has a chance to break his record.
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: Jaguars lead Ravens 17-3 at halftime
summary: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence was 9-of-15 for 197 yards and a touchdown in the first half.
full_text: The Ravens were hanging . . . until they weren't. Baltimore was within one score with less than 2 minutes to play in the first half. But Parker Washington beat Malaki Starks, and after a bobble of Trevor Lawrence's pass, secured the catch and raced 50 yards for a touchdown with 58 seconds left in the half. The Jaguars lead the Ravens 17-3 at halftime. The Ravens started undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve. They opened the game with Derrick Henry in the wildcat and called seven plays out of the formation. The Ravens had 17 runs and 12 passes as they shortened the half. Henry had 12 carries for 51 yards and threw a pass that lost 3 yards. Zay Flowers had two rushes for 16 yards and two catches for 2 yards. Fagnano, who lined up at quarterback for only 12 plays, was 7-of-11 for 30 yards. The Jaguars outgained the Ravens 223 to 101, with Lawrence going 9-of-15 for 197 yards and a touchdown. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, who was questionable to play with ankle and foot injuries, scored a 1-yard touchdown on the team's opening drive. He has 22 yards on eight carries. Jakobi Meyers has four catches for 65 yards, with Washington adding two for 61 and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher one for 52. Linebacker Foyesade Oluokun leads the Jacksonville defense with six tackles and a sack. The Ravens held the ball for 17:31 of the first 30 minutes.
author: Charean Williams

title: Myles Garrett remains limited participant Thursday
summary: Rams outside linebacker Myles Garrett remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
full_text: Rams outside linebacker Myles Garrett remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice. Garrett returned to practice Wednesday, his first practice since Week 1. Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September after playing 40 snaps in the season opener. He was given a six-week prognosis and has missed seven games. He and Aaron Donald could play together for the first time on Sunday when the Rams play the Commanders. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant again. The Rams had only two changes to their injury report: Inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring) did not practice after being limited Wednesday, and offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring) was a full participant a day after being limited. The Rams again practiced without cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) and safety Kam Curl (foot). Wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) remained limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Joe Milton on his first start: The NFL is about being ready when your number is called
summary: Joe Milton has never started an NFL game.
full_text: Joe Milton has never started an NFL game. The closest he came was in Week 18 of the 2024 season when Patriots starter Drake Maye played only three snaps before giving way to Milton, who played the final 61 snaps. Milton looked like a starting NFL quarterback in that game, completing 22 of 29 passes for 241 yards and a touchdown. Less than two years later, Milton is on his third team and has played only 51 snaps in four appearances with Dallas since. He will make his first career start on Sunday when the Eagles play the Giants. “I was just pretty much going through the plays , going through the week like I was a starter, or like I was playing, and just being ready,” Milton said Thursday, via Olivia Reiner of the Philadelphia Inquirer . “And that’s what the NFL is about: Just being ready when your name is called, and just preparing for those moments.” The Eagles signed Milton off the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16 after they placed Jalen Hurts on injured reserve due to blood clots. Tanner McKee started the past three games, but went 0-3 as the Eagles ran their losing streak to six games. Milton has had a crash course in learning the playbook and the terminology, which he said reminds him of the West Coast scheme he had in New England his rookie season. Milton was asked how much of the Eagles’ playbook he knows. “Shoot, whatever’s in this week,” he said with a laugh.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaguars score on opening drive for 7-0 lead on Ravens
summary: The Jaguars didn't waste any time in showing off on national television.
full_text: The Jaguars didn't waste any time in showing off on national television. They took the opening kickoff and moved 77 yards on seven plays, with running back Bhayshul Tuten scoring from the 1 on third down. Tuten was questionable to play with ankle/foot injuries. It was the only third down the Jaguars faced on the drive. Trevor Lawrence was 3-for-4 for 72 yards, including a 52-yarder to rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher. Boerkircher got lost by the defense as Lawrence rolled to his right to avoid pressure. Lawrence also threw a 16-yard pass to Jakobi Meyers. Tuten has two carries for 5 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Thursday Night Football: DE Travon Walker, RB Bhayshul Tuten active for Jaguars vs. Ravens
summary: The Jaguars will have running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker for Thursday Night Football against the Ravens.
full_text: The Jaguars will have running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker for Thursday Night Football against the Ravens. Both players are active after being questionable on the final injury report. Walker has a rib injury and Tuten injured his ankle/foot last week. Walker has played in every game, seeing action on 330 defensive snaps. He has totaled three sacks, seven quarterback hits, one pass defensed and 18 tackles. Tuten has played 241 snaps in seven games, totaling 125 touches for 673 yards and six touchdowns. The Jaguars' inactives are wide receiver CJ Williams, cornerback Alijah Huzzie, safety Cam'Ron Silmon-Craig and defensive end Wesley Williams. The Ravens' inactives are quarterback Kedon Slovis, wide receiver Elijah Sarratt, offensive lineman Emery Jones Jr., defensive lineman Aeneas Peebles, cornerback Nate Wiggins (stinger/illness) and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee). Slovis is the emergency third quarterback, meaning Austin Reed, who the Ravens signed on Monday, will be the No. 2 quarterback behind Joe Fagnano.
author: Charean Williams

title: John Lynch on Brandon Aiyuk: We'll look for a path that works for both sides
summary: Brandon Aiyuk filed for reinstatement from the 49ers' left squad list this week and he's expected to be at the team's facility on Friday to take the next step in resuming his football career.
full_text: Brandon Aiyuk filed for reinstatement from the 49ers' left squad list this week and he's expected to be at the team's facility on Friday to take the next step in resuming his football career. Once he is reinstated, the 49ers will have a choice between keeping him on the active roster, trading him or releasing him. The latter option is seen as the likeliest given the lack of trade interest earlier this year and both head coach Kyle Shanahan and General Manager John Lynch saying that Aiyuk is done playing for the Niners. Shanahan said on Wednesday that his thinking hasn’t changed and Lynch said on KNBR Thursday that the team is working with the league to come up with the best solution. "Look, I think the way I'll characterize it, number one, we've got a 6-1 football team that we think has really got a shot at this thing this year ," Lynch said. "So our focus is going to remain on this team. Kyle spoke of that yesterday. Having said that, I have a job to do, and it entails a lot of different things. This is kind of a unique situation, not one you have — so there's really no playbook, but I always go back to what's my charge, what's my job. My job is to look out for the best interests of the 49ers, and as such, in this particular situation, we're working with the NFL management council to navigate through kind of a different situation. It's fluid. I'm going to kinda leave it at that because I've been recommended to do so, and I think it's the right thing to do. We'll look for a pathway for both sides here that works. Next week we can talk a little more in detail about the process because kind of a fluid situation." Lynch said generally that anything is possible when asked if there's any way Aiyuk could return to the team and said the wideout's new agent Drew Rosenhaus "is a good guy to deal with" before reiterating that he'd have more to say in the future about the entire situation.
author: Josh Alper

title: As Chargers' offense struggles, Mike McDaniel will move from the sideline to the booth
summary: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will get a different perspective on his struggling offense on Sunday against the Texans.
full_text: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will get a different perspective on his struggling offense on Sunday against the Texans. McDaniel said today that he will move upstairs to the booth to call plays after previously working from the sideline. “One of the things that I want to try is call plays from the box to see adjustments for myself and communicate with the position coaches appropriately what things we can focus on between series,” McDaniel said. "I won't be in the same spot." Although the Chargers' offense has been among the worst in the NFL this season and head coach Jim Harbaugh has faced questions about whether he should fire his offensive coordinator, McDaniel insisted that he's not concerned about the criticism. "My problem solving doesn't come from insecurity," McDaniel said. "I'm not trying to prove or justify anything." The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in scoring, having scored only 99 points this season, and they have an NFL-high 17 turnovers. McDaniel said he thinks it's worth trying something different while delegating some of what he had been doing on the sideline to the assistant coaches. “Seems like a good action to take based on how things have gone this year, and realistically something that I’ve only brought up because I've observed, I’m very confident in the rest of the offensive coaching staff and how they’re able to set the tone and communicate information on the sidelines. So I feel a little more comfortable to try that," McDaniel said. If that doesn't work, Harbaugh's next step might be to move McDaniel from the booth to the unemployment line.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Back surgery will keep Robert Kraft from Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame induction
summary: Patriots owner Robert Kraft recently underwent back surgery, which will keep him sidelined on "injured reserve" and force him to miss Rob Gronkowski's induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday.
full_text: Patriots owner Robert Kraft recently underwent back surgery, which will keep him sidelined on "injured reserve" and force him to miss Rob Gronkowski's induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame on Saturday. "As much pain as I was in before having surgery, it pains me even more to miss the ceremony," Kraft, 85, told Mike Reiss of ESPN on Thursday. Doctors ordered Kraft to stay off his feet, so he will also miss the Patriots' game against the Packers on Sunday and the trip to Munich for a Week 10 game against the Lions. Fans voted Gronkowski into the Patriots Hall of Fame in April in his first year of eligibility. Gronkowski, having undergone multiple back surgeries during his playing career, understood Kraft's absence, the owner said. "I always told Gronk that in my next life, I wanted to come back as him, because I had never seen him have a bad day. But after a couple of back surgeries, I take that back. I never want to experience that again," Kraft said.
author: Charean Williams

title: Breece Hall up to full practice Thursday, says he's ready to play this week
summary: It looks like running back Breece Hall will be back in the Jets lineup this week.
full_text: It looks like running back Breece Hall will be back in the Jets lineup this week. Hall practiced in full for the first time since suffering the quad injury that has kept him out for the last five games. Hall said after practice that he is ready to play against the Chiefs. Braelon Allen has impressed during Hall's absence and is coming off a season-high 147 yards against the Raiders. Offensive coordinator Frank Reich was asked about how the team will balance the workload during a Thursday press conference. "We have some plays that are tagged for one or the other, but it's a great problem to have," Reich said, via a transcript from the team. "You got two number one backs. Breece is obviously the bell cow, he's our guy, but it'll be a mix. And as far as hot hand, not hot hand, I think that's always an in-game feel thing, it really is. My experience in it, because I've had that experience, I know I haven't had two guys like this, but yeah, it's just an in-game feel thing." Linebacker David Bailey (groin), linebacker Joseph Ossai (ankle), linebacker Demario Davis (rest), safety VJ Payne (knee), and tight end Mason Taylor (neck) also moved up to full participation. Defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle), linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin), and wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) remained out of practice.

title: Raiders re-sign WR Cody White, waive TE Carter Runyon

Tight end Carter Runyon was waived in a corresponding move. Runyon was activated from injured reserve in the corresponding move to White's Wednesday release. White has eight catches for 112 yards and three touchdowns in eight appearances this season. title: Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy, citing more than $3.45 million in debt
summary: Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice is in the final year of his four-year, $6.45 million rookie contract.
full_text: Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice is in the final year of his four-year, $6.45 million rookie contract. He nevertheless has far greater liabilities than assets. And he's looking to wipe the slate clean as to at least some of them. Via ESPN, Rice has filed for federal bankruptcy protection . The filing cites more than $3.45 million in debts, with $2.1 million of it tied to multiple plaintiffs in the accident caused by his street-racing incident in early 2024. Rice has yet to get a second contract. He's due to become a free agent in March, and he has played well enough to get signed, by the Chiefs or someone else. By then, Rice should have more than enough money to pay all of his debts without relying on the ability to activate Chapter 7 of the bankruptcy laws to discharge some or many of them for cents on the dollar. That could be the first argument made by his creditors. Given Rice's earning potential, it's just a matter of time before he has the money needed to pay all of his bills and settle all of his debts.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joe Brady on cutting S C.J. Gardner-Johnson: "It was the best interests of the football team"
summary: On the day the NFL suspended former Bills safety C.J.
full_text: '' On the day the NFL suspended former Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for spitting on an opponent, Buffalo coach Joe Brady said the team would not be cutting Gardner-Johnson. After the game that Gardner-Johnson missed, the Bills cut him. Meeting with reporters on Thursday, Brady explained the reversal. “There was a lot to evaluate," Brady said. "You know, we got together and figured out, 'Hey, this is what we felt like this was the best thing to do for the Buffalo Bills.' I have so much love for [C.J.]. Like, I really do. I loved getting to coach him. I loved being around him. I loved — I did love the edge, and his personality allowing him to be him, right?, and as a person. So that didn’t make the decision easy at all. "But we also have to be an organization that, you know, it's unfortunate obviously what happened, you know? But it also opened a door and an opportunity for guys the other day, and that was a part of evaluation. And seeing how those guys kind of played, and you know with a lot of the roster moves. And, again, this wasn't — we didn’t come out of the game post Vegas and say, 'This is what we were going to do. We're just gonna do this the following Monday.' We were, you know, the plan was him being here and we were going to evaluate it after the game in Baltimore. And we felt like with some of the moving parts we had to do it was the best interests of the football team .” Gardner-Johnson's suspension opened the door for Damar Hamlin to start the game against the Ravens. And Hamlin apparently did well enough to help the Bills realize that, all things considered, the "best interests" of the Bills meant the Bills were better off without the " high maintenance " Gardner-Johnson.

title: NFL Week 9 picks: Our experts face off on Bengals vs. Falcons, Packers at Patriots and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
It's safe to say that last week lived up to the hype. The Detroit Lions defeated the previously undefeated Minnesota Vikings , the Denver Broncos used a goal-line stand to hand Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs their second consecutive loss, and the Chicago Bears upset the Seahawks in Seattle with some help from trade-deadline addition Jeffery Simmons .
This weekend in the NFL , the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons will battle in Madrid, Jordan Love takes the Green Bay Packers to Foxborough to play the New England Patriots and Baker Mayfield gets a shot at Caleb Williams and the red-hot Bears.
Which teams should you pick in Week 9, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 4 from DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research for its hard work.
Dajani ( Jaguars -10): It's tough to pick this game since we are unaware of the Baltimore Ravens ' quarterback situation. Will they be starting rookie third-stringer Joe Fagnano , or someone else? I believe the Jaguars will win, but any team can cover a double-digit spread at home.
Jacksonville is a remarkable 14-3 over its last 17 games and is the only NFL team leading its division by three or more games. Trevor Lawrence leads the NFL in passer rating (112.6), while the Jags lead the league in points per game differential (+12.1). Sure, you can say the Ravens will just ride Derrick Henry , but the Jaguars have what is statistically the No. 1 run defense in the NFL, and have gone 24 straight games without allowing a 75-yard rusher. … Prediction: Jaguars 28, Ravens 13
Dubin (Jaguars -10): The Ravens simply do not have the horses to compete with the Jaguars this week. Not with their third-string quarterback (who is coming off an injury of his own), and not on a short week. Jacksonville should roll and win with relative ease.  … Prediction: Jaguars 27, Ravens 6
Dajani (Falcons +3): I may take the upset here. I'm aware the Falcons just registered one of the most embarrassing losses of the season in Tampa, but I'm willing to overlook that given how bad the weather was. I have some questions about the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner has a heel injury, and Cashius Howell just broke his wrist. Then, this Cincy defense allowed the lowly Tennessee Titans to put up 440 yards of total offense last week and allowed the first Titans' 300-yard passing game since the 2023 season. Tony Pollard rushed for 117 yards and two touchdowns, so what is Bijan Robinson going to do? Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are the best wide receiving duo in the league, but the Bengals may be due for their first loss in over a month. Remember, this Falcons team beat the San Francisco 49ers the last time they played a game indoors. Give me the points. … Prediction: Falcons 27, Bengals 23
Dubin (Bengals -3): The Cincinnati offense is rolling, with Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins dunking on opposing defenses. Meanwhile, the Falcons have been struggling to run the ball as of late despite the presence of Bijan Robinson (48 carries for 200 scoreless yards in the last three weeks). The Bengals do provide an opportunity for the run game to get back on track (4.8 yards per carry allowed), but Dexter Lawrence has shut down other rushing attacks before. If the Bengals can keep Robinson in check, I'm not sure Atlanta can count on Michael Penix Jr . to go shot for shot with Burrow.  … Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 20
Dajani ( Rams -5.5): I think the Washington Commanders are a feisty team that could cover this number, but don't forget that this is somewhat of a revenge game for Sean McVay. He spent seven seasons in Washington before the Rams made the smart decision to hire this 30-year-old kid to run their franchise. In his first season as a head coach, McVay lost to his former team. Since then, he's 2-0 vs. Washington, winning each game by at least eight points. The Rams are coming off back-to-back wins by 14+ points. They also could get Myles Garrett back on Sunday. LA is 11-2 SU and 10-3 ATS in its last 13 games vs. teams entering below .500.  … Prediction: Rams 27, Commanders 17
Dubin (Rams -5.5): The Rams have finally climbed back to .500 with back-to-back wins over the Raiders and Chargers , and I think they can keep things rolling here by doing what they did against those two teams: running the ball. Washington has actually been pretty good against the ground game this year, but it just lost Daron Payne to a significant injury. On the other side of the ball, I don't think we can count on the Commanders' offense to produce enough points to keep up with LA's offense.  … Prediction: Rams 24, Commanders 16
Dajani (Broncos -2.5): I told you the Broncos would beat the Chiefs last week. The conversation around Bo Nix is so bizarre to me. He's not Josh Allen , obviously, but he's not worth benching either. He's not the most prolific passer in NFL history, but he's Superman when it comes to leading his team to wins in crunch time. Denver does have a great defense, which pulled off that goal-line stand vs. Kansas City, but Nix leads the NFL since 2000 with 9.1 yards per attempt when down by one score in the fourth quarter. He has 15 game-winning drives to his name, which is one shy of the most in a three-season span in NFL history. Nix hasn't even played three full seasons. It hasn't always been pretty, but Nix is pretty good in those fourth quarters.
This week, Denver travels to take on the Carolina Panthers . Bryce Young 's offensive line has some serious issues, and those were evident last week against the Packers. Through Week 8, Carolina has allowed 23 sacks, which is tied for second-most in the NFL, with 11 of those sacks coming in the past two games. Plus, the Panthers' defense has allowed an incredible 42.7 points per contest in their first three home games, which eventually led to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week.  … Prediction: Broncos 24, Panthers 20
Dubin (Broncos -2.5): I'm not buying into Nix as much as Dajani is, but I am buying into Denver's defense being able to get after Bryce Young behind what is an increasingly leaky offensive line and preventing the Panthers from denting the scoreboard. If they can keep this a low-scoring game, I like them to pull out a win on the road.  … Prediction: Broncos 23, Panthers 17
Dajani (Packers +3): The Packers got some extra rest following their Thursday win over Carolina, while the New England Patriots couldn't run away from the Miami Dolphins . This Packers offense has been fun to watch — not counting the ground game,  which has registered the fewest rushing yards (485) by a team above .500 through eight games in NFL history. However, Jordan Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards, while Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are the first duo to have 600 yards receiving each through eight games since Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill in 2022! Drake Maye has been great, having scored at least three touchdowns over five straight games, but this Packers defense will provide quite the test. Green Bay has allowed just 14.6 points per game over its last five.   … Prediction: Packers 27, Patriots 24
Dubin (Packers +3): I also think Green Bay's extra rest will matter here, even if only because it will give Christian Watson some extra time to heal up from the ribs injury he suffered last Thursday night. The Packers are going to need him against New England, even if he ends up drawing shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez , as that will just open things up for Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft . Meanwhile, Green Bay's defense has been excellent for several weeks now, and with the Patriots down multiple weapons in the passing game, I think the Packers can try to make New England one-dimensional here, limiting their chances to move the ball downfield.  … Prediction: Packers 26, Patriots 20
Dajani (Bears -6): I correctly…

title: 100 days until Super Bowl LXI: 100 things to know about the playoff race, contenders, predictions
summary: We are officially 100 days from the Super Bowl. Here are 100 facts and storylines to get you ready
full_text:
It feels like just yesterday the Seattle Seahawks defense dominated the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LX, winning 29-13. Kenneth Walker III became the first running back to win Super Bowl MVP since Terrell Davis, while the Seahawks finished with the best point differential (+246) in a season by a Super Bowl champion since the 1999 Rams . It was a magical — and unexpected — run.
Believe it or not, we are just 100 days away from Super Bowl LXI in Inglewood, California. In honor of the football world reaching this 100-day countdown, let's break down 100 facts about the NFL season as a whole. From tidbits about the "Big Game" itself to the most likely teams to play into the month of February, the players best set up to win MVP, storylines to keep an eye on moving forward, and more.
All odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
1. Super Bowl LXI is Sunday, Feb. 14, 2027.
2. This is the latest Super Bowl of all time. A Super Bowl has never been played this late into February.
3. Kickoff is set for 6:30 p.m. ET.
4. SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, is the site of the Super Bowl this year. (Home of the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers )
5. This is the second time SoFi Stadium has hosted the Super Bowl. The first was in 2022, when the Rams defeated the Cincinnati Bengals , 23-20.
6. California will host a Super Bowl for the 15th time, the second-most of any state behind Florida (17).
7. Super Bowl LXI will air on ESPN with a simulcast on ABC.
8. The Super Bowl will stream on Fubo ( try for free ).
9. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman will call their seventh Super Bowl together.
10. The Monday after Super Bowl LXI (Feb. 15) is Presidents' Day — a federal holiday.
11. The San Francisco 49ers are favored to win the Super Bowl at +550.
12. 49ers vs. Buffalo Bills is the favored Super Bowl matchup at +1250.
13. The 6-1 Bills are favored to win the AFC East (-300).
14. The 5-2 Bengals are favored to win the AFC North (-166).
15. The 5-2 Jacksonville Jaguars are heavy favorites to win the AFC South (-1600).
16. The 6-2 Denver Broncos are favored to win the AFC West (-130).
17. The 4-2-1 New York Giants are favored to win the NFC East (-150).
18. The 6-2 Chicago Bears are favored to win the NFC North (+164).
19. The 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers are favored to win the NFC South (+184).
20. The 6-1 49ers are favored to win the NFC West (-480).
21. Bills QB Josh Allen (+165): The most dynamic quarterback in the NFL has gotten the Bills off to a 6-1 start, throwing for 1,793 yards, 11 touchdowns, five interceptions, plus 270 yards and nine more touchdowns on the ground. He and running back James Cook III are just the third teammate duo in NFL history to each score seven rushing touchdowns through the first seven games of a season, and the first duo since Jim Taylor and Paul Hornung of the 1960 Green Bay Packers .
22. 49ers QB Brock Purdy (+450): Purdy is 6-1 this season and has completed 69.2% of his passes for 1,748 yards, 15 touchdowns and four interceptions. Fun fact: Purdy has the highest passer rating (104.8) in NFL history. Despite all of the injuries at wide receiver in San Francisco, Purdy has thrived in a division that features the reigning Super Bowl champions and an alleged "Super Team."
23. Bengals QB Joe Burrow (+475): Burrow is on a heater. He just became the first player in NFL history to complete 70% of his passes with four touchdowns over three straight games. He leads the NFL in completion percentage (73%) and passing yards per game (302.1) this year, and had a ridiculous outing last week against the Tennessee Titans , where he completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards, five touchdowns and three interceptions, with one rushing touchdown.
24. Bears QB Caleb Williams (+500): Last season, the Bears' quarterback was an exciting playmaker with accuracy issues. This season, Williams looks like a top five quarterback. He just became the first Bears quarterback to lead his team to 30+ points with zero turnovers in three straight games and has completed 74% of his passes for four touchdowns and zero interceptions with a 111.3 passer rating since returning from his hamstring injury.
25. Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence (+950): Lawrence has led the Jaguars to a 6-2 record, and entered Week 9 leading the NFL in passer rating (112.6). His 18 passing touchdowns are the most by a Jaguars player through eight games all-time, and his squad is running away with the AFC South. No other NFL team has been this dominant in their division this season.
26. Detroit Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs is the frontrunner to win Offensive Player of the Year (+155).
27. Houston Texans EDGE Will Anderson Jr . is the favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year (+230).
28. Titans WR Carnell Tate is favored to win Offensive Rookie of the Year (+350).
29. New York Giants LB Arvell Reese is the favorite to win Defensive Rookie of the Year (+220).
30. New Giants head coach John Harbaugh is favored to win NFL Coach of the Year (+225).
31. Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes is the favorite to win Comeback Player of the Year (-150).
Credit to CBS Sports Research
32. The Chiefs need a receiver : Did you know Mahomes has more playoff wins (9) than passing touchdowns on 20+ air yard throws (7) since the Tyreek Hill trade? Mahomes is the only quarterback in the past 20 years to average under 5.0 air yards per attempt over three straight games within a season, and his career-low 5.8 air yards per attempt this season ranks second-lowest in the NFL. The Chiefs have a dynamic running back, but they need a receiver. Who will Kansas City add at the trade deadline?
33. NFC contenders in trouble : Both the Seahawks and Rams are 4-4 entering Week 9. According to CBS Sports' forecasting and projections, there was a 5.7% chance both of these NFC West teams would be .500 or below entering Week 9. Only two teams have won a Super Bowl with a .500 or worse record this late into a season: The 2001 Patriots and 2011 Giants.
34. Tee Higgins WR1? : Ja'Marr Chase is probably regarded as the best wide receiver in the NFL, but he hasn't even been the best wide receiver on his own team this year! Tee Higgins ranks second in the NFL with 726 receiving yards. His 0.82 EPA per target with Burrow ranks best among all duos with 40 attempts this season, and his 36.1% explosive target rate ranks best by any duo through seven games in the past 25 years. Higgins has been unstoppable.
35. Can Bo Nix take the Broncos all the way? : Denver would have likely made the Super Bowl last year if its QB didn't suffer a brutal ankle injury in the divisional-round victory against the Bills. The Broncos made a habit of slow starts followed by explosive endings, and we're seeing the exact same script in 2026. Nix averages the fewest air yards per attempt this year, yet his 9.1 yards per attempt when down 1-8 points in the fourth quarter ranks best in the NFL since 2000. He's 9-1 when down 1-8 points in the fourth quarter over the past two seasons, and 10-1 if you want to include playoffs. Nix's teams average 8.1 points per game in the fourth quarter. That's the best mark by a starting quarterback since 1950. The Broncos have an aggressive defense and a top-tier offensive line. Imagine if the quarterback starts playing with some consistency.
36. Could a team that has never made the Super Bowl make the Super Bowl? : There are just four teams that have never played in a Super Bowl: the Cleveland Browns (5-3), Detroit Lions (5-2), Houston Texans (2-5) and Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2). Three of these teams could win their divisions this season, setting up a road for a Super Bowl run.
37. What about the last remaining undefeated team?: The Minnesota Vikings were the last remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as they started 6-0 before running into the Lions last Sunday. That's not always a good sign for a future Super Bowl run. The last time the last undefeated team won a Super Bowl was in 2006 with the Indianapolis Colts . The Vikings were the last undefeated…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL Week 9 bold predictions: Joe Milton-led Eagles upset first-place Giants, Vikings torture Josh Allen
summary: Plus, the Dolphins stifle Jared Goff and the roaring Lions offense
full_text:
Anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 9 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea.
The Baltimore Ravens defense entered Week 9 on a 12-game streak of not allowing a 50-yard play, but they allowed two to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the first half of a 33-10 "Thursday Night Football" home defeat. It's also incredibly stunning that Ravens running back Derrick Henry has run for under 60 yards in four consecutive games. However, he did surpass Pro Football Hall of Famers LaDainian Tomlinson and Jerome Bettis for seventh on the all-time rushing list Thursday night.
It's also a good thing Baltimore traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett this week because the Ravens have now scored 14 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time in Ravens history.
What other shocking events could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 9 menu of games? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.
The New York Giants (4-2-1) are 3.5-point road favorites at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6), per DraftKings Sportsbook, marking the first time they are favored over the back-to-back NFC East champs since 2016. It makes sense: The Eagles have lost six in a row, and the Giants have gone three consecutive divisional games without a loss.
However, the Eagles will snap their losing streak on Sunday behind new starting quarterback Joe Milton III . Milton, who was Dak Prescott's backup with the Dallas Cowboys since 2025, was scooped up off of the Cowboys' practice squad by Philadelphia. He will take his turn at the wheel of the Eagles' offense after Tanner McKee lost all three of his starts this season.
Milton will bring big plays back to Philadelphia's offense. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer has compared Milton's arm strength to that of Brett Favre , whom he coached with the New York Jets in 2008.
This preseason, Milton showed significant strides in the accuracy and touch departments in Dallas' three exhibition games in 2026. He completed 29 of his 43 passes (67.4%) for 378 yards, three passing touchdowns and no interceptions for a 118.2 passer rating. Milton will use the lessons he learned from Prescott to emerge victorious over a Giants team Prescott has dominated throughout the course of his career.
Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores YOLO defense leads the NFL in the following statistics:
They are bad news for any offense, but especially a Buffalo Bills offensive line that is allowing a 38% quarterback pressure rate, the 11th-highest in the league this season. Bills 2024 NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen has a propensity for going haywire in primetime against the league's top defenses. In the Week 12 edition of "Thursday Night Football" at the Houston Texans last season, Allen absorbed a career-high eight sacks.
Playing on the road in Minnesota on "Monday Night Football" in Week 9 against Flores' ferocious pass rush group could lead to a slightly similar disaster. The Vikings will sack Allen over five times, something that has happened to him just four times in his nine-season NFL career.
The Cowboys' (3-5) defense hasn't recovered from trading away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers less than a month away from the start of the 2025 season. Dallas has allowed 29 points per game since 2025, making them the second-highest-scoring defense in the entire league. That figure is driven by the Cowboys allowing 20-plus points in 15 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the NFL.
However, they will go on the road and hold the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) to under 20 points on Sunday. Indianapolis is fresh off a 42-7 defeat at the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, and they have scored 10 or fewer points in consecutive games for the first time since 2022. Facing a familiar face in Colts quarterback Daniel Jones , whose 68.7 passer rating is the worst in the league this season, the Cowboys will finally hold a team under 20 points for the first time since Week 11 of the 2025 season.
New York appeared to suffer a major blow when Jets running back Breece Hall , whom the team extended on a three-year, $43.5 million contract this offseason, went down in Week 3 with a quadriceps injury. However, 2024 fourth-round pick Braelon Allen slid into the Jets starting running back spot and has balled out ever since. Allen's 504 rushing yards in the five games since Hall's injury are the second most in the entire NFL behind only Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving's 548.
Despite the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs allowing the eighth-fewest rushing yards per game (96.3) in the NFL this season, Allen will go off for over 100 once again to become the first Jet with five consecutive games with 100-plus scrimmage yards since running back Thomas Jones in 2008.
The Detroit Lions (5-2) are soaring this season, leading the NFL in total offense (395.4 total yards per game) and ranking third in scoring offense (29.0 points per game). Quarterback Jared Goff is at the center of that success.
Goff is averaging 280.6 passing yards per game (third in the NFL) with 15 passing touchdowns (tied for fifth in the NFL) and just one interception. Goff is the fourth quarterback to have those numbers through the first seven games of a season, joining Tom Brady (2015 and 2016), Alex Smith (2017) and Patrick Mahomes (2019). Goff is also third in the NFL in EPA per dropback (0.25).
However, the Miami Dolphins (1-6) will keep Goff relatively in check by holding him to under 200 yards passing. The only team to do that to Goff in 2026 is the Vikings, the NFL's No. 1 defense. However, the Dolphins will do it on the strength of 2024 first-round edge rusher Chop Robinson's efforts. Robinson leads the NFL in quarterback pressure rate (20.6%) this season (among those with at least 100 pass-rush snaps), and Robinson will get in Goff's face enough to throw him off his game.

title: Tee Higgins is putting up historic numbers, and it's changing the Bengals offense
summary: Higgins has always been one of the NFL's best contested-catch receivers, but new dimensions in his game have him producing at a historic pace
full_text:
Eight weeks into the NFL season, Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins has been one of the best at his position. Higgins has 43 receptions for 726 yards and four touchdowns, meaning he ranks eighth in receptions, second in yards and eighth in touchdowns despite having already taken his bye week.
On a per-game basis, Higgins averages career-bests in receptions (6.1) and yards (10-3.7) per game, putting him on pace for a full-season receiving line of 104 catches for 1,763 yards and 10 scores. Those are marks that have been matched or exceeded just six times in NFL history: by Jerry Rice and Isaac Bruce in 1995, Antonio Brown in 2015, Cooper Kupp in 2021, Tyreek Hill in 2023 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba in 2025.
Interestingly, Higgins has the exact same number of targets and receptions as teammate Ja'Marr Chase , but he has 234 more receiving yards than his counterpart. It's the per-target efficiency that has been the difference, and it's reversed compared to their previous years together.
Higgins' efficiency across many areas is at a career-best level, in fact. He is being targeted on his routes at the second-highest rate of his career. He's converting those targets into yards, first downs and explosive plays at a higher rate than ever. And he's producing successful gain (in terms of expected points before and after the play, according to Tru Media) at a higher rate than ever.
Higgins is doing a lot of the stuff he's always done. He's making contested catches like crazy, using his body to shield defenders away from the ball and haul in the pass that Joe Burrow places for him on a dime. Higgins so far ranks 10th in the league in tight-window receiving yardage despite ranking just 25th in tight-window targets, per NFL Pro. That's because he's caught 60% of the passes thrown in his direction on those plays, the third-best catch rate among the players with 10-plus tight-window targets. (Only Trey McBride and Nico Collins are ahead of him.)
pic.twitter.com/3Hou18sN2P
Higgins' average separation on targets this year is only 2.5 yards, per NFL Pro, which is the 10th-lowest mark out of 138 qualified pass-catchers, indicating that Burrow trusts him to win in the tightest of windows.
He has been especially effective on back-shoulder throws, which have become a specialty for Higgins over the years. Because he's such a dangerous deep threat, he's able to threaten defenders that he's going straight up the field, then contort his body and reel in the ball when it's thrown just behind him and short of where the defender expects it to go.
pic.twitter.com/G69HqgtFvs
But it's not just the usual stuff that has been effective for Higgins. He's expanded the repertoire this season beyond where he's been effective in the past.
For example, Higgins has been far more involved in the off-schedule passing game so far this season. He already has more receptions and receiving yards on throws at least 2.5 seconds after the snap than he did all of last year, according to Tru Media, and he's on pace to post by far career-best figures in those areas, as well as nearly all efficiency metrics when it comes to targets on extended dropbacks.
pic.twitter.com/oWF1tLkiqU
Higgins has also been more involved in the middle-of-the-field passing game than in the past. Because of his role as the X receiver, Higgins has tended to do most of his work outside the numbers, working the deep ball, back shoulder fades, out routes, corner routes, things of that nature.
But he's running more digs and posts and slants this year, in addition to all the deep and out-breaking stuff, and it's paid off. Higgins has 470 receiving yards on throws between the numbers this season, according to Tru Media, which is already a career high. His 29 receptions on 33 targets on those throws represent an outrageous success rate, as he and Burrow have shown mind-meld chemistry on in-breaking routes so far this season.
pic.twitter.com/7sXTCeb8OT
Higgins' yards after catch numbers have also bounced back a bit this season after trending downward over the last two years. He's almost a full yard per catch ahead of last season's pace despite the fact that he's seen targets a career-high 13.62 yards down the field, on average, and that the farther downfield players are targeted, they generally produce fewer yards after the catch. Higgins is doing the opposite — creating more yards after catch on deeper-than-average throws.
pic.twitter.com/WK6xMurlGh
All of this has resulted in Higgins putting together what looks like a career season. He's been considered over the past few years to be the 1B to Chase's 1A, but their production levels have suggested more that Higgins was the clear No. 2 and Chase the clear No. 1. This season, that hasn't been the case. And the Bengals' offense has been better off for it. Whether that continues through the rest of the season is anybody's guess, but the way Higgins is balling to start the year, I wouldn't necessarily bet against him keeping it up.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: One realistic, one pipe dream trade scenario for every playoff contender
summary: What does each contender need to put them over the top?
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than a week away, and every team is in position to either put themselves over the top in hopes of a playoff push, or to completely reset their franchise and move on to NFL Draft season.
We've already seen big names like LG Quenton Nelson and DTs DeForest Buckner and Jeffrey Simmons getting dealt before the deadline. And I get the feeling that more big names will be on the move once we get to November 10.
For every team in the current playoff picture, we'll break down one realistic trade and one pipe dream trade they can make to put themselves over the top, in addition to a few interesting ones outside of the playoff mix.
Pipe Dream Trade: Jessie Bates, S, Atlanta Falcons
Realistic Trade: Amani Hooker , S, Tennessee Titans
The Bills have gotten more than enough from their defensive front, a unit that I thought would come along slowly in the beginning of the season. EDGE Greg Rousseau is playing at a DPOY-caliber level, and the emergence of DT Deone Walker has helped their defensive line gain some teeth. However, the Bills have given up the fifth-most completions of 20+ yards in the NFL this season and lack impact play from their secondary.
Cornerback is a spot where they could improve, but they have a lot of faith in rookie CB Davison Igbinosun opposite Christian Benford . However, the safety spot opposite Cole Bishop could use some improvement. While most people will point to Arizona Cardinals ' safety Budda Baker as the top target, he and Bishop's skillsets overlap.
Bates is entering the final year of his contract with the Falcons, and he has been an impact player when the ball is in the air and when separating the ball from the player (three PBUs, one INT and three forced fumbles in 2026). Bates is the perfect complement to Bishop and could help tilt the scales back in the Bills' favor.
Hooker makes a lot of sense as a realistic target for the Bills. There's some freedom in his contract as he enters the final two years of his 2025 deal, but he's a reliable post safety who can complement Bishop's skills closer to the line of scrimmage.
Pipe Dream Trade: RB Jonathan Taylor , Indianapolis Colts
Realistic Trade: TE Dallas Goedert , Philadelphia Eagles
I wouldn't be surprised if the Broncos ultimately stand pat at the deadline, after all the rumors and whispers that they're looking for something big. With the emergence of RB Jonah Coleman in this offense, the Denver running game has found some new life to go along with the mandatory second-half Bo Nix resurgence.
However, if the Broncos were looking to make a big swing, it would obviously be for Colts' RB Jonathan Taylor. While Coleman has been very good, the explosiveness Taylor would bring makes a pedestrian Broncos offense more dangerous from anywhere on the field (since 2023, Taylor has 78 explosive runs, 5th-most in the NFL). This season, Denver is 26th in Explosive Play Rate, behind teams like the Philadelphia Eagles and the Tennessee Titans, and offense gets really hard when you can't generate explosives. Taylor is not only a big-play machine but would also loosen some of the constraints on the Denver offense as they try to make the Super Bowl .
Now, for a realistic trade scenario, I do think the Broncos look at other positions. I doubt they'd be able to get him from within the division, but LB Daiyan Henley could really give the Broncos' defense a nitro boost. However, I'm eyeing Eagles' TE Dallas Goedert as a realistic trade target.
The Broncos have gotten next to nothing out of their tight end group this year (second-lowest receiving yards to TEs this season, per TruMedia). Goedert is entering the final year of his contract with the Eagles. He would give the Broncos a reliable player down the seams and a competitive blocker who wouldn't be an obvious tell when he's on the field.
Pipe Dream Trade: WR Josh Downs , Indianapolis Colts
Realistic Trade: CB Amik Robertson , Washington Commanders
The Steelers have surprisingly found themselves at the top of the AFC North behind an offense that's gone fully into bullyball, but at the deadline I think adding a receiver with some separation skills could really give the Pittsburgh passing offense some juice. The Steelers have struggled this season throwing against man coverage, ranking 25th in EPA per play and 30th in Success Rate on all dropbacks against man coverage. DK Metcalf hasn't inspired much confidence in the receiver room, and despite the emergence of rookie Germie Bernard , the room overall doesn't have much teeth.
Enter Josh Downs, who is the exact receiver this version of the Steelers needs. Since 2023, among all players with 175 total targets, Downs is 13th in the NFL in percentage of receptions  (80.4%) against man coverage that go for first downs or touchdowns. While he's more of a slot receiver, he's a guy who can win with crafty route running and acceleration in and out of breaks. QB Aaron Rodgers loves throwing sight adjustments and option slants to receivers when he sees the number count in his favor, but those haven't worked with Metcalf. Downs can win on those and give the Steelers an easy button in their passing game.
Their most realistic option could be on the other side of the ball, however. The Steelers' secondary needs more speed and urgency, and no two words embody Amik Robertson more. The Commanders' CB plays with zero fear and has inside/outside versatility, giving DC Patrick Graham options with the cornerback room. Robertson also has experience with Graham from his time in Las Vegas. He feels like an easy and reliable candidate for Pittsburgh to go after.
Pipe Dream Trade: DT Christian Barmore
Realistic Trade: DT Zach Sieler
The Jaguars were in the market for more interior help even before the injury to DT Davon Hamilton , but with Hamilton out for the rest of the season the need for the Jaguars to add there becomes increasingly important. Even with some of the need at safety, Hamilton was a massive part of why the Jaguars were so good in run defense. Losing him puts a significant chunk into what they want to be defensively, and I think the Jaguars will want to replace his spot as they get ready to make a deep playoff run. On top of that, the Jaguars' pass rush production from the interior has been lacking, with rotational DT Ruke Orhorhoro leading the group in pressure rate at 11.2%. Getting more productivity from the group is paramount.
There are plenty of names that stand out as trade options at DT, but I think the biggest fish they could get is Barmore, a productive and imposing pass rusher who might be on his way out of New England. The Pats have gotten good play from their rotational guys such as Cory Durden and Leonard Taylor , and while Barmore has been a very good pass rusher, the Pats could see him as expendable. Barmore leads the Patriots in total pressures since 2025, and his 11.8% pressure rate since 2025 would be the best on the Jaguars in that same time period. Barmore's presence would make Jaguars' EDGEs Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker's jobs easier as pass rushers as well.
If they miss out on Barmore, Zach Sieler would be a nice consolation for a cheaper price. The Dolphins are looking more towards 2027, and Sieler doesn't seem to be in the plans for the Dolphins' youth movement going forward. Sieler had a down year last season, but he's a hard charging DT who wins with effort and has 16 pressures in seven games so far. He would take the load off of Hines-Allen and Walker, and while not providing as much pop as Barmore, he would be another quality piece added to the Jags' pass rush.
Pipe Dream Trade: WR Garrett Wilson , New York Jets
Realistic Trade: WR Brian Thomas Jr ., Jacksonville Jaguars
Are you sensing a theme with the Chiefs ? Kansas City has been looking for help since Tyreek Hill left, and this season has been one of the most dire for the receiving group. With WR Tyquan Thornton out for an extended period of time, the Chiefs need more explosive capability and…

title: Dak Prescott delivers blunt assessment of Cowboys' offensive identity: 'Are we proud of it? I don't know'
summary: Prescott's frustrations could be boiling over as Dallas reaches its midseason point
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Dak Prescott offered a blunt assessment when asked whether the Dallas Cowboys have established an offensive identity through eight games.
"Is it one we're proud of? I don't know," Prescott said Thursday. "We'll be better, I can promise."
Dallas is scoring 27.4 points per game, but its offense has become less varied and less quarterback-friendly in 2026. The Cowboys rank near the bottom of the NFL in pre-snap motion and use play action and under-center formations less frequently than last season.
The Cowboys ranked in the top half of the league in play-action rate (28.2%), under-center rate (38.4%) and motion rate (56.6%). With Brian Schottenheimer leading the offensive playcalling, the Cowboys now profile as second-to-last in motion rate (36.5%), 22nd out of 32 teams in under-center rate (30.4%) and 21st in play-action rate. This was always going to be a pass-first offense with Prescott and his superstar receivers, but with general inefficacy (94.1 rushing yards per game, eighth-worst in the NFL) in 2026, Dallas is running the football at the fifth-lowest rate in the league at 32.5%.
The disconnect is between Schottenheimer and Prescott, with the coach seemingly believing it's harder to use motion when trailing and that it can "cloud the picture" for a quarterback. Prescott has a different approach.
"Sometimes, it's [motion] just to dress it up and take the defense, give them a different look of us running a core play and breaking some tendencies with a motion to get this play done," Prescott said. "Sometimes it's used strictly for me to see the disguise, to see the matchups that we've got or to create different matchups by moving them from one side to the other and really just getting all the information I can through motion."

If Schottenheimer doesn't reinstall the easy buttons in the Cowboys' offense, Prescott and company may struggle to keep Dallas above water while its porous defense continues to drown.

title: Cowboys stars reject George Pickens trade talk ahead of NFL deadline
summary: As speculation builds about Pickens' future in Dallas, Prescott praised him as a teammate and Lamb explained how the receiver changes opposing defenses
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- There has been plenty of smoke about the Dallas Cowboys considering a George Pickens trade. The NFL trade deadline comes Nov. 10, and the 25-year-old is playing out the 2026 season on the franchise tag.
If the decision about whether or not to trade Pickens was in the hands of Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb , Pickens would not only not be traded but extended when eligible in the 2027 offseason.
"People say a lot of things I don't believe, so I'm not listening to that one, either," Prescott said Thursday when asked about those who think Pickens should be traded.
Lamb credited Pickens for his own strong start to the 2026 season. Lamb ranks third in the league in catches (60), third in receiving yards (709) and tied for second in receiving touchdowns (six). A year ago, Pickens' 1,429 receiving yards ranked third in the NFL. This year, Pickens' 533 receiving yards rank 16th.
"I don't know why that's a thing," Lamb said Thursday of Pickens' trade talks. "C'mon man. Everything that I have been able to accomplish has been because of him and what he's done the year before. Vice versa with everything that I've accomplished the year prior to that. He exposed them [opposing defenses]. Just kind of taking what the defense is giving us, and I feel like that goes hand in hand with why I'm able to do what I'm doing at a great pace."
One of the reasons why Pickens trade talk emerged is because Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer singled him out. After a 23-13 road defeat at the Green Bay Packers , Schottenheimer singled out Pickens' performance as a run blocker after the Cowboys produced a season-low 48 rushing yards. It wasn't just Schottenheimer's critique that fueled the trade talks, it's how Schottenheimer has deployed Pickens since those remarks.
Since Week 7, Lamb clearly leads the way in offensive snaps with 106. Over the last two games, Dallas No. 3 wide receiver Ryan Flournoy (98 offensive snaps) has 19 more snaps than Pickens (79). Lamb leads the way in targets on the team over the last few weeks with 23, and Pickens has just two more targets (10-8) than Flournoy in this span. The team has attributed some of that to Pickens dealing with shoulder and hamstring injuries, and entering Week 9 with the Indianapolis Colts , Pickens is listed only as having a hamstring injury instead of both issues. Prescott maintains that Pickens has been nothing but a great teammate in light of Schottenheimer's recent comments.
"George is a great teammate," Prescott said. "And I say that in the sense of, he's gonna do whatever is asked, he's going to do whatever is called. If it's to go block, if it's to just go run a guy off, he's going to do that. He believes in just doing the right thing, and the ball will come his way at times. And so, that's not on George."
Lamb, who is far and away Pickens' best friend on the Cowboys, is doing what he can to keep Pickens' head up so that he can thrive once again when the football finds its way back to him.
"Just when his time comes, I know that he is going to be ready," Lamb said. "That's the only conversation that we have. When that moment comes, you can't really go off of what just happened because if that's the case, you're going to drive yourself into a ditch to be honest. You have to move on, be grown about the situation, come to practice ready to work again and have that same mentality that you had before the game. Remember how you felt. Use that as fuel."
So what can be done to get Pickens going early for a Cowboys offense that has had bouts of inconsistency in its 3-5 start to the season? Get plays on Schottenheimer's call sheet that feature Pickens early in the game.
"I think if anything is going to really come on this later end of the week and just how we sequence up the starters and the plays, the list that we put together of how we want to start this game," Prescott said. "I think from there, you'll see."
