title: NFL playoff picture: Five games with the biggest postseason implications as Packers face pivotal test
summary: SportsLine projections reveal how Packers-Patriots and four other pivotal matchups could alter postseason chances
full_text:
The NFL season reaches its unofficial midway point this weekend, and teams hoping to be relevant for the final two months of the regular season are seeing their margin for error shrink and shrink exponentially.
No division is better -- or more competitive -- than the NFC North, where the team in last, the 5-3 Packers , would be in the playoffs if they started today. The NFC North has a legitimate shot to be the first division in the current conference alignment to put four teams in the playoffs, but given how tough the in-division games will be, none of them can afford many slip-ups outside the division. Green Bay has done a terrific job rallying from an uninspiring 1-2 start to put themselves in a position to be relevant. But, as we'll see, that's still a precarious position.
Using SportsLine's projections, we take a look at what's on the line for the five most important games of the weekend and how their results will impact the playoff picture.
Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo, try for free )
After unsteady starts from both teams, the Patriots and Packers would both be in the playoffs if they started today ...  but only as the No. 7 seeds in their respective divisions.
But the playoffs don't start today. In fact, we're only just now reaching the halfway point of the regular season. That makes this showdown between big-play quarterbacks Jordan Love and Drake Maye a huge one. After a relatively easy stretch, the Patriots have a tough stretch -- Packers, at Lions , at Chargers , Bills , Vikings , at Chiefs -- upcoming. The Packers, meanwhile, go at Patriots, Vikings, at Rams .
One of these teams will enter the second half of the season feeling really good. The other? Not so much.
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo, try for free )
It's not quite an elimination game -- we're still way too early for that -- but the 4-4 Rams dropping below .500 would be a massive blow for the preseason Super Bowl favorites. Los Angeles has won two straight and should make it three in a row. There just isn't enough room for error left for the Rams, especially when they're favored.
The Commanders, meanwhile, are just kind of sticking around in the lowly NFC East. A Week 10 game against the Giants will be crucial, but if they can spring an upset before that, it'd be a nice boost for their postseason hopes.
Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC (Stream: fubo, try for free )
For the third straight week, the Bears are on primetime, and if it goes half as well as Monday night's statement blowout of the Seahawks did, Chicago will win its fourth straight and move to 7-2.
But let's not just hand this one to Caleb Williams and co. The Buccaneers have won three of four after a nightmarish 0-4 start and now look like a potential frontrunner in the NFC South. Tampa Bay's turnaround has been fueled by a dominant running game and terrific defense.
Both of these teams are in competitive division races, but for very different reasons. The NFC North is historically great. The NFC South is awful. That means big implications.
Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox (Stream: fubo, try for free )
Similar to the Rams, the Seahawks (also 4-4) wouldn't be completely out of it with a loss, but it would be a devastating early blow. The reigning champs simply have to take care of business in games like these. That's what happens when you have a slow start: Your back is starting to get close to the wall by November.
The Cardinals, meanwhile, are looking to play spoiler, and if we learned anything from last week's Gardner Minshew-led comeback win over the Cowboys , it's that Arizona is more than happy to do just that. Seattle's defense, though, is an entirely different beast.
Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network (Stream: fubo, try for free )
The NFL's international games continue after a one-week break, and it's a big chance for both teams. The Bengals can keep up in the AFC North, while the Falcons can get back into the win column and stay right in the thick of the NFC South race. Considering both the Buccaneers (at Bears) and the Panthers (vs. Broncos ) both have tough tasks, the Falcons going abroad and coming back with a win would be a huge result.

title: Cardinals trade updates: Sweat & Budda
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are trying to get back into the thick of things this year. Beating the Dallas Cowboys last weekend after being dominated for the first half is a sign that this roster still has a good degree of fight in it, and that the season is not lost. What is helping is that […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 01: Budda Baker #3 of the Arizona Cardinals exits the field after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are trying to get back into the thick of things this year. Beating the Dallas Cowboys last weekend after being dominated for the first half is a sign that this roster still has a good degree of fight in it, and that the season is not lost. What is helping is that this year, the other teams in the NFC West Division are also struggling, such as the Los Angeles Rams and the Seattle Seahawks. RELATED: BRISSETT TRADED TO THE RAVENS It is true that Arizona still resides at the bottom of the division with a 3-5-0 record, but unlike other years, they are now just one game out of second place. Usually, when teams begin their season badly, when the trade deadline rolls around in November, it is assumed that these horrid teams will begin trading off their best players, who just happen to be some of their most expensive athletes. Because the Cardinals began 2-5-0, they were tossed into this category. And even though the team is on a one-game winning streak, they remain on the “sellers” list, especially after the Jacoby Brissett trade. Here are two players that have been earmarked for being involved in a trade, and their updates. EDGE Josh Sweat For over a month, Sweat has been mentioned by just about every national and local media outlet as a potential trade. Last year, he had 12 sacks, 17 QB hits, and 28 pressures, among other stats. He was a menace on passing downs and proved his worth after being signed to a huge deal in free agency. If the Cardinals had sought out a trade partner during the offseason, Sweat would have brought a bounty of draft picks. But that was last year. His production this season has been subpar, with 3 sacks, 5 QB hits, and 9 pressures through eight games. Which means his trade value has lessened, even though the Cardinals have the same DC and the same defensive scheme as last year. However, it should be noted that Sweat has three sacks in his last five games. What is his update? For one, the franchise is admitting that Sweat is available before the trade deadline on November 10. But GM Monti Ossenfort has also stated that they are fine with keeping him and hope that his production will increase going into the second half of the schedule. Someone tell Andrew Berry Josh Sweat has 3 sacks in his last 5 games pic.twitter.com/EgAYQLFCPo — Mac🦬 (@tha_buffalo) November 3, 2026 And Arizona will most likely retain his services because Ossenfort isn’t letting Sweat go for cheap. Word is, the Cardinals have a high asking price, which will keep some teams in the probability category, while others will simply bow out. Sweat has stated that he would be amenable to a trade, or would be happy to stay put. The Cardinals have complete control over this situation. Considered dead, by coming back and beating Dallas the way they did, it is quite possible that a QB change will alter this offense going forward, and that Arizona isn’t interested in letting Sweat walk away. After all, every NFL club is always looking for a good pass rusher, and Sweat has two more years remaining on his contract. We will see this weekend against the Seahawks how this offense will react with QB Jacoby Brissett being relegated to the bench and Gardner Minshew elevated to the starting role. But this team may, or may not, be more competitive than once thought. Multiple clubs have reached out to Ossenfort so far, with the Cowboys the loudest voice. Other interested teams include the Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals. The San Francisco 49ers have also been mentioned, but the unwritten rule is that a club never trades within the division, and they try not to trade within the conference. Josh Sweat is open to a trade, per @Schultz_Report Multiple teams interested, but Cardinals asking price is believed to be high pic.twitter.com/kijVSsuGcB — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) November 3, 2026 Arizona has not divulged what their asking price is, but all along it has been estimated to be a Day 2 pick, meaning a second or third-round draft pick, with a fourth or fifth-round selection thrown in. The big question remains: Is it worth it to the Cardinals’ defense to suddenly be without their only productive pass rusher for a draft pick that isn’t going to help them at all this season? If things go well against Seattle, look for Ossenfort to stand pat on Sweat, then readdress a trade possibility in the offseason if his production doesn’t increase to last year’s level. Safety Budda Baker Nobody knows where the gossip began about Baker being on the trade market, but every year, his name appears. Maybe his agent starts the rumor. Baker has publicly stated that he is happy playing for the Cardinals organization, and that he likes the defensive scheme and gets along well with DC Nick Rallis. "I don't think Arizona wants to move on from Budda Baker.. He's meant so much to that franchise and he's such a baller" ~ @AdamSchefter #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/OZSjpcBo0k — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 2, 2026 The thinking in the organization at this point is that they are very content with Baker’s production, his tackling numbers, and his leadership in the locker room. The Cardinals are not actively seeking a trade unless they receive an offer that would blow the doors off. Which isn’t going to happen. Recently, on the “Pat McAfee Show,” NFL Insider Adam Schefter stated that Ossenfort has little to no interest in moving Baker.

title: Arizona Cardinals designate Isaiah Adams to return from injured reserve
summary: It has been a rough season with injuries once again for the Arizona Cardinals, but they could be getting at least one piece back. The team announced they have opened the 21 day practice window for Isaiah Adams, and the Cardinals desperately need help along the offensive line. From the team: The Arizona Cardinals Football […]
full_text: It has been a rough season with injuries once again for the Arizona Cardinals, but they could be getting at least one piece back. The team announced they have opened the 21 day practice window for Isaiah Adams, and the Cardinals desperately need help along the offensive line. From the team: The Arizona Cardinals Football Club today announced that the team has designated offensive lineman Isaiah Adams to return from the injured reserve list. Adams can begin practicing and the team can activate him to the 53-man roster at any time during the next 21 days or at the conclusion of the three-week period. In addition, the team has signed running back Jermar Jefferson and wide receiver James Proche II to the practice squad. The signings took place today at the Dignity Health Arizona Cardinals Training Center in Tempe, AZ. Jefferson (5-10, 215) returns to the Cardinals after he played two games with the team last season in addition to spending time on Arizona’s practice squad. In his career, Jefferson has appeared in 11 games (one start) with the Cardinals and Lions and has 96 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 21 carries to go along with five receptions for 33 yards. He entered the league with Detroit as a seventh-round pick (257 th overall) in the 2021 NFL Draft out of Oregon State. Proche (5-11, 193) is a seven-year NFL veteran who has played 71 games (three starts) in his career with Tennessee (2025), Cleveland (2023-24) and Baltimore (2020-22). In his career, he has 34 receptions for 364 yards to go along with 68 punt returns for 591 yards (8.7-yard avg.) and four kick returns for 60 yards. Proche entered the league with Baltimore as a sixth-round pick (201 st overall) in the 2020 NFL Draft from SMU. He was on the Browns practice squad earlier this season. Jefferson will wear jersey #37 and Proche will wear #18. The wide receiver position is obviously one of need as well, so the Arizona Cardinals added a couple of pieces there as well, but Adams is really the one to watch, and hopefully he can make it back on the field in the window.
author: Seth Cox

title: What to know about Falcons – Bengals in Week 9
summary: From rain in Florida to sunny skies in Spain, from a punishing rushing attack to a high-flying aerial assault, from a division rival to an AFC powerhouse in the making. The Falcons are facing a very different kind of challenge in very different circumstances this week, and they must be ready to rise and face […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 18: The Cincinnati Bengals offense lines up against the Atlanta Falcons defense during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 18, 2023 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images From rain in Florida to sunny skies in Spain, from a punishing rushing attack to a high-flying aerial assault, from a division rival to an AFC powerhouse in the making. The Falcons are facing a very different kind of challenge in very different circumstances this week, and they must be ready to rise and face that challenge after a sloppy, stupid loss against the Buccaneers in Week 8. What do the Bengals bring to the table? How will the Falcons have to attack this game if they’re going to win? Here’s a primer for Week 9’s big game in Madrid. Team rankings Team Record Points Scored Yardage Passing Yards Rushing Yards Points Against Yardage Against Passing Yards Against Rushing Yardage Against Turnovers Created Turnovers Surrendered Falcons 3-5 23 21 24 4 17 18 18 18 19 31 Bengals 5-2 2 7 1 30 14 26 26 20 8 18 The Falcons can run the ball better than the Bengals and are less inclined to let offenses march up and down the field on them—though maybe not after last week!—but Cincinnati outclasses them virtually everywhere else. Their passing game is elite, they’re better at not turning the ball over, and they’re better at forcing turnovers, all of which will make life difficult on Sunday. The Falcons just don’t have the profile of a good team right now, both based on their up-and-down play and their broad statistical profile. We’ll see if they can buck that this week. How the Bengals have changed We haven’t seen the Bengals in a while—these two teams last played in 2022—but we’ll just focus on this offseason. The biggest move was a loss, as the Bengals let Trey Hendrickson walk to the division rival Ravens. They made up for that by trading their first round pick for Lawrence, who has absolutely kicked ass, and adding Boye Mafe, Jonathan Allen, and Bryan Cook to the defense. Their offensive additions were essentially a pair of new starting offensive linemen in tackle Orlando Brown Jr. and guard Dalton Risner, and every one of their draft picks is currently a backup, though some of them have considerable promise. There’s a real high-ceiling nucleus here already, though, so the additions at key positions have clearly put the Bengals in a better spot this year, so long as Burrow stays healthy. What to know about Week 9 This is almost the exact opposite of the challenge the Buccaneers presented in Week 8. The Falcons will have agreeable weather in Madrid, more than likely, but they’ll face a Bengals team with a weak rushing attack, weak run defense, and excellent passing game. That’s playing into Atlanta’s relative strengths much more than the past few weeks, but as Caleb Williams showed us in a surgical dissection of the Falcons’ back end, a great one-dimensional attack is still a tough problem to solve. Joe Burrow has 13 touchdowns and and nearly 1,000 yards over the past three games against just three interceptions, and if he’s picked on some lackluster secondaries in Miami and Tennessee in particular, he’s still remarkably dangerous. The fact that he’s throwing to the best wide receiver tandem in football in Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, alongside capable options like tight end Mike Gesicki and running back Samaje Perine, helps his cause a great deal. The Falcons can and basically have to get pressure to counter this. Burrow can be a wizard in the pocket but in his last full healthy season, he absorbed 48 sacks and can hold on to the ball too long to try to make a play. He’s been excellent against pressure the last two seasons but has thrown four picks under pressure in 2026 and is still markedly worse when pressured than when he has a clean pocket, which makes Atlanta’s attacking front a must. The Falcons need to resign themselves to allowing a few big plays and having a day that’s statistically not super pretty, but if they can force a couple of turnovers and a handful of Burrow misses and throwaways, they can potentially swing the outcome. Part of that is because the Bengals cannot run the ball. Atlanta’s run defense has been badly exposed the past few weeks, but the Bengals aren’t equipped to take advantage. Chase Brown and Samaje Perine have had league average success rates, roughly, and Brown is averaging a meager 3.5 yards per carry behind a line that has a couple of shaky run blocking options, most notably Amarius Mims. The Bengals will try for some balance, but hopefully that will be a fool’s errand. If the Falcons can keep Burrow from completely taking over the game, the offense will have to pull its weight. That will start with a major bounceback game from Michael Penix Jr. and the passing game, which just endured an absolute nightmare effort in the rain against the Buccaneers. DJ Turner has been pretty excellent in coverage in 2026 and Kyle Dugger is solid, but the rest of their secondary has struggled with big plays, struggled on a down-to-down basis, or both. Atlanta has a particularly juicy matchup if they can get Kyle Pitts or Bijan Robinson working against linebackers Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter, who have combined to allow 49 completions on 62 targets for 607 yards, or fully one-third of the team’s total allowed passing yards and receptions. The back seven can be picked apart and the defense can be overcome—they just allowed the most points the Titans have scored in five years — should Penix have the time to do so. They do have to watch out for an opportunistic team that has already forced ten fumbles in 2026. That’s not a given, because Cincinnati’s pass rush has been dangerous. Their interior of the lethal Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, and Kris Jenkins have combined for nine sacks already, and Boye Mafe has another 4.5 coming off the edge. The Falcons will need to be very good on the interior in particular to avoid Lawrence and company blowing up Penix’s pocket, which has reliably led to bad outcomes in 2026, whether those be sacks, fumbles, interceptions, or just costly throwaways. The remedy to that will be not letting the Bengals pin their ears back, which means running the ball effectively. Fortunately for Atlanta, the Bengals run defense has been merely decent, as they’re 19th in yards, have missed a lot of tackles against opposing run games, and don’t really have any elite run defenders outside of Lawrence. If there was ever going to be a week to get this ground game going again, it would be this one, when the Falcons will badly need to achieve some balance. The formula here is, once again, clean but complicated to actually execute. If you can slow Burrow and the passing game and take advantage of a talented-but-not-great Cincinnati defense while limiting turnovers, you stand a chance. Falling down in any one of those areas—not being able to run, letting a pressured Penix make costly mistakes, allowing Burrow to really get rolling—likely will mean a rough day in Madrid.

title: Bad weather can’t be the main cause of Falcons’ ugly defeat
summary: After the Falcons’ ugly loss in Tampa Bay, plenty of discussion focused on how the weather affected their performance. A nasty rainstorm affects every team’s play. Look no further than Baker Mayfield, who didn’t complete a pass on three attempts and fumbled multiple times. Instead of forcing a balanced attack, Tampa Bay solely relied on […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons hands off to Bijan Robinson #7 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the Falcons’ ugly loss in Tampa Bay, plenty of discussion focused on how the weather affected their performance. A nasty rainstorm affects every team’s play. Look no further than Baker Mayfield, who didn’t complete a pass on three attempts and fumbled multiple times. Instead of forcing a balanced attack, Tampa Bay solely relied on the ground game and brutalized their opponent. They adapted to the conditions and used their strengths to break a divisional rival down in the trenches. The Falcons couldn’t move the ball efficiently on the ground or stop the run. That put the game in Michael Penix Jr.’s hands, and he proceeded to have the worst game of his career. Todd Bowles’ squad embraced the chaotic environment and flourished in it. Kevin Stefanski’s team was rattled in it and drowned in gruesome fashion. Much more went into that abysmal performance than a rainstorm preventing them from executing. A one-sided defeat stems from self-inflicted errors, personnel breakdowns, coaching miscues, and players not being good enough. That’s what the Falcons have to accept when assessing what went wrong. A quarterback’s miserable meltdown From not being able to push the ball downfield to having to adjust your footwork, a massive rainstorm will challenge how a signal caller operates in the pocket. What it shouldn’t change is how the quarterback reads the field and processes defensive looks, especially when he receives solid pass protection. Penix Jr. was completely discombobulated in the pocket, making numerous costly errors and misses. His inability to see Alex Anzalone on his first two interceptions was perplexing. The first turnover came from Anzalone dropping off the line of scrimmage into the short area of the field. The linebacker never tried blitzing into the C-gap. He went straight back into coverage and somehow capitalized on an errant Penix Jr. pass that was lofted into his hands. Penix Jr. didn’t see him there or on the next drive, where he tried to connect with Jahan Dotson down the seam. That throw went directly to Anzalone once again for another interception. The fourth-down interception to Jacob Parrish was the one excusable turnover, as it was a desperate heave in a collapsed pocket on a make-or-break play. There was no poor processing or decision-making. But that came back to haunt him on the final interception, where Zyon McCollum didn’t bite on the fake smoke screen. While the play design deserves criticism (more on that below), Penix Jr. used a pump fake before attempting to throw with anticipation, assuming McCollum would bite. The cornerback didn’t budge and capitalized on another appalling mistake from Penix Jr. Three of the four interceptions were squarely on the enigmatic quarterback. He had some ugly incompletions because he still doesn’t consistently throw the ball well in the intermediate middle area of the field. Bad weather will limit, not ruin, a quarterback’s ability to perform. Franchise quarterbacks have to prove they can overcome adversity and operate functionally in difficult circumstances. Penix Jr. failed to do that in a big divisional game. Overmatched in the trenches Mother Nature doesn’t impact how your linemen compete in the trenches. On both sides of the ball, the Falcons were mauled during long stretches. The undersized defensive front was bound to have issues against one of the league’s more physically imposing groups. Tampa Bay’s offensive line did its share of damage, but an overall team effort helped spring Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell into the open field. Chris Godwin and Payne Durham made multiple key pin and seal blocks to create space at the second level. As Tristian Wirfs and Cody Mauch imposed their will, the skill position players blocked like demons to disorient the Falcons’ attack front. Defensive linemen were getting erased in the run game. The starting rookie linebacker tandem struggled, particularly Harold Perkins Jr., who couldn’t get off his blocks and missed a few tackles. It was a humbling day for a unit missing size up front, as they didn’t receive much support on the back end, with defensive backs missing tackles all over the place. The offensive line was equally as humbled on the ground. My colleague Tre’Shon Diaz noted in his piece that Bijan Robinson averaged 2.6 yards per carry on 18 attempts if you remove his 30-yard gain. Most of his yards came from an extraordinary effort to keep his balance through a pile to produce an explosive play. Matthew Bergeron has played better in spurts, but he has failed to live up to the lofty contract extension he received this past summer. Ryan Neuzil’s physical limitations have become problematic against bigger fronts. Jake Matthews offers little as a run blocker at this point, while Jawan Taylor was repeatedly behind on his assignments. As much as the Falcons want to be fast and athletic in the trenches, the lack of sheer size and gap-moving power is glaring in these one-sided defeats. Short-yardage shortcomings Per The Athletic’s Josh Kendall, the Falcons faced ten third- and fourth-down plays of two yards or less. They gained a grand total of four yards on those plays. That includes not converting any of their 12 third downs. It was an appalling performance that requires some serious soul-searching. They can’t be solely reliant on Penix Jr. and Charlie Woerner to sneak to convert every time. They also need to understand the challenges facing Tampa Bay’s front. No matter how much you pride yourself on running the ball, you need in-game adjustments for your game plan against specific units. Tampa Bay has one of the league’s strongest run defenses. Calling runs that kept going directly toward Vita Vea was baffling. When the Falcons produced solid gains on the ground, it came from gap-scheme runs with offensive linemen pulling and other personnel making down blocks. They also had flashes of positive gains on stretch runs. It was nowhere near what Irving and Gainwell did, but it proved to be effective in spurts. You can’t call those runs often in short-yardage situations, but more variation is needed to attack a defense playing at a top-ten level. It nearly worked in the first quarter on a third-and-two when Kyle Pitts was open downfield on a deep crosser off play action. After coolly evading a blitzing Anzalone in the pocket, Penix Jr. had the space to hit Pitts for a likely touchdown. He sailed it well over his head with no Tampa Bay defender in sight. Although the execution wasn’t there, that type of clever, aggressive play calling could make the difference in solving these frustrating woes. Screens are becoming wasted plays What was supposed to be one of the offense’s schematic strengths is a genuine liability. Stefanski and Rees were praised for how well they utilized screens in Cleveland. The timing was on point. The execution was crisp. Offensive linemen and skill-position players handled their blocking assignments while defenders chased them downfield. Outside of Bijan Robinson’s opening-day touchdown against Pittsburgh, it’s hard to recall many significant screens. Opposing defenders are diagnosing them as soon as the ball is snapped. They beat opposing blocks by accelerating to the intended target before the ball arrives. Tykee Smith blew up a screen designed for Pitts on 3rd-and-2. While Chris Blair missed his assignment, it’s extremely hard to fulfill it when defensive backs like Smith instantly know where the ball is going. Even though Penix Jr. is at fault for his final interception, the fake smoke screen was oddly designed. It’s bizarre that Woerner is the primary target downfield running a wheel route. Although the design could deceive the defense, the…

title: Ravens Week 9 hangover discussion: top priorities after loss to Jaguars
summary: The Ravens sure know how to ruin a perfectly good Friday. Baltimore dropped to 4-5 with their Thursday night loss to the Jaguars, a pitiful 33-10 effort that had most of the home fans – at least, the ones who showed up in the first place – heading for the exits midway through the third […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 05: Head coach Jesse Minter of the Baltimore Ravens looks on against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the fourth quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 05, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens sure know how to ruin a perfectly good Friday. Baltimore dropped to 4-5 with their Thursday night loss to the Jaguars, a pitiful 33-10 effort that had most of the home fans – at least, the ones who showed up in the first place – heading for the exits midway through the third quarter. The Ravens have plenty of homework in their 10 days before their Week 10 matchup with the Chargers, starting with finalizing their trade for Jacoby Brissett and installing him as their new starting quarterback. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle and offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford need to whip the offensive operation into shape to give Brissett’s a gunslinger’s chance of putting up points in the coming weeks. Tuesday’s trade deadline is also looming for a roster caught in no man’s land between competing and retooling pending Lamar Jackson’s recovery from thumb surgery. A fire sale seems far-fetched, but if a team comes calling after Chidobe Awuzie or even Derrick Henry, should Eric DeCosta pick up the phone? And then there are the big questions. Where is this team going, long-term? How will they handle Jackson’s contract? Can DeCosta remake the roster to fit Jesse Minter’s vision or will the Ravens Way continue year after year with the same disappointing results? You may not want to touch those last few in the throes of another hangover from a rough loss, so let’s focus on the short-term. What should be the Ravens’ immediate next steps heading into the weekend and towards the trade deadline? Nikhil’s take: Step 1 is completing the Brissett trade without giving up more than mid-Day 3 value. Then comes a long, tough conversation about the Ravens’ current roster deficiencies and need for a more aggressive overhaul in the offseason. From there, naturally, trade talk should follow. Anyone on an expiring deal without plans for an extension should be available – including players like Trenton Simpson who could net a compensatory pick in the offseason. The same is true of players who will be released in the offseason, making them ineligible for the comp pick formula. In any even, playing the comp pick game only works if teams do not spend in free agency, and the Ravens might have to if they are truly committed to a new era of football in Baltimore.

title: Ravens discussion: instant reactions to Week 9 loss to Jaguars
summary: The Baltimore Ravens came into their Thursday night matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars with low expectations – which they met. Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano managed just 60 passing yards on a clearly-injured ankle, and the Ravens’ defense allowed far too many explosive plays through the air. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the 33-10 […]
full_text: Nov 5, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Joe Fagnano (12) and Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) exit the field after the game at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: James Lang-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens came into their Thursday night matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars with low expectations – which they met. Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano managed just 60 passing yards on a clearly-injured ankle, and the Ravens’ defense allowed far too many explosive plays through the air. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s instant reactions to the 33-10 defeat: Nikhil Mehta I am going to take a far more charitable tack towards this loss than my colleagues. It went, more or less, exactly as I expected. The Ravens showed up early and looked, in brief spurts, like they could hang around in the game, but it was clearly a mirage. Declan Doyle’s creativity was limited by Joe Fagnano’s apparently inability to plant and throw off his ailing right ankle, especially behind a porous offensive line that could not hold the Jaguars’ defensive front. Baltimore’s defense was not going to miraculously turn around in less than a week, especially against one of the NFL’s top offensive minds in Liam Coen. That’s a perfect recipe for a blowout, especially with a home crowd that was (understandably) ready to check out early. The offense can flush this one and move on with Jacoby Brissett, but the defense under Jesse Minter and Anthony Weaver has been bad. Shockingly bad. The unit needs a major personnel overhaul this offseason. Zach Canter I don’t even know what to say or do at this point. We all knew this game had the potential to get ugly but I don’t think any of us had pictured exactly this ugly. I dont know where the Ravens go for here but there’s still eight more games to go. This product was unwatchable so as much as I hate investing more capital into the 2026 Ravens, the Jacoby Brissett trade seems necessary, just for the fact so the weapons on the outside don’t look as miserable as they did tonight. I don’t think I saw Zay Flowers smile once. At lot of questions need to be answered, but that won’t happen till this offseason. Until then, we trudge on and survive. Hopefully they’ll sell a few pieces at the deadline and kickstart the process. Kevin McNelis I’ve lived through some dark times as a fan of this team, but it’s been a while since I’ve felt this way. Maybe since the Super Bowl hangover when they lost a lot of pieces of the title team, but this iteration hints at some dark days to come with all of the bloated contracts and none of the payoff of having won a title. They should absolutely sell at the deadline. They need a hard reset on the roster and whatever it takes to shift the broken mentality of this group, especially that defense. My thoughts are with Jacoby Brissett. I just hope he goes out there and has some fun playing ball. Mark Myers Rock bottom. Everything that could have gone wrong did. The players plaguing the team with mistakes week after week kept doing so. The few standout players this year struggled today, adding insult to injury. The offense was putrid. Declan Doyle didn’t trust Joey Fagnano to push the ball at all, which is an even bigger statement on the state of a fully healthy offensive line. The defense continued to show a lack of effort. I wonder how Marlon Humphrey will blame the fans this time. Jacoby Brissett is definitely better than Fagnano, but not enough to make up for this woefully underperforming roster. Jacksonville is a great team, but they didn’t need to look like one to win convincingly tonight. Hopefully, the Ravens can show up for the occasion under the lights in Week 10 against the worst team in the league. But, man, I am struggling to find any reason to be excited for that game. Dustin Cox There really isn’t too much to say about this team right now. This simply isn’t a good enough roster, especially without Lamar Jackson at quarterback. An undrafted rookie quarterback never had a chance in this situation on a short week, dealing with an ankle injury on top of everything else. Too many of the Ravens’ top-paid players and veterans continue to underperform, whether it’s Marlon Humphrey giving up a massive completion on the first drive, Mark Andrews fumbling a direct snap on fourth down or he and Ronnie Stanley both having their weekly false starts. Baltimore just needs to get through this season and gut this roster in the offseason. Jackson potentially returning at some point this season almost feels pointless, because even he would have a hard time putting this team over the hump if they somehow, against all odds, made a playoff push. I want to give Jesse Minter a full offseason to try and get his guys in the building to rebuild the defense, but I would be lying if I didn’t admit that he has been extremely disappointing so far.

title: Ravens place QBs Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley on injured reserve
summary: The Baltimore Ravens placed quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve on Thursday ahead of their Week 9 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Jackson is set to undergo thumb surgery with discouraging reports but no firm timeline from the team regarding his potential return later this year. Huntley’s turf toe is thought to […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 20: (L-R) Joe Fagnano #12, Tyler Huntley #5, and Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens look on during a joint practice between the Baltimore Ravens and Minnesota Vikings at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 20, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens placed quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve on Thursday ahead of their Week 9 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Jackson is set to undergo thumb surgery with discouraging reports but no firm timeline from the team regarding his potential return later this year. Huntley’s turf toe is thought to be season-ending, though again, the Ravens have yet to confirm. Both will miss a minimum of four games after landing on IR, making them eligible to return after Baltimore’s Week 13 bye. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano will start against Jacksonville on Thursday night. Once the Ravens finalize acquiring Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals, he will likely take over in Week 10 against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Ravens will drop to 4-5 with a likely loss to the Jaguars. The winless Chargers are about as beatable as they come, and the Texans and Panthers are a combined 5-9. Getting to 6-7 before the bye seems possible, but making the postseason after that relies on a successful return from Jackson. The two-time MVP has stated his reluctance to play before he is healthy enough to do so already this year; feeling comfortable with an injured throwing hand might be an even higher bar to clear. The Ravens promoted Austin Reed from the practice squad to the active roster to back up Fagnano on Thursday night. Kedon Slovis will serve as the emergency No. 3 quarterback. Baltimore also elevated outside linebacker Adisa Isaac and kicker Jake Moody from the practice squad to face the Jaguars. title: AFC North Preview, Week 9: Steelers on bye, Ravens in desperation mode

full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - DECEMBER 17: Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith (0) and Jacksonville Jaguars linebacker Travon Walker (44) pose for a photo following the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Baltimore Ravens on December 17, 2023 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals 5-2 Cleveland Browns 5-3 Baltimore Ravens 4-4 Baltimore Ravens Matchup: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars, 8:15pm EST The Ravens lost their third consecutive game last week and, in the process, lost both of their top quarterbacks to long-term injuries. Lamar Jackson returned only to injure his thumb on the first offensive play, which will place him on IR, while backup Tyler Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury. That left third-stringer Joe Fagnano to play most of the contest against the Bills, which the Ravens lost 36-10. Now in distress at the quarterback spot, the Ravens will have to try to rally on a short turnaround in a tough matchup against the Jaguars — who are 5-2 with the best point differential in the NFL (+85). The Jaguars’ defense allows the fewest rushing yards per game, which doesn’t’ bode well for a Ravens’ offense that will have to rely heavily on the run game with Fagnano starting. Expect the Ravens to give Fagnano quick outlet passes to prevent him from holding the ball too long given the team’s struggles in pass protection up front. On the other side of the ball, the Ravens’ defense will be up against it again following consecutive matchups against top-flight offenses (Bengals and Bills). The Jaguars are outside the Top 10 in passing yards and rushing yards, but they score at a high clip (28 points per game) and have a solid group of playmakers. The last couple of weeks have shown that if the Ravens can’t get pressure on the quarterback and finish sacks, their secondary can’t be relied upon to prevent big plays. Cincinnati Bengals Matchup: vs. Atlanta Falcons, 9:30am EST (Madrid) After a signature blowout win over the Ravens in Week 7, the Bengals narrowly escaped a major letdown loss last week against the Tennessee Titans. The Bengals trailed 13-0 in the first quarter and got into a shootout with the Titans and before emerging with a 43-36 overtime victory. It was a good reminder of the team’s offensive explosiveness while also showing they still have defensive flaws and inconsistencies. This week, the Bengals are traveling to Spain for an international contest against the Falcons. The Falcons are 3-5 and coming off a bizarre 16-0 loss in which their opponent, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, did not complete a pass. The Falcons were shredded for over 300 rushing yards, offering some hope for the Bengals to finally get their run game going in this matchup. So long as Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase continue to play a dominant level, though, it’d be foolish for the Bengals not to keep airing it out to them quite often. On defense, this is a nice potential spot for the Bengals to force a turnover or two. Michael Penix Jr. tossed four interceptions last week compared to only eight completed passes. The key to limiting the Falcons’ offense begins and ends with Bijan Robinson, who is an all-around weapon in the backfield. Expect the Bengals to load the box on him and pressure Penix, who has struggled against the blitz this season. Cleveland Browns Matchup: @ New Orleans Saints, 1:00pm EST The Browns are heading to New Orleans this week, looking to get back in the win column after a blowout loss in Week 8 against the Steelers (27-6). Cleveland turned the ball over twice and ran for just 34 yards as a team on 15 carries, taking a big step back offensively after scoring 27 points the prior week. They’ll likely have to do without the services of Deshaun Watson (concussion) on Sunday, meaning Shedeur Sanders would start at quarterback. The Saints are allowing the fourth-most rushing yards per game this season, opening the door for the Browns to have a bounce-back rushing attack performance. They’ll need to establish at least the threat of a run game to support a backup quarterback on the road. Expect Sanders to target tight Harold Fannin often, as the two showed a good connection last year. Fannin is coming off a season-best showing where he caught 10 passes for 154 yards. Defensively, the Browns can likely afford to prioritize defending the pass. The Saints are a bottom-tier rushing offense and have been riddled with injuries at the running back spot. New Orleans does have an elite wideout in Chris Olave, though, along with some solid supporting pass-catchers. The Browns have been a heavy man coverage defensive team and the Saints are not afraid to take shots downfield. What should the Ravens do at the trade deadline? | Baltimore Beatdown

title: 3 Keys to Victory for Ravens-Jaguars Week 9
summary: The Ravens have a Thursday night game coming off another bad loss in Buffalo. They are once again without Lamar Jackson with the rest of their season shrouded in uncertainty. For now, Baltimore is trying to stay afloat after laying the groundwork to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals. But first, preseason standout Joe Fagnano […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Joe Fagnano #12 of the Baltimore Ravens throws a pass against the Buffalo Bills during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens have a Thursday night game coming off another bad loss in Buffalo. They are once again without Lamar Jackson with the rest of their season shrouded in uncertainty. For now, Baltimore is trying to stay afloat after laying the groundwork to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals. But first, preseason standout Joe Fagnano will start his first NFL game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Can the Ravens somehow stay above .500 with the undrafted rookie at the helm? If they have any chance, they’ll have to follow these three keys: Get the ball out quick An offensive line is clearly in bad shape when they let three quarterbacks get injured while dropping back to pass in the same game. Even after Jackson and Tyler Huntley went down in Buffalo, the Ravens struggled to make protection adjustments and did not prioritize getting the ball out quickly. Right guard Vega Ioane is returning to from a one-game absence, so for just the second time in nine games, the Ravens’ desired starting five offensive linemen will be on the field. The first time was against the Bengals two weeks ago, but that lasted less than a quarter before Ioane’s injury Upgrading the weakest link at right guard should lead to improvements for the unit. That may not be saying much considering the rock-bottom showing in Buffalo, but this group can be at least average, if not gel into something greater than its parts. But until they do, Declan Doyle needs to help Fagnano in his first start. Minimize his processing with quick reads and designed touches that minimize the chance for costly sacks and turnovers. If the line holds, Doyle can consider mixing him some longer-developing route concepts that could give Fagnano a chance to push the ball downfield, like he did in the preseason. Lean on Henry The Ravens’ run game might be helped even more by a health O-line. Ioane’s big, physical presence will be next to zone-specialist center Cam Jurgens for a full game (hopefully) for the first time. Derrick Henry had a solid start to the year behind a more consistent line , scoring seven touchdowns with 374 yards in the first four games. He had another 100-yard performance in the first game without Lamar Jackson in Atlanta, but since then, it’s been three straight games under 60 yards. He looked better in the Buffalo game, scoring his first touchdown since Week 4 and averaging 4.8 yards per carry, but he only got 11 carries. Now the Ravens have a short week, a rookie undrafted quarterback making his first career, a finally-healthy offensive line, and an opponent that Henry has terrorized during his time in Tennessee. In 15 matchups against Jacksonville, he has averaged over 100 yards per game at 5.4 yards per attempt. It’s time to continue that trend and get The King rolling again. Get pressure on Trevor Lawrence Trevor Lawrence’s path has been anything but linear, but the former No. 1 overall pick is finally looking like the true-blue franchise quarterback the Jaguars thought they drafted in 2021. Something clicked for Lawrence under new head coach Liam Coen in 2025, and Jacksonville turned into a wagon of a team. That has continued into 2026,. I won’t be shy in saying that Lawrence has firmly been among the league’s top-t0 passers since partway of last year. Jacksonville has been one of the top AFC teams since then and might be the conference’s best right now. Now the Ravens have the challenge of trying to slow Lawrence and the Jags offense down to keep their season hopes alive. So far this season, there’s been only one true way to slow down Lawrence. He is shredding zone coverage this year, averaging 0.32 EPA/play with a 53.29% success rate and a 74.63% completion rate, per Sumer Sports. He’s been slightly worse against man with 0.07 EPA/play, a 49.21% success rate, and a 52.94% completion rate. Even when he’s blitzed, Lawrence manages to stay positive with 0.08 EPA per play, a 42.86% success rate, and a 58.46% completion rate. His worst numbers come under pressure: an awful -0.44 EPA per play, with a 32.47% success rate and a 47.46% completion rate. Every quarterback is typically at their worst with the pass rush in their face, but Lawrence’s numbers are near the bottom of the entire NFL. The Ravens have got to find a way to get into Lawrence’s grill all night, ideally without blitzing. If they have to send the rush, they should pair it with man coverage.

Mandatory Credit: Lexi Thompson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. The Ravens are in an increasingly precarious position. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve for thumb surgery that could end his season – and who knows when there will be any clarity on his potential return? Tyler Huntley is likely out for the year with turf toe, leaving the 4-4 Ravens to start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano for the foreseeable future. Until Wednesday, when Eric DeCosta laid the foundation to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals. Once finalized, the Ravens will have a new starter who has a better chance of keeping them in playoff contention. But how much better? Can the Ravens score enough points with Brissett under center to overcome an underperforming defense? Right now, that does not seem likely, leaving DeCosta with a series of tough decisions. He has already bought a center and a quarterback, but it may not make sense to invest even more draft capital into this season. But a surprising win against the Jaguars on Thursday night could inspire him to double down and roll the dice on Jackson returning for a playoff run. (History tells us that would be an unwise bet.) DeCosta should already be considering selling at the deadline, and a defeat on Thursday may push him further in that direction. Moving veteran players could recoup crucial draft capital heading into (another) offseason roster retool. For players on expiring deals, the Ravens will have to weigh the offers they receive against the potential for compensatory picks in 2028. So how should DeCosta approach the deadline? He’s already bought a quarterback – is there room for more? Or should he stand pat and maybe even sell players with an eye on the future? title: Bills power rankings: Seven outlets put Buffalo at No. 1 as Vikings tumble ahead of Week 9 showdown
summary: The Buffalo Bills aren’t just sitting atop the NFL power rankings anymore. They’re becoming the nearly unanimous choice. Following their dominant 36-10 victory over the Baltimore Ravens, the Bills (6-1) have claimed the No. 1 spot in seven of the eight national power rankings we track each week. Buffalo entered Week 8 already ranked first […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills aren’t just sitting atop the NFL power rankings anymore. They’re becoming the nearly unanimous choice. Following their dominant 36-10 victory over the Baltimore Ravens, the Bills (6-1) have claimed the No. 1 spot in seven of the eight national power rankings we track each week. Buffalo entered Week 8 already ranked first by four outlets, but apparently dismantling Baltimore was enough to convince nearly everyone else to get on board. Well, almost everyone. USA Today remains the lone holdout, ranking Buffalo sixth despite the Bills sitting atop the other seven national lists. Meanwhile, Buffalo’s next opponent, the Minnesota Vikings (6-1), is heading in the opposite direction. After suffering their first loss of the season, the Vikings experienced a dramatic fall across all eight outlets. But does one loss really change how dangerous Minnesota is? Let’s take a look. Buffalo Bills: Week 9 power rankings Buffalo’s average ranking improved from 2.38 to 1.63, with seven outlets placing the Bills at the very top of the NFL. That’s a significant shift from last week, when four outlets had Buffalo at the top and the remaining four weren’t quite ready to hand over the crown. Apparently, a 26-point victory over Baltimore helped settle the debate. Well, for everyone except USA Today. To its credit, USA Today did move Buffalo up three spots, from ninth to sixth. But with seven other outlets ranking the Bills first, Nate Davis clearly isn’t ready to join the party. At this point, I’m starting to wonder what Buffalo has to do to crack his top five. Score 50? Win blindfolded? Convince Josh Allen to play defense, too? Kidding. Mostly. Trending up: Buffalo’s defense For much of the season, Buffalo’s defense has faced questions about its ability to consistently pressure quarterbacks, create turnovers, and finish games. Against Baltimore, the Bills answered with four sacks, three takeaways, and just 144 total yards allowed. It’s important to acknowledge that the Ravens lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries. That certainly affected Baltimore’s offense. But Buffalo still had to execute. The defense capitalized on its opportunities, controlled the game, and delivered the kind of performance that had been missing in several earlier matchups. The question now is whether that momentum carries into Minnesota. Trending down: The margin for error When seven of eight outlets rank you No. 1, there’s really nowhere left to climb. And with that recognition comes a different kind of pressure. The challenge now isn’t getting to No. 1. It’s staying there. Minnesota Vikings: Week 9 power rankings While Buffalo is enjoying life at the top of the rankings, Minnesota is experiencing the other side of the national media’s weekly mood swings. The Vikings entered Week 8 undefeated and ranked No. 1 by two outlets. Following their 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions, they dropped in every ranking we track. Their average ranking fell from 2.63 to 7.38, a decline of 4.75 positions. NFL.com delivered the harshest punishment, dropping Minnesota eight spots from first to ninth. Sports Illustrated wasn’t far behind, moving the Vikings from second to ninth. That’s quite a fall for a team that still owns a 6-1 record. But while the rankings suggest Minnesota has taken a significant step backward, I’m not convinced one loss tells us everything we need to know about the Vikings. Trending up: A chance to make a statement Minnesota couldn’t ask for a much better opportunity to change the national conversation. After watching its undefeated season come to an end against Detroit, the Vikings now get to host the team nearly everyone considers the best in football. A win over Buffalo would immediately put Minnesota back in the conversation among the NFL’s top contenders. And let’s not forget, this is still a team that won its first six games. Bills fans would be making a mistake if they focused more on Minnesota’s fall in rankings than on the team the Bills actually face on the field. Trending down: Minnesota’s run defense The most concerning takeaway from Minnesota’s loss to Detroit wasn’t simply the final score. It was the Lions’ ability to establish the running game. Detroit piled up 230 rushing yards, with Jahmyr Gibbs accounting for 153 of them. That’s not exactly an encouraging development when your next opponent features James Cook and Josh Allen. Buffalo has demonstrated that it can control games on the ground, and Minnesota’s struggles against Detroit could present an opportunity for the Bills to establish their offense early. Of course, one difficult defensive performance doesn’t automatically mean Minnesota has developed a season-long weakness. But it’s certainly something Buffalo’s coaching staff will be studying. Bills vs. Vikings: Two 6-1 teams heading in different directions For Buffalo, this is an opportunity to prove its performance against Baltimore wasn’t a one-week statement. The Bills need to demonstrate that they can maintain that level of execution, particularly against another team with legitimate postseason ambitions. For Minnesota, it’s an opportunity to prove that its first six victories weren’t a fluke. One team is trying to defend its place at the top. The other is trying to remind everyone why it belonged there in the first place. And with both teams sitting at 6-1, something tells me this matchup will reveal a lot more than the latest power rankings. The Bills have earned the No. 1 ranking. Now comes the harder part: defending it.

title: NFL trade deadline: Buffalo Bills trade candidate – Budda Baker
summary: Time to highlight another safety for the Buffalo Bills ahead of this year’s NFL trade deadline Taking center stage today is Cardinals safety Budda Baker, a 10th-year, smaller, do-everything safety with 8,999 career snaps entering Week 9 who resides on an 3-5 Arizona team that has surprising wins thus far on its 2026 resume but […]
full_text: Time to highlight another safety for the Buffalo Bills ahead of this year’s NFL trade deadline Taking center stage today is Cardinals safety Budda Baker, a 10th-year, smaller, do-everything safety with 8,999 career snaps entering Week 9 who resides on an 3-5 Arizona team that has surprising wins thus far on its 2026 resume but doesn’t feel like a true NFC contender. This article is the tenth in the trade-candidate series I’ll continue to sprinkle onto the site until the actual trade deadline until November 10. Past installments in this series: Derwin James , Brian Thomas Jr. Jessie Bates , Tariq Woolen , Amani Hooker , Antoine Winfield Jr. , Cam Bynum , Zack Baun , Josh Downs Age: 30 A second-round pick in 2017 after an awesome career at the University of Washington, Baker quickly became a key piece on the Cardinals defense, logging 515 snaps as a rookie before 939 in his second season. He’s played over 1,000 in five seasons since. Baker’s first interception came in his fourth professional since, and since the start of 2020, he has nine picks. In his 10 seasons to date, Baker also has 48 pass breakups, and averages 125 tackles and six tackles for loss per year. 2026 snap splits Box: 45.6% Free safety: 38.8% Slot corner: 10.5% Defensive line: 4.7% Baker is listed at 5’10” and 190 pounds. He’s long lived in the box and been plenty productive there. He plays like a small extra linebacker on the field with coverage ability. His career missed tackle rate is 12.3%, which isn’t ridiculously good but given how often he’s near the football, it’s respectable. That rate in 2026 is currently 13.7%, the lowest rate he’s managed since a very low 7.6% in 2023. As he’s gotten older, Arizona has transitioned Baker’s role closer to the line of scrimmage. The 2024 campaign was the last in which he played the most snaps at free safety. Last season marked this move into the box, and he’s stayed there more than any other pre-snap alignment in the first eight games of 2026. How he’d fit with Bills Baker is a good, versatile football player. I’ve always thought he was a touch overrated because he’s never been a true star in coverage. He’s a magnet to the football, plays with insane energy and reckless abandon. Do the Bills need a box safety who can play a little free safety in a pinch? Not really. Cole Bishop has proven to be best in that role, and he’s the one constant in Buffalo’s safety room right now. If anything, they could use a rangy, center-field type. Baker did play that role earlier in his career. At nearly 31, that’s simply not his specialty anymore. Financial obligation for Bills to trade for him 2026 salary: $14.415M If the Bills trade for Baker after Week 9, they’d be on the hook for $7.2M in prorated 2026 base salary. Buffalo has roughly $4M in 2026 space currently, so they’d most likely ask Arizona to eat some of Baker’s remaining salary to facilitate this trade. In 2027, his base salary is $16M. Projected cost to acquire Using Syndicate32.com’s trade machine , the projected cost to trade for Baker is a late third-round pick in 2027 . That feels a bit rich given his age, but his reputation as a tackling machine could keep the compensation in that range. Should the Bills trade for Budda Baker? This is the one deal I’m essentially all the way out on for the Bills. And I’ll be brief with my rationale. Baker is good. He’d help the Bills defense. No doubt. Stability across the board. But he turns 31 in January, is pretty costly, and Buffalo would get the most out of his current-day talents by placing him in the box, where Bishop is clearly at his best. Plus, you’re likely sending a third or fourth-round pick to Arizona for him, not a late Day 3 selection. Baker would simply cause too much disruption in the Bills defensive scheme and on the books for me to view this trade as tenable. But if the Bills really do want to add a veteran safety with a high floor, he might be the only option available.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Buffalo Bills record book Week 9: Josh Allen, James Cook, Greg Rousseau chase history
summary: Last week was a busy one for the Buffalo Bills’ Record Book. Josh Allen, Greg Rousseau, and Tyler Bass all gave us reasons to put down our pencils and pick up the permanent markers. A few records that were on our watch list are now officially in the books, and we can put the erasers […]
full_text: Last week was a busy one for the Buffalo Bills’ Record Book. Josh Allen, Greg Rousseau, and Tyler Bass all gave us reasons to put down our pencils and pick up the permanent markers. A few records that were on our watch list are now officially in the books, and we can put the erasers away for those. Allen moved past Jim Kelly on the franchise touchdown list, Rousseau climbed past Darryl Talley in career sacks, and Bass continued rewriting Buffalo’s kicking records. That’s three fewer things to keep track of, but don’t worry, we’ve still got plenty to watch. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 1: Sure Things Dawson Knox — One Yard Away Dawson Knox doesn’t need much to move up Buffalo’s all-time receiving list. In fact, one yard will do it. Knox enters Week 9 with 2,736 career receiving yards, tied with James Lofton for 16th in franchise history. His next receiving yard would put him ahead of the Hall of Fame wide receiver. But Knox might want to keep an eye on Khalil Shakir. The Bills’ receiver has 2,666 career receiving yards, just 70 behind Knox. With the season only half over, this is going to be a teammate race through Week 18. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2: A Good Bet Josh Allen — The 5,000-Yard Club Josh Allen needs just nine rushing yards to reach 5,000 for his career. After picking up 30 against Baltimore, the Buffalo quarterback sits at 4,991. Nine yards doesn’t sound like much for Allen, but remember, he managed just one rushing yard against Las Vegas three weeks ago. So, we’re keeping the pencil handy for this one. Josh Allen — Passing Peyton Manning Peyton Manning holds the NFL record for the most combined touchdowns through a player’s first 10 seasons with 322. Allen is sitting at 321, and he still has plenty of football left to play in his ninth year. One more touchdown, whether it’s through the air or on the ground, would tie Manning. Two would give Allen the record outright. James Cook — Catching His Quarterback James Cook has been keeping our pencil and eraser busy. His pursuit of Josh Allen on Buffalo’s all-time rushing list started in the Superhuman chapter, moved up to Not Impossible, slipped back to Superhuman, and now he’s made it all the way to A Good Bet. Cook has 4,966 career rushing yards, just 25 behind Allen’s 4,991. He’ll need to outgain his quarterback by 26 yards to take over fourth place on the franchise leaderboard. Like Knox and Shakir, this is one that could prove to be a race – although we will likely have a winner before Week 18 here. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3: Not Impossible Josh Allen — Chasing Two Hall of Famers Allen has 88 career rushing touchdowns, putting him two away from tying Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin at 90. Two rushing touchdowns in one game certainly isn’t out of the question for Buffalo’s quarterback. He’s done it before. But with James Cook carrying the ball and Allen also looking to do damage through the air, we’re not ready to call this one a sure thing. Greg Rousseau — A New Personal Best Greg Rousseau already has seven sacks this season, just one shy of his career high of eight, which he reached in both 2022 and 2024. One sack against the Minnesota Vikings would tie that mark. Two would give him nine on the season and a new career best, with plenty of games still on the calendar this year. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4: Superhuman Greg Rousseau — Chasing Mario Williams Rousseau has already passed Darryl Talley on Buffalo’s career sack list, but the next name is a little farther away. Mario Williams recorded 43 sacks during his time with the Bills. Rousseau has 39, meaning he needs four to tie Williams and 4.5 to move past him. That’s a pretty tall order for one game. But this is the Superhuman chapter, after all. We wouldn’t be doing our job if we didn’t leave room for something a little ridiculous. _____________________________________________________________________________ We’ll keep the pencils sharpened, the erasers handy, and the permanent markers ready. With the way these records have been moving around lately, there’s a good chance we’ll need all three before the final whistle blows Monday night.
author: Rachel Auberger

title: Buffalo Bills Week 9 rooting interests: Who Bills Mafia should cheer for
summary: That was an interesting weekend of football. The Buffalo Bills won, although I’m still trying to figure out how. Seems like that’s happened a lot this season, but, hey, no one ever claimed being a member of Bills Mafia was easy.  Anyway, the Bills won. The Chiefs lost. And, as tough as being a Bills […]
full_text: That was an interesting weekend of football. The Buffalo Bills won, although I’m still trying to figure out how. Seems like that’s happened a lot this season, but, hey, no one ever claimed being a member of Bills Mafia was easy. Anyway, the Bills won. The Chiefs lost. And, as tough as being a Bills fan can be, there may have been a little sweetness in seeing Patrick Mahomes holding the ball when the clock hit zero, unable to get the job done. Really, the only thing that could have made Week 8 any better would have been a Patriots loss. But they say beggars can’t be choosers, and when it comes to New England, the only team to have bested the Bills up to this point, we have to be beggars. At least until Week 13, when Allen and Co. get a chance to even the score. When the dust settled and the lights went out in stadiums across the league Sunday night, the Buffalo Bills were sitting alone atop the AFC. And that sure looked nice. So, let’s take a look at who we, as members of Bills Mafia, need to be rooting for this weekend. After all, there’s a lot of football to be played before the Bills take the field Monday night, and we need something to do while we wait. _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC Standings — Through Week 8 1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) 2. Denver Broncos (6-2) 3. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) 6. Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) 7. New England Patriots (5-3) 8. Cleveland Browns (5-3) 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-4) 11. Houston Texans (2-5) 12. New York Jets (2-6) 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-6) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-6) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC East Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings Root for: Bills The Bills have worked their way to the top of the AFC, and now the job is to stay there. A win in Minnesota would keep Buffalo in control of its own path toward the No. 1 seed, regardless of what happens around the league on Sunday. Go Bills! Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots Root for: Packers The Patriots are the only team to have beaten Buffalo this season, and they’re still the biggest threat to the Bills in the AFC East. New England also holds the head-to-head tiebreaker, at least until the two meet again in Week 13. A Packers win would give Buffalo a little more breathing room at the top of the division. Go Pack Go! Detroit Lions at Miami Dolphins Root for: Lions Miami is sitting at the bottom of the AFC East with just one win, and there’s no reason to help the Dolphins climb out of that hole. A Detroit win keeps another division rival further behind Buffalo, and that’s good enough for us. New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs Root for: Jets Yes, we’re rooting for the Jets. Kansas City is still a threat to Buffalo’s hold on the top spot in the AFC, and another Chiefs loss would go a long way toward keeping the Bills there. The Jets, meanwhile, are far enough behind Buffalo that we can afford to let them have this one. Just this once. J-E-T-S! JETS! JETS! JETS! _____________________________________________________________________________ Rest of the AFC Jacksonville Jaguars at Baltimore Ravens Root for: Ravens Jacksonville is a little too close to Buffalo in the AFC standings for comfort, so we’d like to see the Jaguars pick up another loss. And since the Bills just beat Baltimore, a Ravens win gives Buffalo a little boost in strength of victory. Two birds, one stone. And we don’t even have to like the Ravens — or whoever they have under center. Cincinnati Bengals at Atlanta Falcons Root for: Falcons The Bengals are sitting at 5-2, and that’s a little closer to the top of the AFC than we’d like. Atlanta can do us a favor here by handing Cincinnati its third loss. Nothing complicated about this one. Denver Broncos at Carolina Panthers Root for: Panthers Denver is sitting right behind Buffalo in the AFC standings, and we’d really like to put another game between the two. Yes, a Broncos loss hurts the Bills’ strength of schedule, but with Buffalo and Denver set for a Christmas Day showdown, we’d be happy to see the Panthers play the part of the Grinch in November. Dallas Cowboys at Indianapolis Colts Root for: Colts The Colts aren’t going anywhere in the AFC standings right now, but that doesn’t mean they can’t do us a favor. Indianapolis traded its 2027 first-round pick to the Jets, and the more games the Colts win, the worse that pick gets. The last thing we need is New York getting its hands on a franchise-changing player with the first pick in the draft. Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints Root for: Saints The Browns are sitting at 5-3, and that’s close enough to the top of the AFC for us to want them to stay right where they are. Or, better yet, take another step backward. New Orleans hasn’t exactly been setting the world on fire, but we’re not asking the Saints to win the Super Bowl. Just one game on Sunday will do. Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers Root for: Chargers The Chargers are 0-7, and the last thing we need is for them to turn that miserable season into the first overall pick in next year’s draft. So, we’re rooting for Los Angeles to finally get a win. Come on, Chargers. Surely you can manage just one. Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers Root for: Raiders Buffalo already has a win over Las Vegas in the books, so another Raiders win would give the Bills a little help with strength of victory. Strange how quickly a team can go from an opponent to a temporary friend. _____________________________________________________________________________ NFC Rooting Interests Los Angeles Rams over Washington Commanders — Strength of Victory Chicago Bears over Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Strength of schedule. Games that don’t move the needle for Buffalo: New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks _____________________________________________________________________________ Teams on Bye Pittsburgh Steelers, Tennessee Titans _____________________________________________________________________________ Being at the top of the AFC is a pretty good place to be. The problem is, now we’re going to spend the rest of the season looking over our shoulders to see who’s coming for that No. 1 seed. This weekend, we’ll be keeping one eye on the Patriots, another on the Chiefs, and somehow finding a way to root for the Jets without feeling too dirty about it. Being a Bills fan sometimes requires sacrifices. And if Sunday goes our way, a Buffalo win on Monday night would just be the icing on the cake. Go Bills!

full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Tre'von Moehrig #7 and Will Lee III #24 of the Carolina Panthers react against the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are down at least their top two, possibly their top four corners again this week. Damien Lewis and Jaelan Phillips have also not participated in practice yet this week and are on track to miss a second consecutive game. That could mean that the Panthers porous rush defense and even more porous pass protection as executed by third to fourth to nth string players may be on full display again. The Denver Broncos managed to sack Patrick Mahomes twice and hit him another ten times on 41 dropbacks last week. The Panthers have surrendered 11 sacks in the last two weeks. This is not an encouraging comparison. Hope isn’t dead, however. Longtime do-it-all lineman Brady Christensen may be back this week with odds to plug in at one of the tackle positions. That would send free agent and disappointment Rasheed Walker to the bench for at least the first snap of the game. At corner, Will Lee III and Marco Wilson may form a more competent cornerback duo than one would expect for their original places on the depth chart at the start of the season (third string and on the street, respectively). The Panthers were held together with duck tape and prayer last week and still took the Green Bay Packers down to the wire. The Broncos are another team looking to find their rushing game against the Panthers. I think Carolina takes a small step forward on the injury front this week and use that momentum to surprise a good—but far from invulnerable—Denver Broncos team with an obvious game plan. Maybe I’m too optimistic here, but there is also part of me that just cannot stomach losing to Sean Payton. Couple that with teams west of the Mississippi traditionally struggling to perform in early east coast games and I like the Panthers at +2.5.
