title: Panthers vs Broncos: Key Storylines to watch
summary: The Panthers get to return from their mini bye following two crushing losses to the Buccaneers and the Packers. They fired their defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero following these games, if you hadn’t heard. Funny enough, they’ll be taking on the Broncos, the team Evero coached for as a DC prior to Carolina poaching him up. […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Tetairoa McMillan #4 of the Carolina Panthers warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Panthers get to return from their mini bye following two crushing losses to the Buccaneers and the Packers. They fired their defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero following these games, if you hadn’t heard. Funny enough, they’ll be taking on the Broncos, the team Evero coached for as a DC prior to Carolina poaching him up. This Broncos team is a different iteration compared to that one, as they were a QB injury away from going to the Super Bowl last season and currently sit at 6-2 atop their division for a playoff berth. The Panthers also sit atop their division, albeit with very different circumstances and definitely a seemingly different direction. The Panthers will need to stop the losing skid they are on soon if they want to reclaim control of their season, where the Broncos have the Chiefs nipping right at their heels for control of the division. Let’s dive right into all the key storylines.‘ Defense: Contain Bo Nix The easy story to talk about is the Panthers rushing defense, ranked in the bottom of the league in most categories. However, Denver’s rushing attacks ranks in the mid 20s in the league in yards per rush, yards per game, and rushes per game via TeamRankings.com. The Panthers will also be making a concerted effort to stop the run per Dave Canales this week following their changing of the guard in the coaching staff, so instead I’d like to highlight another problem that has plagued them in losses this year; mobile quarterbacks. EDGE Patrick Jones talked about being more aggressive, specifically along the defensive front, and getting into the backfield more. Nix hasn’t been AS damaging as a rusher this season, averaging short of 4 yards per attempt. But believe me, the man can get away from some pressure and keep plays alive. I would expect the Panthers to unveil an attacking forward defensive approach this week, and rattling Bo Nix will be the best way to keep them in this game. Offense: Dear god offensive line PLEASE The story of the last several weeks has been the Panthers allowing pressure on basically half of their passing snaps. For an offense that cut its teeth early on in the season with aggressive passing down the field, that’s a really bad thing. It was especially apparent against the Packers, as they not only sacked Bryce Young 6 times, but they batted down a ton of passing attempts even when they didn’t get home on the rush. This offensive line is allowing a free rusher at the quarterback at an alarming rate, and they need to figure that out one way or the other. Maybe they execute more rollouts and waggle plays where they get Bryce Young moving, maybe they bring in extra blockers at tight end in the backfield or to chip as they run out on their passes. Either way, the last couple of weeks have not been sustainable no matter who the QB is. It looks like they’ll be without OG Damien Lewis for another week, and his backup Corey Bullock was limited at practice on Wednesday. They did activate OL Brady Christensen from injured/reserve, who practiced in full on Wednesday, but I currently would doubt he plays Sunday. So they appear to once again be looking at fielding a somewhat patchwork line, with the same starters who have been struggling like Rasheed Walker and Luke Fortner. Bonus storyline: Cornerback room changes? I broke down the Panthers cornerback room in depth earlier in the week . While Marco Wilson showed some fire last week in his first start and the Panthers have two guys who seem under utilized at this juncture in the season in Corey Thornton and Chau Smith-Wade, the bottom line is this unit is beaten up and has to try and survive until they get reinforcements. They’ll draw Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, and Marvin Mims Jr in the passing game this week, all guys that can take a pass to the house on a busted play. I’m not entirely sure how they’ll try to scheme against this, especially if Will Lee’s hamstring injury keeps him out of this game on Sunday. But it’ll be up to interim DC Todd Wash to figure that out, with DeAngelo Hall brought in as coaching reinforcements to try and teach some parts of the scheme they want to implement to try and get things going in the right direction. Maybe Hall should pack a game day jersey just to be safe? Tell us down below what storylines you are watching for this week, Panthers fans!

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Cayden Green
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: COLUMBIA, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 03: Cayden Green #70 of the Missouri Tigers blocks Jeramiah McCloud #91 of the Florida Gators at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium on October 03, 2026 in Columbia, Missouri. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. Today our profile will focus on Missouri Tigers offensive lineman Cayden Green. Bio Green (6’5”, 325 lbs.) was a four star recruit and ranked as the state of Missouri’s second best prospect coming out of high school in 2022. Originally signing with Oklahoma, he started five games for the Sooners at left guard before transferring back to his home state. Green continued to hold down the left guard spot until 2025, when the Tigers moved him to left tackle. In his first year at the position, he allowed only seven pressures across over 350 pass blocking snaps, earning him First Team All-SEC recognition. After missing the first game due to injury, Green has been a stalwart at left tackle for the Tigers, allowing five pressures and zero sacks through five games this year. Strengths/Weaknesses One of Green’s biggest strengths is how naturally he took to the change of position. Usually linemen make the transition outside in, but in his first season moving from guard to tackle he earned All-SEC honors. On top of that, the switch to left tackle happened just two weeks before the 2025 season, showing just how coachable and adaptable he is. Green uses his heavy frame to anchor well and has the athleticism to not get beat around the edge on speed rushes. He is a coach’s dream: finishing blocks and playing through the whistle with a true versatility that will total over 1,500 snaps at guard and tackle in his career. While performing well, Green is still new to the left tackle position. His performance this year has really solidified his ranking among the Draft’s top tackles, but there are still some raw moments. He has also battled injuries the last couple of seasons. Nothing major, but still something that some teams might want to look further into. Projection Green is the epitome of a player that every coaching staff wants. He has the coachability and versatility to immediately start at a minimum of three positions on the offensive line, he is consistent in his performance against SEC competition, and he does not commit penalties (flagged just twice so far this season). As he continues to grow into the position, expect his stock to continue rising through the middle of the first round, potentially higher after teams get to interview him at the Combine. The Panthers have had a rash of injuries and poor performance on the offensive line, and Green would be a better version of Brady Christensen. He could start at left tackle (depending on Icky Ekwonu’s status and position moving forward) or right guard (if the Panthers move on from Robert Hunt). I wouldn’t even put it past him to learn the center position and be just as dominant there. Depending on where the Panthers pick in the first round, Green might be available to shore up several spots on their starting offensive line and give them some mix-and-match options in 2027 and beyond. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Cayden Green is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!

title: NFL Trade Deadline: Khalil Mack wants to stay in L.A.
summary: The most buzzed-about rumor leading up to the NFL’s trade deadline is that the Chicago Bears are trying to pry Khalil Mack away from the Los Angeles Chargers. Every network’s insider has reported it, but every report about Mack and a potential trade ends the same way: the winless Chargers don’t intend to trade him, […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2026; El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Khalil Mack at training camp press conference at The Bolt. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The most buzzed-about rumor leading up to the NFL’s trade deadline is that the Chicago Bears are trying to pry Khalil Mack away from the Los Angeles Chargers. Every network’s insider has reported it, but every report about Mack and a potential trade ends the same way: the winless Chargers don’t intend to trade him, or anyone, for that matter. Chargers head coach Jin Harbaugh was asked about Mack yesterday, and he reiterated their desire to keep him. “I want Khalil Mack here. Khalil Mack wants to be here,” Harbaugh said, via The Athletic . “He’s one of the pillars of our team.” Earlier today, The Athletic’s Noah Furtado asked Mack if he directly told Harbaugh and general manager Joe Hortiz that he wanted to remain a Charger. “Yeah, they know how I feel, man,” Mack said . “It’s just tough with all the outside noise. And so, ultimately, I want to be here, and I want to help them win. Even though it’s tough right now, you always see the light at the end of the tunnel.” Mack hadn’t answered similar questions about a possible trade before, and he doesn’t seem like the type of player who would demand a trade through the media, so maybe he’s just saying what a veteran team leader should say. But you never know what motivates a player. Some seek the biggest contract possible. Some chase championships. Some are loyal to their team. Some don’t want to uproot their family. So if Mack is truly comfortable in Los Angeles, the Bears and other suitors will need to look elsewhere for pass-rush help.

summary: The NFL has revealed their latest list of nominees for their annual partnership with USAA to present their “Salute to Service Award.” The 2026 nominee for the Chicago Bears is also one of their longest tenured players on their roster. Per a press release by the NFL the Bears’ 2026 nominee for this distinguished honor […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 2: Josh Blackwell #39 of the Chicago Bears looks on before the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on November 2, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has revealed their latest list of nominees for their annual partnership with USAA to present their “Salute to Service Award.” The 2026 nominee for the Chicago Bears is also one of their longest tenured players on their roster. Per a press release by the NFL the Bears’ 2026 nominee for this distinguished honor will be Josh Blackwell. The prestigious annual award, now in its 16 th year, honors a league member who demonstrates an exceptional commitment to honoring and supporting the military community. Below is their quote for what he’s done to aid the active and veteran military communities. Josh Blackwell, a Chicago Bears defensive back and special teams standout, embodies the spirit of Salute to Service through his continued commitment to service members and military families. For the past two years, Josh has participated in the Bears’ annual Naval Station Great Lakes visit in partnership with USAA. During his visits, he toured the installation, learned what daily life looks like on base, and spent time with recruits and sailors experiencing the demands of boot camp and military training. What stood out most was Josh’s ability to connect with the recruits by sharing both his successes and the obstacles he overcame to become the NFL player and person he is today. By speaking openly about his journey and making his experiences relatable, he encouraged recruits to push through the challenges they faced during training. Josh also spent time signing autographs, taking photos, and meeting with military members and their families. Even as the line grew, he remained engaged with each family, taking the time to create a memorable and meaningful experience for everyone who came to meet the players. Through his continued involvement at Naval Station Great Lakes, Josh has shown genuine respect for those who serve while using his experiences to encourage recruits and build personal connections with service members and military families. He continues to be a strong advocate for our nation’s veterans and service members. That sure brought back some memories from my time at Great Lakes for basic military training to begin my US Navy career over fourteen years ago… Personal nostalgia aside, the last Chicago Bear to have been honored with this award was Jared Allen in 2014. The Salute to Service Award has seen many nominees that include players, alumni, legends of the game, and coaches. For people interested in voting, that has started now and will last until November 30th, 2026. Fan voting will determine the three finalists in advance of the joint announcement in January of 2027. The award recipient will be recognized on “NFL Honors” during Super Bowl LXI week in Los Angeles, CA. Voting can be done by following this link .

title: Caleb Williams is a top-five NFL QB, and he’s doing it his way
summary: Heavy is the head that wears the crown. Caleb Williams has known that since well before the Chicago Bears made him the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and it hasn’t fazed him in the slightest. Say what you want about him, he told reporters at Halas Hall on Wednesday. He’s just […]
full_text: Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) leaves the field after defeating the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Heavy is the head that wears the crown. Caleb Williams has known that since well before the Chicago Bears made him the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and it hasn’t fazed him in the slightest. Say what you want about him, he told reporters at Halas Hall on Wednesday. He’s just going to keep it pushing. “People are going to say what they have to say. I can’t please everybody. That’s not my job. My job is to go win games. My job is to be the best player I can be. My job is to believe in myself, trust in my teammates and go out there and be one of those guys on the field that makes game-changing plays. You like it, you don’t like it, you got to deal with it,” he said. Being an NFL quarterback, particularly one tasked with being the savior of a QB-starved franchise like the Bears, is no picnic. Add being a top pick and former Heisman Trophy winner with a penchant for showing his emotions and painting his nails to the mix, and even being objectively great at the game isn’t enough to get naysayers and trolls off your back. No matter. Because Williams has become a top-five quarterback in the NFL in his third season, and he’s done it by showing the doubters he can do what they said he couldn’t: the little things. A year after being a big-game hunter ( 9.2 average depth of target ) who struggled to consistently complete passes (58.1% completion rate), Williams has transformed himself into one of the most dangerous “game-managers” in the league (70.9% completion rate, second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow). Sure, he’s left some plays on the table and has dramatically lowered his ADOT compared to last year (6.8 in 2026), leading some to believe he’s become little more than a checkdown merchant. But if you watch with your eyes rather than box scores and passing charts, you see what Williams has truly become: a monster who’s capable of beating you any way at any time. caleb wyd pic.twitter.com/K7Jo4WpftV — frank (@realfrankbrank) November 4, 2026 Need him to take a checkdown to D’Andre Swift to make it 3rd-and-manageable or complete a 5-yard hot route to Colston Loveland for a first down? He’s got you. Want to see him rip a 25-yard strike down the middle of the field on a rope to a wide-open Luther Burden III or Rome Odunze, while evading an unblocked rusher? No problem. Playing chess with some of the best defenses in the NFL, including the Seattle Seahawks, like a conductor leading a symphony of offensive destruction? He’s got that in his bag, too. Williams’ second season in Ben Johnson’s offense, which currently sees him on pace to become the Bears’ first-ever 4,000-yard passer despite missing three games, has produced exactly the third-year leap teams beg for from their young quarterbacks. But it hasn’t been about constant fireworks, jaw-dropping downfield throws, and impossible sack evasions. It’s been about doing the boring, mundane stuff that all the greats will tell you wins championships. He’ll never be a guy that makes everyone happy. He’ll never be everything to everyone. But his game is rounding into one of the most complete skill sets in the league—whether the haters like it or not.

title: NFL Week 9 Chicago Bears game preview: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field to cap off a hat trick of primetime games. They’re hoping to finish the three-game stretch at 3-0 as they head into their bye week, but a tough Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad stands in the way. Chicago is riding high after back-to-back wins over last season’s Super Bowl […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Kenny Gainwell #1 and Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers celebrate a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field to cap off a hat trick of primetime games. They’re hoping to finish the three-game stretch at 3-0 as they head into their bye week, but a tough Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad stands in the way. Chicago is riding high after back-to-back wins over last season’s Super Bowl participants, but the Bucs should not be overlooked. Will the Bears fall victim to a trap spot or will Ben Johnson continue to keep the team focused and not let them buy into the hype the media has built up around them? For Tampa Bay, it’s a chance to shake off their 0-4 start and prove their improvements over the last month weren’t a fluke. The Bucs come in having won three of their last four games and the only loss came in overtime. Their defense ranks first in the league. However, the offense has been clunky. Over the last two weeks, they’ve won resoundingly with virtually no passing game (in last week’s 16-0 win, no “virtually” modifier was needed). Dive into the Bucs and what it will take for the Bears to remain on a winning streak. Tampa Bay Buccaneers SB Nation site: Bucs Nation Record: 3-5, second in the NFC South Last week: 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons Game day, time, TV: Sunday, 7:20 p.m. CT, NBC Sunday Night Football Spread: Bears -6.5 Bears all-time record against: 40-22 Historical meetings: Week 10 of the 2001 season. The Bears defense held the Bucs’ offense in check in the first half, allowing only three Tampa field goals. Jim Miller and Marty Booker had their connection going though. They connected for three touchdowns –28-, 44- and 66-yards. A late comeback by the Bucs gave the Bears a scare. Brad Johnson rushed for a 1-yard score and hit Mike Alstott for a 2-point conversion with 2:29 left in the game. Chicago ended up punting back to Tampa but Johnson was picked off by Tony Parrish. Anthony Thomas fumbled, giving the Bucs new life. Johnson hit Warrick Dunn along the sideline but R.W. McQuarters was flagged for unnecessary roughness, giving them another 15 yards. That allowed Tampa to attempt a 48-yard field goal, but they missed it as time expired. The Bears won 27-24. Last meeting: Week 2 of 2023. The Bears offense had its moments, but the defense was shredded. Mike Evans had 171 yards and a touchdown, while Baker Mayfield threw for 317 yards. Justin Fields threw for 211 yards and rushed for a TD. However, he threw two interceptions. DJ Moore had 104 receiving yards. Chase Claypool also had a touchdown. A late pick-six by Shaquil Barrett off Fields sealed a 27-17 Bucs win. Injury report: The Bucs listed five players on their injury report. Limited participation RB Kenny Gainwell (hip) S Tykee Smith (ankle) Did not participate OLB Yaya Diably (knee) WR Emeka Egbuka (foot) DL Elijah Roberts (personal) Offense: The Buccaneers come into Chicago ranked 20th in points and 25th in yards. Their passing offense ranks 29th, while their rushing offense ranks first. Quite the disparity, but the numbers are backed by the past two weeks when they’ve passed for a total of 62 yards. Baker Mayfield (61.8 pct cmp./679 yds./3 TD/2 INT) missed three games with a thumb injury that he’s now playing through. However, he has done minimal passing since returning and Tampa’s numbers reflect that. Emeka Egbuka (28 rec./240 yds./2 TD) is the leading receiver for the Bucs, but he’s been injured. Chris Godwin (27/243/0), Cade Otton (19/186/0) and the running backs Bucky Irbing (18/78/1) and Kenneth Gainwell (12/61/1) are the other receiving leaders for Tampa. Tez Johnson (9/178/1) and Ted Hurst (11/168/1) have also caught some passes. On the ground, however, Irving (148 att./728 yds./5 TD) and Gainwell (58/289/0) are getting the production for the Bucs. They’re each averaging 5.0 yards per carry. In fact, every Tampa player with a rushing attempt is averaging at least 5 yards per carry. Defense: Tampa’s defense comes in ranked fifth in points and third in yards allowed. They rank eighth in passing defense and second in rushing defense. The dominant unit is led by LBs Josiah Trotter (68 tkls/1 INT/3 PD/1 sk/3 TFL/1 QB hits) and Alex Anzalone (42 tkls/3 INT/1 sk/2 TFL/1 QB hits/3 PD). S Tykee Smith (1 INT/43 tkls/3 TFL/4 QB hits/2 PD) is also making plays all over. Up front, OLBs David Walker (4 sk/6 TFL/6 QB hits), YaYa Diaby (3 sk/6 TFL/6 QB hits/2 PD/1 INT) and Al-Quadin Muhammad (2 sk/1 FF/1 PD/4 QB hits/2 TFL) are getting after opposing QBs. Veteran A’Shawn Robinson (1 sk/2 INT/3 PD/1 TFL/2 QB hits) is playing well. In the secondary, Jacob Parrish (2 INT/13 PD/3 TFL) leads the league in pass breakups. Zyon McCollum (30 tkls/2 INT/9 PD/1 TFL) and Keionte Scott (39 tkls/4 PD/1 sk/1 QB hit) are making plays, too. Key matchups: It’s a classic battle of the trenches. The Bears OL needs to best Tampa’s DL to establish the run and allow Caleb Williams to use play action to take downfield shots. Keeping Williams clean will allow the offense to be at its best. On defense, the Bears need to slow Irving and Gainwell down and not allow them to chew up the clock and get easy yards. Forcing Baker into passing situations and play from behind benefits the Bears. Key stats The Bucs have allowed more than 300 yards of offense only three times this year. They beat the Cowboys 24-16 but lost to the Cincinnati Bengals (33-27) and Pittsburgh Steelers (26-19 in OT). The Bears have had less than 300 yards of offense in their two losses. Baker Mayfield has 14 pass attempts and 64 passing yards in the past two games. He’s completed only half of his attempts. The Bucs defense is tied for the best DADOT at 6.6. Their pressure percentage is fifth-worst at 19.3 percent, despite having the seventh-highest blitz percentage at 33.6 percent. Tampa’s pass defense is really good. Opposing QBs have a 74.9 rating against them and just 205.9 yards per game. Can the Bears finish off their trifecta of primetime games against top defenses undefeated? Is this a trap spot for Chicago?
author: Sam Householder

title: Caleb Williams Week 8 QB Grade: Bears @ Seahawks Film Breakdown
summary: Note: Before kicking things off this week, just a quick note. Play breakdowns wont be available this week due to traveling for work, these will continue for week 9. In their stead I added some more interesting data points and nuggets to fill out this weeks’ breakdown. If last week was about Caleb Williams showing […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts at the line against the Seattle Seahawks during the first quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images Note: Before kicking things off this week, just a quick note. Play breakdowns wont be available this week due to traveling for work, these will continue for week 9. In their stead I added some more interesting data points and nuggets to fill out this weeks’ breakdown. If last week was about Caleb Williams showing he could attack a defense in just about any way it presented itself, Week 8 was about proving he could do it against one of the best units in football. Seattle entered Monday night with the NFL’s No. 1 defense, allowing just 144.4 passing yards per game. No quarterback had reached 200 yards against them all season, and the Seahawks hadn’t allowed more than 301 total yards in any of their first seven games. Justin Herbert couldn’t do it. Brock Purdy couldn’t do it. Patrick Mahomes couldn’t do it. Williams did. On the road. In primetime. At Lumen Field. Against the defending Super Bowl champions. If we’re weighing opponent, environment and situation, this might have been the most impressive performance Williams has put on tape this season. He completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions, finishing with a 101.0 passer rating as Chicago walked out of Seattle with a 34-17 win. Williams became the first quarterback to crack 200 passing yards against the Seahawks this season, while the Bears finished with 363 total yards against a defense that had entered the week allowing fewer than 302 in every game. The tone was set immediately. After Chicago’s defense opened the game with a three-and-out, Williams took the offense on a 17-play, 80-yard touchdown drive that burned 8:32 off the clock. He completed eight of 10 passes on the possession before extending a second down play and finding Luther Burden III for the opening score. Seattle hadn’t allowed an opening-drive touchdown in 16 games, and opponents had gone 17 consecutive possessions without even reaching the Seahawks’ red zone. Chicago broke both streaks on its first opportunity, and like they have done so much this season already, never looked back. That opening possession ended up being a pretty good preview of how the rest of the night would go. The Bears weren’t necessarily explosive on every drive, but they remained patient, stayed on schedule and made Seattle’s defense work for everything. Chicago finished with 70 offensive plays and held the football for 35:03, continuing a season-long trend of controlling games through sustained possessions. Bill Zimmerman highlighted just how dominant that time-of-possession battle has become over the season . The broader offensive results when Williams has been able to play a full game have been just as encouraging , which is becoming harder to dismiss as a small-sample fluke with each passing week. And this wasn’t a Seattle defense suddenly playing poorly before Chicago arrived. According to SumerSports, Seattle had not allowed positive offensive EPA in a single game all season . The Bears became just the fourth team since the start of 2025 to generate positive EPA against Mike Macdonald’s defense. That’s important context when looking at Williams’ raw stat line. 247 yards and one touchdown probably isn’t going to jump off the page after back-to-back 300-yard games, but this was never going to be the type of matchup where the numbers told the entire story. Seattle’s defense is designed to affect the quarterback with four rushers, keep bodies in coverage and force an offense to string together long possessions without making mistakes. Williams largely did exactly that. He continued to play efficient football even in obvious passing situations, something George Hatzadony’s charting has consistently highlighted this season , while also showing the same ability to create when Seattle disrupted the pocket. That second part continues to be one of the more encouraging developments of his season. Williams has always had the physical ability to escape pressure. The difference now is that more of those plays are ending with productive decisions rather than simply becoming extended chaos or balls that end up thrown away. PFN noted this week that Williams is one of only four qualifying quarterbacks producing positive EPA under pressure this season , joining Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes and Drake Maye. There were several examples Monday night where Williams escaped the initial rush, reset and still delivered an accurate football rather than immediately abandoning the structure of the play. That balance has become increasingly noticeable. The highlight-reel improvisation is still there, but it isn’t replacing the offense anymore. It’s supplementing it. You could see that especially when Williams began attacking Rome Odunze after halftime. Odunze finished with four catches for 87 yards, with gains of 23 and 22 yards helping set up Chicago’s third-quarter touchdown. Williams consistently attacked the intermediate areas of Seattle’s coverage, an area where the Seahawks had been one of the league’s better defenses entering the game. And when Seattle finally made its push in the fourth quarter, Chicago answered. A Colston Loveland fumble gave the Seahawks a short field and allowed them to cut the lead to 20-17. Lumen Field suddenly sounded like Lumen Field again, and for the first time all night it felt like momentum had completely shifted. The Bears responded with a six-play, 56-yard touchdown drive. The biggest play came on third-and-9 when Williams got the football quickly to Kalif Raymond, who split the defense for 39 yards on what was officially a run play. D’Andre Swift finished the drive with his second touchdown. That’s another area where this team continues to look different. Chicago isn’t simply surviving close games anymore. When opponents have made their push, the Bears have increasingly answered by taking control right back. The 17-point victory was Seattle’s first loss by more than four points in 30 games, including the postseason. Their previous six losses dating back to the start of the 2025 season had come by 17 combined points. Chicago beat them by 17 in one night. Williams also quietly added another piece of NFL history. Monday marked his 36th consecutive regular-season game with at least 20 pass attempts and no more than one interception, breaking Aaron Rodgers’ previous record of 35 . He also became the first quarterback in Bears history to lead the offense to 30-plus points in three consecutive games without committing a turnover, another sign of how consistently clean his football has become . Tom Brady even called Williams the “perfect quarterback” for Ben Johnson’s offense , praising the way Johnson uses Williams’ skill set within an offense that can attack defenses through the run game, quick passing, explosives, screens and misdirection. That’s really what the last three weeks have shown. Atlanta tried to keep everything underneath, so Williams patiently took the completions. New England brought pressure and gave him opportunities downfield, so he punished them with eight explosive completions. Seattle brought the league’s best defense into one of the toughest environments in football and dared Chicago to methodically work its way down the field. Williams did that too. The Bears have now scored at least 30 points in three straight games since his return, and they haven’t trailed for a single second during that stretch. Oh, and Chicago just became the first team in NFL history to beat both participants from the previous Super Bowl in back-to-back primetime games . Patriots on Thursday night. Defending champion Seahawks in Seattle on Monday night. Two wins. If you wanted a stretch that starts making people view this team a little differently,…
author: Gary Baugher Jr.

title: Bears-Seahawks Upon Further Review: A Closer Look at the Referees
summary: Monday Night, November 2, 2026. Lumen Field, Seattle.Crew: Shawn Smith (R #14), Tra Blake (U #3), Jay Bilbo (DJ #84), Jeff Seeman (LJ #45), Dyrol Prioleau (FJ #109), Keith Parham (SJ #41), Dino Paganelli (BJ #105), Mike Wimmer (RO #0). Hello Chicago Bears fans! Chicago flew to Seattle on Monday night and departed with a […]
full_text: Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Chicago Bears defensive line Grady Jarrett (50) questions a call with the officials during the first half against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Monday Night, November 2, 2026. Lumen Field, Seattle. Crew: Shawn Smith (R #14), Tra Blake (U #3), Jay Bilbo (DJ #84), Jeff Seeman (LJ #45), Dyrol Prioleau (FJ #109), Keith Parham (SJ #41), Dino Paganelli (BJ #105), Mike Wimmer (RO #0). Hello Chicago Bears fans! Chicago flew to Seattle on Monday night and departed with a 34–17 statement victory in Big Jeff’s first game. But let’s dive into the calls and no-calls in the game. The Hawks fans are squawking, but we here at UFR take a bird’s-eye view on the calls in the game and no amount of fan noise will ruffle our feathers. Official totals: Bears 10–85 , Seahawks 5–43 . The accepted tape is not, however, where the true story lies. Several judgment calls went against Seattle; several others, however, went against Chicago. One delay of game erased a tackle-for-loss and became the spark for a scoring drive. The same four-tier scale is applied to every accepted flag and every meaningful no-call: Correct, Arguable, Incorrect, Horrible. Weight runs 1–4 by impact (1 for housekeeping, 2 for drive disruption, 3 for scoring or red-zone leverage, 4 for wiped score/turnover or game-ending leverage). Replay overturns are judged against the “clear and obvious” standard. No-calls receive the same grades and weights as thrown flags. The goal is a transparent differential, not a birdbrained screed. The crew under Shawn Smith is under the microscope, but for the most part they were right, so I’m afraid the Hawks fans will be eating crow after this UFR. The Flag of the Game is the fourth-quarter delay of game on Chicago that erased a Seahawks tackle for loss on D’Andre Swift and, on the next snap, set up Kalif Raymond’s 39-yard lateral that put the ball on the five yard line, goal-to-go. The League File is the clear Kyle Williams touchdown that was initially ruled incomplete in the Patriots–Dolphins game. Same method. Same scale. Full breakdown follows. First Quarter CHI 7, SEA 0 (after the opening 17-play, 80-yard drive that ended with Caleb Williams’ 1-yard touchdown to Luther Burden). No-call: Hit on Sam Darnold while sliding. Darnold scrambled on third-and-8 from the Seattle 31. Devin Bush hit him as he went to the ground. No flag. Shawn Smith’s pool-report explanation: “He was scrambling and became a runner. We didn’t see any contact to his head and neck area when he hit the ground.” Darnold had left the pocket and was a runner at the moment of contact. The protection that attaches to a quarterback in the act of passing does not attach once he is a runner. Correct (no-call). Wt 2. How have we gotten so soft in the football community that this is supposed to be a penalty? Darnold is still in the process of his slide and Bush hit him with his back. Just make everything flag football at this point instead of making it impossible to tackle QB's. https://t.co/ORXcUZjjg8 — Derek Larger (@derek_larger) November 3, 2026 No-call: Hit on Tory Horton. On Seattle’s opening possession, third-and-5 from the Seattle 37. Horton was hit. No flag. Smith: the contact was not forcible to the head or neck area. Available angles show the blow to the chest. Correct (no-call). Wt 2. Cam Lewis delivers a devastating legal hit to Tory Horton! That's some old school NFL type of power. pic.twitter.com/UIERoXZqVu — The Goal Line Grind (@theGLgrind) November 3, 2026 Second Quarter Santos field goals from 44 and 38 push the lead to 13–3. With 30 seconds left, Jaxon Smith-Njigba beats coverage for a 43-yard touchdown from Darnold (extra point missed). 13–9 at the half. Process flags and standard holds pad both totals. Correct on the bright-line ones. Wt 1. Third Quarter CHI 20, SEA 9 after Swift’s 1-yard touchdown. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, offensive pass interference, 10 yards. End of the third quarter. Seattle driving deep. Darnold completes a pass to JSN near the goal line. Flag. Smith’s explanation: full arm extension and locked elbow into the defender’s chest; the arm affected the defender’s ability to play the pass. The contact is not incidental hand-fighting. The elbow is extended and the push is active. Correct. Wt 3. Instead of first-and-goal, Seattle faces second-and-18 from the 22. The drive dies. Lots of crying from Hawks fans over the JSN offensive PI. Clear full extension of his arm, he pushes off which turns Stevenson’s body creating separation. pic.twitter.com/J5SfhyTPIs — IDF (@IDF162) November 3, 2026 Fourth Quarter CHI 20, SEA 17 after Cooper Kupp’s 7-yard touchdown and the successful two-point conversion to Tory Horton. Delay of game on Chicago (the Flag of the Game). ~9:01 remaining. Third-and-4 from the Seattle 39. The Seahawks had a stop: D’Andre Swift was dropped for a loss in the backfield. The play is wiped by a delay of game on Chicago. The penalty occurred before the snap, so the tackle-for-loss never counts. Chicago is given third-and-9. On the next play Williams throws a backward lateral to Kalif Raymond. Raymond takes it 39 yards to the Seattle 5. Swift scores from 5 on the next snap. 27–17. Correct. Wt 4. It erased a tackle-for-loss that would have forced a punt and produced a touchdown that stretched the lead to two scores. We will talk about it more in our spotlight. Interception by the Bears eliminated by a holding call on Clark Phillips — Incorrect (All-22). Later in the quarter, a Bears interception is wiped by a defensive holding flag on Stevenson. All-22 shows the contact does not meet the standard. The flag is Incorrect. Wt 3. The interception is erased; the drive continues. (Chicago later intercepted Darnold on a different snap.) This holding call on Clark Phillips was wrong. JSN come out selling a run block on the play action and initiates contact. Then suddenly bursts into a route. Negated an interception and two plays later the Seahawks scored. #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/1h0XT31u4x — Clay Harbor (@clayharbs82) November 3, 2026 No-call: Hold on Jeffery Simmons on the two-point attempt. On the Seattle two-point conversion that made it 20–17, a hold on Simmons is not called. The contact is visible and restrictive. Also – it looked like two players were in motion on the play. Incorrect (no-call). Wt 2. Additional process and holding flags on both sides. Correct or Arguable depending on the angle. Wt 1–2. Delay of Game #2: Chicago, goal-to-go. Later in the fourth quarter, with the Bears inside the Seattle 10 and the game still within reach, the officiating crew stood over the ball and would not allow Chicago to snap. The play clock expired while the officials were positioned in a way that prevented the snap. Delay of game was called. This is distinct from the earlier flag that erased the Swift tackle-for-loss. The second delay occurred in a goal-to-go situation and was the product of the crew’s positioning rather than a pure late substitution by the defense. Correct under the written rule (clock expired). Wt 2. The enforcement is technically accurate; the circumstance that produced it is the same structural timing risk placed entirely on the offense. It is also an egregious loophole. A Seahawks defender had lollygagged onto the field after a late substitution, contributing to the timing. The rule does not require the defense to be set in a reasonable time; it only requires the offense not to snap after the clock expires. The crew applied the rule as written. The system allowed the defense to create the condition that produced the flag. Absolutely embarrassing for the league to call this delay of game. The defender ran into Caleb as he went to the line! pic.twitter.com/a6CVB4zxrz — Depressed Bears Fan (@ImBearsFan) November 3, 2026 Swift scores again from 5 after the Booker-tipped interception by James Lynch. 34–17 final. Calls against Chicago…

title: How the Chicago Bears Are Controlling the Clock This Season
summary: One of the more notable aspects of the Chicago Bears‘ performance this season has been their ability to control the clock. The Bears are averaging 35:26 in time of possession, putting together extended drives, consistently moving the chains, and giving opposing offenses fewer opportunities with the football. On Monday night, the Bears put together a […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Kalif Raymond #14 of the Chicago Bears stiff-arms Nehemiah Pritchett #28 of the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the more notable aspects of the Chicago Bears ‘ performance this season has been their ability to control the clock. The Bears are averaging 35:26 in time of possession, putting together extended drives, consistently moving the chains, and giving opposing offenses fewer opportunities with the football. On Monday night, the Bears put together a 17-play, 80-yard opening drive against the Seattle Seahawks that took 8:32 off the clock. Caleb Williams noted that sustaining drives was something the offense spent time working on during training camp and OTAs. “We do these long-drive drills in training camp and OTAs that you hate, that you dread at the end of practice,” he said. “They show up in big moments for us.” And while the Bears’ offense is well-prepared to execute those extended drives, Johnson’s priority remains making the most of each possession rather than focusing on how long a drive lasts. “It’s not something we stress,” Johnson said. “We really talk more about getting explosive plays. I would rather have a one-play drive for a touchdown than a 10-play drive for a touchdown. But the ability to stay efficient, stay on schedule, I think that’s something that good offenses show that they can do.” Johnson also pointed out that long drives leave little room for mistakes, since one misstep can bring an otherwise promising possession to an end. “I prefer some more explosive plays be mixed in there, just so it takes the onus off just a little bit,” Johnson explained. “It feels like you’ve got to be perfect throughout those long drives, and one mistake could derail you.” One factor contributing to the Bears’ success in controlling possession has been their performance on third down on both sides of the ball. The Bears convert 44.3% of their third downs, the fifth-best mark in the NFL, while their defense ranks No. 1 in the league, allowing conversions on just 23.8% of third downs. Key behind the Bears' success this season has been third downs for both sides of the football. Chicago converts on 44.3% of third downs, ranked 5th in the NFL, while boasting the No. 1 defense in that category at just 23.8%. — Chris Emma (@ChrisEmma1) November 3, 2026 What’s made Chicago particularly dangerous on third down is that the offense hasn’t just been converting in those situations. Some of the Bears’ most explosive plays this season have come when they’ve needed to move the chains. Williams connects with Odunze on a spectacular third-down throw vs. Patriots CALEB WILLIAMS LASER ON THIRD AND LONG. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/HLNowyCVnN — NFL (@NFL) October 23, 2026 Kalif Raymond breaks loose for a big gain to set up Bears touchdown vs. Seahawks Third-and-long, need a play, and Ben Johnson dials this up. A game changer for the Bears. pic.twitter.com/gjh71QN5sJ — Chris Emma (@ChrisEmma1) November 3, 2026 Luther Burden III comes up big with a 24-yard touchdown on 3rd and 17 CALEB WILLIAMS. LUTHER BURDEN III. TOUCHDOWN! Watch Patriots vs. Bears live now on @PrimeVideo #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/KdMGo5mzV4 — NFL on Prime Video (@NFLonPrime) October 23, 2026 Time of possession might not be a statistic Ben Johnson puts much emphasis on, but the Bears’ ability to win on third down and sustain drives allows Chicago to control the clock and dictate the tempo of games is certainly part of what makes this team special.

title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. the Atlanta Falcons
summary: The 5-2 Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the 9:30 a.m. ET game this week in Madrid, Spain. Their opponent will be the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons. While Atlanta doesn’t have the greatest record in the league, they have been a tough out almost every week, with a big victory just 2 weeks ago against the San […]
full_text: The 5-2 Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the 9:30 a.m. ET game this week in Madrid, Spain. Their opponent will be the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons. While Atlanta doesn’t have the greatest record in the league, they have been a tough out almost every week, with a big victory just 2 weeks ago against the San Francisco 49ers. What are 3 keys to the Cincinnati Bengals leaving Spain with a victory this week? Let’s dive into it. Slow down Bijan Robinson You are never going to completely shut down Bijan Robinson. He is the best running back in football. He isn’t just elite at running the ball, but he is dynamic at catching passes out of the backfield. He is about to eclipse 1,000 all-purpose yards on the season already, but hasn’t run for over 80 rushing yards in the last 3 weeks of the season. I do not want to be the team that he goes off against after a few subpar performances by his standards. It will be a total team effort if they are going to keep him in check this week. They cannot have missed tackles like they have been known for over the past few seasons. Robinson will make you pay if you let him slip out of your initial grasp. If the Bengals want to win this game, they have to find a way to not allow Robinson to go nuclear. Dax Hill with the missed tackle pic.twitter.com/woytb1465P — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Establish the run While the Bengals are never going to be a run-centric team, this is a week they have to find some balance. Atlanta lost to Tampa Bay last week, 16-0, in a rainy game that the Buccaneers did not complete a single pass in. They were able to instead rush for over 300 yards against the Falcons’ defense. Another reason you need to establish the run is how good Atlanta has been generating pressure this season. They are 2nd overall in the league in pressures with 179 on the season. They have done that without James Pearce Jr., who is returning from an 8-game suspension this week. This is not a game you want to be throwing the ball almost 50 times. Establish some balance with getting carries and short passes to Chase Brown and Samaje Perine this week. If you don’t, you will see Atlanta get the victory. Chase Brown finished the game against the Titans with 55 rushing yards and 46 receiving yards pic.twitter.com/vE8UkWeGRX — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Pressure Michael Penix early and often Michael Penix is completing 61% of his passes this season. He has just 9 passing touchdowns to 5 interceptions. If the Bengals can get pressure on Penix this week, you can force him into some turnovers. Boye Mafe is 6th in the league for defensive ends with 35 pressures this season. The Bengals also have a dangerous interior pass rush with Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen on the interior. Both of those guys are in the top 12 for defensive tackles in pressures, with 24 for Dexter and 23 for Allen. Myles Murphy is coming off his second game in the last 3 played where he recorded 5 pressures on the day. Without Cashius Howell this week, they will need a guy like Murphy to continue generating pressure opposite Boye Mafe. Boye Mafe forces the fumble and Dexter Lawrence scoops it up for the turnover. I thought we were about to see an electric touchdown rumble for a moment… pic.twitter.com/vZTUsXTZiv — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026

title: Bengals News: Salute to Landon Robinson
summary: It’s November, which means two things when the Cincinnati Bengals are concerned. One: Joe Burrow and the offense have woken up from their annual offseason slumber (that extended a little too far into the season, as usual). And two: it’s Salute to Service Month. With Veterans Day just a few days away, the NFL is […]
full_text: It’s November, which means two things when the Cincinnati Bengals are concerned. One: Joe Burrow and the offense have woken up from their annual offseason slumber (that extended a little too far into the season, as usual). And two: it’s Salute to Service Month. With Veterans Day just a few days away, the NFL is in its military-appreciation month, and the Bengals happen to have a defensive tackle from the Navy and a Marine on the roster. After being named the Bengals’ Salute to Service Award nominee , Landon Robinson spoke with Bengals.com’s Geoff Hobson about his time at Navy, his service, and his future before the team left for Spain. The Bengals selected Robinson with the No. 226 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. That’s the same pick the Arizona Cardinals spent on former NFL safety and former Army Ranger Pat Tillman. “I took a class where we did a case study on him [Tillman] and learned about his story and what he did in the NFL and made the decision to go serve. When I saw I got drafted 226, ‘Wow, that is crazy,’” he said when he was asked about the coincidence by Hobson. You can read the entire interview here . Here’s what else is going on: DJ Turner, key Bengals get injury updates from Madrid Quite a week for Turner, the No. 1 cornerback who appeared to suffer a serious injury just one week ago. The fact the Bengals even had him board the plane overseas, though, was a big hint he had a real chance to play. ‘That’s the Only Glaring Need That They Have’ — Ex-Bengals WR Pushes Cincinnati To Make Trade for 3-Time Pro Bowler “I like the Bengals,” Hawkins said about the best fit for Taylor. “I think that’s the only glaring need that they have offensively. Joe Burrow obviously can throw for 450 yards a game, but is that sustainable? Especially as you get later in the season and into the playoffs. They have a great schedule ahead of them. They could use some more firepower offensively.” Quick Hits | Bengals Stars Find Their Feet In Soccer World “I watch him on TV all the time. You know what I mean? Higgins said. “It’s so crazy. We just talked about how fast this dude is, right? How do you run that fast, dribbling the ball on your feet? That’s crazy. And then the moves he throws, it’s amazing. Just having that type of player at the game would be great to see.” HOW THE BENGALS ARE TACKLING A TEST OF LOGISTICS, ROUTINE IN MADRID “One above all is keeping the schedule as close to our routine as possible,” Taylor said. “We’ve got a team of people that logistically have handled this for us that are top-notch. My hat is off to everybody that has helped us set up and hit the ground running. There are two teams here. Your job is to handle the week better than the other team as much as possible. I don’t know Atlanta’s itinerary; I won’t be able to watch their practice or anything like that, but we are only playing one other team. Not 31 other teams. Control everything you can control. … This game is going to count the same as all the others, so shame on us if we are not prepared.”

title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Falcons
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain, this week. The Bengals are coming off a 43-36 victory against the Tennessee Titans, while the Falcons lost 16-0 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buccaneers did not complete a pass during the game, and yet still won by double digits in a […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain, this week. The Bengals are coming off a 43-36 victory against the Tennessee Titans, while the Falcons lost 16-0 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buccaneers did not complete a pass during the game, and yet still won by double digits in a rain-soaked contest. Even with that loss this past week, the 3-5 Falcons are not a team to take lightly. They have victories over the Packers, Saints, and the 49ers this season. They also have one-score losses against the Steelers, Ravens, and Bears. They will be getting back their best pass rusher, James Pearce Jr., this week also. He is coming off an 8-game suspension he served for violating the NFL’s conduct policy. Orlando Brown Jr. vs. James Pearce Jr. With the aforementioned Pearce coming off of his suspension, he is listed as the starter at right outside linebacker in the Falcons’ 3-4 defense. That means he is likely to face off against Orlando Brown Jr. this week. Brown struggled at times on Sunday when faced off against the speedier pass rush of Jacob Martin. He will see a similar test with the athletic Pearce this week. Orlando Brown Jr. allowed a season-high 6 pressures versus Tennessee. He was also credited with allowing a sack. Brown will have to play much better this week against Pearce. Last season Pearce produced at an elite level for a rookie. He finished the season with 45 pressures and 10.5 sacks for the Falcons. The Bengals will need to keep Pearce and the rest of a dynamic Falcons pass rush in check this week. Jacob Martin was giving Orlando Brown Jr. trouble on Sunday. pic.twitter.com/oGzLwiQXst — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Bijan Robinson vs. The Bengals Defense Slowing down Bijan Robinson is going to take a full team effort. While it will be up to everyone to try and limit him this week, I am specifically curious to see how Barrett Carter, Demetrius Knight Jr., and Jordan Battle play. Those three players have struggled with missed tackles the last couple of seasons. Robinson is one of the most dynamic and elusive running backs in the league. He can make guys look absolutely silly out in space, and that trio will have to play sound football. If they don’t, we are going to see them all over the Bijan Robinson highlight reel. Bijan already has 780 rushing yards on the season. Toss in another 203 receiving yards, and he is about to eclipse 1,000 all-purpose yards already this season. The best running back in the league rushed for over 1,400 yards last season. He also finished the year with over 800 receiving yards. A player who can absolutely put the Falcons team on his back at times. If the Bengals’ effort against the run looks like it did on the long Tony Pollard touchdown run this past week, they are going to be in for a long day in Spain. Yeah, this shit was bad pic.twitter.com/ceoXlA5RzK — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Kyle Pitts vs. TBD I have no idea what the Bengals will plan on doing this week against Kyle Pitts at tight end. While Pitts hasn’t had the career many expected, he is still a dynamic receiving threat for the Falcons. Add in the fact that the Bengals cannot stop a tight end at all again this season, and Pitts could be in for a career game this week. The Bengals allowed Gunnar Helm and Daniel Bellinger to grab eight receptions for 112 yards this past week against the Titans. I am never really sure what their plan for guarding tight ends is on a weekly basis. Jordan Battle made a couple of plays guarding tight ends, but most of the game we were just seeing guys completely wide open down the field at the position. I put it to be determined here because I don’t know why they won’t give Tacario Davis more of a chance to guard tight ends. I think that role would be DJ Ivey, but he has been thrust into starting at corner after the injury to Jalen Davis. Good play by Jordan Battle to force a Titans punt pic.twitter.com/DtHx0n7O9h — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026 Regardless of who ends up being responsible for guarding Kyle Pitts this week, I am fully expecting him to put up a hugely productive game. Dexter Lawrence vs. Ryan Neuzil Neuzil and the rest of the Falcons interior offensive line will be tasked with trying to stop the unstoppable in Bengals defensive tackle Lawrence this week. Lawrence is coming off a week with 7 tackles, a sack, and a fumble recovery. Lawrence is playing at an elite level this season, and now has 24 pressures and 5 sacks through his first 7 games of the year. Neuzil has allowed just 6 total pressures and 1 sack this season for Atlanta. However, Dexter Lawrence is a completely different animal to face. Neuzil will get help from Matthew Bergeron at left guard and Chris Lindstrom at right guard on Lawrence during this game, as well. Bergeron has allowed just 8 pressures with 0 sacks this season, while Lindstrom has allowed only 6 pressures and 1 sack. That interior offensive line has held up pretty well, but the Bengals are one of the toughest matchups to date for those guys. It should be a really fun matchup throughout the day. Dexter Lawrence with another dominant performance on Sunday. Lawrence is now up to 24 pressures and 5 sacks on the season. pic.twitter.com/fT8otsKIYF — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 2, 2026

title: NFL ranking of top 50 trade prospects is full of potential Bengals targets
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 as they prepare for their Week 9 game in Madrid, Spain, against the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons. They’re riding a two-game win streak, though the wins were ugly at times, and are very much in the mix to make a run at the AFC North title to host a playoff game […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 as they prepare for their Week 9 game in Madrid, Spain, against the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons. They’re riding a two-game win streak, though the wins were ugly at times, and are very much in the mix to make a run at the AFC North title to host a playoff game for the first time since 2023. Things aren’t all sunshine and rainbows, though. The Bengals are dealing with some injuries, and many analysts believe they’re aggressively pursuing an acquisition to help the team make a run. Considering they already traded the No. 10 overall selection in this year’s draft to the Giants for Dexter Lawrence, a rare mid-season trade from the Bengals would likely blow the collective minds of fans across the globe. Here are some of the players the Bengals could benefit from, in order from top to bottom on the list: No. 2: Jonathan Taylor, RB Colts Taylor is one of the best running backs in the league and has been for some time. Since he was drafted in 2020, Taylor has more scrimmage yards than all RBs except for Derrick Henry. He is the type of explosive player who could change an offense. After firing GM Chris Ballard, the Colts should be considering all options, including a full tear-down and rebuild. Taylor signed a two-year extension with the Colts in August. Indianapolis would take on $10 million in dead money in 2027 if it traded Taylor, so the contract is not preventive. This would have made sense a couple of weeks ago, but there are issues in the secondary that can’t be ignored. Still, the Bengals do need to figure out how to fix their running game, because they’ll need it in December and January. No. 9: Josh Downs, WR Colts Downs is in the final year of his rookie deal, and he has developed into one of the better route runners in the league. He is predominantly a slot player, aligning inside on more than 74 percent of his career offensive snaps. The Colts signed receiver Alec Pierce to a four-year, $114 million extension in the offseason. Pierce has played 49 snaps this season while battling injuries. Downs is good, cheap and on an expiring deal. He would be a potentially valuable trade piece if interim GM Ed Dodds is tasked with bolstering the draft cupboard. Do the Bengals really need a wide receiver? No. But Downs could fit in nicely. He’s a true slot receiver, and he would immediately be the Bengals’ WR3, which is a spot currently held by TE1 Mike Gesicki. With some injuries at wide receiver, including to Andrei Iosivas, and the relative inexperience of everyone else, adding another talented receiver wouldn’t hurt. No. 11: Amani Hooker, Safety Titans Though Hooker is under contract through 2028, he does not have any fully guaranteed money on his deal after this season. He is a versatile safety who can fulfill multiple responsibilities — post safety, split-field safety, nickel, dime, underneath zone and man-to-man on tight ends and slot receivers. He is a strong tackler who can impact in the running game, and he has the instincts in zone coverage to feel routes and bait quarterbacks into throws. The Titans would take on $8.6 million in dead money in 2027 if they traded Hooker. How crazy would it be for Hooking to pick Joe Burrow off three times in Week 8 just to join him a couple of weeks later? The Bengals have dealt with injuries at safety. Bryan Cook has missed a couple of games, as has Kyle Dugger, and Jordan Battle has been hit or miss (mostly miss). A trade for Hooker could shore up the secondary. No. 18: Amik Robertson, CB Commanders Robertson signed a two-year, $16 million deal with the Commanders in free agency. He has been one of the few bright spots from Peters’ offseason. Robertson does not have any fully guaranteed money on his deal in 2027. The Commanders would take on $3 million in dead money in 2027 if they trade him before the deadline. Robertson is a capable man coverage corner who could help a number of teams in the secondary. He can play inside and outside. Here’s really where the Bengals need some help, especially if DJ Turner is forced to miss some time. The cornerback position was pretty much an afterthought this offseason, and now they’re potentially going to pay the piper for it. If the Bengals do make a move, I predict it will be for a corner. No. 26: Riq Woolen, CB Eagles Woolen won a Super Bowl with the Seahawks last season. He then hit free agency and, rather surprisingly, a market did not materialize for him. Woolen ended up signing a one-year deal with the Eagles. Although he has given up two touchdowns, Woolen has played well in coverage down-to-down for Philadelphia. He was in tight coverage on the Parker Washington one-handed touchdown in the Eagles’ loss to the Jaguars in Week 5. The combination of size and speed will always make Woolen an intriguing piece. Another possibility at corner. He could join Boye Mafe, whom he won a Super Bowl with in Seattle. He could fill in for a starter on the outside should the need arise. That way the Bengals wouldn’t be forced to rely on Josh Newton, who reportedly spent much of the offseason in the doghouse. No. 28: Donte Jackson, CB Chargers Jackson is in the final year of a two-year free-agent deal he signed in 2025. He has missed the past two games with a hamstring injury. Jackson is one of the most compelling defensive backs on this list. He is on an expiring deal. He is relatively cheap, so he is an option for teams tight against the cap. And he is an experienced veteran who can acclimate quickly to a variety of schemes, though a zone-heavy scheme would be the best fit. Jackson has 23 career interceptions, tied for fifth-most among active players. Same thing here. The Bengals could definitely use some help in the cornerback room. Even if Turner’s heel injury allows him to play this weekend, will it limit him? He’s required to be able to stay hip to hip with some of the best athletes in the world. If his foot hurts, will he be able to? No. 40: Nahshon Wright, CB Jets The Jets signed Wright to a one-year deal in free agency, and he has yet to play a defensive snap this season for coach Aaron Glenn. Wright should be a trade candidate even if the Jets win games over the next three weeks. He had five picks playing for the Chicago Bears in 2025. Wright lacks some burst and change-of-direction ability. But his ball production last season was very impressive. At 6-foot-4, he has receiver-like skills in 50-50 situations. The Bengals were actually listed as one of the best fits for Wright, who had a good 2025 season but is struggling to get on the field this year. He could be had for little and potentially make a major impact for Al Golden’s secondary. No. 48: Tony Pollard, RB Titans Pollard, who signed with the Titans in free agency in 2024, is on an expiring contract. He has been getting the bulk of the work in the Tennessee backfield over Spears. Pollard is a veteran doubles hitter with some vision. He is reliable in pass protection. Pollard has the potential to be a supplemental piece in a running back rotation. Pollard carried the ball 21 times for 117 yards and two touchdowns against the Bengals in Week 8. He might not be as flashy as Taylor or Saquon Barkley, but he would probably help. At least more than Tahj Brooks. There were obviously others, but these were just some that caught my eye. What trade targets from the list (and not on the list) are you most interested in for the Bengals before the Nov. 10 deadline?
author: Jason Garrison

title: J.J. Watt, Cris Collinsworth want Bengals to trade for Jonathan Taylor
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have been floated in a couple of trade rumors ahead of November 10th’s trade deadline. A team that is 5-2 with Super Bowl aspirations could be aggressive ahead of the deadline if they think there is a player or players who could put them over the top. Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been floated in a couple of trade rumors ahead of November 10th’s trade deadline. A team that is 5-2 with Super Bowl aspirations could be aggressive ahead of the deadline if they think there is a player or players who could put them over the top. Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Bengals are one of a few teams “aggressively pursuing” Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, although no deal to any team seems imminent. The Cincinnati offense has been lighting it up in the passing game, but the running game has left much to be desired so far in 2026. With those rumors out there, former NFL great and current CBS broadcaster J.J. Watt is urging the Bengals to make the move. “I really do believe the Cincinnati Bengals make sense for a guy like him because of what their offense has in terms of the passing game and they just haven’t been able to get going on the ground,” Watt said during an appearance on CBS’ “Set Hut” show . As the Colts have started a fire sale following the firing of General Manager Chris Ballard, Taylor is widely expected to be moved before the deadline, but the Colts appear firm on getting top-tier value for him. Aside from the Dexter Lawrence II trade this offseason, the Bengals aren’t known for trading away draft capital. With the clear urgency in the locker room, though, the Bengals could surprise us once again. Former Bengal Cris Collinsworth also believes the Bengals should make the aggressive move. “Now with the defense and Dexter Lawrence comes in and Boye Mafe comes in, and the Bengals make moves that they’ve just never made, it’s right now, it’s this year, so go do it,” Collinsworth said on the PFF NFL Show . Should the Bengals trade for the former All-Pro running back? Let us know in the comments! The Bengals have built up their defense and offensive line… is it time to trade for Jonathan Taylor for a Super Bowl run? 🧐 | @JacCollinsworth @CollinsworthPFF pic.twitter.com/XHNUTQeY2l — PFF (@PFF) November 3, 2026 . @JJWatt on a couple of moves he could see ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline 👀 Jonathan Taylor to the Bengals & Garrett Wilson to the Chiefs 😳 #SetHut pic.twitter.com/6zytIezFON — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 3, 2026

title: Bengals News: Should Jets RB Breece Hall be trade target for Cincinnati?
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have been linked through insiders to be checking in on a possible trade for running back Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts, but another running back may be just as good of a target. The New York Jets may be looking to see what they can get for running back Breece Hall […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been linked through insiders to be checking in on a possible trade for running back Jonathan Taylor from the Indianapolis Colts, but another running back may be just as good of a target. The New York Jets may be looking to see what they can get for running back Breece Hall as he gets healthy from a quad injury. Jason Buechler from Sports Illustrated also brought up a good point for Hall being a decent target for teams: Hall is in the first year of a three-year contract, so this is more than a rental. Hall could slot into the Bengals’ offense and take over the backfield immediately. With the Ohio team holding all its 2027 draft picks, including an extra third-rounder, New York could push for the Bengals’ second-round pick. While it is true that Hall and Taylor both have two years left on their contracts after this season (Hall has a couple void years attached to his), Hall’s overall cap hit and age are much closer to what Cincinnati would prefer to take on. Not to mention the team could cut ties very easily before the 2028 season and save roughly $12 million in cap space, according to Over The Cap . Taylor’s deal has a similar out, but his caph hit exceeds $20 million starting next season. The other thing here to consider is the cost. A third round pick could get this pick done for a player who is still well within their prime while also costing less money. Taylor is a wonderful player, but considering the Colts would like a multiple pick return which would seemingly need to include a second round pick, it makes that a hard pill to swallow. We are of course playing in the hypothetical space where the team had to choose one. I think a vast majority of fans would agree that adding a couple of players to the back seven would do worlds more to improve this team overall than a running back. Who Dey! title: Browns are still struggling to change the team’s culture
summary: The Cleveland Browns have long been the league’s little brother that other teams like to bully, especially in the AFC North. There have been times over the years when a player has tried to insert that missing level of fight back, with former quarterback Baker Mayfield coming to mind. Even though Mayfield is five years […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have long been the league’s little brother that other teams like to bully, especially in the AFC North. There have been times over the years when a player has tried to insert that missing level of fight back, with former quarterback Baker Mayfield coming to mind. Even though Mayfield is five years and three teams removed from the Browns, he has not lost any of his feistiness, which was on full display during Sunday’s game against the Atlanta Falcons. While attempting to block down the field on Kenny Gainwell’s fourth-quarter touchdown run, Mayfield was dumped into a mud puddle by Atlanta safety Jessie Bates III. Mayfield popped back up, but more importantly, one of his offensive linemen quickly came to his defense and got after Bates. Baker Mayfield is a football guy 😤 🔜 #TBvsCHI Nov. 8 @ 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC pic.twitter.com/rwDrJOl391 — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) November 3, 2026 Now contrast that with two plays from Sunday as the Browns were once again bullied by the Steelers. On the game’s opening possession, quarterback Deshaun Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Pittsburgh safety Jaquan Brisker that left Watson lying face down on the field. While he was able to return to the game, Watson suffered a concussion that will likely sideline him for this week’s game against the New Orleans Saints. Later in the game, defensive end Jared Verse was dangerously dropped on his head by Pittsburgh offensive lineman Mason McCormick during an extra-point attempt. Verse was fortunate that he was not injured in what was clearly a dirty play. #Browns DE Jared Verse has been talking plenty of trash about the #Steelers …. Well, Steelers G Mason McCormick just did this to him. 😳😳 pic.twitter.com/OP1iknS4JP — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 1, 2026 Brisker and McCormick were both penalized for the plays, but did anyone on the Browns stick up for Watson or Verse? Did a lineman let Brisker know that the quarterback is off limits? Or call out McCormick? If you have watched the Browns for any time, you know the answer to those questions. Watson has not commented on the hit as he is busy recovering in the league-mandated concussion protocol. But on Thursday, Verse let it be known that he was not happy that no one stepped up when he went down, according to Mary Kay Cabot at cleveland.com : “The lack of reaction by those around me upset me a lot. Not any aspect of anybody; we’re focused on the game and everything like that. But a similar play happened to Derek Barnett; I think the next field goal and I spazzed. I lost it because it was my brother and my teammate. When you do something like that, it really upsets me very deeply. “So, I could tell that from that point on, I was like, we have to do better. We have to get better on every aspect of the game of being mentally aware of, these are my brothers and we’re not fighting for each other. We’re just kind of focused on the one aspect of the game.” Several of Verse’s teammates, including linebackers Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, said they did not see the play, while Barnett said he would have defended Verse if he had seen the play, but cautioned that the Browns can’t let a situation like that get out of hand. No one is looking for the Browns to turn into the Oakland Raiders of the 1970s, although they were the only team that stood up to the Steelers, so maybe a little bit of that attitude would be nice. Winning, of course, is the best revenge. But if the Browns are truly committed to changing the culture of the team, which is something that Verse has been vocal about since arriving in town from the Los Angeles Rams, then standing up for a fallen teammate from time to time would not be such a bad idea. The Browns 2026 seventh-round draft pick has: been waived to make room for QB Dillon Gabriel signed back to Cleveland’s practice squad been elevated for Week 8 versus the Pittsburgh Steelers signed to the Browns active 53-man roster on Wednesday once again waived on Thursday The last one, today, is an interesting one, and was first shared on DBN in The Feed: Cleveland practiced earlier in the afternoon on Thursday, with no indication of an issue with Ryan. The Browns are coming off of a bad loss to the Steelers, but it looks like they’ll have a change at quarterback this week (forced by injury) with Shedeur Sanders being under center. The Saints are well-rested, coming off of a bye. Note that some of the picks below were written up before the Browns’ quarterback news. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 9 game between the Browns and Saints: NFL.com (Various) Why Brooke picked the Saints: Shedeur Sanders is in line to start for the Browns with Deshaun Watson, who was playing his best ball since 2020, entering concussion protocol earlier this week. The biggest difference with Sanders under center appears to be his willingness to stretch the field, as his 7.1 air yards per target in 2025 are more than Watson’s 6.7 mark through eight games this season. Sanders is also working with a better receivers than he did a year ago with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion earning big roles in Todd Monken’s offense. None of that will ultimately matter if the run game is dormant — as it was last week (34 yards) in Pittsburgh. The Saints’ defense has been anything but great against the run, allowing 139.4 rush yards per game (29th in the NFL) and have given up north of 100 yards in all but one game in 2026. But I do see this being a get-right game for the Saints on all fronts fresh off the bye. Changes were made to the run game ( firing run-game coordinator T.J. Paganetti, signing RB Audric Estimé) and the kicking ranks (Charlie Smyth is expected to handle kicking duties after Daniel Carlson’s release), and the entire roster got a little healthier. First-round receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice and could be a boon — if he indeed makes his NFL debut — for Tyler Shough opposite Chris Olave. Getting Kelvin Banks Jr. back along an O-line that has struggled to keep Shough clean in the pocket should also benefit Kellen Moore’s unit. Sanders can smile all he wants, but the Saints will get the last laugh Sunday. CBS Sports (Pete Prisco) – Saints 17, Browns 14 The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. Sporting News (Bill Bender) – Saints 20, Browns 17 Both offenses are struggling. Deshaun Watson has taken a league-high 33 sacks, and the Browns average 97.6 rushing yards per game. New Orleans has been worse on the ground, but a bye week comes at the right time. The Saints are 0-4 S/U this season – and this game is a candidate for a walk-off field goal either way. Tyler Shough needs to avoid the interceptions, but New Orleans wins a coin-flip game. Below are our Week 9 NFL staff picks:
