title: 5 things we learned about the Browns in the Steelers loss
summary: The Cleveland Browns compiled a 5-2-0 record before meeting the Pittsburgh Steelers for the second time this season. Despite beating the Steelers 27-24 in Cleveland in Week 4, the Browns were taken to the woodshed in the rubber game by losing 27-6. The game pitted two teams that had identical records and were tied for […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns compiled a 5-2-0 record before meeting the Pittsburgh Steelers for the second time this season. Despite beating the Steelers 27-24 in Cleveland in Week 4, the Browns were taken to the woodshed in the rubber game by losing 27-6 . The game pitted two teams that had identical records and were tied for the AFC North Division lead. Now, Pittsburgh sits atop the division all alone, while the Browns are now situated in third place after the Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Tennessee Titans to grab second place. RELATED: RUN DEFENSE IS SCARY What did the Steelers’ loss teach the Browns’ fanbase ? Their coaching staff? The front office? Here are five things likely learned: The Browns will not be giving QB Deshaun Watson a contract extension Cleveland’s coaching staff has not hinted at benching Watson for the season. He has been a roller coaster and just isn’t any degree of the elite signal-caller he once was with Clemson and the Houston Texans. And now, he is on concussion protocol, which means he will have to sit out at least one game. This year is Watson’s first without getting injured while playing for the Browns; then he was placed in concussion protocol on Wednesday . To date, he hasn’t completed a full season despite being a roster member since 2022. He has missed a total of 57 games. Realistically, he has had only two great games with Cleveland: Week 10 in the 33-31 win over the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, and the Week 7 27-24 victory over the Titans this year. Watson has had a few good games this year with exceptional completion percentages in several games, including 80.0% (Bucs), 72.7% (Jaguars and Steelers first game), and 69.4% (Titans). All five triumphs in the win column this year were orchestrated by a comeback win by Watson. There were rumblings that perhaps if the Browns made the postseason, the front office should re-sign him to an extension and keep him going forward. Those thoughts were questioned when Cleveland lost to a lesser team, the New York Jets. In that contest, Watson had a 45.5% completion rate and struggled against a defense that challenged a clean pocket. The Steelers this past weekend used that blueprint and made Watson appear minimal on passing downs. They exposed Watson’s inability to get to safety once the pocket walls began to crumble. Pittsburgh also showed that Watson could not finish drives, especially when the drive concluded in the Red Zone. After the first quarter, Watson was 1 for 2 for three yards passing and no points on the board. At the half, he was 9 for 13 for 107 yards, was sacked four times, and his offense had just two field goals. To put an exclamation mark on sub-par play, Cleveland failed to score any points in the second half. Despite Watson being mentioned for the league “Comeback Player of the Year,” those views have now dissipated. The defense’s soft spot is right up the gut The Steelers ran for 200 yards, with RB Jaylen Warren doing much of the damage (143 yards). The majority of these yards were up the middle of the defense. Repeatedly, MLB Carson Schwesinger was moved out of position by either a blocking tight end crossing from the corner or an offensive lineman who pulled and led the running back through the hole provided. 5️⃣1️⃣ YARDS 🚂 @Nunless2 pic.twitter.com/3d2lNSEUfv — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 Look at the above clip from the first quarter. The right guard took out DT Maliek Collins and moved him to the right while the center blocked down on DT Mason Graham, then released as Steelers’ LG Mason McCormick had pulled and finished blocking Graham and kept pushing him to the left side. Suddenly, there was a big hole. Meanwhile, the center, Zach Frazier, pulled and led Warren into the hole and attacked Schwesinger. At the same time, the RT, rookie Max Iheanchor, went to the second level and engaged LB Quincy Williams and walled him off completely. Now, Warren is at the second level, and the only players he has to be concerned about are the safeties and the left corner, Denzel Ward. Receiver Brandon Smith took out Ward’s angle, and Warren was able to run right by him. S Grant Delpit came up, and Warren made a move around him. The tackle was finally made on this play by CB Tyson Campbell, who had lined up on the opposite side when the play began and ran all the way across the field. Schwesinger assisted, having trailed. Warren peeled off this run for 51 yards and set up the Pittsburgh offense into field goal range. Up the gut all day long. Block the defensive tackles to the left and right, send an offensive lineman to take out Schwesinger, and suddenly the play is off to the races with good downfield blocking. Here is a breakdown of Pittsburgh’s run selection: Around right end: 1 play Between right tackle/right guard: 3 plays Up the middle: 19 plays Between left tackle/left guard: 1 play Around left end: 4 plays Breakdown of the Steelers’ u p the middle gains: 15 yards, 9 (TD), 15, 51, 0, -2, 4, 23, 5, 6, 1 (TD), 2, 3, 13, 2, 1, 4, -1, -1 The Steelers gave every opponent left on the Browns’ schedule a blueprint of how to attack their defense. TE Harold Fannin is the best player on the field for Cleveland The Steelers’ strategy was to take out the Browns receivers and not let them hurt them. That worked. It did open up the match for TE Harold Fannin, who once again had a monster game. And Pittsburgh seemed fine with that. They already knew that the Browns could not run on them with their #7 ranking against the run. They just didn’t want to get burned with long passing plays to either Denzel Boston, Jerry Jeudy, or KC Concepcion. Boston had six receptions for 37 yards, Jeudy had zero catches, and Concepcion hauled in three catches for 37 yards. Fannin had 12 targets, 10 catches for 154 yards. Fannin isn’t really a serious deep threat, although his YAC yards are always good every single game. Fannin has 411 receiving yards, with 233 being YAC numbers. He is a human bowling ball going down the field and tough to bring down. With Myles Garrett now gone, the question was asked before the season began as to who was the new face of the Browns. It is Fannin. Thank goodness for a good kicker Kicker Andre Szmyt has taken drives that stall out and converted them into points. He has missed just two field goals, both in the 40-49 range, and is 2-for-2 with kicks of 50+. Very calm guy who simply walks onto the field and will nail the game-winner. 11 of 12 on PATs. Cleveland has scored 139 points, of which Szmyt has accounted for 59 (43%). Accounted for all the scoring against the Steelers. Cleveland’s offensive line is a problem This offensive line has only one alteration since Week 1 on a permanent note: OT Austin Barber was inserted at right guard in place of Teven Jenkins, who remains out because of back issues. So, it is not a continuity problem. Collectively, this group just isn’t very good. Welcome to the sack party 🥳 pic.twitter.com/VwOqfkHWU0 — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 3, 2026 On passing downs, the Steelers collapsed the pocket from the inside. This was accomplished by bull rushing the center and both guards, which pushed the pocket backwards. When Watson decided he needed to exit the pocket, the edge rushers were right there, giving no escape route. This happened over and over. Eight sacks against Pittsburgh, and another eight against the Jets. How many times did you notice Watson trying to leave the pocket and then run right into a defender? summary: Like last season, the Dallas Cowboys are one of the most disappointing teams in the NFL in 2026. full_text: Like last season, the Dallas Cowboys are one of the most disappointing teams in the NFL in 2026. After hearing from Brian Schottenheimer, Christian Parker, Klayton Adams, and most of the key players this week, it seems like there is a lot of reflecting going on inside The Star currently. With the decimated Indianapolis Colts coming up this week in the noon window, the Cowboys are desperate for a win, not only for their playoff hopes, but for the locker room sanity. Frustrations boiling over as Cowboys’ offensive inconsistencies persist: ‘We stop ourselves’ – Calvin Watkins, The Dallas Morning News The Cowboys locker room is clearly frustrated with what’s going on. While the talking point this week has been “execution”, the Cowboys coaching staff needs to hold up their end of the bargain as well on the offensive side of the football. Over the last three weeks, the Cowboys have converted 38.5%, 61.4% and 37.5% on third-down plays. The ups and downs of their season are attributed to execution. “It’s hard to say we’re pressing,” quarterback Dak Prescott said. “But, yeah, when you’ve got the talent we’ve got, when you’ve got the expectation, the standards that we have for ourselves and you go three-and-out or you don’t score a touchdown, yeah, that’s frustrating and you’ve got to make sure that you don’t allow that to continue to bleed because then that bleeds into guys making [mistakes] or not doing the details the right way because they want the big play rather than just sticking to it.” Cowboys offense looking to find their fastball vs. Colts – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys lack of identify on offense points directly to their head coach and play-caller. Each week they seem to bounce back and forth from a run-first team to a pass-heavy team. That lack of consistency may be a big reason the team has been so inconsistent so far this season. While the numbers and league rankings for the Cowboys may be in the upper part of the league, Dallas still feels as though they haven’t played their best as offense through eight games in 2026. For Pro Bowl WR CeeDee Lamb, part of the core issue is staring back at the offense in the mirror. “We stop ourselves,” Lamb said. “That sh** is frustrating. It’s annoying. I hate it. And then ultimately, we end up losing.” Cowboys CB DaRon Bland Gets Blunt Assessment From Christian Parker – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Christian Parker gives a brutally honest and correct assessment on cornerback DaRon Bland ahead of week nine. The Cowboys need a lot more out of Bland and Parker if they want to turn things around on defense during the second-half. That’s why defensive coordinator Christian Parker recently said he and Bland have discussed the need for improvement from the fifth-year defensive back. “We need more from him. He knows that, we’ve had some good talks about that. I think he’s battling. The frustrating thing for him and for us has been he’s been close and contesting. Now, it’s about the final piece of just finishing those plays,” Parker said via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “We just got to get back to making that consistent.” Download the SB Nation app today! Which matchup will you be most focused on? Quinnen Williams got off to somewhat of a slow start this season, but recently has been playing at an elite level. title: Cowboys at Colts: 3 causes for concern in Week 9
summary: After a demoralizing loss a week ago, the Dallas Cowboys will look to bounce back on Sunday as they face off against the Indianapolis Colts. While the Colts do have a 2-6 record, they do some things well that may cause issues for Dallas. With that thought in mind, here are three causes for concern […]
full_text: (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a demoralizing loss a week ago, the Dallas Cowboys will look to bounce back on Sunday as they face off against the Indianapolis Colts. While the Colts do have a 2-6 record, they do some things well that may cause issues for Dallas. With that thought in mind, here are three causes for concern in Indianapolis. 1) Colts Rushing Attack In what has been a disastrous season, one thing the Indianapolis Colts have done consistently well is run the ball. Led by All-Pro running back Jonathan Taylor, who may be entering his last game as a Colt, Indy has been one of the league’s better running teams. The Colts have recorded 100 or more rushing yards in six of their last eight contests, including three games over 125. Indy is fourth in the league in offensive rush EPA (-0.002) and ninth in rush success rate (43.1%). Before last week’s disaster performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Taylor was on an absolute tear. From Weeks 4 through 7, the star runner recorded 329 rushing yards on 74 carries and four touchdowns. Those numbers come out to a full-season pace of 1,398 rushing yards and 17 rushing touchdowns. If the Cowboys want to beat the Colts, they’ll need to contain Taylor and Indy’s run game. Dallas’ defense has been the third-worst run defense in terms of rush EPA (-0.020) while also allowing the second-most rushing Y/A (5.0). If the Cowboys play as poorly against the run as they have all season long and let Taylor and the Colts’ running game get rolling, it’s going to be a long day for their defense. 2) Indianapolis Third-Down Defense This season, we’ve seen just how important it is for a defense to be strong on third down. While Dallas has been by far the league’s worst defensive unit on the most important down in football, the Colts have been one of the best. Indy has held opponents to a 32.6% third-down conversion rate this season, the seventh-best in the league. In five of Indy’s last six games, their defense has held opponents to a third-down conversion rate of 36% or lower, including three games at 30% or better. 3rd Down Conv. HOU 4/11 WAS 2/15 PIT 4/11 TEN 3/10 MIN 3/11 The Cowboys offense will face a big challenge this week in extending drives and moving the ball downfield. Last week, Dallas converted six of 16 third-down attempts against the Arizona Cardinals. They’ll need to execute better offensively this week to get that conversion percentage higher against a stingy Colts defense. 3) The Anthony Richardson Factor This season has been a disaster for Colts starting quarterback Daniel Jones. The veteran signal-caller has thrown just five touchdown passes to nine interceptions, turning the ball over at least once in seven of the Colts’ eight games. Jones has looked even worse as the season has worn on, recording five interceptions and a 59.2 Passer Rating over Indy’s last three games. Given his performance over that span, it’s no surprise the Colts are 0-3 in those matchups. The Colts are 2-6 and, after trading away two of their best players, with a third likely to follow, have no chance of competing for a playoff spot. They have nothing to lose, and if Jones struggles early this week, there’s a good chance Indy could pull the trigger and bring in backup quarterback Anthony Richardson. While Richardson’s NFL career has been fairly disastrous to date, he is extremely physically talented and could bring a different element to the table if the Colts put him in the game. We saw Dallas’ defense meltdown last week when the Cardinals made a mid-game quarterback change; it’s fair to worry that history will repeat itself if Indy follows suit on Sunday.

title: Cowboys offensive line vs. Colts defensive line examined
summary: If the Cowboys want to get back on the winning track, a dominant performance from their offensive line would certainly help. Let’s see how they match up against the Colts defensive line. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far.  Pass Block Win Rate – 53% (8th) Run […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images If the Cowboys want to get back on the winning track, a dominant performance from their offensive line would certainly help. Let’s see how they match up against the Colts defensive line. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 53% (8th) Run Block Win Rate – 69% (31st) Pressure rate allowed – 30% (15th) Sacks allowed – 11 (4th) Last three-week trend: One step forward, one step back The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Adetomiwa Adebawore is now the player Dallas has to find DeForest Buckner is gone after Indianapolis traded the three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle to San Francisco last week. That sounds like great news for Dallas, but his replacement might actually be the most dangerous individual pass-rushing matchup on the Colts defense. Adetomiwa Adebawore has quietly put together an excellent season. PFF currently credits him with 16 pressures and five sacks, while his 84.4 pass-rush grade ranks third among qualifying interior defensive linemen. That is the matchup Dallas cannot overlook simply because Buckner has left town. Interior pressure is especially dangerous for Prescott. When an edge defender gets around Tyler Guyton or Terence Steele, Dak Prescott can often step forward. When Adebawore wins directly through the middle, there is nowhere to step. That puts Tyler Smith, Cooper Beebe and Tyler Booker under pressure to restore order after a poor performance against Arizona. PRESSURE POINT: The tackles need a response Tyler Guyton had been enjoying a strong season before Sunday, then Arizona changed that. Guyton finished with a 44.7 PFF grade, while Terence Steele was only slightly better at 48.2. Four of Dallas’ five starting offensive linemen graded below 50. Indianapolis does not have an elite edge rush, but there are still players capable of punishing another poor performance. Laiatu Latu earned an 84.0 PFF grade against Jacksonville and recorded a sack. Jaylahn Tuimoloau also recorded a sack and generated four pressures, producing a 22.2% pressure win rate in the game. Still, the Colts rank last in ESPN Pass Rush Win Rate. If Guyton and Steele surrender quick pressure anyway, it becomes a major concern for a Cowboys offensive line that was supposed to be settling down. Against Philadelphia, Prescott was barely touched. Against Arizona, he went down four times. Dallas needs the Philadelphia version back. WHERE TO ATTACK Every defensive line has a weakness, here’s the Colts soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Run straight at the post-Buckner Colts This might be the clearest green light Dallas has seen all season. Indianapolis has allowed: 1,054 rushing yards 131.8 rushing yards per game 4.9 yards per carry 26% Run Stop Win Rate which ranks 29th Then the Colts traded Buckner. Their first game without him ended with Jacksonville rushing for 183 yards, that is an invitation. Dallas cannot respond by putting everything back on Prescott. Javonte Williams carried 24 times against Arizona but gained only 56 yards. The blocking simply did not give him anywhere to go so this week needs to look different. Tyler Smith and Tyler Booker are two powerful guards. Cooper Beebe can work combination blocks with either of them. Dallas should use that interior strength and force Indianapolis to prove it can hold up without Buckner. Even Grover Stewart has not been dominant this season. His current PFF run-defense grade sits at 60.4, 43rd among qualifying interior defenders. Adebawore has been much more dangerous rushing the passer than anchoring an entire run defense, so make them both play the run and make Indianapolis’ linebackers tackle Williams repeatedly. And most importantly, do not abandon the run if the first few attempts only gain three yards. The Colts have been worn down by opposing running games all season. Dallas should test that weakness for four quarters. GREEN LIGHT: Make Indianapolis win with its four-man pass rush The ESPN number is difficult to ignore as you will see below, Indianapolis’ Pass Rush Win Rate is at 40%, that ranks 32nd. That means the Colts have been the NFL’s least successful team at quickly defeating pass blocks on an individual basis, and their sack production confirms it. Indianapolis has only 16 sacks through eight games, that ranks 23rd. Dallas should trust its offensive line when the Colts send four. Put the running backs and tight ends into routes and force Indianapolis to cover CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Jake Ferguson and the running backs. If Indianapolis wants to rush four, Dallas’ five offensive linemen need to win. The Chaos Report Here’s the Arizona Cardinals defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 16 (23rd) Pass Rush Win Rate – 40% (32nd) Run Stop Win Rate – 27% (28th) QB Pressure Rate – 21% (32nd) Last three-week trend: Weak and getting weaker Matchup of the week Tyler Smith vs. Adetomiwa Adebawore When Indianapolis lines Adebawore up across from Tyler Smith, watch it, this is strength against strength. Adebawore is now the most disruptive interior pass rusher on the Colts roster and Smith is the Cowboys offensive lineman best equipped to deal with that combination of speed and power. Adebawore is only 282 pounds, which makes this matchup particularly interesting. He wins with explosion and quickness, and Smith wins with strength. When the Cowboys run, Smith needs to put his hands on Adebawore early and move him, instead of allowing him to shoot through a gap. That also helps later in pass protection. If Adebawore spends the afternoon dealing with Smith coming forward in the running game, he cannot simply spend every snap attacking backwards toward Prescott. Best Route to Success Dallas should not make this game complicated since the Colts cannot stop the run and those numbers should immediately tell Brian Schottenheimer where this game needs to begin. Get Smith and Booker moving forward, feed Williams, use play-action once Indianapolis starts bringing its linebackers downhill, then trust the tackles against a pass rush that ranks last in Pass Rush Win Rate. Dallas cannot repeat what happened against Arizona, where one week of dominant offensive-line play disappeared immediately. The Cowboys have already shown how good this unit can look, Indianapolis provides the perfect opportunity to prove Philadelphia was not a fluke. Injury Updates: Dallas currently has no new injury concerns among its five starting offensive linemen, but keep watch on Jake Ferguson. This could bring Brevyn Spann-Ford to the mix who’s been a much better blocker this year. Veteran edge defender Arden Key remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, while Micheal Clemons has also been on IR with a toe injury.

As the Cowboys nickel CB and the Colts slot WR, Caleb Downs should see plenty of his brother Josh throughout the game Sunday afternoon in Indianapolis if Caleb plays. These two will no doubt be trying to get the better of one another as brothers do, which could create an interesting matchup. There is a chance though one, possibly both, don’t play this week. With Caleb currently in concussion protocol and Josh seeking a trade, one or the other may not suit up. The brotherly connection aside, this is very much an important matchup. The head-to-head matchup with rookie Jalen Farmer, a fourth-round pick this year, is one No. 92 should dominate. Look for him to make multiple plays behind the line of scrimmage this week in both the run and pass defense. RB Javonte Williams vs. Colts run defense We can probably expect a heavy dose of Javonte Williams Sunday afternoon against the Colts. Indianapolis is currently ranked 27 th in the league in run defense, allowing 131.8 rushing yards per game. This is a weakness the Cowboys should exploit, especially considering Indianapolis’ Pro Bowl CBs Sauce Gardener and Charvarius Ward and the rest of their secondary are only allowing 211.8 passing yards per game (12 th in the league). title: Cowboys at Colts: 2 players Dallas should use more in Week 9
summary: The 2026 Dallas Cowboys may have reached rock bottom. After an embarrassing loss to the Arizona Cardinals a week ago, Dallas looks to start its climb out of the grave against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. If the Cowboys want to avoid another loss, they’ll need to change some things up. With that thought in […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Dallas Cowboys may have reached rock bottom. After an embarrassing loss to the Arizona Cardinals a week ago, Dallas looks to start its climb out of the grave against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. If the Cowboys want to avoid another loss, they’ll need to change some things up. With that thought in mind, here are two players Dallas should use more against the Colts. 1) RB Tyler Goodson One of the more disappointing things on the offensive side of the ball for the Cowboys this season has been their inability to sustain success in the run game. Dallas is in the bottom ten in rushing yards (753) and rushing Y/A (3.8). Since Week 4, the Cowboys have recorded more than 95 rushing yards in a single game just once. While most of Dallas’ struggles in the run game fall on the performance of the offensive line, starting running back Javonte Williams had an uncharacteristic performance in last week’s loss. Williams looked worn down and lacked any burst and power, something he brought in a big way during his career day in Philly less than a week prior. It’s fair to question if his early-season workload has caused a decrease in production. Williams has the ninth-most carries in the league and has averaged less than 4.0 Y/A in six of Dallas’ eight games this season. Coming into the season, keeping Williams fresh should have been a focal point for Dallas’ offense. To this point in the year, they’ve done a bad job of keeping their top runner at his best. The Cowboys need to lean more on backup running back Tyler Goodson, who’s shown plenty of juice in limited opportunities. While Goodson did average just 2.0 Y/A last week against Arizona, he has three 10+ yard runs on the season in just 28 rushing attempts. The Cowboys don’t need to go to a true 50/50 split, but giving Goodson five or six more carries a game will help Javonte Williams get back to form and keep him playing at a high level the rest of the regular season. 2) OT Broderick Jones It’s time for the Cowboys to pull the plug on Terence Steele. It’s been two years now since we’ve seen Steele perform as a starting-caliber offensive tackle. Steele has allowed 17 pressures, 10 of which have come in the past three weeks, to go with 14 QB hurries. The Cowboys have 25-year-old Broderick Jones waiting in the wings, and they need to see what he can do in an increased role. Steele’s struggles in both the pass and run game were a big reason why the Cowboys were not able to consistently move the ball against the Cardinals. While Jones is far from a sure thing, he deserves a chance to see if he can at least perform better than Steele has. The Cowboys are very stubborn, so it likely won’t happen, but Broderick Jones should be Dallas’ starting right tackle on Sunday in Indianapolis.

title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: Inconsistency looms as huge obstacle
summary: It’s one thing for a football team to be inconsistent from game to game. That can make it hard to accomplish much. Being wildly inconsistent within the same game is possibly even worse. We just saw the Dallas Cowboys wrest a stunning defeat from the jaws of what looked until halftime was going to be […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images It’s one thing for a football team to be inconsistent from game to game. That can make it hard to accomplish much. Being wildly inconsistent within the same game is possibly even worse. We just saw the Dallas Cowboys wrest a stunning defeat from the jaws of what looked until halftime was going to be a pretty decent win over their nemesis, the Arizona Cardinals. They dominated things before halftime, building a 17-3 lead. The offense wasn’t exactly crisp, but a couple of takeaways and some sacks let them put points up while keeping the Cards under control. But Arizona pulled Jacoby Brissett and put Gardiner Minshew in at QB, and suddenly they were an offensive juggernaut. Dallas still managed to add 13 points to their score, but could not stop the Cards from scoring TDs on four consecutive drives. Still, thanks to a missed extra point, the Cowboys had a chance to win it in overtime, only to see their offense continue a slump that started in the fourth quarter. This inconsistency now hangs over their heads as they visit the Indianapolis Colts next Sunday. Our Sean Martin and Tom Ryle discuss the unfortunate realities of this year’s Dallas team. Tom – It’s hard to process the abject failure we witnessed at AT&T Stadium. After bottling up the Arizona offense for the most part, the Cowboys’ defense just seemed to crumble once Minshew came in. What is really mystifying is how the most damage was done by running back Tyler Allgeier. Another bevy of missed tackles and bad defensive alignments let him run free. The defense had really been the main reason Dallas built a 14-point lead at half. Then it just fell apart. Meanwhile, their offense was also displaying its own version of inconsistency. After a good showing against the admittedly depleted Philadelphia Eagles, we once again saw multiple missed opportunities. The run game went back to sleep. A rash of sacks of Dak Prescott also played a big part. We are seeing evidence that he has to have a clean pocket to make the passing game work. Once that breaks down, things go off the rails. Now the chance for the first winning streak has been blown, they are facing another ‘must win’ game. The Colts do look very beatable. The challenge is that Dallas cannot play down to the level of the competition again. Sean – Our worst nightmare has been realized, as now it requires beating the San Francisco 49ers to get back-to-back wins, and still needing until mid-November to do so. The inconsistency really makes the fan experience hard to enjoy, we have to say at this point we’ve been conditioned under Brian Schottenheimer to just expect a letdown after each and every win. And here’s the crushing thing that goes with that too – even Schotty’s wins this season aren’t impressive. There were some things to like about how the team took a workmanlike attitude out of the Eagles win, instead of getting too high like usual, but clearly this somehow didn’t help them get up off the mat once hit with adversity at home against the Cardinals. That is ridiculous. Tom – I would choose ludicrous as my description. This is a team with veteran leadership that looks rudderless. And clearly the coaching staff is doing an enormously inept job. Although I will not tabulate any fetal barnyard fowl, I do think there is a better than even chance they will beat the Colts. Maybe by a comfortable margin, or just eking out a win. But as I said, that is hardly a given. And if they do manage to avoid an even bigger disappointment against 2-6 Indy, that, as you said, still leaves the NFCW-leading 49ers to face. Given how things have gone this season, the most likely scenario is that they will get a win at the Colts, then get totally embarrassed by San Francisco. That is another home game for Dallas, and they have only managed one win this season in their own house. Trying to find things to build hope on is very hard. Sean – This game was really a wild meltdown in three parts. Early on, it didn’t feel like the Cowboys had a lot of energy, but the score held at 17-3 for a while and there was some thought that maybe this would be a win stamped by the defense , which would be a welcome sight to say the least. Then it became just trying to hold on for dear life, to the point where even a win doesn’t bode all that well for seizing any momentum. My only thought at this point was that it is the Cardinals, these games are for whatever reason never easy, and let’s just get the win in the bank. Finally, the collapse was complete, and now there really is only one way to describe this upcoming Colts game as far as I’m concerned – two bad teams going at it. The Cowboys have zero quality wins and a list of bad losses that some head coaches don’t compile in multiple seasons on the job, yet Schottenheimer has five and room to add more before Thanksgiving here in year two. Tom – I for one am so tired of wasting talented players. I don’t know if it’s bad coaching, a failure to have a better supporting cast so the talent at the top is nullified, or maybe some kind of culture issue. Maybe some of all three, and things we just can’t figure out. I am getting an uneasy feeling that we are watching yet another season go down the drain. No, it’s not just a feeling. It’s a growing sense of inevitability. At least I came into this year without great hopes, believing it was always a long shot to make the playoffs with no real chance at going far. So I’m not disappointed as much as I’m just disgusted. Sean – Likewise Tom, my concern is about trying to get something out of this season that protects what’s hopefully the best possible future for this franchise, but that feels rocky right now. Doing virtually no work on one side of the ball (offense) in the offseason won’t be an option; by the time we slog our way through this latest wasted season, the offense is going to have concerns, question marks, and need to be shaken up. It could very well have a new head coach, offensive coordinator, or both on top of all that. The best path forward for the defense is likely still to get to a second season with the same coordinator in place, but is it too much to ask for the coordinator earning that chance to not give up 33 points to the Cardinals? This organization is going to have a hard time selling a year 12 for Dak Prescott being the one they finally use to get over the hump, and we don’t even know if that will include both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens remaining together. They sure didn’t seem interested in using this duo to their advantage against the Cardinals anyway. Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams will be a year older, and they’ve needed EDGE help since the start of this season, another thing that hurt them in this latest loss. Normally, the generic answer here would just be that seeing which players continue to play hard through adversity is always something a team can build off of. Right now though, that just feels like a play into the whole “culture build” that Schotty sold us a bill of goods on, and appeasing to a coach long term that doesn’t have a long term future here as far as any of the fan base is concerned. *Gulps* We might have to continue having the conversation that the best thing for this current 2026 team is to still try and win the NFC East, which physically makes me feel gross to even say.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys news: The lack of snaps for George Pickens explained
summary: If the Cowboys are going to find themselves in any kind of position to win a bad NFC East division, their defense has got to improve. Multiple players have spoken about the state of the unit, and the solutions don’t seem to be that difficult, but they have to put it all together on the […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images If the Cowboys are going to find themselves in any kind of position to win a bad NFC East division, their defense has got to improve. Multiple players have spoken about the state of the unit, and the solutions don’t seem to be that difficult, but they have to put it all together on the field. One of the big topics around Dallas lately has been wide receiver George Pickens and his playing time, or lack thereof. There’s been speculation as to why this is, but it was recently cleared up by head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Brian Schottenheimer Explains George Pickens’ Lack of Snaps, Targets in Recent Cowboys Games – Mike Moraitis, SI.com The reduction of snaps for Pickens has been very noticeable over the last few weeks. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer breaks down why that’s been the case. “Brian Schottenheimer told me that George Pickens snaps have been limited by his injuries,” Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys said. “He has been taken off the field because blocking in the run game.” Schottenheimer added that it “would be poor coaching by me” to keep Pickens off the field for any reason. That checks out because Pickens was added to the injury report in Week 7 due to a shoulder issue and he remained on it through last week. Cowboys defense searching for answers after meltdown loss: ‘Execute on Sunday’ – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram The Cowboys defense has had trouble with consistency in 2026. According to defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, the solution is quite simple. In going back and watching the film, one thing stood out to the defenders on what did not happen: execution. “The biggest thing is execute,” defensive tackle Quinnen Williams said. “We got to execute. We haven’t been executing this whole season. We executed for three quarters and didn’t execute that last quarter, and the film says it all. We have to execute and stack days.” Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Cowboys injury updates: Dallas secondary might be extremely shorthanded again – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Its been a tough season on the injury front for the Cowboys secondary. When they face the Indianapolis Colts this Sunday, it could be slim pickings in terms of who is available in that area. It looks like those injuries could be a factor again. The Cowboys had 11 players who didn’t practice Wednesday or were limited due to injury. That included two starting defensive backs in corner Caleb Downs and safety P.J. Locke. Both suffered concussions in Sunday’s 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals . Schottenheimer said both Downs and Locke were still in concussion protocol as of Wednesday. Both were seen on the field during practice participating in workouts with helmets, but not drills. Wetzel: $17 billion Cowboys have a penny-pinching owner in Jerry Jones – Dan Wetzel, ESPN Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said earlier this week that he didn’t see any correlation between how much a team spends on a head coach and winning. That could be part of the reason why Dallas hasn’t won in such a long time. Or, as a coaching agent told NFL Network’s Jane Slater when asked how aggressive Jones had been in looking for a veteran coach after the 2024 season: “Jerry won’t pay $13M and up, and that’s the starting point.” Instead, Dallas promoted Schottenheimer, its own offensive coordinator and a longtime assistant. The Cowboys were the only team to interview him that year. Schottenheimer might prove to be a good coach despite his 10-14-1 start, but should the most valuable team on the planet be led by a guy who has to grow into the job? Shemar James explains mindset of Cowboys ‘urgent’ defense – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Dallas has had another shaky season defensively so far. With that said, linebacker Shemar James says the unit is eager to get things on track. “I feel there’s a sense of urgency every week, whether we win or lose, because every week is a dogfight,” James added. “I mean, we’re in a National Football League, so there’s not going to be a week that we have circled like, ‘Oh, we’re going to beat these guys.’ “You can’t take [a game] off. Every week, we have a sense of urgency to go out there and execute, and it just didn’t get done this weekend. And that’s why we have another week to go out there and prove to people that we’re the defense that we know we can be.”

title: Jonah Coleman continues to turn heads with the Broncos
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Jonah Coleman continues to impress. The rookie running back consistently takes advantage of the opportunities he gets on the field and runs with them, literally. In the 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, he had the game-changing reception that set up his game-winning touchdown. Now comes the next chance for […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball against the Kansas City Chiefs in the first quarter of a game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Jonah Coleman continues to impress. The rookie running back consistently takes advantage of the opportunities he gets on the field and runs with them, literally. In the 28-24 win over the Kansas City Chiefs, he had the game-changing reception that set up his game-winning touchdown. Now comes the next chance for Coleman on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers and their 30th-ranked rushing defense. When Broncos head coach Sean Payton was asked how Coleman has impressed despite the injury, Payton said: “We had those glimpses in the spring and in training camp and in the preseason. Atlanta, there’s a run, it just stood out to you. So the one thing that was unique about him is oftentimes you don’t get to see them in third-down protection plans, but he was someone that we had quite a bit of tape on. Advanced protection plans, and he’s built to handle the blitz. “It’s one thing to know who I have, but then also to be strong enough to do it. I would say that there were three backs — we just saw one of them that we really had visions for. Each one may be a little differently, but his versatility, to your point, that doesn’t always — you don’t get to stamp that with a lot of rookie backs that you feel like they’re going to develop into. We saw enough that we felt like he was going to be a good third-down protecting back as well, with the way he was built.” In the victory over Kansas City, Coleman finished with 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown, as well as four receptions for 63 yards. Obviously, that total is boosted by the 51-yard reception to put Denver on the 4-yard line. But it’s clear the rookie brings an element to this offense that the other running backs on the roster cannot. Coleman has shown great vision, instincts, and runs with physicality that is fun to watch. “I think he’s playing really well with confidence,” Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said to the media. “He’s a very intelligent young running back. What sticks out the most is he can handle a lot. You can put a lot on his plate. After we learned that R.J. Harvey wasn’t going to play last week, he got a little bit more of the bulk of R.J.’s stuff. “It’s impressive to see him be able to be used in a lot of different ways. When he gets in there, he’s a natural runner. That’s what he’s drafted for. That’s the position he plays. It’s the out-of-the-backfield stuff that I think is making a good impression on us right now.” What’s most impressive is how Coleman is handling pass protection. That’s one of the toughest aspects for a rookie running back to grasp. What’s exciting to contemplate is that Coleman can get even better the more he plays. “We caught him in the right pressure there,” Payto said to the media. “Yes, he’s very comfortable. He’s a different type (of) player than RJ (Harvey), but there were a lot of traits to like. More importantly, there was the exposure in an offense that sometimes the player just doesn’t have that exposure, so you can’t know for sure. I think we knew a little bit more with his tape.” All of this to say, Coleman brings a spark to the Broncos. “I think that started since rookie minicamp, and then the preseason game against Atlanta, and then the Jacksonville game, and now this game,” Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb said to the media. “I think every time he gets an opportunity, he’s showed up. His teammates love him. He’s smart, he’s mature, and he’s going to continue to get better, which is awesome.” Broncos links

title: Broncos pass rush has returned with a fury through eight games
summary: While the sack numbers are a bit off pace to the previous two seasons, the pressure rate is actually higher. The Denver Broncos defense is forcing quarterbacks to get rid of the ball quick or face the consequences. The reason the sacks are off pace is due to the competition this defense has faced. These […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - NOVEMBER 1: Malcolm Roach (97) of the Denver Broncos sacks Patrick Mahomes (15) of the Kansas City Chiefs on the final play of the game as Nik Bonitto (15) adds a hit during the fourth quarter of the Broncos' 28-24 win at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, November 1, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images While the sack numbers are a bit off pace to the previous two seasons, the pressure rate is actually higher. The Denver Broncos defense is forcing quarterbacks to get rid of the ball quick or face the consequences. 144 quarterback pressures . 12 more than second place. 74 combined sacks and QB hits . 15 more than second place. 51 quarterback hits . 11 more than second place. PFF’s top ranked pass rush grade . Best pass rush win rate. The reason the sacks are off pace is due to the competition this defense has faced. These quarterbacks are really good at avoiding sacks: Patrick Mahomes x2, Trevor Lawrence, Matthew Stafford, and Brock Purdy. Those guys have a combined 41 sacks between them. The other three quarterbacks Denver faced: Justin Herbert, Jacoby Brisset, and Sam Darnold have a combined 59 sacks between them. Of the remaining eight quarterbacks on the schedule, four quarterbacks are in the Top 5 in sacks taken and all but Josh Allen and Kirk Cousins are in the Top 10. Those sack numbers should start to stack for this Broncos defense down the stretch. Broncos daily recap Broncos focused on taking care of business against Panthers The Denver Broncos have a shot to be 7-2 before their bye week if they can topple the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. How the Denver Broncos can beat the Carolina Panthers The Denver Broncos head on the road to face the Carolina Panthers in Week 9. Here is how they can earn their seventh win of the season. Broncos vs. Panthers: 3 Things to Watch in Week 9 Here are three storylines to watch when the Denver Broncos battle the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Alex Singleton named AFC Defensive Player of the Month What a turnaround from Week 1 for Alex Singleton and the entire defense. Singleton especially has been balling out during the Denver Broncos four game win streak! Potent quotables Vance Joseph On the defense’s performance in goal-line situations “I think we just play. We don’t worry about where the ball’s put down. We just play. Those things we practice every single week. I’m not surprised that we’re good down there. We spent a bunch of time down there. It’s been our fourth year together. We have our four or five calls we love down there that we’re good at. So if we do it right, we expect to win.” On if he’s surprised that ILB Alex Singleton wasn’t previously recognized for his high level of play “No, that’s the league. When you’re playing well on defense, guys do get recognized. He’s been consistent for a long time. He had 175 tackles [three] years ago. No one talks about that. I’m not surprised he’s playing well again.” On young players like DE Sai’vion Jones and OLB Que Robinson being ready to play “It’s coaching. I think when you’re picking your roster, you have to pick your roster with guys that fit your scheme. I think here that’s what we’ve done. So when you lose one player, we have guys who can fill in who have the same skill set. So I’m not surprised those kids play well. Again it’s NFL football. It’s the same coach, it’s the same room. When it’s their turn to play, they play to the standard. If they don’t fit and they can’t play, they shouldn’t be here. Every guy on this team who makes our roster on defense, if they have to play for us, nothing changes in my mind. Let’s go win the game. There are certain areas where I can’t call certain things with certain players, but the standard of doing it right, that never changes here.” Darren Rizzi On determining special teams rotations during games “I think one of the things people might not recognize is we do a pretty good job of keeping track of reps during the game. We have guys up in the box kind of doing a rep count and making sure no one’s getting too many. As you know, there are some games where you might have 18 special teams plays, and there are some games where you might have 35. It really just depends how the game plays out. So we’ll do a good job. We’ll have a plan kind of going in. Dispel those guys if needed. They’re going to have to do obviously some things. They might not do the full workload as they normally do. Then again, they might depending on how the game plays out. So we’ll kind of track that as we go. Yes, my depth chart sheet will be an interesting one. Be like the old, what’s the movie? The old Matrix . It’ll be a lot of stuff going on there.” On the challenges of kicking field goals and extra points in the rain and how they prepare for those conditions “I think obviously because we play outdoors at our home games, weekly we’ll maybe do some wet ball drills and things like that. It’s weird when the K-balls are a different ball than the quarterback ball. They’re a little bit smoother because they get kind of worked. So when those balls get a little bit wet, they actually get really slippery. It’s not the ball that’s soaked, it’s the ball when it just starts raining. If you’ve talked to all the specialists over the years, the snappers and the holders and the punter catching the operation, those are the ones. So right away when you see any precipitation come down, those guys are off on the side and they’re getting work and whether or not they use a towel, gloves, whatever we’re allowed to use. Yes, it certainly makes that operation. So as soon as we know we’re going to get any kind of weather, we certainly practice it. Then those guys on gameday are going to be working on the sideline and gauging the weather.” On the challenges of kicking at sea level when they’re accustomed to altitude “I think the pregame warmup for us may be more important than any other position because you kind of get an idea of how the ball’s going to travel on that particular day, whether it’s wind, weather. I’ve coached at sea level for more than 16 years in the NFL and then a bunch of years in college. The ball may not travel as well. We’ll see what the weather is there. The pregame for the kicker and the punter is probably more important than people would anticipate because you kind of get the wind direction, you know which way if it’s sideways wind or north-south wind, if you will. Then how well the ball’s traveling. So we kind of have, [Head] Coach [Sean Payton] will always ask me right before kickoff, ‘What’s our line going each way for us and them?’ So the ball certainly travels a little bit better here in altitude, but I think sometimes it gets overblown, overdid a little bit. We’ll see how it is there in pregame on Sunday morning.” Davis Webb On the spark RB Jonah Coleman brings to the offense “I think that started since rookie minicamp, and then the preseason game against Atlanta, and then the Jacksonville game and now this game. I think every time he gets an opportunity, he’s showed up. His teammates love him. He’s smart, he’s mature and he’s going to continue to get better, which is awesome.” On how Head Coach Sean Payton has prepared the team for its next game following an emotional win “I think if you look at Carolina’s record, you can be one of those guys that overlooks them. If you look at the Chicago game, they put up a lot of points on offense. You look at the Detroit game, they beat them. There are plenty of examples of this team being really, really good there. A playoff team last year, arguably should have beat the Rams in the playoffs last year. So they’re a couple plays away from having a winning record. This is the NFL. There are not many cupcakes out there, so this is going to be a good one on Sunday.” On the challenge of facing a team with a new defensive coordinator “I think the first quarter’s going to be interesting in regards to seeing what they have new, what’s…

title: Alex Singleton named AFC Defensive Player of the Month
summary: The Denver Broncos have been on a tear through October, winning all of their games with the defense emerging back into its dominant form that its had over the previous two seasons. The man in the middle of that defense, Alex Singleton, has been a huge part of that rise. Through the month of October, […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Alex Singleton #49 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after his team's 28-24 win against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have been on a tear through October, winning all of their games with the defense emerging back into its dominant form that its had over the previous two seasons. The man in the middle of that defense, Alex Singleton, has been a huge part of that rise. Through the month of October, Singleton has one game where he didn’t log double-digit tackles in a game. But even more, his quarterback pressures have jump significantly over that span too. For that, he has been named October’s AFC Defensive Player of the Month! Went to work in October. RT to congratulate @alexsingleton49 on being named AFC Defensive Player of the Month! 👏 pic.twitter.com/kEd0oYeT1e — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 5, 2026 Let’s recap his October stats: Week 4 vs 49ers: 14 total tackles, 1 TFL Week 5 vs Chargers: 8 total tackles, 1 TFL Week 6 vs Seahawks: 13 total tackles, 1 TFL, 2 QBHits Week 7 vs Cardinals: 19 total tackles, 1 TFL, 2 QBHits, 1 Sack He hasn’t slowed down either. He just finished against the Chiefs with 14 total tackles, 1 TFL, 1 QBHit, 1 Sack, and 1 PD. He is leading the league in total tackles too by a wide margin with 101 total tackles. Second place is all the way back to 82. Singleton has been in beast mode out there. Singleton becomes the first player since Pat Surtain II in 2024 to be awarded AFC Defensive Player of the Month. Von Miller has the most of those awards — by far — with four. Champ Bailey is second with two. Alex Singleton On being named AFC Defensive Player of the Month for the first time “It’s sick. It’s cool. Obviously it’s not just me, it’s everyone else on our defense. I’ve said all the time, it’s a privilege to just get to be around the 10 other guys on the field, and then ‘VJ’ (Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph), [Inside Linebackers Coach Jeff] Schmedding, all those guys that really put in all the hours and all the work. It’s awesome. It’s really cool.” On what Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph’s support and confidence in him means “It’s everything. I would assume he’s probably 99 percent of the reason I’m here, maybe if not more than that. So yes, to have him say that, it means everything because he means so much to my career. So to have his support is everything.” On how he evaluates the quality of a tackle “It depends when they are, where they are in a game, situations, all that stuff. I’ve said, I told you guys two weeks ago, the Kansas City game in Week 1 is a lot of cleaning up stuff, and then you’re just getting them. I would say the last seven weeks, our entire defense, it’s just every tackle’s been a guy making a play. There haven’t been a lot of mistakes that we’ve made in the last two months. So it’s just a lot of making plays. So then those are good ones.”

title: Broncos vs. Panthers: 3 Things to Watch in Week 9
summary: The Denver Broncos have a chance to notch their seventh victory of the season on Sunday. The Carolina Panthers stand in the way of the Broncos becoming winners of five in a row. Here are three storylines I’ll be watching closely in Denver’s Week 9 matchup. Who gets the lead role in the Broncos’ backfield? […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: J.K. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos after defeating the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have a chance to notch their seventh victory of the season on Sunday. The Carolina Panthers stand in the way of the Broncos becoming winners of five in a row. Here are three storylines I’ll be watching closely in Denver’s Week 9 matchup. Who gets the lead role in the Broncos’ backfield? Earlier this morning, I gave my thoughts on how the Broncos can beat the Panthers. My first major point was getting the run game going. The Panthers have a bottom 5 run defense in the National Football League and it’s clearly their biggest weakness as a team. I think the Broncos will try and take advantage of this. However, I’ll be interested to see how the carries shake out for the Broncos. Without RJ Harvey, the Broncos three-headed rushing attack is down to just J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman. In the second half of the Chiefs game, Dobbins was virtually absent from the field. Coleman dominated the second half playing time and went on to notch 104 all-purpose yards, a touchdown, and had several big plays that helped guide the Broncos to a huge victory. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton was asked whether or not the Broncos are trying to manage Dobbins’ workload. Payton seemed to imply that the media and fans are making a bigger deal of his second half absence versus the Chiefs than anyone inside Dove Valley is. “He’s a huge part of what we’re doing. Each week we look at—a lot of times who’s the back that’s in there with the hot hand. But he’s been fantastic. To answer your question: No, that’s not a hot button topic with us here. It might be with you guys, but not with us. We’re good. We’re good with the rotation,” stated Payton. Dobbins has carried the ball 94 times this season for 306 yards and 3 touchdowns. His 3.3 yard per carry average is the second worst of any running back in the NFL who has at least 90 carries on the season. While Coleman’s body of work is limited, it’s quite obvious he is the ‘hot hand’ in Denver’s group of running backs and should be in store for more carries. Payton has always said it’s easier to gameplan for two running backs as opposed to three. With that in mind, I’m quite curious to see who ends up getting a majority of the work in the ground game versus the Panthers. Will it be an even split or will one back prevail as the clear-cut favorite? Will rookie Tyler Onyedim see his first action of the season? The Broncos were able to come away with a big victory last week against the Chiefs. Unfortunately, several players exited the game with injury and may not be able to go versus the Panthers on Sunday. Those would be cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, safety Brandon Jones, and defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike. None of them participated in yesterday’s practice session . If Uwazurike isn’t able to go, that would a big loss for the Broncos. He has been a big part of their defensive line rotation this season and has the third most snaps behind Zach Allen and Malcolm Roach. However, his potential absence would provide rookie third-round draft selection Tyler Onyedim with a path to see his first action of the season. Onyedim has been a healthy scratch in every game thus far. The Broncos’ depth at the position is a big reason why. While I wouldn’t expect him to get a bunch of snaps, I am excited at the prospect of him getting his first reps of the season. Denver has embraced the next-man up philosophy numerous times over the past few seasons. If he does play, I’m hoping he can show some flashes in his regular season NFL debut. Can Bo Nix continue to build upon his success the past two weeks? The Broncos have a shot to be 7-2 before the bye. I consider that quite the accomplishment considering how inconsistent their offense has been. It’s even more impressive when you factor in the tough slate of opponents they have faced in the first half of the season. Just how good Denver can become on offense will likely determine how far they can go this season. As of right now, it’s certainly not a Super Bowl caliber offense. Even so, quarterback Bo Nix has made some great strides the past few weeks. They weren’t big-time games statistic wise, but there is a lot to be excited about. The Panthers’ run defense is suspect, but they enter Sunday’s matchup being a Top 10 unit in several aspects against the pass . They rank high in completion percentage allowed, passing yards per game, yards per attempt, and touchdowns. That came as a surprise to me, especially since they don’t have a lot of top-notch players in their secondary. However, they have really struggled to get after opposing quarterbacks. Carolina ranks in the bottom 5 in the NFL with just 11 sacks on the season. Not only that, but they are banged up in the defensive backfield and could be down one of their starters on the boundary. Those issues may give Nix and Denver’s aerial attack enough of an advantage to finally take flight. If the Broncos’ offensive line can hold up and give him time to through, I think Nix is poised to have one of his best games to date. At the midway point the past two seasons, things really began to click for him. I’m hoping Sunday is the best performance we witness from Nix thus far and a sign of greater things to come in the second half of the season.

title: How the Denver Broncos can beat the Carolina Panthers
summary: The Denver Broncos sit atop the AFC West with a 6-2 record. On Sunday, the Broncos will battle the Carolina Panthers who are 3-4 and in first place of the NFC South for their Week 9 matchup. Denver has momentum entering the game being winners of four in a row, whilst Carolina has dropped back-to-back […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos sit atop the AFC West with a 6-2 record. On Sunday, the Broncos will battle the Carolina Panthers who are 3-4 and in first place of the NFC South for their Week 9 matchup. Denver has momentum entering the game being winners of four in a row, whilst Carolina has dropped back-to-back games. Here are three ways I think the Broncos can earn their seventh victory of the season. Ride the running attack and give Jonah Coleman more opportunities Last season, Denver had an effective running game in the first half of the season. Unfortunately, it tapered off greatly after J.K. Dobbins was injured. This year, Denver has experienced the opposite. It’s been a relatively slow start for them establishing the run, but injuries have played a part in that this year too. While Denver’s current stable of backs isn’t completely 100-percent health-wise, I think there is a huge opportunity here to revitalize their run game on Sunday. Why? Because the Panthers have one of the worst run defenses in the National Football League. It’s clearly a giant weakness for the Carolina. They are allowing nearly 5 yards per carry. Moreover, they’ve been dreadful in four of seven games with respect to rushing yards. They gave up 291 on the ground to the Chicago Bears, 258 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 157 to the Atlanta Falcons, and 132 to the Cleveland Browns. I’d love to see a healthy dose of Jonah Coleman in this game. The rookie running back has looked good in his limited opportunities and deserves a majority of the carriers moving forward. It’s a road game, so dictating the pace of it will be essential, and enforcing a consistent rushing attack is key to that. Whether or not the Broncos will be buyers at the trade deadline remains to be seen. However, the more opportunities Coleman gets, the easier the evaluation process for him as a player gets. And in turn, would help answer whether or not the franchise needs to trade off quality draft capital to add to the room prior to November 10th. Rev up the pass rush and rattle Bryce Young Believe it or not, the Panthers enter Sunday’s matchup as a Top 10 offense in the National Football League. Quarterback Bryce Young has played a big part in that. He has thrown for 1,921 yards, 13 touchdowns, and has just 5 interceptions thus far in his fourth season leading their offense. Young sported a few hot games to start the season. However, he has struggled recently. The former top-pick has 3 interceptions and just 2 touchdowns in their back-to-back losses. His accuracy has also experienced a big drop-off—completing less than 57-percent of passes the past three games. In 2025, Young was one of the least sacked quarterbacks in the NFL with just 27. In seven games, he has already been sacked 23 times. The crazy part? Eleven of those have come in the past two games alone. Knowing that, this seems like a prime week for Denver’s defensive trenches to rev up the pass rush. If they can rattle and get after Young early and often, they’ll have a great shot at winning. The Broncos have to start converting on third down The Broncos are a 6-2 football team despite struggling in many key areas. One major issue for them since Week 1 has been their inability to convert on third down. The Broncos are now dead last in the NFL with under a 30-percent conversion rate. It’s true Denver has faced some really good defenses. However, that isn’t an excuse for their poor play in this regard. This is arguably the biggest area the Broncos have to improve upon as they gear up for Sunday’s matchup—as well as the second half stretch of the season after their bye week. The Panthers have a bottom 5 third down defense in the NFL. Opposing teams are converting 46-percent of third downs against them each week. Head Coach Sean Payton, quarterback Bo Nix, and the rest of the offense need to find a way to sustain drives and move the field on third down. Last season, Courtland Sutton was the go-to guy if Denver needed to move the chains. Perhaps this weekend the Broncos make the savvy veteran their main target in the passing attack when they need a big play. He has been clutch through his career in that aspect. If not, who on offense can step up and be that player?

title: NFL picks and predictions: Broncos vs. Panthers and the rest of Week 9
summary: Welcome back to the ninth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. My Week 8 slate of predictions was my best thus far. I finished with a 12-2 record with my only losing picks being the Cowboys and Seahawks. Not too shabby! We’re basically at the halfway point of the season, so […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the ninth installment of Hart’s Picks for the 2026 NFL regular season. My Week 8 slate of predictions was my best thus far. I finished with a 12-2 record with my only losing picks being the Cowboys and Seahawks. Not too shabby! We’re basically at the halfway point of the season, so I thought I’d give a review of where I stand to date. Week 1: 11-5 Week 2: 10-6 Week 3: 9-7 Week 4: 8-8 Week 5: 10-5 Week 6: 7-7 Week 7: 9-5 Week 8: 12-2 Thus far, that’s 76 correct picks and 46 wrong picks. That’s good enough for 63-percent accuracy. However, that is still several points behind where I have been the past two seasons. This week there are 15 games with just the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans on their bye week. Jacksonville Jaguars at Baltimore Ravens — Thursday Night Football With Lamar Jackson likely out for the rest of the regular season due to a broken thumb and Tyler Huntley being on injured reserve, the Ravens will be starting Joe Fagnano against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football . However, they did strike a trade to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals to keep their playoff hopes alive. That won’t matter this week, since he won’t be playing. Due to an unstable quarterback situation in Baltimore, I’ll be giving Jacksonville the edge here. Winner: Jaguars Cincinnati Bengals at Atlanta Falcons — Sunday (Morning Game) This will be an international affair taking place in Madrid, Spain. The Bengals are coming off an overtime win against the Titans. Meanwhile, the Falcons were shutout by the Buccaneers in a game where Tampa Bay didn’t even complete a pass to win. All things considered, I’ll be taking Cincinnati in this one. I think they will light up the scoreboard. Winner: Bengals Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints — Sunday (Early Game) The Browns are coming off a loss, and the Saints are fresh off their bye week with an extra week of rest and preparation. The key storyline to watch in this one is who starts at quarterback for Cleveland. Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol, which mean Shadeur Sanders could get the nod on Sunday. If so, I’m worried about Cleveland’s ability to get things done on offense. I’ll be taking the Saints at home in this one due to that. Winner: Saints New York Jets at Kansas City Chiefs — Sunday (Early Game) Both of these teams are coming off Week 8 losses. I’m far more confident in Andy Reid and the Chiefs’ ability to bounce back from a loss at home as opposed to the Jets being able to find a way to win at Arrowhead. Sorry Jets fans, but I’m picking Kansas City in this one. But hey, you have three top ten picks currently in the 2027 NFL Draft. That’s something to look forward too—unless most of the top underclassmen at QB opt to go back to school. Winner: Chiefs Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders — Sunday (Early Game) Both these NFC teams earned wins in Week 8. The Rams have now pulled to 4-4 on the season and aren’t out of it yet. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 2-4-1 and a few games out of the lead in the NFC East. At the end of the day, I think the Rams are the much better team and will find a way to win on the road. It’s an absolute must to keep their playoff hopes alive in a tough NFC. Winner: Rams Dallas Cowboys at Indianapolis Colts — Sunday (Early Game) The Cowboys and Colts have certainly underwhelmed thus far. Both teams have failed to meet the expectations many fans and analysts had prior to the regular season. If Dallas wants to keep their playoff hopes and NFC East title chances alive, this is a must-win road game against the Colts who seem determined to acquire as much draft capital as possible to embark on a complete rebuild. I’ll be taking another road team and am picking Dallas. Winner: Cowboys Detroit Lions at Miami Dolphins — Sunday (Early Game) Each week, there seems to be a game I think is a surefire win that winds up backfiring on me. Looking at this week’s slate of games, this is about as close to an easy pick for a matchup I can find. I think the Lions roll on offense and cause a lot of problems for a Dolphins’ defense that is one of the worst in the NFL. Winner: Lions Denver Broncos at Carolina Panthers — Sunday (Early Game) They haven’t been playing their best football, but the Broncos continue to find ways to win. They have a four-game winning streak and all the momentum heading into their Week 9 road matchup versus the Panthers. I think Denver’s offense will run the ball with authority and dictate the pace of the game to earn their seventh win of the season on Sunday. Winner: Broncos New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles — Sunday (Early Game) The Eagles have been an absolute flop this season and have lost six in a row. Meanwhile, the Giants have been one of the league’s surprise teams and lead the NFC East. It hasn’t always been pretty, but they’ve been finding ways to win and are pretty balanced on offense and defense. I’m getting a bit wild here picking road teams, but I like the Giants in this one. Winner: Giants Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Texans are a bad football team at 2-5. There is no doubt they have woefully underperformed expectations. Quite honestly, the only other team in AFC that has been more disappointing are the winless Chargers at 0-7. I expect the Texans to get back on track here and take care of business on the road since the Chargers are terrible. Winners: Texans Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Raiders are back to being a .500 ball cup. On the flip side, the 49ers had an extra week of preparation after their Week 7 loss to the Falcons to gameplan for the Raiders. I think that is going to make all the difference here. I just don’t see them dropping another game to an underdog. I’ll take Kyle Shanahan’s crew. Winner: 49ers Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots — Sunday (Afternoon Game) This is one of my favorite matchups of Week 9. The Packers and Patriots are both 5-3 and coming off Week 8 victories. I feel they are evenly matched. It could definitely go either way, though I’ll be giving the Patriots the nod here because of their homefield advantage. Winner: Patriots Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks — Sunday (Afternoon Game) The Cardinals were able to shock the Cowboys last weekend. I honestly didn’t see that coming. Meanwhile, the Seahawks lost to the Bears in primetime—the other matchup I failed to get right last week. At 4-4, the Seahawks are starting to slip in the NFC West. They need this victory to get back on the right track. I’m confident they will pull out a victory at home. But Sam Darnold needs to perform better, and they have to start running the ball effectively. Winner: Seahawks Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Chicago Bears — Sunday Night Football The Buccaneers may have been able to pull off a win last weekend without completing a pass. However, they are going to have to be firing on all cylinders to keep up with a top-notch Chicago offense. I’m not sure that’s possible. Caleb Williams is really hitting his stride and playing well. I think Chicago won’t have any issues beating Tampa Bay at home. Winner: Bears Buffalo Bills at Minnesota Vikings — Monday Night Football The Vikings were the last unbeaten team in the NFL until the Lions beat them last weekend. The Bills were able to obliterate the Ravens and are now 6-1 and the top team in the AFC. I’m excited to see how Brian Flores tries to combat Josh Allen and the Bills’ offense. That’ll be great to see in primetime. Though I remain confident Allen and the Bills can do enough to win on the road in Minneapolis. Winner: Bills

title: Broncos focused on taking care of business against Panthers
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos have gone through their fair share of ups and downs to start their 2026 gridiron campaign. Nevertheless, the team touts a 6-2 record and has continued its penchant for gutting out close games and embarking on miraculous fourth quarter comebacks. This Sunday, the Broncos will battle the Carolina […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Alex Singleton #49 and Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos celebrate after the final play of the game in their team's 28-24 win against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos have gone through their fair share of ups and downs to start their 2026 gridiron campaign. Nevertheless, the team touts a 6-2 record and has continued its penchant for gutting out close games and embarking on miraculous fourth quarter comebacks. This Sunday, the Broncos will battle the Carolina Panthers. Carolina are currently the leaders of the NFC South despite a 3-4 record. Some have pegged this as a “trap” game . Though yesterday after practice, quarterback Bo Nix dismissed that notion. He chimed in about the importance of their Week 9 matchup versus the Panthers and how Denver has gotten so good at being able to refocus after big wins. “It starts with Coach. Coach Payton is really good at that. He talks about every game in the NFL is an important game. There’s no such thing as a trap game because they’re all that way. They’re all must-wins. If you don’t play well, you’re going to end up messing around and getting beat,” stated Nix. “We know the importance of this week right before the Bye Week. We can’t go on a Bye early. This is a really important game for where we want to go. As captains and as leaders, it’s just all about practice. Details have to go up a notch, as if it isn’t already. More attention to detail, more communication. If you do everything a little bit more and maximize your time this week, I think we’ll be in a good spot.” The Broncos are the top team in the AFC West. They currently hold the second seed in the AFC playoff race thanks to performing better than the Pittsburgh Steelers, who are also 6-2, in conference games. Eight teams in the conference have at least five wins. For the first half of the season, I certainly didn’t imagine things being this close across the board. Nix is right. Denver’s Week 9 matchup is extremely important. Going into the bye riding a five-game winning streak and being 7-2 is a lot better than the alternative. Even though the Panthers are losers of two in a row and struggling on both sides of the ball, the Broncos can’t afford to underestimate them. They’ve proven to be a consistent offense that is Top 10 in many metrics. Carolina has a strong running game and quarterback Bryce Young has done a great job getting numerous players involved in the passing game. Denver’s defense will have to find a way to limit their impact. Meanwhile, the offense will have to continue to get better. We’ve seen some promise and flashes from Nix the past two games. Yet there is still much work to be done and plenty of room for improvement. He noted that getting better on third downs while continuing to maximize their opportunities in the red zone will be critical to achieve a victory on Sunday. If they can do that, Denver is going to be in a great position heading into their bye. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .
