title: Colts reportedly have received enticing trade offer for remaining starting veteran defensive tackle
summary: According to The 33rd Team NFL Insider Ari Meirov, the Indianapolis Colts have received a better trade offer for veteran starting nose tackle Grover Stewart than they did for his former interior teammate DeForest Buckner: For reference, Buckner was traded to the San Francisco 49ers early last week for their 2027 4th round pick, which […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 13: Grover Stewart #90 of the Indianapolis Colts reacts following the 41-23 loss against the Baltimore Ravens at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to The 33rd Team NFL Insider Ari Meirov, the Indianapolis Colts have received a better trade offer for veteran starting nose tackle Grover Stewart than they did for his former interior teammate DeForest Buckner: I can confidently say they’ve already been offered more for Grover Stewart than they got for Buckner. — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 5, 2026 For reference, Buckner was traded to the San Francisco 49ers early last week for their 2027 4th round pick, which presumably means that Indianapolis can either acquire a 4th round pick that’s from an NFL suitor worse than the 49ers (6-1), or perhaps, although it would be surprising, there could be a potential 3rd round pick. I would realistically heavily lean much towards the former, given Stewart’s age, play, position, and pending free agency. While it’s arguable that the Colts failed to maximize Buckner’s true trade value (*especially in light of the ensuing Jeffery Simmons trade), by doing him and his family a solid by dealing him back to the franchise that drafted him as a first rounder back in 2016, and with whom he played his first four seasons for prior to being traded to Indianapolis, it would still be surprising to see Stewart garner more draft compensation, all things considered. As a looming free agent at 33-years-old, Stewart is your typical one dimensional run stuffing nose tackle, and has had a bit of a down season for his normally high standards. That being said, it’s highly possible that a change of scenery to a playoff hopeful and defensive tackle needy team could bring out some vintage ‘Big Grove’ out of the gates for the season’s final stretch run. On the season, Stewart has 26 tackles (8 solo), 2 tackles for loss, 0.5 sacks, and a pass defensed during all 8 starts during the 2026 campaign. Stewart has long been a personal favorite of Colts team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon, much like star running back Jonathan Taylor remains for that matter—which could make him especially difficult to part with on a personal level and regarding his longstanding veteran leadership in the Indianapolis locker room. That being said, if they could get a 3rd or 4th round pick for Stewart, then that’s a move the franchise should make, as he’s getting a bit long in the tooth at defensive tackle and doesn’t factor into the team’s long-term plans, especially with an ongoing rebuild realistically taking at least the next 2-3 seasons—if all goes according to plan.
author: Luke Schultheis

title: Colts reportedly still hoping for ‘Christian McCaffrey-esque’ trade package for Jonathan Taylor
summary: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the Indianapolis Colts remain at a standstill regarding trading their star running back Jonathan Taylor. The Colts are hoping for a ‘Christian McCaffrey-esque’ trade capital return to actually move Taylor, which for historical reference, was between the Carolina Panthers and San Francisco 49ers on October 20, 2022, and netted […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, the Indianapolis Colts remain at a standstill regarding trading their star running back Jonathan Taylor. The Colts are hoping for a ‘Christian McCaffrey-esque’ trade capital return to actually move Taylor, which for historical reference, was between the Carolina Panthers and San Francisco 49ers on October 20, 2022, and netted the Panthers the 49ers’ following picks: 2023 2nd round, 2o23 third round, 2023 forth round, and 2024 5th round pick: “Where we’re at is essentially where we’ve been, which is several teams interested in Taylor,” said Rapoport on GMFB on Thursday morning . “Willing to offer a significant pick package, but maybe not quite what Ed Dodds, who is running personnel now in place of Chris Ballard, who was fired, wants, and what the organization wants.” “They want a Christian McCaffrey type package for Jonathan Taylor. It’s clear they don’t have it yet. Obviously, they would’ve already made the trade.” “The other part of this thing is, this is not really someone they want to trade. This is someone they believe is a big part of their future. They’d like to build around him. So it would take a big package to get the Colts to move on from him.” There’s been some school of thought that the Colts could even be coveting a first round pick to actually part with Taylor, who team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon potentially considers a major cornerstone of the recently jumpstarted rebuild—regardless of who the next general manager is for the franchise. That would make a great deal of sense, given that Indianapolis is without its 2027 first round pick, which unfortunately looks like a possible Top 5 pick now and belongs to the New York Jets due to last year’s trade deadline Sauce Gardner deal. At any rate, it doesn’t appear as though the Colts ideal asking price has been quite met . . . yet. However, with Indianapolis reportedly holding out until closer to the trade deadline early next week to maximize Taylor’s trade return, it’s possible a very interested suitor could potentially cave and meet their significant asking price to win the Taylor trade sweepstakes over competitors. To me, some of this seems like some posturing by the Colts though—although I applaud them for holding out hope of maximizing Taylor trade return until closer to the trade deadline, given they arguably didn’t get full trade value return on either DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson earlier last week. Taylor has been one of the Colts best running backs in franchise history, as he’s second to only franchise leader Edgerrin James in rushing yards (2,208) and carries (1,699) but is the Horseshoe’s all-time leader in rushing touchdowns with 77 respectively. That being said, he turns 28-years-old in January, and while he’s been a great player for the franchise, remains a strong Ring of Honor candidate, and is on a Hall of Fame track, NFL running backs typically do not age gracefully into their early 30’s—meaning Taylor may only have 2-3 elite years left. That’s realistically the same amount of time it takes to complete a successful rebuild for a franchise—if all actually goes according to plan. For what it’s worth, Rapoport also noted that the Colts are holding out hope for either a 3rd or 4th round pick for starting slot wide receiver Josh Downs, who’s a pending free agent that requested a trade from Indianapolis earlier last week and has drawn interest from at least a handful of wideout needy teams.

But the belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs the… https://t.co/R9AJq2MRRR pic.twitter.com/1p08ZP9gIi — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 5, 2026 There’s been some reported thought and speculation around the industry that the Colts potentially moved too quickly on trading two of their veteran pillars, Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner earlier last week, and did not possibly maximize the full trade return of either longtime organizational standout respectively. All of whom have appeared to garner trade interest, albeit to different levels of possible received compensation, from prospective suitors. The NFL’s trade deadline is Tuesday, November 10th, at 4 PM EST. In particular, Taylor projects to garner a significant return in draft capital, but there’s increased speculation around league circles that the Colts are hoping for at least a “Christian McCaffrey” trade haul coming back to Indianapolis, if not, at least a first round pick entirely. To me, it makes sense for the Colts to hold out for better draft capital if they haven’t received the offer they’ve ideally wanted for each of their respective readily available players. The offers they have already received figure to largely still be there early next week, as they’re the major trade seller dictating this year’s trade deadline activity—with other teams reacting and following suit.

title: The Jets will have the last laugh on the Colts
summary: As this season continues to spiral, the effects are currently being felt. All of the losing has cost the Indianapolis Colts two of their franchise pillars. More could fall soon. The losing is taking its toll on fans and players alike. Sometimes there is a silver lining, though. The good thing is that it’s true […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Sauce Gardner #1 of the Indianapolis Colts arrives prior to an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As this season continues to spiral, the effects are currently being felt. All of the losing has cost the Indianapolis Colts two of their franchise pillars. More could fall soon. The losing is taking its toll on fans and players alike. Sometimes there is a silver lining, though. The good thing is that it’s true in this case. The bad thing is that silver lining belongs to the New York Jets. Two first-round picks were surrendered for Sauce Gardner. Two. The first one was felt as the Colts dropped from Super Bowl contention and into the middle of the draft. That is pain most can live with. It’s this year’s lingering pain that has carried over and is making this dreadful season that much worse to watch. Instead of the Colts anticipating a potential top-ten pick in the first round of the draft, the Jets are sitting pretty at fourth overall. You can’t have a rainbow without the rain, and sometimes there is a pot of gold at the end of that rainbow. That isn’t the case for the Colts this year. Normally, pain is rewarded with a great opportunity to start fresh, gather new cornerstones to build your franchise out of the ashes. Yes, the Colts, with whatever horrific record they finish, will still have good positioning in subsequent rounds, but that lack of a first-round selection could haunt them. Let’s not even talk about the return. As good as Gardner can be, he has missed way too much time in his short stint with the Colts to be deemed worthy of the trade. Oh, and what did the Colts throw in at the end? Adonai Mitchell. He seems to be having a bit of a resurgence after getting into Shane Steichen’s doghouse and being a throw away piece. Seeing any success he has is also a tough watch. These are the stings that can stick with a franchise for a long time. If it all holds, not having the fourth overall pick is going to make some people sick. It has already cost some their jobs. That will only compound the issue. If the Jets select a Hall of Fame player with that selection, look out. This is the state of the Colts, and the Jets will be laughing all the way to the bank

title: Jaguars Defense Drowns Ravens in Rainy Baltimore
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars weathered the storm in Baltimore, and the Ravens had no answer for the elements or Anthony Campanile’s defense. In a rainy Thursday night showdown, Jacksonville completely smothered Baltimore, turning a hostile road environment into a blowout victory. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 9 33-10 road win over the […]
full_text: Jacksonville Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile looks on before an NFL football matchup at EverBank Stadium on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026, in Jacksonville, Fla. The Jaguars defeated the Browns 34-10. [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union] | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Jacksonville Jaguars weathered the storm in Baltimore, and the Ravens had no answer for the elements or Anthony Campanile’s defense. In a rainy Thursday night showdown, Jacksonville completely smothered Baltimore, turning a hostile road environment into a blowout victory. Here’s everything you need to know from Jacksonville’s Week 9 33-10 road win over the Baltimore Ravens. Favorite Highlight: Mr. Consensus Boards, tight end Nate Boerkircher, adjusting on the fly to Trevor Lawrence’s extended scramble, was exactly what Jacksonville needed to get the game started early. Boerkircher with a great adjustment for 52 yards, pic.twitter.com/ICvAg2otKI — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) November 6, 2026 Post-game notables: Taking The Show on the Road After three home blowout victories in the 2026 season, the Jacksonville Jaguars put together their first multi-score victory away from Duval County. A looming question heading into this matchup was whether Liam Coen’s squad could replicate their clear home dominance (+85-point win differential) when on the road. On Thursday, they answered this call, and then some. Turnover Party Anthony Campanile’s defense dominated rookie undrafted free agent quarterback Joe Fagnano in a clear way, limiting the Baltimore quarterback to 60 total passing yards, sacking him once, forcing two interceptions, and allowing no touchdowns (a 22.7 passer rating). Notably, a passer rating for simply hiking and spiking the ball earns a 39.6. To put this performance in context: Baltimore wide receiver Zay Flowers caught just one more Fagnano pass attempt than the Jacksonville defense. Additionally, Jacksonville has allowed just 10 first-quarter points this season, fewest in the NFL. Liam Coen’s Continued Dominance As noted by Jaguars on SI’s John Shipley, since 2024, Liam Coen offenses have averaged 36 points per game when facing defenses run by Jesse Minter. The 2024 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with Coen as the offensive coordinator, scored 40 points; Jacksonville scored 35 against the Chargers in Week 11 of 2025; the team scored 33 on Thursday. Tight Ends Matter The Jacksonville tight end room combined for 6 catches for 98 yards on Sunday, in a dominant showing of offensive versatility. Nate Boerkircher – 2 catches for 61 yards Brenton Strange – 2 catches for 22 yards Tanner Koziol – 2 catches for 15 yards In Case You Missed It The Jacksonville offense opened the matchup with back-to-back scoring drives: an opening 7-play, 77-yard drive capped by a one-yard Bhayshul Tuten score, followed by a 10-play, 47-yard drive that ended with a 36-yard Cam Little attempt to retain a seven-point lead. Ravens’ third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano, in his first NFL start, clearly played second fiddle to running back Derek Henry early on in the rainy Baltimore night. With the Ravens leaning on a package of Wildcat offense, read options, and quick game offense, the Baltimore offense played a disciplined, ball control, first half offense. However, the offensive limitations were clear. Anthony Campanile’s defense held Baltimore to 2 of 6 on third down (30%) with a 3.3 yard average per play. Great disguised blitz with Jarrian Jones forcing a Ravens punt pic.twitter.com/zhnIc9ObRW — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) November 6, 2026 However, the Baltimore defensive dam finally broke via an explosive, 50-yard touchdown, as Lawrence found Parker Washington streaking across the middle to kick off the rout. PARKER WASHINGTON TO THE CRIB. JAXvsBAL on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/M79mYxS3b2 — NFL (@NFL) November 6, 2026 Halftime Stats: Score: 17-3 Time of possession: 17:31 to 12:29 Baltimore Third Down Defense: 2/7 (28.6%) Defensive Sacks: 1 to 0 Jacksonville Rushing yards: 76 to 26 Baltimore Passing yards: 197 to 25 Jacksonville Redzone Offense: 1/2 (50%) Jacksonville to 0% (0 attempts for Baltimore) QB Trevor Lawrence ended the half 9/15 for 197 yards and a touchdown (126.4 passer rating), while RB Bhayshul Tuten had 8 carries for 22 yards and a touchdown. Following the half, the Jacksonville defense continued their early dominance, forcing the game’s first turnover on the series, as Montaric Brown secured a diving throw from Fagnano, which resulted in a 45-yard field goal. Jaguars with seven guys on the line of scrimmage forces the rookie qb to make a mistake. Montaric Brown gets himself a pick pic.twitter.com/vdwgBgQgO5 — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) November 6, 2026 Campanile’s defense refused to let up, securing another turnover on the following drive with Jourdan Lewis bringing in the diving interception. Jourdan Lewis: another #Jaguars INT pic.twitter.com/xhY6qqeV7U — Daniel Griffis (@DanDGriffis) November 6, 2026 With the game falling out of reach, Jacksonville poured it on, with Jalen McLeod securing a fumble on the following kickoff, leading to a Chris Rodriguez touchdown. Linebacker Foye Oluokun secured the game’s only sack, while wide receiver Travis Hunter surrendered Jacksonville’s lone turnover, a third-quarter fumble. However, the defense held Baltimore without points following the turnover, turning it over on downs. Game balls: Special Teams : K Cam Little – Four field goals in the rain, with a long of 47 (3/3 on extra points) Defense : DC Anthony Campanile – 4/14 on third downs (28.6%); two defensive turnovers, and less than 60 net passing yards (unit award) Offense : QB Trevor Lawrence – 16/26 for 242 yards, 1 touchdown (105.0 passer rating) View the full box score here Pre-Game Inactives For the Jaguars: DE Wesley Williams WR CJ Williams CB Alijah Huzzie S Cam’Ron Silmon-Craig For Baltimore: S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) CB Nate Wiggins (stinger/illness) QB Kedon Slovis (Emergency QB) WR Elijah Sarratt G Emery Jones DL Aeneas Peebles In-Game Injuries None Live blog: Recap each of the big plays from tonight’s game in our live blog ! A blowout win with no injuries makes for a great, long weekend for Duval! What are your thoughts from tonight’s game, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments!

title: AFC Playoff Picture: Jaguars move up after squashing Ravens
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars won on Thursday night and moved up in the AFC standings. With the Pittsburgh Steelers on a bye, the Jags’ position will be at least third by the end of the weekend, and they can move into second and a tie for first place if everything goes their way. Let’s not get […]
full_text: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars won on Thursday night and moved up in the AFC standings. With the Pittsburgh Steelers on a bye, the Jags’ position will be at least third by the end of the weekend, and they can move into second and a tie for first place if everything goes their way. Let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves. Here are the standings as we stand now, then we will get into the rest of the weekend. AFC playoff standings after the Jaguars win 1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) 2. Denver Broncos (6-2, 3-1 AFC) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, 5-2) 4. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, 3-2 AFC) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (5-2, 5-1 AFC) 6. Cincinnati Bengals (5-2, 4-2 AFC) 7. New England Patriots (5-3, 5-1 AFC) 8. Cleveland Browns (5-3, 3-3 AFC) 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5) 11. Houston Texans (2-5) 12. New York Jets (2-6, 2-3 AFC) 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-6, 1-5 AFC) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-6) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) Explaining the 6-2 tiebreaker between the Jaguars, Steelers, and Broncos The Jaguars, Broncos, and Steelers all go in together and while they will all play each other eventually, that hasn’t happened so we skip the head-to-head-to-head tiebreaker. The tiebreaker moves to conference record where the 3-1 Broncos best the 5-2 Jaguars and the 3-2 Steelers. Denver is the two seed. The Broncos and Steelers haven’t played each other yet, so the AFC record is applied again here and the 5-2 Jaguars slip ahead of the 3-2 Steelers. Jacksonville is the three seed and Pittsburgh is the four seed. How high in the standings can the Jaguars get before the end of Week 8? The Steelers are on a bye, but the Jaguars are already ahead of them. The Broncos can lose to the Carolina Panthers and fall to 6-3. The Buffalo Bills, though, can’t fall behind Jacksonville. The Bills could lose to the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night to fall into that 6-2 tie, but they are 5-1 in the AFC and that isn’t going to change. The highest the Jaguars can get is second behind Buffalo — for now.

title: NFL predictions: Will Liam Coen school Jesse Minter yet again?
summary: We’re previewing THURSDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL, y’all! Get excited! Here are some predictions for what we’ll see tonight when the 5-2 Jacksonville Jaguars take on the 4-4 Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Prediction #1 The good news is that the Ravens will not have an NFL-caliber quarterback on the field on Thursday night. Two-time MVP […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 28: Head coach Liam Coen of the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during a preseason game at EverBank Field on August 28, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re previewing THURSDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL, y’all! Get excited! Here are some predictions for what we’ll see tonight when the 5-2 Jacksonville Jaguars take on the 4-4 Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Prediction #1 The good news is that the Ravens will not have an NFL-caliber quarterback on the field on Thursday night. Two-time MVP Lamar Jackson (thumb) and familiar backup Tyler “Snoop” Huntley (toe) are both on injured reserve. Baltimore attempted to salvage its season by trading for veteran pocket passer Jacoby Brissett, but he won’t be available for this Week 9 matchup on a short week. The Jaguars will be facing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who posted a 40.0 passer rating in his first NFL action last week. Lucky us. The bad news is that the Ravens still have Derrick Henry. The Yulee native has rushed for the most yards (1,564) and touchdowns (16) of any NFL player against Jacksonville. Henry has six career games of 120+ rushing yards and at least 1 touchdown against the Jaguars. He had that one 99-yard play where he— I don’t need to remind y’all. It’s been 1,033 days since Henry last faced his hometown team (and the same amount of time since he suited up for the Tennessee Titans), but we all know that he’s one of the few non-quarterbacks in the league who can put an offense entirely on his shoulders. This will be the Jaguars’ first matchup against Henry in a Ravens uniform. While Jacksonville will surely miss defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton, Jackson’s absence is a far greater factor. Henry averages 4.5 yards per carry and is stuffed on 16.0% of rushes with Jackson on the field this season, compared to 3.5 yards per carry and a 22.9% stuff rate without Jackson, per NFL Pro. Over the past three weeks, a span in which Jackson played 1 offensive snap, Henry was hit behind the line of scrimmage at the league’s highest rate (60.0%). He averages a league-worst 0.8 yards per carry on such plays this season, compared to 6.2 yards per carry when he is not contacted in the backfield. Even with the Ravens starting an undrafted rookie at quarterback, the Jaguars will need a sound strategy to contain wide receiver Zay Flowers… but the top priority in the defensive game plan this week should be preventing Henry from hitting his stride. The prediction: Derrick Henry gets stuffed repeatedly, finishes with under 50 yards Henry’s rushing over/under prop is set at 68.5 yards on FanDuel. Prediction #2 On the other side of the ball, Jacksonville is as close to full-strength as it can get. Trevor Lawrence is operating the offense at an MVP-caliber level; skill players are taking turns having breakout games; and the offensive line is doing juuuuust fine. The obvious driver of Jacksonville’s success is its head coach and offensive playcaller, Liam Coen. He’s been in a Steph Curry-like flow state for much of the season. The Jaguars have scored 30+ points in four of seven games, including each of their past two outings, and their +85 point differential leads the league by a country mile. Ravens fans would probably like to see their head coach and defensive playcaller, Jesse Minter, be viewed as the defensive version of Coen. A young, innovative mind who can lead a locker room just as well as he can devise a game plan. However, in two career meetings between a Coen offense and a Minter defense, the former coach had far more success. In Week 7 of 2024, Coen called the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ offense, and Minter called the Ravens’ defense (as defensive coordinator). The Bucs converted 12/18 late downs, produced 481 yards of offense, and scored 31 points. In Week 11 of 2025, Coen called the Jaguars’ offense, and Minter called the Los Angeles Chargers’ defense. The Jags converted 8/15 late downs, produced 345 yards of offense, and scored 35 points. Is Minter really going to be the guy to stop this freight train? The prediction: Liam Coen’s offense scores 30 or more points yet again Jacksonville’s team total is set at 24.5 points on FanDuel. Prediction #3 The Jaguars are incentivized to get Brian Thomas Jr. going. As many are quick to point out, the NFL is a “what have you done for me lately?” league. A few good games from Thomas could boost his trade value and convince another team to acquire him for significant draft capital. But the Jaguars should want Thomas to stack strong performances, regardless of their interest in trading him. We’ve all seen what he’s capable of on an NFL field. The best-case scenario for Jacksonville isn’t “Thomas plays well enough that we can trade him for a haul.” The best-case scenario would be “Thomas plays well enough that he refinds his groove and helps make our offense as dangerous as possible.” Both of his touchdowns this season came in the redzone. According to NFL Pro, Thomas has run a deep route on 3.3 plays per game, compared to 5.1 deep routes per game in 2024 and 5.9 in 2025. He only has 3 deep targets this season and has not caught any. This week looks like a good matchup, though. Baltimore’s defense ranks bottom three in completion percentage (65.1%) and EPA per attempt (0.67) allowed on downfield passes. Minter’s unit has also allowed in-breaking passes to be wide open by 5+ yards of separation at a league-worst 24.8% rate. Can we get a deep post from BT, pretty please? The prediction: Brian Thomas Jr. scores his first long touchdown of 2026 Thomas’ receiving over/under prop is set at 12.5 yards on FanDuel. He has +550 odds to score a touchdown. title: Jaguars vs. Ravens: Staff roundtable and game picks for Week 9
summary: Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! This week, we’re previewing the Jacksonville Jaguars’ first primetime game of the season. They went 1-1 on national television when playing in London, but this is Thursday Night Football, baby. The Jags are going up I-95 to take on the Baltimore Ravens in Week 9. Let’s talk about […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - DECEMBER 17: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars throws the ball during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at EverBank Stadium on December 17, 2023 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Big Cat Country’s staff roundtable! This week, we’re previewing the Jacksonville Jaguars’ first primetime game of the season. They went 1-1 on national television when playing in London, but this is Thursday Night Football, baby. The Jags are going up I-95 to take on the Baltimore Ravens in Week 9. Let’s talk about it. Question 1: What’s your top question/concern about the Jaguars this week? Dillon Appleman : Will the run defense remain elite without DaVon Hamilton? Losing D. Ham in the middle of the defense is hard to overstate. He was playing at an elite level and was the unquestioned anchor of the NFL’s top run defense this season. With him out, Matt Dickerson and potentially Albert Regis will be leaned on to help replicate what Hamilton was providing. I’m curious to see how they perform against Derrick Henry. Travis Holmes : Can you perform on the road like you do at home? The Jaguars are 3-0 at EverBank Stadium, outscoring opponents 111-23 following their 35-point demolition of the Indianapolis Colts’ future. However, their 2-2 record away from Duval is hard to overlook, with an 85-88 scoring differential and a noticeable difference in accepted penalties. A loss at Denver, a close win over a severely limited Bengals offense, an improbable London win over the Eagles, and a loss to a previously struggling Texans team all paint the picture of a Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde identity for this 2026 team. Can the Duval version of this team make an appearance elsewhere? Gus Logue : How quickly can the Jaguars build a lead in this game? The only team scoring more 1st half points than Jacksonville (15.7 per game) and Baltimore (15.6) this season is the Buffalo Bills (17.1). Both of these teams tend to get off on the right foot, but in terms of 2nd half scoring, Jacksonville ranks 14th (12.3), and Baltimore ranks 31st (5.9). Late-game catastrophes have become regular for the Ravens, so Jags fans don’t need to panic if the Thursday Night Football scoreboard is close at halftime. That said, it would be great to see Liam Coen’s team jump to an early lead and win comfortably, rather than sweating out another tight game against a backup quarterback. Henry Zimmer : My biggest question for this week is how the Jags will do on a short week on the road. Jacksonville got a little dinged up in the rain against the Colts, so not having the full slate of rest or even a home game could be a cause for a little concern. Question 2: What’s the key to a Jaguars victory this week? Dillon : Considering the QB situation for Baltimore, the key for a Jacksonville Jaguars victory is to force Joey Fagnano to throw the ball. That means preventing Derrick Henry from getting chunk gains on early downs and forcing more third-and-longs than third-and-shorts. Travis : Can Jacksonville box in the Ravens’ run game? Baltimore currently ranks sixth in the league in rushing yards per game (133.5) and eighth in yards per carry (4.6). While the Jaguars rank first in both categories in 2026, those rankings may certainly be impacted by the loss of Davon Hamilton. With a former Jacksonville Jaguars nightmare from his Tennessee Titans days, Derrick Henry licking his chops, this will be our first glimpse of what Anthony Campanile’s run-stopping defense looks like sans Hamilton anchoring the middle. Albert Regis, Matt Dickerson, and Ruke Orhorhoro will certainly be tested Thursday night. Gus : Winning in the trenches. The obvious matchup to watch is Baltimore’s run offense against Jacksonville’s run defense, especially with each unit missing its linchpin player, but the inverse matchup is interesting as well. Can the Jaguars’ offensive line take care of business against Trey Hendrickson, Nnamdi “Justin” Madubuike, Travis Jones, and our old friend Calais Campbell? Given their quarterback situation, the path to a Ravens win on Thursday is narrow, but it would probably involve big games from Derrick Henry and their defensive front. Jacksonville will win by multiple scores if Trevor Lawrence is kept clean. Henry : The Jags should be able to beat whatever quarterback Baltimore throws at them, so stopping the run would be my key. There’s no way Baltimore should be able to throw. They will have to try and establish Derrick Henry against a DaVon Hamilton-less Jaguars defense. Stop the run like you have, and you stop the Baltimore offense in its tracks. Question 3: Who will be an X-factor for the Jaguars this week ? Dillon : My X-factor this week is going to be Ventrell Miller. With the middle of the defense without its anchor, I’m looking for Miller to be the one getting downhill to fill those potential gaps in the run game. Travis : Ladies and gentlemen: Chop wood. Carry water. It’s officially a Parker Washington week. The Baltimore Ravens rank 21st in the league in passing yards allowed per game, having already surrendered 100-plus receiving yards to Drake London, Tee Higgins, CeeDee Lamb, and Carnell Tate. This matchup simply feels like one where the Jaguars could lean heavily into the passing game and worry slightly less about offensive balance, particularly against a Ravens run defense that is surrendering the eighth-fewest yards per carry. With inconsistent cornerback play from Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins, I think Parker Washington is in line for a huge performance. Gus : I’m sorry, but I can’t shut up about Chris Rodriguez Jr., who should not be forgotten even with Bhayshul Tuten stealing the spotlight in the backfield. He’s actually rushed for more yards per carry (4.6 to 4.5) and just as many touchdowns (3 each) so far this season. With Tuten missing three straight practices and carrying a “questionable” injury designation going into Thursday Night Football, this could be the week that Rodriguez’s value to the offense is on full display. Henry : My X-Factor this week is Cam Little. Why Little, you may ask? If this Jaguars offense sputters for one reason or another, it will be on the leg of Little to keep things together. Maybe short week and the travel throws a wrench in the offense, so Little could be called upon more often than not. Final score prediction? Dillon : Jaguars 20, Ravens 10 Travis : Jaguars 32, Ravens 13 Gus : Jaguars 24, Ravens 10 Henry : Jaguars 20, Ravens 10 What are your Week 9 predictions, Jaguars fans? Let us know in the comments! But the Jaguars have significant injuries of their own to manage. Can they continue taking care of business on their quest for the AFC’s No. 1 […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - DECEMBER 17: Travon Walker #44 of the Jacksonville Jaguars celebrates during an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at EverBank Stadium on December 17, 2023 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today, the Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) will take on the Baltimore Ravens (4-4) in Week 9. Can they continue taking care of business on their quest for the AFC’s No. 1 playoff seed? “When you have guys go down, it’s the NFL, nobody cares,” head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday. “Really nobody cares. These guys get paid to do the job and they care about the job. They love doing it. They wouldn’t be doing it otherwise.” “When they understand the expectation, when they have belief in what they’re doing, and the coaches and players and building are able to continue to pour into them, regardless if you’re a starter for every single game, or if you’re a practice squad elevation guy, or if you’re on IR, whatever it is that you’re feeling like you’re in it, you’re involved, you’re a big part of what we’re doing, I think maybe helps guys believe in themselves when they do have to go and step up and give us meaningful reps.” Keep an eye out for rookie defenders Albert Regis and Jalen Huskey as they step into larger roles, as well as Walker Little’s matchup on the blindside against Pro Bowl edge rusher Trey Hendrickson. The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy, claims he owes over $3.45M in debts | ESPN In the filing, Rice claimed to have $677,054 in personal assets, including $421,825 in “deferred compensation.” The filing claims Rice has $13,640 in his checking accounts. He claims to rent a residence and that he does not own any property. Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which is for “individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their debts and who are willing to allow their non-exempt property to be used to pay their creditors,” according to the bankruptcy filing. Rice claimed $39,241 of his personal assets to be nonexempt. The documents claim Rice’s largest creditor is still owed $979,837 as part of a 2025 civil settlement related to the crash. Rice is disputing potential debts in some of the civil trials, including a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit. The NFL trade deadline is nearing. Here’s what the Chiefs need to solve | The Kansas City Star Well, it’s absent again in his absence. A month later, that aforementioned completion in Week 4 against the Raiders remains the most recent time the Chiefs have completed a pass downfield (defined as targeted receiver more than 20 yards beyond the line of scrimmage). They have played three full games without him. In those games, Mahomes is 0 for 5 when targeting a receiver deep into the secondary. Chiefs Announce Legend Kendall Gammon As 2026 Salute to Service Award Nominee | The Mothership Following a 15-year NFL career, Gammon has used his experiences with adversity, mental health challenges and the transition from professional football to connect with veterans navigating similar challenges after military service. “I am truly honored to be nominated as the Kansas City Chiefs representative for the Salute to Service Award,” Gammon said. “It means so much to have the opportunity to support service members, veterans, and their families who have given so much in service to our country. Connecting with Kansas City’s military community has been incredibly meaningful and has allowed me to stay close to Chiefs Kingdom in a special way.” Chris Jones Has an Interesting Explanation for Chiefs’ Frustrating Sack Drought | Sports Illustrated During a media appearance on Wednesday, Jones reiterated why he believes the sacks will eventually come. “It’s all about perspective from my angle. We’ve got 10 games [left], right?” Jones said. “So, continue to chop wood. This year is an awkward year for all of us. Sacks started off slow, but you’ve got to continue to do what you’ve been doing. Eventually, they’re going to start coming, and when they come, they come in bunches.” Jets expected to get star RB back for matchup with Chiefs | KCTV5 New York Jets star running back Breece Hall has been sidelined for weeks due to a quad injury. This week, as his team is poised to come to the Midwest, the Wichita, Kansas, native and Iowa State product is expected to return to action. Hall practiced in full Thursday and is expected to suit up for Sunday’s game between the 2-6 Jets and 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs. It would be Hall’s first game since Week 3 of this season. Around the NF L Trevor Lawrence, Jaguars roll past Ravens. Is Jacksonville now the AFC team to beat? | The Athletic Are the Jaguars the most complete team in the entire AFC right now? Yes. The Jaguars check just about every box you would want in a contender. They didn’t capitalize on as many opportunities as they could have against Baltimore, but they still have an offense that’s capable of scoring on big plays and grinding out tough yards. They have a defense that can get after the quarterback and generate turnovers. Not only do the Jaguars lead the NFL in point margin, they also went into Thursday tied for first with a plus-7 turnover margin. Murray has had a challenging start to the 2026 season — his first in Minnesota. With Murray behind center for the majority of the season, the Vikings’ offense has struggled mightily, ranking 29th in yards gained per game, 31st in passing and 27th in points scored per contest (20). Brandon Aiyuk to return to 49ers’ facility Friday afternoon, reportedly discussing forfeiture of $13 million bonus | Yahoo! Sports In June, Aiyuk continued to publicly ask the team to cut him so he could sign somewhere else, specifically the Washington Commanders. But that wasn’t going to be possible until he was reinstated from the the reserve/left squad, where he landed because he failed to show up for mandatory team activities, including training camp. In a video, the receiver said that he would never step foot in the 49ers’ facility again; he also claimed that he had fired his agent. Now, with Rosenhaus leading Aiyuk’s negotiations, the receiver will hope to finally get his new start elsewhere, assuming the 49ers trade or cut him. Johnson’s 128 receiving yards were the most by an NFL running back in one game this season (and also the only 100-yard receiving-yard game by any back). title: Chiefs sign wide receiver Bub Means to the practice squad
summary: According to Thursday’s NFL Transactions Report, the Kansas City Chiefs have added another receiver to their practice squad. Bub Means, a fifth-round pick of the New Orleans Saints in the 2024 NFL Draft, was listed as a practice-squad transaction for the Chiefs a day after he tried out for a spot. He was one of […]
full_text: (Photo by Derick E. Hingle/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Thursday’s NFL Transactions Report, the Kansas City Chiefs have added another receiver to their practice squad. Bub Means, a fifth-round pick of the New Orleans Saints in the 2024 NFL Draft, was listed as a practice-squad transaction for the Chiefs a day after he tried out for a spot. He was one of nine players Kansas City hosted for tryouts on Wednesday. The Chiefs also signed wide receiver Jacob De Jesus, who spent time with the team this offseason. Listed at 6 feet 2 inches tall and 215 pounds, Means has not played in a regular-season game since his rookie year in New Orleans in 2024, when he appeared in seven games and produced 118 yards and seven first downs over nine receptions. All of his production came in a three-game stretch, Weeks 6-8 of that rookie campaign. He spent 68% of his snaps as an outside receiver during that period with an average depth of target of 12 yards. Rattler to Bub Means. Both of their first TD's pic.twitter.com/MqVkjiur7c — Saints Film Room (@SaintsFilmRoom) October 13, 2024 Means was cut after the preseason this year, then spent time on the Cleveland Browns ‘ practice squad this season. Before he was a fifth-round selection out of the University of Pittsburgh, Means racked up 1,552 yards and 10 touchdowns over two seasons at Pitt and one prior at Louisiana Tech. Means was originally a three-star high school recruit who enrolled at the University of Tennessee. During his last year in college, 42% of Means’ targets were 20 or more yards downfield; he caught 10 passes for 395 yards and five touchdowns on deep throws in 2023, according to Pro Football Focus . At the 2024 NFL Scouting Combine, Means had notable arm length measured at 33 1/4 inches (86th percentile for receivers) and 10 1/8-inch hands (91st percentile). He ran a 4.43-second 40-yard dash with a 10-yard split of 1.55 seconds. He recorded a vertical leap of 39 1/2 inches (88th percentile) and a broad jump of 10 feet 2 inches. The 25-year-old joins Justin Watson and Jacob De Jesus to form a trio of practice-squad receivers for the Chiefs to call up; Andrew Armstrong was signed to the 53-man roster from the practice squad a couple of weeks ago.

full_text: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Each practice day this season, the Kansas City Chiefs release an official injury report ahead of the next game. In Week 9, the Chiefs play the New York Jets on Sunday afternoon. Here is the Chiefs’ first official injury report of the week, courtesy of the team’s official website : Chiefs Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) did not participate in practice for the second consecutive day after suffering the injury early in the Week 8 loss; he walked gingerly to the sideline without stopping the game after taking on an open-field block. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) was a limited participant in practice for the second consecutive day. He has been dealing on and off with the same shoulder injury since training camp. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was a limited participant for the fifth consecutive practice since being designated to return from the Reserve/Injured list; next week is the final week before he must be activated on the 53-man roster. Returner Nikko Remigio (hip) was a full participant in practice Thursday after being limited Wednesday. On Wednesday afternoon, the Chiefs signed rookie returner Jacob De Jesus to the practice squad, seemingly insurance in case Remigio did not make progress. Wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was a full participant in practice on Thursday after being marked as limited on Wednesday. Speaking with local media this week, Rice said he is “100%” ahead of the limited participation in practice on Wednesday. Tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was a full participant in practice on Thursday after being marked as limited on Wednesday. He came up with a limp in his ankle during Week 6, but hasn’t missed any game time since. The following Chiefs players were full participants in practice on Wednesday and Thursday: Linebacker Nick Bolton (neck) Linebacker Drue Tranquill (pectoral) Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) Jets No. 1 wide receiver Garrett Wilson entered concussion protocol on Monday after a helmet-to-helmet hit in Week 8 and did not participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday. He has racked up 527 yards and three touchdowns over 43 receptions this season. Starting defensive tackle Harrison Phillips (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday or Thursday practice. He has 24 tackles, three quarterback hits, and a fumble recovered while playing 57% of the defensive snaps for New York this season. The Jets placed defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat (knee) on the Reserve/Injured list last week. Rookie phenom edge rusher David Bailey (groin) was upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice after being limited Wednesday and missing Week 8. He has 5.5 sacks and seven tackles for loss while playing 81% of the Jets’ defensive snaps. Tight end Mason Taylor (back) was a full participant in Thursday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday; he missed time earlier in the season due to a thumb injury. Starting running back Breece Hall (knee) has been on the IR since Week 3 but could return this week, according to reports; he was a full participant in practice Thursday after limited action on Wednesday. He has 265 total yards and a touchdown this season. His backup, Braelon Allen, has 565 rushing yards and three touchdowns in relief. Rookie safety VJ Payne of Kansas State saw his practice window open for the first time this season after suffering an injury in the preseason.

title: Chiefs defense is looking in the mirror for a ‘killer instinct’
summary: On the first play of the fourth quarter in Week 8, the Kansas City Chiefs converted a third down while leading 24-13 against the Denver Broncos. With a new set of downs and an 11-point lead, it felt like the game — and the AFC West lead — was in the Chiefs’ control. Three plays […]
full_text: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On the first play of the fourth quarter in Week 8, the Kansas City Chiefs converted a third down while leading 24-13 against the Denver Broncos . With a new set of downs and an 11-point lead, it felt like the game — and the AFC West lead — was in the Chiefs’ control. Three plays later, the Chiefs were punting away on fourth and inches, and nothing seemed to go right for Kansas City from there. We know the offense failed to finish the next two drives, both crucial possessions that could’ve put the game in the Chiefs’ favor. However, the defense allowed the Broncos to find their fourth-quarter magic, allowing two touchdowns in just 11 plays on the field. At his press conference on Thursday, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo described the loss as “sickening” before answering questions about the 28-24 defeat. “You have an 11-point lead going into the fourth quarter; the responsibility falls on the defense to make sure you win the game, and we didn’t do that,” Spagnuolo acknowledged. “I know that everyone wanted to score at the end. [Patrick Mahomes] has bailed us out a number of times in the eight years I’ve been here, but we don’t like to put the offense in that situation.” Leading into Denver’s nine-play touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, the Chiefs had forced three consecutive three-and-outs. In retrospect, with the defense giving way over the next two possessions, Spags had a message for his unit following the collapse. “I asked everybody to look in the mirror and ask themselves this question: Did we let up? Did we lose our edge? Did we lack the killer instinct?” “I think we all have to look at that,” Spags reflected. “Did I call it differently? Does it need to be called differently? And so we had that conversation, and hopefully we will be presented with that situation again.” While it may take self-reflection to finish these big games, the Chiefs are still looking for answers to finish plays, like opponent dropbacks. Kansas City is tied with the Miami Dolphins and New York Giants for the fewest sacks in the NFL. However, Chiefs defensive end George Karlafits leads the NFL in batted-down passes (7) after Week 8. For a team with a low sack total, that’s a silver lining worth pointing out for the coach. “I am happy with the six pass breakups,” Spagnuolo said. “When the offense drops back to throw the ball, all we’re concerned about is the end result. And quite frankly, sacks are glamorous… but on a third-down play, if a defensive lineman is knocking the ball down, you’re really getting the same thing: they’re punting.” “What would be really nice is if we could get some of those first- and second-down sacks when they throw it,” Spagnuolo acknowledged. While Spagnuolo’s point about early-down sacks helps, it seems that’s the only time the Chiefs get sacks this year. Out of the team’s nine sacks this season, only one has come on third down, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . Whether it’s a killer instinct needed or a better pass-rush plan, the Chiefs’ defense needs to finish more pass plays to the ground to help finish close games like last week’s in Denver.

title: The Chiefs have lost their fastball against quality opponents
summary: One of my favorite skills Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes possesses is his ability to be one step faster than any player chasing him. It doesn’t matter if it’s a defensive tackle or a cornerback; he’ll outrace them to the sideline to get his throw off. It’s magic. That ability has seemingly rubbed off […]
full_text: (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images One of my favorite skills Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes possesses is his ability to be one step faster than any player chasing him. It doesn’t matter if it’s a defensive tackle or a cornerback; he’ll outrace them to the sideline to get his throw off. It’s magic. That ability has seemingly rubbed off on the Chiefs over the years. Think about how many times we’ve seen this team be so much better than the opposition. It doesn’t really matter who the opponent is on the opposing sideline. The Chiefs just seem to find a way. It’s that Mahomes Magic. I miss it. Things changed last year. The team couldn’t find that extra gear early on, especially against the quality opponents on the schedule. The Chiefs’ one-score sorcery evolved into one-score nightmares. The entire season was a disaster from start to finish. This year would be different. It certainly felt different in the first month. The Chiefs sprinted to a 5-0 start. The vibes were generally positive. Things were back on track. Everything seemed to flip on a dime. I’m not sure exactly when it happened, but one play against the Seattle Seahawks sticks in my mind that I haven’t been able to shake. Nick Emmanwori put the athleticism on display to put the pressure on Mahomes 😤 KCvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GJtsfssHa9 — NFL (@NFL) October 26, 2026 In the second quarter, the Chiefs line up rookie running back Emmett Johnson behind Mahomes in the pistol formation. Mahomes fakes a pitch to Johnson to the right and rolls to his left, and he has to beat a defender to his spot to get the throw off as he had done so many times before. A step faster than every defender, right? Not this time. He has met his match. Safety Nick Emmanwori chased down Mahomes from behind and forced a bad throw to Jalen Royals, resulting in a Seahawks interception. The Chiefs were trailing 3-0 at the time. The Seahawks took a 10-0 lead on the next drive and never looked back. Was that the moment the bad vibes returned? It’s hard to say. The Chiefs didn’t immediately follow that game with another terrible performance. They were leading 24-13 entering the fourth quarter on the road against the Broncos. That’s a game they should win. But they didn’t. They fell short. Again. It’s becoming a trend, the kind I never thought we would see under head coach Andy Reid and Mahomes. This team just doesn’t seem to have that ability to keep quality opponents at arm’s reach any longer. The Chiefs were 16-7 from 2022-2024 in the regular season with Patrick Mahomes as the starter against teams that finished the year at or above .500. They have gone just 3-9 against that same caliber of opponents over the past two seasons. They went from the second-best winning percentage in the NFL from 2022-2024 against opponents who finished with at least a .500 record to the team with the 13th-worst record in the league over the past two seasons against opponents with at least a .500 record. What gives? A little bit of everything. As you have probably learned by now, I’m a bit of a contrarian by nature. After their past couple of performances, my initial suspicion was that the defense was the main culprit for the Chiefs’ downward spiral against quality opponents. It seems, at least anecdotally, that the Chiefs have struggled to get off the field on key downs. And we all know the pass rush has steadily declined in recent years. Maybe that’s the issue? Statistic: 2022-2024 Defense: 2025-2026 Defense: Points Allowed Per Game: 19.5 22.2 Total Yards Allowed/Gm 328 321 Passing Yards Allowed/Gm 218 225 Pasing TDs Allowed 28 15 Interceptions 10 5 Takeaways 18 8 3rd Down Conversion Rate Allowed 42.6% 43% Sacks Per Game 2.9 2.2 Pressures Per Game 10.7 8.7 The defense has, indeed, regressed against quality opponents. But not as much as I suspected. They’re effectively giving up an extra field goal per game, and the pass rush has fallen off a bit. But we knew that. The rest of the numbers are… fine? They’re mostly right in line with where they were from 2022-2024. Okay, so if it’s not the defense that’s taken a serious step back, I guess it’s the offense? Well… Kinda. Statistic: 2022-2024 Offense: 2025-2026 Offense: Games Played 23 12 Points Per Game: 23.6 20.6 Total Yards/Gm 356.5 333.7 Passing Yards/Gm 248.2 220.8 Pasing TDs 44 14 Interceptions 15 11 Turnovers 20 11 3rd Down Conversion Rate 46% 39% Sacks Per Game Allowed 1.7 2.25 Field Goal Rate 38/42 (90%) 16/21 (76%) Red Zone TD Efficiency 63% TD Rate 60% TD Rate The Chiefs offense, much like the defense, is basically a field-goal-worse per game. The passing offense has taken a pretty significant step back, as one would expect, and that shows up prominently in the Chiefs’ inability to convert on third downs. It’s worth noting the offense is a field goal worse per game, and roughly half of those points reflect missed field goals by Harrison Butker. The truth is it’s a bit of everything. The Chiefs are losing on the margins. The pass rush isn’t getting home quite as often. The passing offense isn’t connecting on key third downs. The kicking game isn’t as strong. The Chiefs just don’t have that one thing that keeps opposing coaches up at night the way they once did. None of this is to say they can’t develop that thing. The trade deadline is still a week away. There’s time to get this back on track. I suspect this team will look quite good over the next three games against the New York Jets , Atlanta Falcons and Arizona Cardinals , and they’ll likely enter Week 12 against the Buffalo Bills with an 8-2 record and the ability to control their own destiny down the stretch with contests looming against the Bills, Los Angeles Rams , Cincinnati Bengals , New England Patriots and San Francisco 49ers . That’s a month of games looming against quality opponents. It wasn’t that long ago the Chiefs thrived in these kinds of games. It’s time to recapture that magic. It’s going to take a slight uptick in play from each and every player. And probably a trade or two, to boot.

title: George Karlaftis can relate to R Mason Thomas’ rookie progress
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs made a splash in April’s draft by selecting former Oklahoma pass rusher R Mason Thomas in the second round. Thomas made his presence felt immediately in his NFL debut by registering a sack against Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix in Week 1. While he has had promising moments since — and […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs made a splash in April’s draft by selecting former Oklahoma pass rusher R Mason Thomas in the second round. Thomas made his presence felt immediately in his NFL debut by registering a sack against Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix in Week 1. While he has had promising moments since — and has nine quarterback pressures on the year — Thomas has yet to get home again on an opposing quarterback. Kansas City’s entire pass rush has had a woefully slow start to 2026 with only nine total sacks on the year. Speaking before Wednesday’s practice, defensive end George Karlaftis recalled his own slow start to his career in 2022. He knows what Thomas — as well as first-round defensive tackle Peter Woods — are going through as the stat sheet continues to elude them. “I had this conversation before this season,” Karlaftis explained, “and we’re having conversations from time to time in season. ‘Look guys, I was a first round pick. Whatever success I’ve had, I was a first-round pick, and I didn’t have a full sack until after Thanksgiving. ‘” Adjusting to the NFL can be daunting. Ultimately, Karlaftis tallied 5.5 sacks over the last seven games of his rookie season and finished with 21 pressures. “There’s ebbs and flows,” continued Karlaftis. “You doubt yourself. You see yourself do something good on the tape, and it makes a man of you to be honest. You’ve just got to produce at the end of the day. With those guys, always keep at it. It’s like in Finding Nemo when Dorie says, ‘Just keep swimming.’ “ The veteran believes the advice from the animated feature will eventually come through for the rookies. “Those guys love football,” he said of Woods and Thomas. “When they just keep at it, keep chopping wood, keep improving, keep finding those little details in you game to where maybe that pressure becomes a sack. Or maybe that missed tackle becomes a TFL. It’s really about just finding the little things. I can remember myself vividly going through hours after games or after a bad practice of just figuring it out because it’s a long process and it takes everything out of you.” In Karlaftis’ rookie season, a Week 8 bye week after facing the San Francisco 49ers provided a chance to work on his game. “For me, personally,” he recalled, “I feel like it started clicking after the bye week. We played San Fran, and I felt like during the fourth quarter I missed two or three sacks. I was so ticked off. I was pissed at myself. I remember calling Joe Cullen maybe 20 times that week. ‘I’ve got to get it right. Coach, can you help me out?‘ “We kind of laid together a play of how I could be successful or how I could help this team more. I felt like it clicked. Whenever you have time off as a rookie — or as a vet t00 — you get a chance to reflect and review and ultimately improve on everything. For me, it was during that time. I really took a step back and I was like, ‘What am I doing well? What can I improve on?’ That’s really for me what it was.“

full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: David Njoku #83 of the Los Angeles Chargers walks off the field following an NFL game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 13, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Wednesday, Jim Harbaugh told reporters ahead of practice that the team would be opening the 21-day activation windows for both tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman. Activating both of these players would leave the Chargers with three remaining activations from IR for the remainder of the 2026 season. Njoke joined the Chargers as a free agent this offseason and began his tenure with the Bolts on a high note through the team’s first two games, catching five passes for 58 yards against the Raiders before leaving that game with an injury. Perryman has been on IR since before the regular season began. In his place, former undrafted free agent Del’Shawn Phillips has been the starter in the middle alongside Daiyan Henley. His return would bring back a veteran presence with plenty of experience, which is a positive even if the defense has been getting by just fine through injuries to that side of the ball. With the Chargers going down to three remaining activations this year, they will have to make some tough choices about who is worth bringing back and who isn’t. Right now, left tackle Rashawn Slater, safety Derwin James, offensive lineman Trey Pipkins, fullback Alec Ingold, and backup quarterback Trey Lance are all on IR. Slater and James are certainly going to take two of those spots — if it’s even worth bringing them back in a season such as this — but who ends up being that last activation? Perhaps it is someone who hasn’t been injured yet. Holding it for later could actually be the smart choice.

title: What is Rams’ plan for Ty Simpson?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams had a plan to futureproof the quarterback position. They hid their intentions well during the spring before shocking the NFL by selecting Ty Simpson with the thirteenth overall pick. But a plan—at least a good one—doesn’t stop at drafting a player. We knew Simpson was a green prospect entering the draft. […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams cheers on his teammates during the half of a preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams had a plan to futureproof the quarterback position. They hid their intentions well during the spring before shocking the NFL by selecting Ty Simpson with the thirteenth overall pick. But a plan—at least a good one—doesn’t stop at drafting a player. We knew Simpson was a green prospect entering the draft. He looked as ready as you possibly could during the preseason. For someone who the consensus said needed time to develop, Simpson looked poised under pressure and kept the ball out of harm’s way during the exhibition games. Through eight weeks Simpson has been a healthy scratch on game days. He still dressed as the emergency third quarterback behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett, although he cannot step onto the field unless the two signal callers ahead of him are unavailable because of injury. It’s time to reassess whether Simpson should be the third quarterback. That is not to say that Simpson should be starting over Stafford, although just two weeks ago it was difficult to see LA climbing out of the hole they put themselves in. I have a hard time believing that Bennett is more capable and dependable than Simpson. It’s probably time for the rookie to usurp the veteran within the depth chart. Stafford is also managing an elbow injury that requires him to frequently ice his elbow, which could help explain his decline in play this season. It’s worth mentioning: the Rams owe Bennett nothing. His contract is set to expire at season’s end. It would take more money to retain him, which the team probably won’t do. The most likely outcome is that Bennett goes to team that runs a similar offensive scheme to Sean McVay and where he has a chance to get onto the field. So if the Rams are headed towards a separation with Bennett, why not give Simpson any reps as the number two quarterback and allow him to backup Stafford on gamedays? It could be that the team is waiting for their bye week to make a change. That comes after the next two games. Still, we know the Rams have a plan to develop Simpson. The details are simply unclear. At some point the rookie will replace Bennett as the backup. It’s really just a matter of when. Why not right now?

Ultimately, Los Angeles needs some positive injury news. The Rams have the talent to compete, but staying healthy is becoming an increasingly difficult obstacle to overcome.

title: Rams holding punt returner competition
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are looking for a new player to fair catch punts for the rest of the season. full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are looking for a new player to fair catch punts for the rest of the season. Sean McVay told reporters this week that Kyren Williams and Tutu Atwell are the leaders in the clubhouse to win a job that nobody really wants because it only comes with dire consequences and no upside. The Rams have already released two punt returners during this season in Xavier Smith and Alex Bachman. It’s not that Williams or Atwell are in danger of being released, but they also don’t have anything to gain and that’s why the only real outcome left is to simply make sure you don’t muff or fumble the punt. Sean McVay said Kyren Williams and Tutu Atwell are candidates to return punts. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) November 4, 2026 If you think that McVay is worried about Williams’ health on punt returns, you’re seeing this job the wrong way. All he’s going to do if he gets the job is throw his hand up in the air and make a fair catch. That’s the most that McVay can hope for at this point after years of stumbling through special teams additions. Williams has six career punt returns in the NFL and an average of 6.6 yards per return. He had 14 punt returns in his final year at Notre Dame. There’s no hope of breaking one off for 60 yards. This is a “fair catch” job only. Atwell had 10 punt returns in 2021 and four punt returns in college. He’d only be out there to fair catch the ball. Ronnie Rivers is set to be activated this week and he has more extensive college returning experience than either of those players. He would also just fair catch the punt. Rams RB Ronnie Rivers is back to practice today. He’ll be activated this week and will return to the No. 3 RB role with special teams duty, too. He’s an option at kick returner. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) November 4, 2026 Brennan Presley and Bachman (re-signed a day after he was released) would also be options from the practice squad. What would be their assignment if McVay asked them to return punts? Fair catch. That’s all the job is. Don’t muff. Let’s see who can handle it.

title: Trade deadline options at cornerback for the Rams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams took a major hit with Jaylen Watson now going on injured reserve due to his shoulder injury. If the Rams want to look outside the facility for another starter at corner, or even just depth, there are a few options out there. No one Los Angeles can add right now will […]
full_text: (Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams took a major hit with Jaylen Watson now going on injured reserve due to his shoulder injury. If the Rams want to look outside the facility for another starter at corner, or even just depth, there are a few options out there. No one Los Angeles can add right now will be as good as Watson has been this year, or at least it’s severely unlikely. According to Next Gen Stats, among outside cornerbacks, Watson entered this past week with the fifth-lowest completion percentage allowed to opposing targets, and is tied for the third-most pass breakups in the league (alongside teammate Quentin Lake). That’s not easy production to replace in general, let alone in the middle of a playoff race. Still, a few serviceable players are available, even if they will further weaken the Rams’ already limited draft pick pool for 2027. RIQ WOOLEN One name that could be available is Riq Woolen, the former Seattle Seahawks corner who hasn’t quite fixed the Philadelphia Eagles’ severe CB2 woes like the latter franchise hoped he would. Still, Woolen brings size to the table at 6-foot-4 and 210 pounds, which is actually bigger than Watson’s frame (and size is a major selling point for Watson). He hasn’t been great this season, there’s no denying that, but he does have at least a decent track record. He’s also hardly the biggest reason why the Eagles have struggled defensively this year. Philadelphia has already traded away an offensive contributor and is in a bad spot with a losing record and their starting quarterback unavailable. They’ve turned to Joe Milton at quarterback, which tells you all you need to know. Woolen may not cost too much to acquire, and his contract isn’t completely daunting. With the trade deadline coming up, Riq Woolen's name has come up. And he hears it. https://t.co/4m4zBeQldM — NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) October 30, 2026 AMIK ROBERTSON Another NFC East player, Amik Robertson is having a solid season for the 2-4-1 Washington Commanders. He’s a completely different body type than either Woolen or Watson, standing just 5-foot-9 and 183 pounds. This season, Robertson is allowing a 90.3 passer rating as the closest defender, which isn’t spectacular but beggars can’t be choosers if you need a player in a pinch. It is encouraging that he had one of his best games of the year this past week in a win over the Eagles, allowing a meager 11 yards on four receptions while being targeted six times. The Guarantee! DB Amik Robertson says the Commanders will win this game on Sunday night against the Eagles. Amik said, "we definitely need to win this game and we will." I then asked "sounds like a guarantee?" Amik responded, "it has to be." pic.twitter.com/5nhQN4U7A7 — Scott Abraham (@Scott7news) October 28, 2026 JUJU BRENTS The Miami Dolphins have had some frisky moments this season, but they’re decidedly not a good football team. They need a ton of help going into next season, and adding a pick in exchange for a cornerback on an expiring rookie contract may be appealing to them. Similarly, it could appeal to the Rams that Brents is both cheap and playing well as he gears up for his first free agent payday. According to NFL stats whiz Aaron Schatz in commentary for ESPN , Brents is third in coverage DVOA for qualified cornerbacks this year, only behind Jahdae Barron of the Denver Broncos and current Ram Trent McDuffie. Don’t forget folks, JuJu Brents returns to the Dolphins in 2026 after an impressive sample size, most notably vs the Bills #PhinsUp pic.twitter.com/kacOumEp2k — Cameron Sparks (@Cam3ronSparks) April 28, 2026 The Rams have enough needs and such little 2027 draft capital that they may decide that promoting from within is the best way to fill the cornerback void long term. But there are options out there if they feel the need to find outside assistance.
