title: For the Rams, one player leaves as another enters?
summary: It is awful news that Jaylen Watson is out for the year, and you have to wish the player all the best. On the flip side, Myles Garrett is coming back for the Los Angeles Rams, right? Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1 and he’s practicing this week, but no announcement has been made that […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 10: Jaylen Watson #35 and Myles Garrett #95 of the Los Angeles Rams are seen during a Los Angeles Rams NFL media availability at Marvel Stadium on September 10, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is awful news that Jaylen Watson is out for the year, and you have to wish the player all the best. On the flip side, Myles Garrett is coming back for the Los Angeles Rams, right? Garrett hasn’t played since Week 1 and he’s practicing this week, but no announcement has been made that he’ll be playing this Sunday or next Sunday, but unless there is a setback, the expectation is that he will be playing. Eventually. For Watson, his season ends just as the Rams were hoping to really get their year rolling. Watson has been tremendous, but he’s been nursing a shoulder injury since earlier this year (at least since their game against the Denver Broncos), and at a certain point, it is better to shut a player down than risk further injury. It’s better for the player, and the Rams expect to have Watson another couple seasons, so let him heal. Still, the news is a bummer for the person, and for the team, to put it lightly. In other news Quentin Lake was talking some smack on Justin Herbert. So there’s that. Rams CB Jaylen Watson is out for season after shoulder surgery. Myles Garrett returns to practice (houstonchronicle) “But Watson missed a game earlier this season after dislocating his shoulder, and the two-time Super Bowl champion hurt that shoulder again in the Rams’ 24-9 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers last Sunday. “That’s a big blow, a bummer for him,” McVay said. “He’s been such a stud for us. He wanted to be able to play through it, but just kind of understanding the totality of it all, it was recommended for him to get that surgery, and he’ll be on IR. He’s been awesome, and whenever he gets back next year, we’ll be better. He’s been everything and that much more that we’d hoped.” Rams CB Jaylen Watson is out for season after shoulder surgery. Myles Garrett returns to practice (houstonchronicle) “But Garrett was in practice with his teammates for the first time since his zero-tackle Rams debut in Australia nearly two months ago. The two-time AP NFL Defensive Player of the Year had knee surgery and missed seven games. McVay isn’t certain whether Garrett will be ready to play at Washington, saying the Rams will make that decision later in the week. Garrett will take about half of the practice reps on Wednesday to see how his body responds. “It’s exciting,” McVay said. “It’s great to be able to get him back out there. Just trying to stay in the moment, one day at a time.” Rams star safety cooks Justin Herbert for ‘throwing deli meat’ in Chargers loss (nypost) “I mean, [Herbert] was throwing deli meat out there. He’s seeing ghosts, I’m not going to lie,” Lake said with a laugh during his appearance on the “St. Brown Podcast.” “Bro, I don’t know what’s going on, but we knew we were getting a couple,” he added. Herbert has been the butt of many jokes this season — and for good reason. But it’s one thing for fans to roast Herbert about his mediocre performances. It’s another thing for one of his peers to do so on a podcast, where the whole world can hear about it.“ Rams lose Pro Bowl cornerback for the season with news of shoulder surgery (sports.yahoo) “”Unfortunately, Jaylen Watson has to get surgery on his shoulder. He will be out for the year. That’s a big one,” said Rams’ head coach Sean McVay on Wednesday afternoon. “He’s been such a stud for us. He wanted to be able to play through it, but just understanding the totality of it all and some of the different things, it was recommended that he get that surgery.” McVay added that Watson will be put on IR for the rest of the year. Watson aggravated the dislocated right shoulder he suffered against the Denver Broncos earlier this season during the Rams’ win against the Los Angeles Chargers this past weekend.“ With no-huddle offense working so well, could Rams use it more? (ramswire) “The numbers do not do the situation justice in terms of how much the offense benefited from going at a faster pace. With their no-huddle approach, the Rams ran five plays on their final drive of the half, going 66 yards, with Matthew Stafford throwing four completions on four attempts before Kyren Williams ran in the score. The Rams caught the Chargers struggling to organize defensively, with Tutu Atwell burning his defender for a 40-yard gain, setting the Rams up in the red zone. Before that drive, the Rams had five other drives, and they were awful. Three points, no first downs, and their only score came after an interception by Quentin Lake that set the Rams up in the red zone.“ Rams May Be Better Equipped to Overcome Jaylen Watson Injury Than Expected (si.com) “With Watson out, the Rams will be relying on Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes in his spot. While there is certainly a difference in being a rotational player and playing full time, the Rams have gotten good production out of Wallace and Forbes this season. “I think those guys have done really well,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Jimmy Lake has done such a great job really with those corners as a whole group. Josh has played a lot of snaps. I thought ‘E-Forbes’ really played well last week. Both of those guys have been tapped in. They’ve been ready to step up and it seems like there have been a lot of games that we’ve had our top corners get banged up and they’ve played a lot more.” Rams stars get emotional over Jaylen Watson’s devastating injury: ‘We’re going to do it for him’ (sports.yahoo) “Linebacker Byron Young went one step further, dedicating the remainder of the season to Watson, injured defensive tackle Poona Ford and the other teammates whose seasons have ended prematurely. “I hate to lose a guy like that, but we’re going to keep going,” Young said. “We’re going to do it for him.” Watson’s season is over, but his influence isn’t. Lake believes the veteran’s football intelligence and leadership can continue helping the secondary from the sidelines during his recovery.“ 3 things for the Rams to know about the Commanders (ramswire) “Washington may not win, but it won’t be for a lack of trying Washington’s effort level this season has been unreal, and for a team that has been struggling, there’s a reason why head coach Dan Quinn’s seat isn’t as hot as others in the NFL. The Commanders play with a passion and an attitude that goes above and beyond. It feels like there’s a real belief within the organization behind what they’re about, and if they can clean up their on-field operation – especially with penalties – they could turn the corner.“ Rams-Commanders injury report: McDuffie, Curl DNP to start Week 9 (ramswire) “The Rams released their first injury report of Week 9 on Wednesday and a total of 12 players were listed on it, five of them being non-participants. McDuffie did not practice, nor did Colby Parkinson, Kam Curl or Joe Cardona. McDuffie injured his back last week against the Chargers, Parkinson is still dealing with a rib injury and Curl picked up a foot injury. There is some good news, though. Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Ronnie Rivers were all designated to return and were back at practice. None of them have been activated from IR yet but it’s a good sign that they’re practicing again. Rivers was a full participant, and Garrett and Ferguson were both limited.“ Commanders dealing with injuries on defensive line ahead of matchup with Rams (nbcwashington) “Defensive linemen Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne were both placed on injured reserve, with their seasons likely both over, coach Dan Quinn said Wednesday. Kinlaw had knee surgery, while Payne has a foot injury. And yet, Washington’s defensive line has been a mostly consistent unit so far this year, even as the defense has had issues elsewhere through the course of two months. “I just think the mentality and…

title: Las Vegas Raiders’ defense must find answers for San Francisco 49ers Kyle Juszczyk packages in Week 9 key matchups
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are in the AFC playoff picture with a 4-4 record heading into Week 9, but the Raiders haven’t proven they can beat a playoff-caliber team yet. Facing off against the NFC-leading 6-1 San Francisco 49ers this Sunday is a great opportunity for Las Vegas to announce itself as a legitimate postseason […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are in the AFC playoff picture with a 4-4 record heading into Week 9, but the Raiders haven’t proven they can beat a playoff-caliber team yet. Facing off against the NFC-leading 6-1 San Francisco 49ers this Sunday is a great opportunity for Las Vegas to announce itself as a legitimate postseason contender by winning the three key matchups below and the game. Raiders’ Defense vs. Juszczyk Packages While fullbacks have become less common in modern NFL offenses, Kyle Juszczyk has become one of many valuable weapons in Kyle Shanahan’s offense over the years. In 2026, the 49ers have leaned on 21 personnel more than any other personnel package, leading the league with a 34.5% rate (6.6% more than any other team) and 141 total plays (22 more plays than any other team), per Sumer Sports . Unsurprisingly, San Francisco also tops the charts in total EPA (11.21) when using 21 personnel, according to Sumer. While Shanahan’s crew dips to eighth in EPA per play (0.08), all of the teams ahead of them have 10 or fewer plays in those packages this season. Additionally, they are one of two offenses to have a positive EPA per pass (0.05, ranks 13th) and per rush (0.1, sixth) in 21 personnel. The New York Jets are the other club, and the Jets have just four plays with that grouping on the field. Juszczyk’s unique skill set allows the 49ers to lean so heavily on these packages. While his 58.8 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus might seem low, that ranks fourth among fullbacks with at least 27 run blocks and is only 1.8 points behind the position’s leader, Adam Prentice (60.6) from the Denver Broncos. Additionally, Prentice has less than a third of the run-blocking snaps that Juszczyk has (30 to 99). On top of that, of running backs who have at least 20 carries with 21 personnel on the field, San Francisco’s Kaelon Black has the highest yards per carry (4.52) and Christian McCaffrey is second (4.49), per Sumer . Meanwhile, the Raiders’ defense has only seen 27 rushes against 21 personnel, but ranks dead last in EPA per rush allowed (0.133) and 28th in success rate (48.1%). Additionally, the fullback’s impact extends to the passing game. He has a modest eight catches for 76 yards and two touchdowns, but the pair of scores highlights how he needs to be accounted for as a receiver in the red zone. Also, of tight end George Kittle’s 34 catches and 425 yards this season, nine catches (26.5%) and 139 yards (32.7%) have come in 21 personnel, and all nine grabs are charted as “impact plays” by Sumer . Las Vegas is closer to the middle of the pack when it comes to defending the passing game against said packages, ranking 15th in EPA per pass (negative 0.104) and 19th in success rate (50%). However, the sample size is small with just 18 plays, and Shanahan doesn’t always use his fullback in the traditional sense. Per PFF , Juszczyk has lined up as a tight end or wide receiver (66 snaps inline, 45 in the slot and 17 out wide) more often than he has in the backfield (52 snaps) this season. That goes back to his versatile skill set, as Shanahan uses 21 personnel to run 12 personnel plays with the “fullback” and Kittle on the field at the same time. That’s been an issue for the Raiders’ coverage unit, facing 60 pass plays with two tight ends on the field and ranking 22nd in EPA per pass (0.169) and 20th in success rate (51.7%), according to Sumer . Additionally, the defense had a tough time against the New York Jets’ 12 personnel packages last week, giving up 0.32 EPA per pass and a 50% success rate , and 0.3 EPA per rush and a 57.1% success rate on the ground. So, whether Juszczyk is lined up as a traditional fullback or at tight end, the Silver and Black have to find answers when he’s on the field. Those packages are a big factor in the 49ers’ offense that ranks fourth with 28.1 points per game . Raiders’ IOL vs. 49ers’ Interior Pass-Rush We’re essentially at the halfway point of the 2026 season, and it’s pretty clear that the Raiders are a passing offense. For context, they rank third in passing yards per game ( 265.1 ) and are second-worst in rushing yards per game (77.3). Diving even deeper into the efficiency metrics, the Silver and Black are sixth in EPA per pass (0.18) and second-to-last in EPA per rush (negative 0.24), according to Sumer . That’s led to a career resurgence for Kirk Cousins, who has the third-most passing yards ( 2,124 ) and second-most touchdowns (19) in the league through eight weeks. However, he’s a different quarterback when under pressure. With a clean pocket, PFF has Cousins with the 10th-best passing grade (88.4), tied for seventh in “big-time throws” (seven) and tied for the eighth-fewest “turnover-worthy plays” (two) out of 35 qualifying quarterbacks. However, those figures dip to 15th in passing grade (50.1), tied for 17th in BTTs (three) and tied for the 13th-most TWPs (five) when under pressure. That’s where the 38-year-old’s lack of mobility and arm strength show up. Meanwhile, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner will be making his return to San Francisco on Sunday after the club traded for him during the bye week. Buckner, who was the 49ers’ first-round pick in 2016 and spent four seasons with the team, has a reputation as one of the better interior pass-rushers in the league. In seven games with the Indianapolis Colts, he registered 20 pressures (tied for 16th among defensive tackles), per PFF , and four sacks this season. The 11-year pro also has three batted passes (tied for sixth) and a 73.7 pass-rush grade (17th) on the campaign. But San Francisco’s pass-rush goes beyond the new acquisition who hasn’t played a snap for the team yet. Osa Odighizuwa is 15th among defensive tackles in pressures (21), while rookie Gracen Halton has flashed on limited opportunities to post a 70.7 PFF pass-rush grade (27th). Those three could be problematic for the Raiders’ interior offensive line. Left guard Spencer Burford has surrendered the third-most pressures ( 19 ) and has the 10th-lowest pass-blocking grade (41.0) at his position, while right guard Trey Zuhn III will make just his second career start. Zuhn had a decent showing last week by yielding just two pressures on 27 opportunities, but the Jets don’t have nearly the same interior pass-rush as the 49ers do. Luckily, center Tyler Linderbaum should be able to help the two guards out. While the big-ticket free-agent signing has faced some scrutiny for not living up to his contract so far this season, that’s primarily due to the ground game, as he’s been stingy in pass protection. Linderbaum has surrendered just eight pressures on 307 opportunities and is 13th among centers with a 70.3 pass-blocking grade . For the record, he’s been better as a run-blocker over the last two weeks with back-to-back PFF run-blocking grades above the baseline (60.0) after being below it in four of the first six contests. Especially with edge rusher Nick Bosa missing the last five games with a calf injury — and potentially on a pitch count if he returns this week — San Francisco’s interior pass-rush figures to be a key factor on Sunday. Mayer vs. Warner Brock Bowers may draw the headlines in Las Vegas’ tight end room, but Bowers is used more like a wide receiver in Klint Kubiak’s offense. According to PFF , nearly 85% of his pass snaps have come either out wide or in the slot. As a result, Michael Mayer is the Raiders’ more traditional tight end, spending 72.5% of his pass snaps inline. Also, he’s having a career year. Eight games into the season, Mayer has already logged personal bests in catches (36) and receiving yards (351). Additionally, those figures rank fourth and ninth among tight ends , and one more receiving touchdown will match his previous single-season high with two. The fourth-year pro’s YAC ability — which accounts for 180 or 51.3% of his yardage total — has provided Cousins with a reliable check-down option in the passing…

title: Next 3 games are critical for Raiders
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders salvaged their season when they pulled off a 38-33 comeback victory at the New York Jets on Sunday. The victory snapped a four-game losing streak. Had the Raiders, who trailed by two scores at halftime, not came from behind and lost to the woeful Jets, they would have fallen to 3-5. […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders salvaged their season when they pulled off a 38-33 comeback victory at the New York Jets on Sunday. The victory snapped a four-game losing streak. Had the Raiders, who trailed by two scores at halftime, not came from behind and lost to the woeful Jets, they would have fallen to 3-5. They would have been in big trouble in the AFC. Now, they have a chance. Las Vegas has the ninth best record in the AFC, tied with the Baltimore Ravens at 4-4. But the Ravens are without star quarterback Lamar Jackson, so the Raiders can push forward. While the Raiders saved their season in Week 8, the work is just starting. The play at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, then host the Seattle Seahawks and then visit the AFC West leading Denver Broncos. The three teams are a combined 16-7. The Raiders’ four wins have come against teams with a combined 5-24. The Raiders need to find a way to win two of these three next games to end a tough eight-game stretch with a 3-5 record after starting the season a perfect 3-0. If the Raiders can head to Thanksgiving with a winning record, they will be in good shape in the AFC playoff hunt with a manageable final six games. But being 5-6 or worse, would make things tougher. The Raiders responded when they needed to in Week 8, now they have to continue that trend.

title: Brock Bowers dominates as a wide receiver
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 38-33 win at the New York Jets on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the San Francisco 49ers: Brock Bowers: The first-round pick had seven catches for […]
full_text: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 38-33 win at the New York Jets on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the San Francisco 49ers: Brock Bowers: The first-round pick had seven catches for 92 yards and a score. According to Next Gen Stats, six of his catches, for 87 yards, were when hew as lined up as a wide receiver. It’s the most by a tight end in the NFL in 10 years. He is a wild weapon. And, yes, his contract talks next offseason are going to be very interesting. Jackson Powers-Johnson: The second-round pick remained on the bench for the third straight game. He is now a backup and he did warm up at just center Sunday, so he may not even be a guard anymore. D.J. Glaze: The third-round pick started at right tackle as usual and performed well. Tommy Eichenberg: The fifth-round pick from Ohio State played 22 defensive snaps and had his ups and downs. He also played 26 snaps on special teams, which was tied for the team high. Dylan Laube: The sixth-round pick made a huge impact with a 95-yard kick return for a touchdown in the second quarter. The Raiders may have lost the game without it. It was the first kick return for a score in the league this season and the Raiders’ first in 15 years. Laube is, by far, the kickoff leader in the NFL at 34.1 average. He has a 2.8 yard lead over any other returner. Only four players have finished a season wit ha higher average with the most recent coming in 1970.

title: Lions vs. Dolphins injury report: Jaylen Wright does not practice; Jack Campbell update
summary: The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions this weekend, hoping to bounce back after a disappointing loss to the New England Patriots last week. Both the Dolphins and Lions released their first injury reports for the week on Wednesday. The Lions, who beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, estimated their injury report after holding […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Jaylen Wright #5 of the Miami Dolphins in action during the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins host the Detroit Lions this weekend, hoping to bounce back after a disappointing loss to the New England Patriots last week. Both the Dolphins and Lions released their first injury reports for the week on Wednesday. The Lions, who beat the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, estimated their injury report after holding a walkthrough rather than a full practice. Jaylen Wright does not practice The Dolphins’ second-string running back missed practice with a quadriceps injury. While Wright’s contributions on offense have been minimal this year, picking up just 41 yards on 22 carries, he has been strong as a kick returner, where he is averaging 27.6 yards per kick and has a long of 79 yards. If Wright is unable to play this weekend, rookie running back Kaytron Allen, the Washington Commanders’ sixth-round pick who Miami claimed off waivers last month, could be in line to backup Ollie Gordon II. Allen, however, was limited in practice with a quadriceps injury of his own. Kadyn Proctor practices Dolphins rookie guard Kadyn Proctor fully participated in Wednesday’s practice but remains in the league’s concussion protocol, according to head coach Jeff Hafley. “He is progressing in the protocol,” Hafley said. Jarrett Kingston, an August waiver claim from the Houston Texans for Miami, started in Proctor’s place last week. Good news from Detroit’s Jack Campbell The Lions’ All-Pro linebacker sustained an ugly injury against the Vikings after tackling tight end T.J. Hockenson. Caught in an awkward position, Campbell hit Hockenson and had his head compress back onto his neck. He fell to the turf and lay motionless before being carted off the field and taken to a hospital. Campbell released a statement on Wednesday, indicating that he is progressing well in his recovery from the injury ( via Pride of Detroit ) : My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this. I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done. To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough. God is good. My faith is strong. Jack Campbell Campbell is on the injury report as a non-participant, as the Lions have not moved him to injured reserve yet, but none of that matters. It is just great news to hear that he has full lower-body movement and is progressing with his upper body. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he’ll play or not. Kevin O’Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson’s absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the ‘playing through it’ variety and don’t seem like they’ll keep those players out on Monday night. For the Bills, a laundry list of players on the injury report including three offensive line starters. Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins did not practice Thursday with a rib injury, nor did starting guard Alec Andreesen, with an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown was limited with a back issue. Backup wideout Joshua Palmer also missed Thursday’s practice with a hamstring injury. Other than that, the rest of the players on the list appear to be more of the playing through minor injuries type, except backups Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock who have their windows open to come back from the PUP list and IR, respectively. We’ll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Saturday. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Vikes Views: Wentz to the Rescue?
summary: The Minnesota Vikings have announced they will start Carson Wentz at Quarterback for Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. Kyler Murray is nursing a hamstring injury and will be unable to suit up. There is already plenty of speculation that this is a “soft benching.” I’m not a doctor, nor do I have any […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Carson Wentz #11 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up during an NFL football game against the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings have announced they will start Carson Wentz at Quarterback for Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. Kyler Murray is nursing a hamstring injury and will be unable to suit up. There is already plenty of speculation that this is a “soft benching.” I’m not a doctor, nor do I have any interest in pretending to be one, so I’ll take the team at its word and assume Murray is injured. What I do wonder is whether the Vikings might actually be better off this week because of it. Wentz helped the Vikings win their first two games, though nobody is going to confuse those performances with the 2017 version of Carson Wentz. The 9-3 victory over Chicago was about as exciting as watching paint dry, but he avoided the catastrophic mistake and let the defense do the heavy lifting. At this point in his career, Wentz is not the future. The problem for Murray is that he hasn’t exactly looked like the answer either. Through seven games, the offense has remained the weakest part of a team that sits at 6-1 largely because of its defense, special teams, and ability to force turnovers. I picked the Vikings to win last week because they have the best defense in football. I probably would’ve picked them to lose this week regardless of which quarterback was under center.

title: The Kyler Murray Experiment is Over
summary: Kevin O’Connell announced that Carson Wentz will start on Monday night for the Minnesota Vikings, while Kyler Murray will be week-to-week with a hamstring strain. This can and should be interpreted as a ‘‘soft-benching’ which happened with J.J. McCarthy as he was struggling last year and also with Kyler Murray as the Cardinals looked to […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-NOVEMBER 1: Quarterback Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings walks off the field after an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Kevin O’Connell announced that Carson Wentz will start on Monday night for the Minnesota Vikings, while Kyler Murray will be week-to-week with a hamstring strain. This can and should be interpreted as a ‘‘soft-benching’ which happened with J.J. McCarthy as he was struggling last year and also with Kyler Murray as the Cardinals looked to move on from him after he was injured last season. The reason to interpret it as a soft benching is because the Vikings offense continues to be anemic and the reason for the lack of production is because Murray still isn’t comfortable or acclimated running the offense and that has led to missed opportunities. The Lions game last week was the clearest example of that. Hall of Fame QB Kurt Warner breaks down some of the issues that led to the missed opportunities for the Vikings offense in the Lions game, below. And while there is a variety of issues depending on the particular play, most of them center around Murray not progressing fast enough and/or not getting the ball out fast enough. This is a continuation of the same issue for Murray so far this season. He’s hesitant and really more concerned about making a mistake than making a play, and/or he simply isn’t confident enough or acclimated enough in the offense to get the ball out on time on many occasions. Whatever the reason, he’s playing a bit slow and that is resulting in missed opportunities. For an experienced quarterback like Murray, who’s now halfway through the season, this simply isn’t good enough. Sure it can take some time to get acclimated, and it makes sense to be patient in that regard, but at this point things should be clicking more than they are. At some point either Murray can do it at a high-enough level or he can’t. It seems like the Vikings coaching staff is arriving at that point and the answer is that he can’t. It may be that the coaching staff, who has a lot of confidence in Carson Wentz’ ability to run the offense, is giving Murray some time away from the weekly game planning to figure some things out- although the bye-week would have provided that too- and perhaps come back with a fresh start. But whether Murray gets another opportunity remains to be seen. That will depend partly on Wentz, who has his physical limitations, and how well he performs. But Wentz is more comfortable with the offense and at least mentally may be the better option right now. And the Vikings don’t have any commitment to Murray, either contractually or from a development standpoint, where they need to play him. If Wentz plays well enough to win, it wouldn’t be surprising if he continues as the starter. Murray Won’t Be the Starter Next Year What is happening now with Murray is the Vikings coaching staff losing confidence in him. Ultimately that has longer-term implications. At the beginning of the season, the assumption was likely that if Murray plays well, he’ll be extended. I doubt that is the plan going forward now. Next year’s starter is not on the roster. And that has implications for Nolan Teasley as he considers options before the trade deadline next week and managing the salary cap next year and beyond. There will be several options for the Vikings next year at quarterback. Mac Jones may be high on the list, but I wouldn’t be surprised if Kirk Cousins, Anthony Richardson, Sam Darnold, Daniel Jones, and Justin Herbert, among others, may be available considerations. The last three are currently under contract with their teams next year but could nevertheless become available. And there is also the possibility of a draft pick too. How It Impacts the Trade Deadline and Salary Cap Considerations If Murray is unlikely to be extended, that means the Vikings may not necessarily have to prepare for a big salary cap that would likely come had Murray played well enough to be extended. I suspect most of the above options could be available for cheap or no more than medium quarterback contracts, which would be easier to manage. That may also influence what the Vikings may want to do as far as trading for a player(s) before the deadline. The Vikings have very limited cap space right now, so that is part of the considerations, but if the Vikings don’t have to absorb more than a mid-tier quarterback contract in the future, maybe they would be more open to trading for a player like Jonathan Taylor, who has a bigger cap hit the next two years. But the Vikings have no shortage of veterans on expiring contracts they may want to extend as well, so not paying as much for a quarterback may allow them to extend more of them. Can Murray Still Make a Come Back? Anything is possible, but Murray’s slow start doesn’t bode well for a spike in performance in the next two months, which is what it would take to earn an extension. There will be more options available this offseason and I expect the Vikings and new general manager Nolan Teasley will want to explore them. It seems unlikely that Murray will be the best option, even with an uptick in performance the rest of the season- if he gets a chance to return as the starter. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Vikings to Start Carson Wentz at Quarterback Against Bills
summary: Going into their Week 9 Monday Night showdown with the Buffalo Bills, the Minnesota Vikings are making a change at the quarterback position. The team has announced that Kyler Murray will be out this week with a hamstring injury, meaning that Carson Wentz will take over behind center when the team welcomes the Bills to […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Carson Wentz #11 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on against the Indianapolis Colts in the third quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into their Week 9 Monday Night showdown with the Buffalo Bills, the Minnesota Vikings are making a change at the quarterback position. The team has announced that Kyler Murray will be out this week with a hamstring injury, meaning that Carson Wentz will take over behind center when the team welcomes the Bills to town this week. In Week 1 against the Packers, Wentz took over for Murray after he suffered a concussion early in the first quarter, and he also started the Week 2 matchup against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field. He didn’t exactly put up the most artistic of performances in either of those games, but they were effective enough to get the job done. Wentz threw three touchdown passes as the Vikings scored 39 points in their Week 1 win, and he didn’t turn the ball over in less-than-ideal weather conditions in Chicago as the Vikings beat the Bears in a 9-3 slopfest. In the five games since then, the Vikings’ offense has struggled against teams that, by and large, it really shouldn’t have struggled against offensively. The team has gone over 20 points just twice in the last five games, and in one of those two games, they went over 20 because they got a punt return for a touchdown. The Vikings’ offense, for the season, has scored just 11 touchdowns in seven games, with five of them coming in the Week 1 win over the Packers. We don’t know for sure if the move to Carson Wentz is going to spark the Vikings’ offense or not, but the Bills are bringing the 30th-ranked pass defense in the NFL to the Twin Cities this week, so it can’t hurt to try to find out. Once again, the Minnesota Vikings have announced that they will be starting Carson Wentz at quarterback this week on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. What do you think of this development, folks?

title: Patriots mailbag: Pats to be buyers or sellers at NFL trade deadline?
summary: It’s a busy weekend in Foxboro as Rob Gronkowski and the 2016 Patriots are back in town, while the current New England Patriots squad has a big game themselves against the Green Bay Packers days before the trade deadline. Before all the action begins, let’s get into this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. Trade […]
full_text: It’s a busy weekend in Foxboro as Rob Gronkowski and the 2016 Patriots are back in town, while the current New England Patriots squad has a big game themselves against the Green Bay Packers days before the trade deadline. Before all the action begins, let’s get into this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. Trade talk! Would they really trade Barmore? I could see it if they were 3-5, but seems like it would leave them very weak at a position that isn’t terribly strong to begin with in a year when everything is still on the table in front of you. Maybe that’s a move you make in the offseason, no? – RRDMuz My belief entering this year was that this is Christian Barmore’s last season in New England. Barmore has no guaranteed money remaining on his contract and the value of the deal has not matched his play since his return from blood clots. Pair that with long-term concerns over a lingering knee injury and it would make sense to move on. As for the rest of this season, however, I’d still expect him and Carlton Davis to be on the roster at this time next week. Where’s the line between buy and sell? How do you think they see this beat-up team’s chances for a deep playoff run? Moving Barmore weakens them badly for this year, so maybe if that’s happening it’s not worth adding pieces? If it doesn’t, maybe some depth? Or do they just stay the course and any playoff appearance or win becomes gravy? – ed.liebfried With Drake Maye and Mike Vrabel, the Patriots will always have a chance to compete and make a run in the playoffs. When it comes to selling, I do think there’s a logical argument for getting younger and adding draft capital, but the time and place for that is next offseason. At this deadline, I think the Patriots will focus on finding minor upgrades to bolster the roster. The best-case scenario would be finding the next version of Kyle Van Noy, who they acquired in exchange for a late-round pick swap. And while I hate when teams like the Red Sox use injured players returning as a reason not to be active at the deadline, I think it’s a different story in football. The Patriots getting players back like Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs and Alijah Vera-Tucker in upcoming weeks are a significant boost to the roster. What’s up with Henderson and the trade talk? Not a culture fit? Or system fit?? It seems odd he’s not even practicing – Groganator Henderson has now missed over a week with a legitimate illness, which is why he has been absent. The trade speculation stems from some of his struggles this season, but I wouldn’t be ready to give up on the 24-year-old second-round pick, who posted over 1,100 yards and 10 touchdowns last season. The hope should be that Henderson can get healthy from both his illness and ankle injury and that the coaching staff can find a way to get him going on the field. If this team is fully healthy where would you look to improve – XGhost-PepperX As we discussed, we are expecting more minor additions to the roster. With wide receivers and linemen coming back from injury, a blocking tight end would be the main spot we’d look on offense. Part of the run game issues have been with the tight ends blocking the edges as that is not Hunter Henry’s game and Eli Raridon has had up-and-down moments like most rookies. On defense, the defensive line has played better in recent weeks but a true nose tackle and edge rusher — as they still only three on the roster — would be players to add. Another linebacker to allow the defense to play more true base defense against heavier personnel groupings could also be a target. Williams, Douglas, and Chism were productive against Miami. Was that because it was Miami? Or, in the playoffs, might we have 6-8 skill position players who are dangerous? – WannaBe Pats GM We’ve been in the camp that all three are quality wide receivers in this league. They might not be bonafide No. 1 options, but they all have unique skillsets that make that strong complimentary pieces who can also take on larger roles when players above them are injured. We’ll also continue to push for more Kyle Williams snaps, specifically in the slot like he was used in college. He’s a dangerous player with his speed and the Patriots should look to exploit that more. Will the New England Patriots activate both WR Mack Hollins and FB Reggie Gilliam this week? – For Pats Sake Hollins looks ready to go. Gilliam isn’t ready yet but has increased his presence in the locker room in the past week. With so many QB injuries around the league, do you think one of our QBs have some value to bring good draft value (not a sixth round) or some one we can exchange with? – sumeetw Tommy DeVito has started games in the league so could have some attraction. But, I’d say the injuries around the league show how valuable it is to have depth at that position. Any quality backup quarterback is more valuable for a competing team compared to a late-round draft pick. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

summary: The New England Patriots’ game in Miami last Sunday was partially played in miserable weather. full_text: The New England Patriots’ game in Miami last Sunday was partially played in miserable weather. This week’s contest against the Green Bay Packers will see a return to better playing conditions. The Patriots will be hosting the Packers at Gillette Stadium for a battle of 5-3 teams, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. At that point in time, WBZ Boston projects temperatures of 56°F, which will drop to 52°F at the half and into the high 40s toward the end of the game — noticeably cooler than last week, but most importantly with minimal if any precipitation in the forecast. “The good news is the risk of rain looks to be decreasing, clouds breaking apart,” said meteorologist Sarah Wrobleski on Friday morning. “But temperatures will fall from the mid-50s into the upper 40s, and we’ll have a breezy wind, too.” That wind is projected to bring gusts of up to 24 mph, which could create challenging patterns inside the Patriots’ home arena. As a reminder, the two teams have had some kicking issues so far this season: New England’s Andy Borregales has made 30 of his 34 combined field goal and extra points (88.2%), with Green Bay’s Trey Smack at only 27-for-35 (77.2%) — giving him the lowest success rate in the league. Similar projections are also shared by other outlets such as NFL Weather or the National Weather Service . If those turn out to be accurate, Sunday would become the Patriots’ coldest contest of the season so far. It would also be the first to see temperatures drop into the 40s over the course of the game.

title: Drake Maye’s early-season turnaround earns him October honors
summary: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. The award comes after Maye led the Patriots to a 3-1 record, completing 67.2% of his passes for 1,199 yards, 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions. He also added 129 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Maye became […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots throws a pass against the Miami Dolphins during the first half of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was named AFC Offensive Player of the Month for October. The award comes after Maye led the Patriots to a 3-1 record, completing 67.2% of his passes for 1,199 yards, 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions. He also added 129 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Maye became the first Patriot to earn the honor since Tom Brady during the 2017 season. “That’s something to be proud of for Drake,” Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. “I always look at those things as team achievements. Certainly nobody’s going to win an individual award in football without all the guys that do their jobs around him. I think you celebrate that as a group. “He’s certainly deserving of it, and a lot of credit to him for just kind of improving as September finished and got into the next month of the season. A lot of little things he did better, and hopefully we can continue to do that.” It marked a significant turnaround for Maye after the 24-year-old struggled to open the season. The quarterback was perhaps the biggest reason the Patriots found themselves with a 1-2 record through the first three weeks, throwing just one touchdown against six interceptions. Improved ball security has been one of the biggest factors in Maye’s resurgence. He has thrown just one interception over the last four weeks, while his 1.2% turnover-worthy play rate in October ranked third among qualified quarterbacks. Additionally, Maye’s trademark deep ball has returned despite the Patriots losing several of their top pass catchers to injuries, while has has operated as one of the league’s better quarterbacks when dealing with pressure. “He has worked really diligently for two years now on becoming a better passer from the pocket,” McDaniels said. “Everybody talks about how his athleticism is, and it’s great, and he made another great play outside the pocket last week. But I’d say he’d probably be more excited about the one that he slid to the right and climbed up into the pocket, and makes the throw down the field to Kyle [Williams]. So I think he’s worked really hard at it. “I think it’s repetition and I think it’s confidence in the protections. I think that’s where it stems from.” Maye’s November started strong as well as he scored three total touchdowns to lead a come from behind win in Miami. The quarterback will look to keep things going against the Green Bay Packers this Sunday.

title: Patriots rooting guide for NFL Week 9
summary: And just like that it’s November. In football terms, this means the real season is about to start. full_text: And just like that it’s November. In football terms, this means the real season is about to start. For the New England Patriots, it starts with a game against the Green Bay Packers at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday. There are 14 other contests on the menu this weekend, however, so let’s find out who to root for in the non-Patriots games. Thursday 8:15 p.m. ET Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) at Baltimore Ravens (4-4) : Go Ravens! Baltimore is down to its third-string quarterback, and even he is banged up. It would take a lot for them to win, but that’s precisely what we are rooting for on Thursday night. | Prime Video Sunday 9:30 a.m. ET Cincinnati Bengals ( 5-2 ) at Atlanta Falcons (3-5) : Go Falcons! It’s your classic AFC-vs.-NFC matchups that naturally has us rooting for the NFC side. | NFL Network 1 p.m. ET Denver Broncos (6-2) at Carolina Panthers (3-4): Go Panthers! Same reason as above. We are picking the NFC team over the AFC team. | CBS Dallas Cowboys ( 3-5 ) at Indianapolis Colts (2-6) : Go Cowboys! The Colts’ season is spiritually over already, and they are headed into a major rebuilding process. Still, as long as there is a theoretical chance they could go on a run, it’s better to be save than sorry. | FOX New York Jets (2-6) at Kansas City Chiefs ( 5-2 ) : Go Jets! The Patriots have a major advantage over their division rivals already, both in total standings and head-to-head, so rooting for them over the Chiefs makes the most sense with the playoff picture in mind. | CBS Detroit Lions ( 5-2 ) at Miami Dolphins (1-6) : Go Lions! The Patriots’ Week 10 opponent visiting their Week 8 opponent has us rooting for the NFC team. We are not quite yet in “let’s mess up their draft position territory” yet, but we will be getting there soon one would imagine. | CBS Cleveland Browns (5-3) at New Orleans Saints (2-5) : Go Saints! Another clear-as-day pick that has us go with the NFC team over the AFC team. | CBS New York Giants (4-2-1) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-6) : Go good game! This matters not from a Patriots point of view. | FOX Los Angeles Rams ( 4-4 ) at Washington Commanders (2-4-1) : Go good game! This game also has no direct impact on New England. | FOX 4:05 p.m. ET Houston Texans (2-5) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) : Go Chargers! There are two reasons to be rooting for the Chargers’ first win of the season: to keep the Texans at two wins and to help New England’s sixth-round draft pick that was acquired in the Marte Mapu trade. A win-win. | CBS 4:25 p.m. ET Arizona Cardinals ( 3-5 ) at Seattle Seahawks ( 4-4 ) : Go Seahawks! This pick comes down to the Patriots’ strength of schedule tiebreaker. | FOX Las Vegas Raiders ( 4-4 ) at San Francisco 49ers (6-1) : Go 49ers! While this would hurt said tiebreaker, we are rooting for the NFC over the AFC team here. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Tampa Bay Buccaneers ( 3-5 ) at Chicago Bears ( 6-2 ) : Go Bears! Once again we are back at strength of schedule. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET Minnesota Vikings (6-1) at Buffalo Bills (6-1): Go Vikings! In a week of many easy picks, this might be the easiest. If the Patriots want to defend their AFC East crown, they need the Bills to lose some non-head-to-head games. This looks like a potential candidate, despite the Vikings’ high probability of being a paper tiger at the end of the day. | ESPN/ABC

title: Patriots trade deadline 2026: News and rumors tracker
summary: Even though they have already matched their total losses from last year, the New England Patriots once again look like a legitimate contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. However, in order to get there, they will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that have ravaged their roster over the first […]
full_text: Even though they have already matched their total losses from last year, the New England Patriots once again look like a legitimate contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. However, in order to get there, they will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that have ravaged their roster over the first two months of the regular season. While the expectation is that they will get several players back from injured reserve at some point, they also could go for a more radical approach in hopes of improving their team and gearing up for a stretch run in 2026. Like they have done multiple times in 2026 already, they could look at the trade market. Will there be additions to a list that already includes the likes of A.J. Brown, Jaylen Reed, Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse? Or could they move on from some of their players, like they did in 2025 ? We will know soon: the NFL trade deadline is coming up on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET. Until then, please make sure to bookmark and regularly revisit our Patriots trade deadline tracker for all the latest developments. Patriots trades TBD Patriots trade rumors 2026 Latest rumors at the top. The Patriots are “lurking” in the wide receiver trade market ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline. They currently have four wide receivers on their active roster, but with A.J. Brown nursing a knee injury could benefit from more depth. Some of it will come in the form of Mack Hollins, with Romeo Doubs expected to return from IR after the Week 11 bye. | Report The Patriots are not actively shopping Christian Barmore or Carlton Davis. title: A.J. Brown knee injury ‘raises some concerns’ about Patriots future
summary: The New England Patriots trading first- and fourth-round draft picks to the Philadelphia Eagles for wide receiver A.J. Brown was a gamble. On the one hand, he was a proven No. 1 wide receiver capable of adding a new level of playmaking ability to what was one of the best offenses in football in 2025. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots trading first- and fourth-round draft picks to the Philadelphia Eagles for wide receiver A.J. Brown was a gamble. On the one hand, he was a proven No. 1 wide receiver capable of adding a new level of playmaking ability to what was one of the best offenses in football in 2025. On the other hand, he was heading into his age-29 season off of his least productive season in four years. Eight weeks into the season, the gamble has not paid off. Brown has appeared in just three games so far, catching nine passes for 101 yards. A bigger concern than his output, however, is his injury situation. Not only did he spend four games on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain, he also is currently dealing with a knee injury that has forced him to miss four straight practices and last Sunday’s win in Miami. While that knee injury has not prompted another move to IR, Brown’s short-term availability has been impacted. And beyond that, there are questions about his long-term outlook as well as addressed by ESPN’s Adam Schefter on Thursday morning. “Let’s go back to the offseason, when Philadelphia was shopping A.J. Brown and they were talking to teams,” Schefter said. “One of the reasons that I believe there wasn’t more interest was there were some teams that had some questions about his knee. In fact, when they were advanced discussions for a trade with the Los Angeles Rams that was at one point close to being completed … I think the Rams had some concerns about his knee. The concerns that other teams have had have now manifested themselves in New England this season. “It flared up. … The knee held him out last week, and the knee is threatening to hold him out this week. It’s a knee that I think raises some concerns as to how long he’s going to keep playing here in New England, and producing at a high level.” More Here: pic.twitter.com/qJbKrjlrr4 — Carlos A. Lopez (@LosTalksPats) November 5, 2026 Worries about Brown’s knee are nothing new. Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf himself spoke about them earlier this year. “It’s a factor, but we examined him,” Wolf said back in June. “He’s got a knee that has some wear and tear that we were aware of. Our training staff and medical staff signed off on it.” Regardless of his current availability issues, the Patriots moving on from Brown in the near future is not expected. His contract structure alone would likely prevent such a move from happening: if released next offseason, for example, New England would take on a dead cap charge of almost $26 million. For the time being, though, Brown remains with the Patriots and part of their 53-man roster. How quickly he can return to the field will be seen, though; one line of thinking is that he might be kept out through the team’s trip to Germany next week and into the Week 11 bye to get fully ready for the stretch run. Whether he will be, only time will tell.

full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Kindle Vildor (28) looks on against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second quarter at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A veteran of 85 NFL games has returned to Gillette Stadium to fill the open spot on the practice squad. The New England Patriots officially re-signed cornerback Kindle Vildor to the 17-man scout team on Thursday after he had been released from the 53-man roster earlier in the week. Vildor, 28, first made his way to Foxborough on a one-year contract as an unrestricted free agent in March. The 5-foot-11, 190-pound vested corner intercepted a pass in preseason action before beginning the regular season on the practice squad. After serving as a standard elevation for the 29-26 AFC East upset of the Buffalo Bills, he was promoted to the active roster and earned a game ball from head coach Mike Vrabel following the 45-17 rout of the Las Vegas Raiders. In all, Vildor has appeared in five games this fall while notching seven tackles, including one for loss, as well as one forced fumble and one pass deflection. His stay spans 53 snaps on defense to go with 32 snaps on special teams. New England currently carries Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis III, Marcus Jones, Charles Woods, Channing Canada and Karon Prunty on the active cornerback depth chart, while the midweek re-signing joins Al’zillion Hamilton on the practice squad. Entering the NFL with the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall, Vildor has also made stops with Tennessee Titans, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. A 27-game starter during his time in the league, the Georgia Southern product has recorded 147 tackles, one sack, two forced fumbles and two interceptions through 2,158 snaps on defense and 605 snaps on special teams. After safety Elliott Davison cleared waivers and circled back, one spot remained vacant on the practice squad. The Green Bay Packers visit Gillette Stadium on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

title: Bill Belichick again nominated for Pro Football Hall of Fame after controversial 2026 omission
summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame is one step closer to righting some wrongs. After its selection committee controversially decided against longtime New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick in his first year of eligibility, the 74-year-old is now nominated for induction for a second year. Belichick is one of five former coaches announced as […]
full_text: The Pro Football Hall of Fame is one step closer to righting some wrongs. After its selection committee controversially decided against longtime New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick in his first year of eligibility, the 74-year-old is now nominated for induction for a second year. Belichick is one of five former coaches announced as nominees by the Hall of Fame on Thursday. He is joined by Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan. Belichick spent time in Baltimore, Detroit and Denver before joining the New York Giants in 1979. He eventually helped the team win two Super Bowls as its defensive coordinator before departing for the Cleveland Browns. He later had stints with the Patriots and Jets before returning to New England via trade in 2000. With Belichick at the helm, the Patriots won a combined 69% 0f their regular season and playoff games between 2000 and 2023. A three-time NFL Coach of the Year winner, he left the organization with six Super Bowl wins, nine conference championships and 17 division titles under his belt. Including his tenure with the Browns, he ranks second all-time in NFL coaching wins with 333 and first with 31 postseason victories. Under normal circumstances, Belichick should be seen as the clear favorite to emerge past the next round of voting and eventually earn the famous golden jacket in the summer of 2027. However, as the 2026 voting process showed, anything is possible. In arguably the most controversial decision in the institution’s history, Belichick did not garner enough votes to clear the final hurdle — a decision that drew heavy criticism and raised questions about the integrity of the vote and those making the decisions. In the aftermath, the Hall of Fame announced sweeping changes to its process . The next step in Belichick’s Hall of Fame journey will come Nov. 17, when the committee will decide on one finalist to be presented to the full selection committee. The final vote will take place in early 2027, with the eventual Pro Football Hall of Fame class announced in the lead-up to the Super Bowl. Also among this year’s nominees is Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who is one of five contributors still in the running.

title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 9 preview vs. the Browns
summary: Coming out of the bye week, the New Orleans Saints made some needed changes, and now they have to show that a real impact was made. The rookies can make that happen. WR Jordyn Tyson Finally, it’s time for Tyson’s debut. Right away, Tyson’s addition to the team will massively help the offense. It takes […]
full_text: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 13: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints participates in drills during a joint practice at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on August 13, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming out of the bye week, the New Orleans Saints made some needed changes, and now they have to show that a real impact was made. The rookies can make that happen. WR Jordyn Tyson Finally, it’s time for Tyson’s debut. Right away, Tyson’s addition to the team will massively help the offense. It takes pressure away from Chris Olave, allows Tyler Shough to have yet another incredible weapon, adds the threat of a dynamic player after the catch, and could open up the run game. The issue is it won’t solve the run game issues. The Saints will have a lot of work to do on the offensive side of the ball, and although Tyson’s addition helps, it will be for nothing if the rushing attack and offensive line continue with their struggles. DT Christen Miller Out of the bye week, there is absolutely no reason for Christen Miller to be benched. He is the future at the Saints’ defensive tackle spot; he should be the best run defender as well. He will develop with reps. Even if the Saints end up not starting him, he should be playing way more snaps than he has so far. It’s time to see what the Saints have in their second-round pick. TE Oscar Delp Similar to Miller, Delp must be elevated to a larger role in the offense. He has primarily been utilized as a blocker, which has created a tell in the offense. Trying to play on that and trick the Browns could be reallt smart, and a way to do that is by using Delp as a receiver more. Noah Fant hasn’t been bad this season, but Delp should be TE2 moving forward. OG Jeremiah Wright News on Cesar Ruiz’s injury has not been released yet, so it’s unknown if Wright is going play, but if he does, good luck to him. The Browns defensive line is very good and it’s going to be his biggest test yet. He wasn’t horrible against the Steelers, but it was also not good and he looked like a rookie out there. That’s the expectation, but the Saints will need to see more from him against the Browns. WR Bryce Lance With Tyson’s return, it’s going to be interesting to see how the Saints use Lance. He will now be WR4/5 with Barion Brown, and although his involvement in the passing game will likely drop, his blocking is too important to not use. Also, special teams may be an option for him. WR Barion Brown Recently, Brown has been more involved in the offense, and it has had a positive impact. Like with Lance, Brown’s role will likely be reduced in the passing game, but I wouldn’t be shocked to see him utilized as a deep play threat throughout games. Then on special teams, he has been better recently, which is definitely nice to see for New Orleans. RB CJ Donaldson CJ Donaldson is in a weird situation. He has had some good runs and great blocks, but not consistently, and although Kendre Miller may be traded soon, the Saints signed Audric Estime. Estime is very similar to Donaldson so that’s bad news for the rookie. OT Mason Murphy It seems like Kelvin Banks Jr. is on his way back, so Murphy’s chances of starting become even lower. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Similar as always, Styles will likely stick with the special teams unit, but it will be interesting to see what happens if Justin Reid gets traded.

title: Our Offense vs. Their Defense: Cleveland Browns
summary: The New Orleans Saints are returning to action after a bye week with more questions than they had to start the season. Now, this matchup with the Browns serves as a litmus test for the changes that were made during the bye, not just for the coaching staff but for the entire organization. This game […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints scrambles with the ball under pressure from Charlie Jones #89 of the New York Giants during the second quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are returning to action after a bye week with more questions than they had to start the season. Now, this matchup with the Browns serves as a litmus test for the changes that were made during the bye, not just for the coaching staff but for the entire organization. This game against the Browns is a really intriguing matchup for the offense because this defense is exactly what the Saints need to face right now. The Browns’ biggest weakness on defense is rushing yards allowed. Cleveland ranks 24th in rushing defense in the NFL, surrendering 126.9 yards per game and 4.68 yards per carry. Just last week against the Steelers, the Browns allowed 200 rushing yards. Everyone knows the Saints have had issues running the ball, and now, with C.J. Donaldson suffering an injury, that only compounds their rushing problems. But there may be some hope after all. The Saints have added Audric Estime back to the roster, claiming him off waivers. Estime showed a lot of promise at the end of last season, when the Saints were struggling to run the ball, and throughout the preseason. It caught a lot of people off guard when the Saints opted to release him before the season started, but he’s back now and will be a welcome addition come Sunday afternoon for an offense that is averaging only 86 rushing yards per game and ranks 28th in the NFL. Running the ball will be very important in this game because if the Saints become one-dimensional, it will play right into the hands of the Browns. Cleveland currently has the sixth-best defense against the pass, allowing only 196 yards per game. The Browns have been so successful in pass coverage because they have an elite interior pass rush. Mason Graham, Maliek Collins, and Adin Huntington have combined for 11 sacks. Quarterbacks cannot step up into the pocket against this defensive front, and there is consistent pressure off the edge from Isaiah McGuire, who has 3 sacks, and Jared Verse. Verse has 0 sacks right now, but he is still an edge rusher the Saints have to be aware of. The Saints are averaging only 229 passing yards per game, which ranks 14th in the NFL. If the Saints get into the red zone, they have to convert. Cleveland allows touchdowns on 73.9% of opponents’ red-zone opportunities, while the Saints are converting only 52.2% of theirs. While Jordyn Tyson is trying to make his way back onto the playing field, Chris Olave remains one of the best receivers in the league. Over the past few weeks, his production has dipped a bit because of the attention he receives, and this week will be no different. Kellen Moore will have to find creative ways to get him open because Olave will be matched up against Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell. The Browns’ cornerbacks are very physical, and Moore will have to find ways to counter that. To win this game, the Saints will have to run the ball against this weak run defense and keep the offense balanced. They have to commit to a decent number of rushing attempts. This will help slow down Cleveland’s pass rush. The Browns have 21 sacks, with 11 coming from the interior. Run at them and slow down their pass rush! The Saints have allowed 15 sacks so far this season, and Tyler Shough is already fighting through broken bones in his non-throwing hand. Run the ball, protect Tyler Shough, and get creative. Design plays that get your playmakers in space and work in concert with the running game. Use motions, shifts into different formations, and heavy run-action plays. Make this defense play with its eyes and not its instincts. Will the Saints come out of this game looking like they have improved, or will it just be more of the same? Hopefully, the changes that were made will lead to better results this week. How do you think the Saints’ offense will handle this Browns defense? Do you feel good about the changes that were made during the bye week?

title: Giants-Eagles matchup: How does QB Joe Milton change the equation?
summary: The 4-2-1 New York Giants travel to Philadelphia this weekend to face the 2–6 Philadelphia Eagles, who enter the matchup on a six-game losing streak. Philadelphia is coming off a disappointing 27–10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football in Week 8. Things are unraveling in Philadelphia. The Eagles are dealing with a […]
full_text: Joe Milton | Getty Images The 4-2-1 New York Giants travel to Philadelphia this weekend to face the 2–6 Philadelphia Eagles, who enter the matchup on a six-game losing streak. Philadelphia is coming off a disappointing 27–10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football in Week 8. Things are unraveling in Philadelphia. The Eagles are dealing with a rash of injuries and have switched from quarterback Tanner McKee to Joe Milton. Head coach Nick Sirianni is facing mounting questions from the media about offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, while general manager Howie Roseman has traded valuable assets in exchange for draft capital. To put it simply, things are far from sunny in Philadelphia. Still, the Eagles will look to defend their home turf against a Giants franchise that hasn’t won at Lincoln Financial Field since 2013. New York enters the matchup well-rested after its bye week, presenting an opportunity to snap that frustrating losing streak. And with the John Harbaugh era bringing a different identity and renewed expectations to the Giants, this team may finally have what it takes to change the narrative. Eagles’ statistics The Eagles’ offense has struggled all season. Philadelphia ranks 30th in the league in points per game, with an average of just 17.1 points. They’re 29th in total yards (2,122 yards), 32nd in yards per game (265 yards), and they’re last in yards per play ( 4.4 YPP ). Philadelphia ranks 24th in passing yards per game ( 196.4 ) and 27th in rushing yards per game ( 88.1 ). They have a 37.3% third-down conversion rate, which ranks 26th in the league. Tanner McKee has completed 63.2% of his passes for 638 yards with a pair of touchdowns and interceptions. Joe Milton, though, poses a much different skill set that the Giants must account for. DeVonta Smith has missed a handful of games, including the loss to Washington last week; he still leads the team with 310 receiving yards. Saquon Barkley is hobbled and played on a pitch count last week. He leads the Eagles with 274 rushing yards ( 4.9 YPC ), with two rushing touchdowns. Elijah Mitchell is the backup running back with Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, and Dameon Pierce all on injured reserve. Eagles’ personnel Milton played three seasons at Michigan dating back to 2018 before he transferred to Tennessee. He threw for 2,813 yards with 20 touchdowns and five interceptions and a 64.7% completion rate in Josh Heupel’s offense back in 2023; he also rushed for 299 yards and seven touchdowns that year. Milton spent time with the Patriots, Cowboys, and now the Eagles. Saquon Barkley played 32% of the snaps in Week 8. He touched the football often in his limited snaps over the last two weeks – he played 15% of snaps in Week 7. Mitchell is the primary backup now, and Jaydon Blue played 12% of snaps last week. The running situation – including the push up front from the line – has been poor. Smith missed the last two weeks, and the two weeks prior to Week 6. Dontayvion Wicks hasn’t played since Week 6. It’s been the rookies, Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper, who have played more than 90% of the snaps over the last two weeks. Both players have flashed. Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore were the only other two wide receivers to play snaps against Washington, who operated heavier personnel packages without Smith. Tight end Dallas Goedert played 80% of the snaps, as Johnny Mundt and Eli Stowers both played 19% of snaps. Grant Calcaterra played 17% of snaps. Jordan Mailata is the starting left tackle with rookie Markel Bell starting on the right side; Lane Johnson retired a few weeks ago, forcing Bell into the starting lineup. Tyler Steen mans the right guard spot, with Landon Dickerson playing left guard; Dickerson has been playing through a pectoral injury. Drew Kendall is the starting center now that Cam Jurgens is no longer an Eagle after he was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. The matchup Starting Milton could provide the Eagles with a spark. The 6-foot-5, 245-pound quarterback is an excellent athlete with a howitzer arm, but he’s bounced around practice squads and hasn’t found consistency yet. Still, his mobility and strength in the pocket could allow him to escape the Giants’ rush. It’s an exciting move for Philadelphia — all things considered — but he’s never proven consistent with timing, accuracy, and other nuances of the quarterback position, albeit he’s just 26 years old. New York has blitzed at a 36.6% rate this season, which ranks second only behind the Minnesota Vikings. I expect the Giants to dial up the pressure against the young quarterback, with a heavy middle-of-the-field closed approach. The Eagles have struggled offensively, but the Giants must focus on stopping Barkley when he is on the field. The Giants can run man-to-man situational defense and focus on Cover-3, with a focus on stopping the run. Adjustments to middle-of-the-field-open defenses will happen in third-and-long situations. Fire-zone blitzes and a pre-snap loaded line of scrimmage should be employed in an attempt to force mistakes from the young quarterback. New York’s cornerbacks should press up on the line if Philadelphia attempts to run quick game often, as plenty of teams have attempted to run against the Giants. If pressure starts to get home on Milton and New York establishes a lead, the Giants can sit comfortably in zone to force check-downs underneath, as Washington did at the end of their win against Philadelphia. If Philadelphia leans on more 12 personnel, especially with Eli Stowers, how do the Giants respond? Base or Nickel? Since New York will likely want to stop the run, they may respond with a heavier base package – five-man front. Philadelphia may look to try and get Stowers isolated against a linebacker or safety in those heavier tight end packages. The Eagles’ offensive line has been susceptible in both pass protection and as run blockers, relative to what we’re accustomed to seeing every year. The Giants have to maintain the level of knock-back and physicality that they had against Houston. If they can do that, the Giants shouldn’t have a problem winning the game. Final thoughts The Giants are the better football team. Still, winning in Philadelphia hasn’t been an easy venture for the Giants. I believe they get over the hump and win convincingly in Philadelphia. Pick: 30-13, Giants.
