full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get ready to face the Eagles in Philadelphia this Sunday. John Harbaugh ’ s Giants take aim at ending 13-game nightmare in Philly | The Record This is inherited franchise history for John Harbaugh and the 2026 New York Giants, not earned. But it’s notable history nonetheless, resurfacing every time the Giants’ buses hit the Turnpike and travel to what has become a house of horrors for this organization. The head coaches have changed. The players have changed. So have the circumstances. Giants are Must-See TV "The Giants are football." @isaacrochell91 explains what he loves about watching the @Giants 🙌 pic.twitter.com/7dDcY9lblb — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) November 5, 2026 Mike Lupica: J.J. McCarthy has a Giant shot to flip the script on the Eagles | New York Daily News The Eagles were supposed to win the NFC again. If they were going to fight for the title in the division, it was supposed to be with the Cowboys. Now those teams have a combined record of 5-11 and the Giants are talking about being buyers at the trade deadline instead of sellers, maybe even with Jonathan Taylor, one of the star running backs of the league, for a long time. For now, it starts with McCarthy, clearly sold and mightily by one Harbaugh to another. Twenty-three years old. Giving Giants fans the kind of hope that J. Dart did last season. With a chance to be as great an in-season acquisition as the Giants have ever had if he keeps going like this, and if they keep going. Door wide open for the Michigan kid, and his coach, and his new team. They just have to make sure the Eagles don’t slam it in their faces on Sunday. New York Giants believe Dominic Zvada is ‘long-term answer’ at kicker | USAToday.com John Harbaugh reaffirmed his confidence in kicker Dominic Zvada on Wednesday, saying the New York Giants are looking for consistent results but are not concerned about the position. The coach noted that the staff continues to evaluate technique and fundamentals, with the clear expectation that kicks will travel straight through the uprights. “We’re looking for kicks to go between the sticks, right through the upright, straight. Looking for straight kicks,” Harbaugh told reporters. “But you’re also looking at the technique and the fundamentals, but we’re not worried about him.” What 18 contenders should do at the NFL trade deadline: Who could get aggressive? | ESPN.com Luxury target: Taylor might cost too much for a New York squad that’s already down its fourth- and fifth-round picks in the 2027 draft, but what about Derrick Henry? If the Ravens decide their season is up without Lamar Jackson on the field, Henry could be a potential trade candidate. He’s owed only $650,000 over the rest of 2026 and $12 million in 2027. And while the future Hall of Famer has struggled for most of the season, playing with a more mobile quarterback in McCarthy might help create some running lanes. Bargain target: With the Chargers still winless, Harbaugh could call up former Ravens executive Joe Hortiz (and brother Jim Harbaugh) and attempt to make a move for Dalvin Tomlinson. The well-traveled defensive tackle has slipped as a pass rusher from his 2020-24 peak, but Tomlinson would be a rotational player for a Giants team that’s barely getting by on the interior. NFL Trade Deadline: Biggest needs for all 32 teams | PFF New York Giants: Defensive Interior. Given how they have played early in the season and the Philadelphia Eagles‘ struggles, the Giants have a serious chance of winning the NFC East. Since it is John Harbaugh’s first year in New York, they probably shouldn’t mortgage the future to get better this season, but they could add someone next to DJ Reader on the defensive line. Reader has earned a 90.4 PFF grade to lead all interior defensive linemen so far this season, but he is their only player at the position to have played at least 50 snaps and earned a PFF grade above 55.0. Isaiah Likely on trade rumors Isaiah Likely was asked about the trade deadline: "The more the merrier when it comes to great players" pic.twitter.com/aiHvGRVuJE — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) November 5, 2026 Giants must be aggressive, not reckless in 2026 NFL trade deadline pursuits | SNY.tv External NFL sources, not from within the Giants building, vary in whether they believe a Taylor trade actually gets done. Several sources SNY touched base with are hellbent in their conviction that Harbaugh will do whatever he can to get him, seeing an opportunity for New York to make a run. Others, familiar with what the Colts are asking for, believe the price is so steep Indianapolis isn’t actually interested in dealing him. He’ll remain with them throughout this season, with a trade revisited in March. Still, their stance to this point is the right one. Do everything you can to help your team accomplish that … within reason. They shouldn’t waver. Harbaugh must fight the temptation to do more over the coming week. title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 9 preview — Start/sit and more
summary: Welcome to Week 9. Somehow, we are already at the halfway point of the 18-week NFL season. That was fast. Week 8 was strange. Tampa beat Atlanta 16-0 without completing a single pass. Dallas and Kansas City both blew double-digit fourth quarter leads. Joe Burrow accounted for six total touchdowns. Running backs absolutely ran wild […]
full_text: Running Wild! | Getty Images Welcome to Week 9. Somehow, we are already at the halfway point of the 18-week NFL season. That was fast. Week 8 was strange. Tampa beat Atlanta 16-0 without completing a single pass. Dallas and Kansas City both blew double-digit fourth quarter leads. Joe Burrow accounted for six total touchdowns. Running backs absolutely ran wild on Sunday. Baltimore lost two quarterbacks to what might be season-ending injuries in the first half at Buffalo. Minnesota held Detroit to its lowest point total of the season, but also scored the fewest against them, and absorbed its first loss. The Giants grew their NFC East lead without playing. It was that kind of weekend – eerie and weird — kind of fitting for Halloween. What’s in store this week? Six teams – Philadelphia, Seattle, Baltimore, Minnesota, fCleveland, and Arizona – are switching to a different starting quarterback. That raises a bunch of questions and decisions for fantasy managers. Stats of the Week, Bucs-Falcons (sorry, this HAS TO get its own section – one day you’ll tell your grandkids about that time in 2026 when two NFL teams played a high school football game): Tampa became the first team since 1974, and the third since the forward pass was invented in the 1930s, to win a game without completing a single pass. Tampa is the first team in NFL history to have two players (Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell) with 25+ rushes and 125+ rushing yards in the same game. Tampa’s defenders caught four more passes than Tampa’s offensive players. Despite not completing a pass, and rushing for just 14 yards with no TDs, Baker Mayfield had more fantasy points than, and triple the passer rating of, Michael Penix, Jr. Over their past two games (both wins, with 59 total points scored), the Bucs called 16 passes and 104 runs, and Baker Mayfield had seven completions for 64 yards. Stats of the Week, Everyone Else No team in AFC North is over .500. Every team in the NFC North is over .500. Every team in the NFC South is under .500. The NFC North is a combined 22-3 in non-divisional games. Bo Nix has engineered 13 fourth quarter comebacks – the most in NFL history for a quarterback in his first three seasons. Since the start of last season, the Broncos are 3-3 in games where they trailed by 11+ points during the fourth quarter. The rest of the NFL is 11-215 in such situations. For the first time since 2003, six running backs had at least 140 rushing yards on Sunday. The Browns have lost 23 straight games in Pittsburgh, which ties the NFL record for a road losing streak vs. one team. The Bears have 17 rushing touchdowns, which is the most for a team through their first eight games since 1956. Since 2000, Arizona was 1-147-1 when trailing by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter, and Dallas was 69-0 at home when leading by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter. That all changed on Sunday with the Cardinals’ late comeback. On to Week 9. Note: CIN @ ATL is being played in Spain. Set those lineups early! Bye Weeks: PIT, TEN Week 9 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start Joe Burrow . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did well, with a lot more hits than misses. You can check my work here. My biggest miss was my Ride of the Week, Zay Flowers. He scored zero points. I’ll repeat that – A bagel. A donut. Zero point zero. I obviously couldn’t foresee the quarterback injuries, but I’ll take the L. My Fade of the Week hit (Bryce Young, 11.4 fantasy points, QB18) and so did my Sleeper of the Week (Geno Smith, 19 fantasy points, QB13). *** Ride of the Week: Matthew Stafford (@WAS). Stafford is ranked outside the Top-10 QBs this week and I think that’s too low. The Commanders can score behind Jayden Daniels and they also give up points. This game’s Vegas total of 50.5 is the second highest on the board and I think it goes over. Washington is tough to run on, but generous in the passing game. They’re one of seven teams that has allowed at least 15 TD passes so far this season, and they’ve given up the third most fantasy points per game (FPPG) to opposing QBs. Stafford is coming off his second worst fantasy output of the season and I think he’ll rebound. He came out of last week’s game with a sore elbow, so keep an eye on that. Fade of the Week: Zay Flowers (vs. JAC). Well, this is a first for me, as Flowers goes from Ride of the Week to Fade of the Week in just five days. UDFA rookie Joe Fagnano gets his first NFL start for the Ravens, on a short week and a bad ankle. If the Ravens get to ten points, I’ll be surprised. Their implied total is 15, which is the second lowest on the Board, and they haven’t topped 13 points in any of their last three games. Jacoby Brissett will help – in Week 10. Jacksonville’s defense must be licking its chops after it throttled another dead team last week. Flowers is a terrific receiver who was having a great season before last Sunday, but this QB situation is too much to overcome. He’s ranked inside the Top-20 at the position this week and I have him outside my Top-30. Sleeper of the Week: Drew Lock (vs. ARI) . The Cardinals are coming off that improbable comeback in Dallas, while Seattle will look to rebound after getting spanked by the Bears at home. This should be a get-right game for the Seahawks, and a potential let-down affair for the Cardinals (who had a let-down two weeks ago, after their big upset win over the Rams in Week 6). Seattle may struggle to run the ball against a defense that just stymied Javonte Williams. Arizona has allowed the most TD passes (18) and second most FPPG to opposing QBs. Lock is ranked as the QB29 this week, which is absurd. He’s behind Fagnano, Gardner Minshew II, and Shedeur Sanders? No. None of them have JSN to throw to. Obviously, he shouldn’t be started over a Top-12 option, but I like him as a QB2 this week. In his only start of the season in Week 2, he put up 21 fantasy points at…you guessed it…Arizona. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Josh Allen , Lamar, Drake Maye, Brock Purdy, Jared Goff, and Joe Burrow ; the analysis starts below them. Rides: Three QBs ranked in the Top-10 this week who should smash: Dak Prescott (@IND). The Colts have given up, or at least, they don’t have the ability to compete at the moment. Dak should have his way with this mediocre defense, which has allowed the tenth most FPPG to opposing QBs. Dallas can’t afford another stupid loss. Trevor Lawrence (@BAL). The Ravens have a decent defense that’s middle of the pack against opposing QBs, but there’s almost no scenario where they don’t lose this game by a lot. Their offense won’t be able to stay on the field, so Lawrence should have plenty of scoring chances. Patrick Mahomes (vs. NYJ). Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three TDs at Denver, to break a mini-cold streak and this week he gets a much softer defense, at home. Kenneth Walker might run wild, but I think Mahomes will get his too. The Jets have allowed 14 TD passes this season and have only one pick (ahem, that’s since the start of last season). title: NY Giants cut QB Jake Haener, work out four veterans
summary: The New York Giants have cut backup quarterback Jake Haener on Thursday. Haener, 27, joined the Giants late in the summer following Brandon Allen’s poor performance in the preseason. The two battled to be the Giants third quarterback behind Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston, and the Giants ultimately chose Haener. Haener was cut in the […]
full_text: Jake Haener | Getty Images The New York Giants have cut backup quarterback Jake Haener on Thursday. Haener, 27, joined the Giants late in the summer following Brandon Allen’s poor performance in the preseason. The two battled to be the Giants third quarterback behind Jaxson Dart and Jameis Winston, and the Giants ultimately chose Haener. Haener was cut in the Giants’ final cuts down to their initial 53-man roster, but was signed to their practice squad. He served as the Giants’ primary backup behind Jameis Winston immediately after Jaxson Dart’s injury and when J.J. McCarthy was still learning the Giants’ offense. He’s since reverted to being the Giants’ 3rd quarterback once McCarthy was elevated to the starting job. Haener will likely be signed to the Giants’ practice squad. The move to cut Haener opens a roster spot which could be used by RB Eric Gray or WR Jalin Hyatt following the recent hand injury suffered by returner/receiver Charlie Jones . Jones was seen trying to field punts one-handed in practice, which reportedly didn’t go well. The Giants also worked out a quartet of veterans on Thursday. WR/KR Steven Sims – Sims is a wide receiver and kick returner who has played for the Washignton Commanders (2019-2020), Buffalo Bills (2021 – offseason), Pittsburgh Steelers (2021-2022), Houston Texans (2023-2024), Baltimore Ravens (2024), Seattle Seahawks (2025 – offseason), Arizona Cardinals (2025) WR/KR Maurice Alexander – Alexander is a former undrafted free agent out of Florida International who has played for the USFL Philadelphia Stars (2022), Detroit Lions (2022 – 2024), Chicago Bears (2025) WR River Cracraft – Cracraft is a 32-year old veteran receiver with return experience. He was an All Pac-12 player who went undrafted due to a knee injury. He’s played for the Denver Broncos (2018-2019), Philadelphia Eagles (2019 – practice squad), San Francisco 49ers (2020-2021), Miami Dolphins (2022-2024), Seattle Seahawks (2025 – offseason), Washington Commanders (2025) P Wes Pahl – Pahl, 24, played for Western Kenucky and Oklahoma State over the last four years, averaging 46.1 yards per punt on 116 punts in 52 collegiate games. He was signed by the Cleveland Browns and recently released from their practice squad.

full_text: Malik Nabers | Getty Images New York Giants wide receiver M alik Nabers , the NFC Offensive Player of the Month , missed practice on Thirsday with a knee issue. Running back Cam Skattebo missed his third straight practice on Thursday, increasing the likelihood that Skattebo will miss Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles due to a hamstring injury. Nabers missed most of the 2025 season after suffering a torn ACL. Nabers told media after practice that he would “ be good ” for Sunday. You have to believe this is a game Skattebo would very much like to play in. The Giants will be at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, the place where Skattebo suffered his season-ending ankle injury in 2025. Getting that opportunity might not, though, be in the cards for Skattebo. If Skattebo can’t play, Devin Singletary and Gregory Desrosiers are on the 53-man roster, and Phil Mafah and Eric Gray on the practice squad. “It’s going to be the utmost importance to keep the run game going,” offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said on Thursday. “You can’t be one dimensional and just be dropping back, throwing. You’ve got to be able to keep that run game going. So, no matter who’s back there with the carries, we’ve got to be efficient with the run game.” Star edge defender Abdul Carter returned to practice after sitting out Monday and Wednesday due to an illness. Charlie Jones, the Giants’ primary kickoff and punt returner as well as being a backup wide receiver, practiced on a limited basis with a hand injury. That is concerning for a player who has to catch and protect the ball. summary: Three former New York Giants head coaches headline the Coaches Subcommittee’s ballot for the 2027 Hall Of Fame class. Giants’ fans will obviously have a […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants head coach Tom Coughlin celebrates with the Vince Lombardi Trophy Three former New York Giants head coaches headline the Coaches Subcommittee’s ballot for the 2027 Hall Of Fame class. Tom Coughlin, Bill Belichick, and Dan Reeves, along with Mike Shannahan and Mike Holmgren, make up this year’s Head coach nominees for induction into the Pro Football Hall Of Fame . Giants’ fans will obviously have a soft spot for Coughlin, who was the Giants’ head coach from 2004 to 2015, winning two Super Bowls over that span. He was also the Jacksonville Jaguars’ first head coach, coaching them from 1995 to 2002. He took the Jaguars to the AFC Championship game in 1996 (their second season in existence) and again in 1999 on the strength of a 14-2 season. He was named Coach Of The Year following the 1996 season and Coughlin has the distinction of being one of just two coaches to beat fellow nominee Bill Belichick in the Super Bowl — and did so twice. Belichick was a coach for the Giants from 1979 to 1990, coaching special teams and linebackers before being named defensive coordinator by Bill Parcells in 1985. Belichick made his name as one of the NFL’s keenest defensive minds, and his gameplan from the Giants’ win over the Buffalo Bills in Super Bowl 25 is already in the Hall Of Fame. Belichick went on to be the head coach of the Cleveland Browns and New York Jets, but found almost unprecedented success with the New England Patriots. There he won six championships, tied for the most all time, but was also plagued by scandal. Dan Reeves coached the Giants from 1993 to 1996, and was named AP Coach Of The Year following the Giants’ 11-5 record. His subsequent seasons weren’t nearly as successful, but Reeves was one of the most successful coaches in NFL history. He’s one of just 13 head coaches to win (at least) 200 games between his time with the Denver Broncos (1981 to 1992), Giants (1993-1996), and Atlanta Falcons (1997 – 2003). Reeves passed away on January 1, 2022. Only one head coach can be inducted into the Hall Of Fame each year, and the former Giants’ coaches face stiff competition from Mike Holmgren and Mike Shanahan.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Giants’ DC Dennard Wilson: Too many coaches ‘scared to have hard conversations’ with players
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Before the New York Giants’ Week 7 game against the Houston Texans, defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson called out “traitors to the defense” after being unhappy with player effort on several snaps in a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints. The defense responded with an inspired effort in a 27-21 […]
full_text: Arvell Reese and the Giants’ defense responded in week 7 to Dennard Wilson’s criticism. | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Before the New York Giants’ Week 7 game against the Houston Texans, defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson called out “ traitors to the defense ” after being unhappy with player effort on several snaps in a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints. The defense responded with an inspired effort in a 27-21 victory, giving up a season-low 237 yards. “They responded in a great way,” Wilson said on Thursday. “They responded the way I knew they would respond. Obviously, we talked about watching the tape and seeing ourselves not running to the ball. “They’re a proud bunch. I really didn’t have to say much. They knew that they had to come out and they had to run to the ball and play with toughness and physicality, and that’s what we did in the game.” Wilson using such strong language to publicly criticize player effort is considered unusual in the modern game. It could have had a different result, with players who are not used to that responding in a negative manner. When I asked him if there was a risk in speaking that aggressively about players, Wilson smiled, then gave a long and revealing answer about his coaching philosophy. “I think we get too caught up into not speaking the truth,” Wilson said. “The film doesn’t lie, and it never lies. It’s always evidence. “It’s the silent tape. What I said in front of this podium, they’ve heard me say it from the first day they were here. It’s nothing that they haven’t heard before.” The Week 7 victory over Houston featured this incredible effort by rookie linebacker Arvell Reese: Dennard Wilson just raved about Arvell Reese's hustle on this play. When I spoke to Reese about it, he was mostly frustrated that he missed the sack. "I should have got a free lay-up sack. I beat the guard. I was supposed to get the sack, but I jumped. Then I'm like, 'Dang, I… — Dan Duggan (@DDuggan21) November 5, 2026 “Obviously he should have got a sack if he didn’t jump,” Wilson said. “But once he jumped and he put his foot in the ground and you saw the tenacity and the effort that he had to run to the ball, that exemplifies what a good, nasty defense should look like. And that’s like that play within itself is what everybody should strive for in defense in terms of running to the ball with that type of energy and effort.” Wilson, in his first year as Giants defensive coordinator, pointed out that in his “traitors” remarks he did not call out specific players. “It’s not calling out a specific player,” Wilson said. “It’s calling out a behavior. It’s calling out what we’re not doing collectively because at the end of the day, it’s me as well. “If I let it slip, shame on me. It’s about us upholding the standard that we set in that room that we want to exemplify on a daily basis when we go out and play. I think too many coaches these days are scared to have those hard conversations.” Coaches often talk about telling players the truth and holding them accountable. For many, in an age where players are coddled more than pushed, the John Harbaugh-led Giants coaching staff is an exception. Harbaugh and his staff are certainly not afraid to drive players hard, and to tell them the truth. The tough love, and players’ acceptance of it, is one of the reasons the Giants are 4-2-1 and have a chance to win an NFC East title for the first time since 2011. “It goes back to this. What is your relationship with the group? What is your relationship with the player?,” Wilson said. “If you build a relationship and you have this bond and you have this tight-knit group, you can speak to them in a certain way and identify certain things without attacking them personally. It’s not a personal attack. It’s a behavioral attack. “That’s how I go about it and that’s how I’ve been trained to do this since I was a young coach 20-something years ago.” Maybe that is an old-school approach. Maybe it wouldn’t work for every modern player. It certainly is working for this team, though.

title: NY Giants WR Malik Nabers named NFC Offensive Player of the Month
summary: Malik Nabers is clearly all the way back after last season’s torn ACL. The New York Giants star wide receiver has been named NFC Offensive Player of the Month after four straight 100-yard receiving games. Nabers’ streak is tied for the longest active streak in the NFL. It matches the second-longest streak in Giants history. […]
full_text: Malik Nabers | Getty Images Malik Nabers is clearly all the way back after last season’s torn ACL. The New York Giants star wide receiver has been named NFC Offensive Player of the Month after four straight 100-yard receiving games. Nabers’ streak is tied for the longest active streak in the NFL. It matches the second-longest streak in Giants history. Odell Beckham Jr. eclipsed 100 yards in four consecutive games in 2014, and then six straight outings in 2015. Nabers is the only player in the NFL this season with 500+ receiving yards and 35+ receptions in a four-game span. In four October games, Nabers had 36 receptions and 509 receiving yards, with two touchdowns. He also had eight receptions of at least 25 yards. Nabers has had 51 targets over his last four games, and his average of 10.0 targets per game is ninth in the league. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy jokingly said on Thursday that Nabers’ high volume of targets “goes to the beginning of the season when he threatened me.” Nagy, again jokingly, added that the Giants have a “fiduciary responsibility to get Malik a bunch of catches.” It’s been working. Even though opposing defenses know that is where the ball is going.

title: Can J.J. McCarthy become the NFL’s next reclamation QB — and lead the Giants to the playoffs?
summary: There is now a fairly common, if somewhat circuitous, path to quarterback success in the NFL. Get drafted high by your first NFL team, bomb out with that team for whatever reasons, wander the desert as a backup with other franchises for a while, find the right environment after all you’ve learned, and whammo — […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images There is now a fairly common, if somewhat circuitous, path to quarterback success in the NFL. Get drafted high by your first NFL team, bomb out with that team for whatever reasons, wander the desert as a backup with other franchises for a while, find the right environment after all you’ve learned, and whammo — all of a sudden, you’re a credible starting quarterback! It’s worked in the last few years for Geno Smith, Baker Mayfield, Sam Darnold, and Daniel Jones, and J.J. McCarthy may be the next name on the list. The Minnesota Vikings selected McCarthy with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 draft — in fact, they traded up to do so — and it never worked out. Between injuries and McCarthy’s own lack of development and established skills as an NFL-level prospect, it became very clear that Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell — one of the brightest offensive minds in the league, and the man who had helped to facilitate Darnold’s and Jones’ career turnarounds — would not be the one to transform McCarthy from college game manager (McCarthy’s Michigan teams were led by great defense and a powerful rushing attack) to NFL franchise guy. Which is why the Vikings traded McCarthy to the Giants on September 28 for a 2027 fifth-round pick. That’s how far McCarthy’s stock had fallen — he was the team’s third-string quarterback behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz — and the Giants were just trying to settle things at the game’s most important position after Jaxson Dart suffered meniscus and MCL injuries in his left knee in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams. Suddenly, Big Blue needed depth behind Jameis Winston, and McCarthy just needed a fresh start. That fresh start came quite unexpectedly in the Giants’ 34-27 Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints. Winston threw an interception with 12:28 left in the game, and the G-Men were down 34-10 after putting up a 10-0 early lead. Head coach John Harbaugh put McCarthy in to get some kind of spark going, not suspecting that he was unleashing something far more nuclear in nature. In less than a full fourth quarter, McCarthy completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown, one interception, and a passer rating of 90.0. He wasn’t doing this with quick throws and yards after the catch — McCarthy had several explosive downfield throws that were right on the money. J.J. McCarthy explosive passes in his entire NFL career before Sunday: 17 J.J. McCarthy explosive passes in less than one full quarter on Sunday: 4 pic.twitter.com/8m84fXUQrD — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) October 19, 2026 McCarthy made Secret Superstars in Week 6 for that performance , and he was named the starter for the Giants’ Week 7 game against the Houston Texans. DeMeco Ryans’ Texans defense is not what it was in 2025 — perhaps the NFL’s best — but it was still a serious test. Which McCarthy passed with relatively flying colors. He was eager to show off what he had learned, and McCarthy’s connection with offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, and passing game coordinator/quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan. Very few people were excited about those hires this past offseason, but it’s all worked out very well in McCarthy’s favor. Against the Texans, McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards, no touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 99.1 in a 27-21 overtime win. The Giants leaned heavily on the run game, but McCarthy was throwing darts again. Moreover, you started to see the development of the route concepts, and how they helped McCarthy do what he can at this point in his career. Not that O’Connell didn’t build concepts for his quarterbacks — of course he did — but sometimes, a new environment makes all the difference. J.J. McCarthy made some impressive downfield one-on-one throws against the @HoustonTexans , and I really liked how the @Giants ' coaches set him up with route concepts and designed openings that gave him confidence. pic.twitter.com/clOQ2KD9OJ — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) November 5, 2026 “Preparation,” McCarthy said after the Texans game, when asked how the tight-window throws have been such a big part of his recent performances. “I feel like preparation, over the years of playing football, you just refine the routine each and every week. I feel like I’m in a really good spot right now, just Monday through Saturday and just being able to have that trust in these guys as early as now, since I’ve been here. I haven’t been here long, but I trust those guys every time the ball comes out of my hand. I trust the offensive line up front. I trust the backs are going to get us in great situations when I do hit the checkdowns, but at the end of the day, it’s the players around me.” Now, the 4-2-1 Giants prepare to face a 2-6 Philadelphia Eagles team that has been an epic disappointment for all kinds of reasons, and the extent to which Vic Fangio’s defense has fallen down is truly surprising. On Tuesday, Fangio spoke about the Giants, and about McCarthy specifically. “They’ve got a really good offense. They’ve got skill at the receiving position. They did a nice job raiding the Ravens, not only for John [Harbaugh], but for [TE Isaiah] Likely and [FB Patrick] Ricard. They’ve got a lot of the Ravens-type offense that they had when Greg [Roman] was there, and they’ve intermixed Kansas City-type passing in there with Matt [Nagy]. They’ve got it going right now. They’ve got good wideouts, good tight ends, two good backs. The quarterback has come in, in a short period of time, and really done a nice job, for them to get him for a [fifth-round] pick is a steal.” If McCarthy continues to tell his own reclamation story this season, and even leads the NFC East-leading Giants to the playoffs for the first time since the 2022 season, it will open up a new chapter in his career. For now, Harbaugh and his crew will just enjoy the unexpected benefits.
author: Doug Farrar

title: NFL predictions, Week 9: Lucky 13 for NY Giants vs. Philadelphia?
summary: The New York Giants have not beaten the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field in Philly since 2013. That’s 12 straight losses on the Eagles’ home turf. Can the Giants end that streak this Sunday? Read on to see how the Big Blue View staff sees Giants-Eagles and the rest of the Week 9 slate […]
full_text: The Giants and Eagles are vastly different teams than they were a year ago. | Getty Images The New York Giants have not beaten the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field in Philly since 2013. That’s 12 straight losses on the Eagles’ home turf. Can the Giants end that streak this Sunday? Read on to see how the Big Blue View staff sees Giants-Eagles and the rest of the Week 9 slate unfolding. Chris Pflum I think I’ll always be uneasy when the Giants go on the road to play the Eagles. Weird (and generally bad) things tend to happen to the Giants at the Linc. But dare I hope that some of the smoke from burning sage and the power of Danhausen lifting the curse on the Knicks leaked from Madison Square Garden over to the Giants’ facilities this summer? The Giants are favored over the Eagles on the road for the first time in recent memory, and John Harbaugh’s record coming off of bye weeks is impressive. Cam Skattebo’s hamstring is obviously a concern, and we have to respect the Eagles’ playmakers and their ability to generate explosives. That said, I also have to believe Andrew Thomas, Jermaine Eluemunor, and Abdul Carter getting a much-needed break will have a positive impact on their play. The Eagles were already struggling after the departures on their coaching staff, and fell into disarray with the retirement of Lane Johnson, the trade of Cam Jurgens, the loss of Jalen Hurts, and Saquon Barkley’s injuries. Those excuses, however, fall flat considering the Giants are also without their starting quarterback, their offensive tackles have been gutting their way through injuries, their best pass rusher and a starting defensive lineman are on the injured reserve, and they’ve been dealing with injuries in their backfield and secondary — but have held it together and persevered. I think I’ll always have a (at least) a kernel of concern when the Giants play in Philly. But this seems like a great week for a statement game. Winner: Giants Tony Del Genio This is a must-win game for the Giants. Not because they can’t win the NFC East if they don’t – this division is bad enough to revive memories of the 2020 “NFC Least.” It’s because we don’t know yet whether the Giants are frauds who’ve made a couple of plays late in games against bad teams, or a rising team that just has what it takes to win. The opening win over Dallas was impressive…but the Cowboys are a 3-5 disaster. The most recent win in Houston was impressive…but that team is now 2-5. In fact, the Giants haven’t yet even played, much less beaten, a team that is currently above .500. The Philadelphia Eagles are a train wreck this season, having lost many key players to retirement or injury and having parted ways with the best offensive line coach around, Jeff Stoutland. Still, that Eagles defense has Jalen Carter on the IDL, Zach Baun at linebacker, and quality defensive backs in Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. Most importantly they have defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, whose two-high safety zone defenses with post-snap rotation have confused many quarterbacks and limited explosive pass plays.Will J.J. McCarthy be able to read that defense and exploit it, or is this the week he throws three picks and comes back to Earth? The Eagles’ offense hasn’t really scared anyone this season. They traded A.J. Brown, DeVonta Smith and Jalen Hurts are out, Saquon Barkley is playing injured, and the formerly fearsome offensive line is a shell of its former self with future HOFers Jason Kelce and Lane Johnson retired and the rest of them injured or playing poorly. The wild card is that Joe Milton III will make his first start at QB for them. The Giants saw a little of him as a Cowboy in the final game last season, and Jalin Hyatt will have fond memories of a QB who actually completed a deep pass to him for a TD in college. Milton has a rocket arm and is more mobile than predecessor Tanner McKee, but the Giants should be able to limit him, if they can produce an effective pass rush. That said, Dallas Goedert always hurts the Giants, and Dontayvion Wicks, Hollywood Brown, and rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon can make plays. At The Linc, you never know. It’s been 13 years since the Giants won in Philly. There’s no excuse for them not to break that streak Sunday, and do so easily…unless they’re frauds. I’ll guess that they’re not. Winner: Giants Nick Falato The New York Giants enter the matchup riding momentum after their bye week, while the Philadelphia Eagles are mired in a six-game losing streak and rapidly falling toward the top of the 2027 NFL Draft order. The Giants defense is playing well, and the offense received a spark in Week 7 against Houston. Philadelphia’s offensive line struggles to protect Tanner McKee, who isn’t exactly fleet of foot. Philadelphia has averaged just over 14 points per game through this six-game losing streak. Philadelphia’s defense surrendered 27 points to Washington, 38 to Dallas, and 25 to the Carolina Panthers over their last three contests. It’s bleak in Philadelphia. The Giants have not won in Philadelphia since 2013 — a 15-7 Giants’ win where Josh Brown kicked five field goals, and Matt Barkley played for the Eagles. Eight of the Eagles’ 12 victories were one-possession games, and New York had some brutal losses at Lincoln Financial Field. But new circumstances have arrived, and the Giants have an opportunity to end a disturbing chapter in this rivalry. Giants should comfortably win, 30-13. Winner: Giants David Hartman The last time the Giants were favored at the Eagles was in 2009. The last time the Giants beat the Eagles in Philadelphia was in 2013. That’s a lot of history going against Big Blue as they travel to Philadelphia as 3-point favorites on Sunday. The Eagles are enduring a season from hell and after six straight losses, they sit at 2-6. They’ll be starting their third QB of the season when Joe Milton gets the first start of his career on Sunday. Milton has appeared in five NFL games, and his last game action came against the Giants at MetLife Stadium in Week 18 last season, in mop-up duty of a meaningless contest with the Cowboys. He’s a big guy with a big arm, and is a bit of an unknown quantity. For his career, he’s thrown two touchdown passes and two interceptions. Philadelphia is obviously hoping he can spark an anemic offense that’s mostly been without its star running back (who is quite familiar to New York fans), its top two receivers, and multiple first-string offensive linemen. J.J. McCarthy draws his second start for Big Blue, who should be well-rested off the bye. Philadelphia’s defense is still a capable unit, although it hasn’t played all that well, in part because the offense can’t sustain drives. If Philly has any chance to save its season, winning this game against the division leader is a must. I can see their defense giving maximum effort and posing problems for McCarthy, who I still don’t trust completely. This game scares me. The Giants are riding high after their big win over the Texans in Week 7 and Philadelphia is desperate. I also don’t have confidence in Dominic Zvada if the game comes down to him, which it might. I’ll give the G-Men the nod because they’re the better team at the moment, but it won’t be easy. Pick: Giants in a close one Valentine’s View I was asked during a podcast appearance this week whether I was picking the Giants to win. I said yes, with great trepidation. This is Philly we’re talking about, and whenever the Giants visit something always seems to go wrong. This, though, is the first time in a long while where these teams have met with the Giants having a clear upper hand. The New York Giants being favored to win in Philly? Who saw that coming when the season started? Good teams win games like this against struggling teams. I am going to trust that John Harbaugh and the Giants see the opportunity in front of them in the NFC East, and that they will take advantage Sunday of a team they should beat. Pick: Giants Giants…

title: Eagles Injury Report: Saquon Barkley upgraded to limited
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their second official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 9 game against the New York Giants. The Eagles listed seven players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Michael Carter II, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks are both tracking […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 26: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley #26 runs the ball during the game between the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 26th, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their second official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 9 game against the New York Giants. The Eagles listed seven players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Michael Carter II, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks are both tracking to miss their third straight game. With Covey also looking unlikely to play, the Eagles will be down to Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore at wide receiver. Campbell is tracking to miss his second game in a row. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. will make another start at off-ball linebacker. MC2 will likely be out after aggravating an abdomen injury in Week 8. If Covey can’t play, look for Cooper DeJean to return punts. Jones’ absence will leave the Eagles in need of a new top backup cornerback. The Eagles listed five players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Saquon Barkley, Tanner McKee, Jake Elliott, Jalyx Hunt, and Jonathan Greenard. Barkley was upgraded to limited after not practicing on Wednesday. It doesn’t seem great to me that Barkley is playing despite clearly being hampered and in pain. Especially when the Eagles have a chance to sit him down for this game ahead of a Week 10 bye, giving him a two-week break. Nevertheless, here we are. McKee was downgraded from full participation with a chest injury on Wednesday to limited with a rib injury on Thursday. Conspiracy theory: Maybe an injury is being embellished here to stealth bench McKee to being the emergency third quarterback? Maybe the Eagles want Cole Payton to be the No. 2. now. We’ll see. Elliott, Hunt, and Greenard were limited for the second day in a row. They’ll probably be able to play, though Hunt and Greenard will likely be on snap limits. title: Jason Kelce refutes rumor that Eagles players wanted Jeff Stoutland out of Philly
summary: The Eagles run game and offensive line have struggled this season, and as we approach Week 9, and as Nick Sirianni begins to field questions about getting rid of legendary OL coach Jeff Stoutland, rumors about Stout’s departure sprouted up online. According to a report citing an unnamed source, suggested Stoutland not returning to the […]
full_text: Photo by John Jones/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Eagles run game and offensive line have struggled this season, and as we approach Week 9, and as Nick Sirianni begins to field questions about getting rid of legendary OL coach Jeff Stoutland, rumors about Stout’s departure sprouted up online. According to a report citing an unnamed source, suggested Stoutland not returning to the Eagles was not just an organization decision, but something players requested, as well. Given the timing of the report, the optics for the team leaking this information don’t look great. It’s hard to think that anyone from last year’s starting line would want to be rid of Stoutland — they are all staunch and loyal Stout supporters. During Jason Kelce’s segment on 94 WIP this week , the former Eagles center wanted to put the rumors to rest, and instead points the finger back to the team for Stoutland leaving — Kelce was even careful with his words, changing “when Jeff Stoutland left,” for “when Jeff Stoutland announced he wasn’t coming back.” Kelce pointed out that Jordan Mailata and his wife had dinner with Stoutland the night he made his announcement, and when Lane Johnson retired, he only met with one coach, and it was Stoutland. “I take great offense to somebody alluding to players not fighting really hard for Jeff [Stoutland] — and I don’t know the way the last season went, because I wasn’t there, I know it wasn’t great. But, that one very much upset me, because the reason we moved on from Jeff Stoutland had nothing to do with the players, [it] had to do with the building wanting to go in a different direction — and that’s fine, but don’t give me this crap trying to defer direction on the decisions you guys wanted to make.” Earlier in his rant, Kelce also made note that when seasons start come crashing down, people will start leaking things like this to avoid responsibility. The future Hall of Famer was not having any of it, and made it clear that the decision to move on from one of the best offensive line coaches in the NFL was a team decision, not something that came from the players.

title: Eagles-Giants Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 9 enemy
summary: Six straight losses for the Philadelphia Eagles. Can the Birds snap the streak against the New York Giants, a division foe they’ve owned for a long time? In order to preview this Week 9 NFC East matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Big Blue View. The earnest Ed Valentine kindly took the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles sacks Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants during the third quarter in the game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Six straight losses for the Philadelphia Eagles. Can the Birds snap the streak against the New York Giants, a division foe they’ve owned for a long time? In order to preview this Week 9 NFC East matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Big Blue View . The earnest Ed Valentine kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Ed’s questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to BBV .] 1 – The Giants are off to their most encouraging start to a season in a long time. What has John Harbaugh specifically contributed to this team’s turnaround? Credibility. That is the first word that comes to mind. He had 15 winning seasons in 18 years in Baltimore, and he didn’t have to prove himself to anyone. He has driven the Giants hard and made them believe they have earned the right to win because of what they have done. I think this piece I wrote on Tuesday is instructive. Harbaugh isn’t afraid to challenge players or to step on toes to make the Giants better. 2 – J.J. McCarthy’s playing time has been limited but he’s shown some promise. To what extent is there confidence in him moving forward this season? I don’t know that there is confidence. There are, of course, already fans willing to trade Jaxson Dart and run with McCarthy next year. It is way too early for that, though. I think the best word is “excitement.” The Giants did not give up on the season when Dart was lost. They went out and traded for McCarthy, which delivered the message they were not throwing in the towel. McCarthy has shown arm talent and mobility in 5 quarters. He gives them more upside than Jameis Winston. His skillset allows them to run the offense the way they designed it for Dart. Can he keep it up? Can he force the Giants into a Dart-McCarthy debate this offseason? I don’t know, 3 – Who are the some of the more underrated Giants players this season? Perhaps some for the Eagles to keep an eye out for in this game? That’s hard, honestly. Rookie WR Malachi Fields is developing nicely. Bryan Hudson has taken the center job away from John Michael Schmitz. Abdul Carter doesn’t have big sack numbers, but he has been hell to block all season. Deonte Banks has been playing well, really well. He looked like a No. 1 shutdown cornerback in Week 7 against Nico Collins of the Texans. 4 – What’s the biggest matchup in the Giants’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The run defense has been hit and miss. Saquon Barkley hitting the home run still scares me. The Giants are solid against the run, until they aren’t. When they aren’t, they give up big plays. Other than that, the thing that scares me is that I still think the Eagles defensive front can dominate games. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Giants currently listed as 3-point road favorites (first time they’ve been favored in Philly since 2009), what’s your score prediction? With great trepidation, I will pick the Giants to win. I’m still wrapping my head around the Giants being favored. They were 10.5-point underdogs two weeks ago in Houston. They have not won in Philly since 2013, and I am well aware that bad things always seem to happen to the Giants at the Linc. I have said for year, though, that at some point things have to turn around. I think this is the year they finally do. I will say Giants 24, Eagles 17 .

title: Eagles News: Kliff Kingsbury among potential head coach candidates
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jeffrey Lurie’s track record shows that he doesn’t tolerate failure, especially on offense. Nick Sirianni could be in real trouble if things continue to go poorly over the rest of the season. In the event that Sirianni isn’t back, I do […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD,CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Assistant Head Coach Kliff Kingsbury of the Los Angeles Rams looks at a play card during an NFL football game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Jeffrey Lurie’s track record shows that he doesn’t tolerate failure, especially on offense. Nick Sirianni could be in real trouble if things continue to go poorly over the rest of the season. In the event that Sirianni isn’t back, I do think Kliff Kingsbury could be one of their targets. He interviewed for the team’s offensive coordinator opening in 2024 and they reportedly had some interest in him during their last OC search. Kingsbury also has connections with Lincoln Riley, who has a relationship with Howie Roseman . Lurie has yet to hire a retread as a head coach but Kingsbury might be on the better end of candidates that will be willing to take the job in Philly. Are you interested in him or any other candidates … or do you want Sirianni back for 2027? Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Five Eagles head coach candidates, if Nick Sirianni is fired – PhillyVoice Kliff Kingsbury played quarterback in the NFL for five different teams, and he spent some time in NFL Europe and the CFL. He became known for running the “Air Raid” offense, which is a spread, up-tempo, mainly shotgun approach. Its effectiveness is contingent on how well the players can master and execute a limited playbook. He is best known for his four-year head coaching tenure in Arizona, a span during which Kingsbury led the Cardinals to a 28-37-1 record. The following is a snapshot of the Cardinals’ offensive rankings during Kingsbury’s reign. [….] The Cardinals’ best season under Kingsbury was in 2021, when they jumped out to a 10-2 record, before losing four of their last five games followed by a blowout loss in the wildcard round of the playoffs. He also had success in Washington as an offensive coordinator working with Jayden Daniels, who was a rookie phenom under Kingsbury’s tutelage. Currently, Kingsbury is serving as the assistant head coach under Sean McVay in Los Angeles. The Eagles interviewed Kingsbury for their open offensive coordinator position prior to the 2024 season, and they were reportedly close working out a deal. NFL trade rumors: Landon Dickerson draws interest as Eagles trade target – BGN The Eagles have less than a week until the NFL trade deadline, and the expectations are that they’ll be making several moves between now and then. Landon Dickerson has been a name that’s been floating around as a potential trade candidate, and the latest report by Ryan Fowler reveals that the guard is drawing interest from teams. A New QB – Iggles Blitz This move will seem desperate to some, and that is a fair criticism. But I’m okay with it. McKee needs the right circumstances to be successful. He showed potential in 2024 when playing with a great OL, dynamic receivers, and an elite RB. This offense is world’s different. McKee had to do more of the heavy lifting and his limitations showed. He’s just not a guy who can carry an offense. Milton might not be that guy either, but his physical tools give him a better chance of handling that role. If protection breaks down, he can use his legs to make a play. If he’s got a clean pocket, Milton can use his arm strength to get the ball downfield on intermediate or deep routes. The offense has struggled all season so I don’t see the harm in trying a new QB. McKee threw 2 TDs and 2 INTs in his three starts. It isn’t like you’re walking away from much. What 18 contenders should do at the NFL trade deadline: Who could get aggressive? – ESPN Luxury target: The Eagles might not be dealing all of their veterans, but I wonder if Howie Roseman could be talked into a move for Zack Baun, who has been one of the league’s best linebackers since moving to the position on a full-time basis in Philadelphia. Baun is coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl seasons and has allowed a 72.8 passer rating in coverage this season, but he’s also about to turn 30, and the Eagles might need to devote resources toward positions Roseman values more consistently. Baun would cost the Bengals only $607,500 over the rest of 2026 before $17 million in salary in 2027, which is the final year of his current contract. The Eagles might also be interested in supplementing their defensive line depth by taking a shot on 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart, which would reduce the amount of draft capital the Bengals need to send to get a deal done. Eagles turn to Joe Milton, the first of two QB auditions they must stage to make the most of 2026 – Inquirer The one criticism you might make of the decision to start Milton is that it wasn’t a decision to start Payton. The beefy dual-threat lefty has lingered on the active roster all season after the Eagles selected him at No. 178 overall out of North Dakota State. Milton will now be the fourth quarterback who has been ahead of him on the depth chart, after Hurts, McKee, and veteran Andy Dalton. It’s a good bet that Payton will get his chance at some point. For now, it makes sense to go in this order. If Milton sets the world on fire, great. House money. If he doesn’t, the Eagles will at least buy another handful of weeks before they can again switch things up and inject a sense of the new. These are the considerations they must prioritize now. The only good that can come from 2026 is whatever helps them in 2027 and beyond. Milton and Payton at least offer them that, however marginal the likely payoff. Eagles locker room rallying around rocket-armed QB Joe Milton – NBCSP If you happened to be in South Philadelphia on Wednesday afternoon and have supersonic hearing, you might have already known the Eagles have a new starting quarterback. Joe Milton has that type of arm. “He zips it. He zips it,” receiver Darius Cooper said shaking his head. “You can hear it flying in the air.” The rest of the world found out the Eagles made the decision to bench Tanner McKee and go with Milton from ESPN less than 2 hours after head coach Nick Sirianni failed mention a thing during his Wednesday press conference. And neither Milton nor McKee were available to reporters after Wednesday’s practice. But despite some janky attempts at obfuscation from a couple of starting offensive linemen on Wednesday, the team knows who is starting against the Giants on Sunday afternoon. It’s Milton. Dallas Goedert said he and his teammates found out the news in a meeting minutes before the public heard. “We were kind of hoping that it would stay under wraps,” Goedert said. “It would be a competitive advantage and they wouldn’t find out until Saturday. But it didn’t take long for people to know.” Nick Sirianni: I’ve always felt complete support from Jeffrey Lurie – PFT “I’ve always felt nothing but complete support from Mr. Lurie in everything, through good times, through bad times,” Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. “That’s huge. That’s huge to be able to know that the owner has your back in all situations. We’ve been high of highs, we’ve been low, and I’ve felt nothing but support and my communication remains the same with him as it has [been] whether we’re on a winning streak or whether we’re on a losing streak. I love that steadiness, and I’m trying to give that same thing to the guys: the consistency, the steadiness, because I know I’m receiving it from the very top.” The Best Bets of NFL Week 9 – The Ringer The Eagles have never won as a home underdog with Nick Sirianni (0-8), and he’s in serious danger of bottoming out here. I’ll probably just wait to play the Giants in the second half. NY Giants injury update: Cam Skattebo, Abdul Carter still not practicing – Big Blue View Head coach John Harbaugh said “we’ll see” when asked on Wednesday if Skattebo would be…

title: Jalen Hurts provides “morale boost” by showing up to Eagles practice facility
summary: There have been few, if any, updates since the Eagles placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR as he deals with blood clots that traveled to his lungs. QB1 deserves his privacy and time to heal above all else, but the unknown surrounding how he’s doing, has been a dark cloud lingering over the city and […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images There have been few, if any, updates since the Eagles placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on IR as he deals with blood clots that traveled to his lungs. QB1 deserves his privacy and time to heal above all else, but the unknown surrounding how he’s doing, has been a dark cloud lingering over the city and fanbase. Thankfully, we finally get a bit of good news, with ESPN’s Tim McManus reporting that Hurts was at the Eagles practice facility on Wednesday, and even sat in on meetings. Eagles QB Jalen Hurts was at the practice facility today, per sources. He sat in on both the team meeting and other meetings. He did not address the team but his presence did provide a morale boost for some. Some players haven’t seen Hurts since he was placed on IR. — Tim McManus (@Tim_McManus) November 4, 2026 There had been early speculation that the quarterback would be allowed around the team, as his recovery would only limit him physically, but head coach Nick Sirianni wouldn’t comment on if Hurts had been, or planned to be, involved in the rest of the season. Earlier on Wednesday, Sirianni would only say that he’s seen Hurts and had been in constant communication with the quarterback, but wouldn’t say whether he was in the building. “ Q. Is there anything you can share with us about how QB Jalen Hurts is doing? Have you talked to him? Have you seen him, communicated with him? ( Reuben Frank ) Nick Sirianni: Of course, I’ve seen him, and I have no new update on anything. But of course, I’ve talked to him and am in constant communication with him and know he’s resting and recovering. I miss him like crazy. But nothing new on that front. I know he’s resting and recovering, and we’re all still praying for him and hoping for a speedy recovery. Q. Has he been here? ( Jeff Neiburg ) Nick Sirianni: Yeah, like I said, no new information there on that.“ Players appreciate the lengths Sirianni will go to protect their privacy, and that carries more weight when talking about potentially life-threatening medical situations. BUT, now we know that Hurts is back in the building, and McManus reports that his presence brought a morale boost to his teammates — and it did the same for Eagles fans. That he’s well enough to be around the team, and also be in meetings to help turn things around, is a welcomed update from a situation that turned serious so quickly.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Here’s where the Steelers’ defense still has room to grow
summary: It’s a good time to be a Steelers fan. Pittsburgh sits atop the AFC North entering a Week 9 bye, coming off a big win over the rival Cleveland Browns where the Steelers both scored a lot of points (27) and didn’t give up many (six). As a result, you’re going to see a lot […]
full_text: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images | Getty Images It’s a good time to be a Steelers fan. Pittsburgh sits atop the AFC North entering a Week 9 bye, coming off a big win over the rival Cleveland Browns where the Steelers both scored a lot of points (27) and didn’t give up many (six). As a result, you’re going to see a lot of positive Steelers coverage over the next two weeks. And for good reason. The team’s running game and front seven were undoubtedly elite against Cleveland. Pittsburgh has been playing like one of the NFL’s best teams as of the late. But as knowledgeable NFL writers/podcasters Jon Ledyard and Derrick Bell quipped following the Browns game, a lot is going right for the Steelers, “but the forward pass, especially on offense, still stands between them and greatness.” Most are aware of the Steelers’ passing deficiencies on offense, but I’d argue that on the other side of the ball, Pittsburgh’s passing defense could be a similarly limiting factor on the team’s long-term potential. Pittsburgh’s safety room has been an apparent issue since before the season started, and even with Robert Spears-Jennings blowing past Year 1 expectations as a seventh-round rookie, the play at the position has been a weaker spot on defense. DeShon Elliott missed much of the early season with injury and hasn’t been that impactful since returning, while free agent signing Jaquan Brisker hasn’t always been able to rise to the challenge when it comes to coverage ability and instincts. Meanwhile at cornerback, the group’s injury issues have largely subsided at this point in the season. But with Joey Porter Jr. — by far the best player in the secondary — never suiting up for the black and gold before being traded to Dallas, an expected strength on defense has turned into a position that’s been solid at best in 2026. All of that’s to say, despite Pittsburgh having not allowed 20 points in each of its last three games, the “elite” label the defense has earned as of late doesn’t feel accurate to the state of the secondary, which looks like a potentially ticking time bomb with Joe Burrow, CJ Stroud and Trevor Lawrence still waiting on the schedule. Pittsburgh’s season defensive stats match the eye test. While ranking near the top of the league in stopping the run (third), sacking the quarterback (first), and forcing a quick time to throw (third — partially explaining a surprisingly middling pressure rate), the Steelers are middle of the pack when stopping the pass (17th) and among the worst in yards after catch allowed (30th) and average separation allowed per target (32nd). The dichotomy was obvious in Pittsburgh’s recent big win over Cleveland, where the Steelers’ front seven dominated to the tune of eight team sacks and only 34 rushing yards allowed, holding the Browns to single-digit points. However, Browns quarterback DeShaun Watson passed for 324 yards — and while it’s more than fair to point out that Cleveland was in a must-pass situation for much of the game and against a prevent-oriented Steelers defense late, the Browns also missed a number of open passing opportunities that would’ve juiced Watson’s numbers even more. Essentially, in the rare instances when the Steelers’ pass rush wasn’t completely dominating on Sunday, the Pittsburgh secondary wasn’t exactly holding up its end of the bargain. Here are some of the bigger plays the Steelers gave up in the passing game on Sunday: The Steelers defense has been great in recent weeks. I'm still a little concerned with the secondary. pic.twitter.com/xrosiUndtY — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) November 6, 2026 In the first clip above, Brisker just gets beat, plain and simple, when manned up against a good receiving tight end in the Browns’ Harold Fannin Jr. On the second, the Browns find the open space in the Steelers’ two-high coverage, with Brisker stuck in no man’s land between the running back and the corner route. In the final clip, there’s a miscommunication between Daylen Everette and Asante Samuel Jr., with both jumping the same route as KC Concepcion scoots by both for a 20-plus-yard gain. To be fair, only the last play is a true breakdown in coverage, with the first two being the sort of man- and zone-beaters you expect to see work at some point in an NFL game (even if you would hope Brisker holds up better against tight ends in coverage). However, it could’ve been a lot worse: Some almosts for the Cleveland passing attack pic.twitter.com/UtNuJtQYqV — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) November 6, 2026 In the first clip above, Samuel loses Jerry Jeudy (bottom of the screen wide receiver) in coverage; the Browns receiver was open for a 70-yard touchdown well before Watson threw the ball. Instead, the play goes for just a first down to Fannin. On the next play, the Browns run a play-action concept, and with both safeties preoccupied by the deep route, Samuel is left to choose between covering Denzel Boston and going after Watson. He never really commits to either, and is saved by a terrible throw by Watson. It negates what would’ve been a 20- or 30-yard gain. The next play is much tighter coverage and a bit more nit-picky than the other examples in this article, but Boston clearly gets a step on Jamel Dean with the Steelers in quarters. Brisker stops his feet and leaves the corner on an island, losing inside leverage. A good throw closer to the post is a touchdown. Finally, there’s a late-game extended play where Jeudy once again finds himself open, with no Steelers defender within five yards of him in any direction. Watson steps up in the pocket, draws Jeudy even more open, and then checks it down to the running back — who still gets the first down. Of course, you can go back and watch any good NFL defensive performance and find open players who were missed. However, I’d argue there were a lot more than usual in the Steelers’ Sunday win. But there’s also another level of nuance: It was a good gameplan by the Steelers, who knew they could beat the Browns with pressure, unleashing their second-highest single-game blitz rate of the season thus far (30%). Watson, who has actually had a solid 2026, looked uncomfortable and inaccurate all game. The Steelers’ front seven feasted, the secondary benefited from off-target throws, and Pittsburgh didn’t give up a touchdown in a three-score win. Honestly, my thoughts in this article can best be summed up by the below play, where Robert Spears-Jennings jumps Denzel Boston’s route, throwing Watson out of rhythm and into an eventual sack. With no coverage help behind Spears-Jennings, Boston was left wide open — but the aggression, paired with pressure, resulted in a positive play for the Steelers. pic.twitter.com/YJ7WMAfo6E — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) November 6, 2026 However, it won’t always be that easy — especially later in the season and postseason against better quarterbacks and passing offenses (Frankly, besides Burrow and Drake Maye, have the Steelers faced many good passers this year?). The Steelers’ pass defense as a whole has been adequate this season, but it hasn’t been at the level the team’s overall defensive numbers would indicate. Whether it’s athleticism in man defense or chemistry in zone, there’s still a lot of work to do. But it still does feel like an improved Steelers defense than in past seasons. The pass rush has been revitalized, and as evidenced by the Browns game, that can cover for a number of sins on the back end. And the Steelers have two rookies in Robert Spears-Jennings and Daylen Everette who should only continue to develop and improve the secondary with time. In the short term, the Steelers also have an entire bye week to aid their preparation ahead of a rematch with a high-flying Bengals passing game in Week 10. The Steelers’ secondary has some notable issues, but it’s far too early to call it a season killer.
author: Ryland Bickley

With the Jaguars’ win, they climb to the No. 3 seed due […]
full_text: (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are on their bye week after a 6-2 start. title: Alex Highsmith reveals what has helped the Steelers’ defense play at a high level
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defense held the Cleveland Browns to season lows in points and rushing yards in their dominant 27-6 victory at Acrisure Stadium this past Sunday. As they enter the bye, the Steelers defense ranks third in scoring defense, allowing just 18 points per game through eight games. However, it wasn’t always sunshine and […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers defense held the Cleveland Browns to season lows in points and rushing yards in their dominant 27-6 victory at Acrisure Stadium this past Sunday. As they enter the bye, the Steelers defense ranks third in scoring defense, allowing just 18 points per game through eight games. However, it wasn’t always sunshine and rainbows for the defensive unit early in the season. In fact, the first time the Steelers and Browns met this season, T.J. Watt was caught yelling into a headset on the sideline at defense coordinator Patrick Graham after a miscommunication led to a Cleveland touchdown. After that game, Graham moved from the booth to the sidelines with his players. The Steelers have rattled off four consecutive wins since Graham moved to the sidelines, backed by exceptional defensive play. Appearing on “NFL Report” with Andrew Siciliano , Steelers edge rusher Alex Highsmith detailed how Graham’s move down to the sidelines has changed the Steelers’ defense. “You know, I do believe that was a turning point for us,” Highsmith said. “Obviously, he’s been on the field with us ever since and so just him being down there is just really helped us a lot, for sure. But, you know PG’s been awesome, ever since he came in he’s just had a desire for us to be great. He’s a football guy, he knows football so well, and so I just think as we continue to gel as a unit, gel as a defense, you know it’s only going to be better from here on out. Like I said, I just love the way we are progressing as a defense so we just gotta continue to play like we have been and with him (Graham) calling plays, just excited to see what he continues to scheme up to put guys in positions to make plays.” Steelers undefeated (4-0) since DC Patrick Graham listened to Amy Winehouse on the Ohio Turnpike. 🎥 Alex Highsmith on @NFL Report @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NAwDdbpqPw — Andrew Siciliano (@AndrewSiciliano) November 4, 2026 Pittsburgh boasts the third most takeaways in the league with 13, while allowing just 83.9 rushing yards per game to opponents at the midway point in their season. It seems like Pittsburgh finally has the right man leading the charge defensively in Graham. Highsmith’s praise of the scheme and putting guys in positions to make plays is a great sign that the players have bought into what Graham is selling them. The Steelers look well on their way to having their first season with a top-ten scoring defense since 2023, and it seems like it only took a simple move to the sidelines to make a world of difference. title: Steelers insider says team will not make WR trade
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves 6-2 with sole possession of first place in the AFC North as the trade deadline looms. Perhaps the biggest need on the team is a wide receiver, as giving Aaron Rodgers another weapon on the outside could propel the Steelers in their playoff push. However, one of the longest tenured […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves 6-2 with sole possession of first place in the AFC North as the trade deadline looms. Perhaps the biggest need on the team is a wide receiver, as giving Aaron Rodgers another weapon on the outside could propel the Steelers in their playoff push. However, one of the longest tenured Steelers beat writers seems to think the Steelers won’t make any major moves for a receiver at the November 10th trade deadline. In his weekly Steelers chat on Wednesday, Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette was asked plenty of questions from readers about Pittsburgh adding another weapon. Despite consistent efforts from reads to gain any insight into the Steelers deadline plans, Dulac seemed adamant that Pittsburgh would not be making any move for a receiver. “They’re not seriously pursuing any,” Dulac replied. “What I’m hearing is they are not likely or intending to make a trade, but as I always say, never under-estimate the desperation of an NFL GM who might coming knocking for a deal.” It also seems as if the Steelers already feel they made a swing this season by trading for wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. I can understand this thought process, considering Pittman Jr. has been banged up for the good majority of the season so far, it’s impossible to know what exactly he could have provided the offense. With all of the hype around the Steelers right now amidst an active four-game winning streak and the possibility of adding even more talent to the team at the deadline, Dulac gives us an important reminder – the Steelers could very well stand pat at the deadline and hope their receiver room gets healthier, and hope they become quality separators against zone coverage all of a sudden. For now, it’s all speculation from now until we see a move become official. Let us know what you think in the comments . full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers were one of only a handful of teams to keep four quarterbacks on their final 53-man rosters back in August. Most expected this, but it leaves the Steelers in a peculiar position with two veteran options on expiring contracts and two young fliers developing behind the scenes. Is it all possible Pittsburgh considers moving a quarterback at the deadline with a laundry list of injuries around the league? It’s not crazy to ask, in fact, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN listed the veteran quarterback as a potential trade candidate ahead of next week’s deadline. “Quarterback Mason Rudolph,” Fowler wrote. “The Steelers are more likely to bring in players at the deadline. In fact, I don’t expect Pittsburgh to move anyone. But it has a surplus at quarterback, and should more quarterback injuries occur around the league, perhaps teams call on Rudolph with an attractive offer.” Rudolph has started just one game over the course of the last two seasons for Pittsburgh. It’s important to keep in mind that this is simply speculation, and Fowler even says that he doesn’t expect Pittsburgh to move anyone. It would not make much sense for the Steelers to move a veteran quarterback like Rudolph who they have familiarity with and confidence in that he can run the offense and win some games should Aaron Rodgers miss time. However, crazier things have happened. Who’s to say the Steelers won’t get an offer for Rudolph that they can’t refuse? At 6-2 overall with sole possession of first place in the AFC North, it could be a very active next few days in the trade market for general manager Omar Khan and his Steelers.
