title: Stats and Snaps – 2026 Week 8, Eagles vs. Commanders
summary: Watching Sunday’s ultimately decisive win against Tanner McKee and the injury-ravaged Philadelphia Eagles, I couldn’t escape the feeling that there is the nucleus of a good football team, struggling to escape the grip of poor coaching and preparation. On this occasion, that team broke free toward the end of the first half to overcome a […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 1: Trey Amos #23 of the Washington Commanders breaks up a pass intended for Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter of an NFL football game at Northwest Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Watching Sunday’s ultimately decisive win against Tanner McKee and the injury-ravaged Philadelphia Eagles, I couldn’t escape the feeling that there is the nucleus of a good football team, struggling to escape the grip of poor coaching and preparation. On this occasion, that team broke free toward the end of the first half to overcome a 7-point deficit and hand a 10-27 loss to their division rival, on the way to earning its second win in seven games. Will the Commanders be able to ride the momentum from the come-from-behind win to victory over the visiting LA Rams in Week 9? Who knows. But there was plenty to like, as well as plenty of areas for improvement, in the Commanders’ takedown of the dirty birds. On the positive side, the Week 8 victory featured the best coverage performance by the secondary this season as well as the best games in burgundy and gold by WR Treylon Burks, OLB Dorance Armstrong, NT Shy Tuttle and DE Charles Omenihu. Despite some lapses, the OL gave Jayden Daniels plenty of time in the pocket, and CB Trey Amos played a nearly perfect game of shutdown coverage. On the not so positive side, the team continues to start slow. It took nearly a full half of football to get the offense going and to stop committing penalties. In the first half, the Commanders committed 7 for 50 yards, compared to just 2 for 20 yards in the second half. If the Commanders can figure out how to start games like they started the second half against the Eagles, they will give themselves a chance to beat a better opponent in Week 9. But before we get ahead of ourselves, let’s have a look at where they lined up, who stepped up, who could have done better in the Commanders’ first divisional win of the season. Technicalities: Stats were sourced from the official NFL gamebook via NFLGSIS, Pro Football Reference (PFR), Pro Football Focus (PFF) and ESPN’s total QBR. In cases where advanced stats are scored differently, I have chosen preferred providers (eg. QB pressures – PFF, yards before contact – PFR). Where differences in advanced stats result from judgment calls (eg. Coverage yards allowed, broken tackles) I have gone with a modified consensus approach. When there is fundamental disagreement between sources, the stats won’t be reported. Minor differences between sources that support the same conclusion are reported. If advanced stats are reported without attribution of source, it means there was consensus. As always, official NFL stats override conflicting data from other sources. BIGGEST PLAYS OF THE GAME These plays had the largest impact on teams’ scoring potential within a drive, as judged by Expected Points Added (EPA). Threshhold: EPA = +/- 2.25 Biggest Plays for Commanders Q3, 2:51, 1 st and 10 at WAS 40: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep right to Treylon Burks for 53 yards. Penalty on Quinyon Mitchell: Illegal Contact, 5 yards (declined). EPA 4.0 Q4, 2:18, 1 st and 10 at PHI 37: Rachaad White left tackle for 33 yards. EPA 3.16 Q4, 8:30, 2 nd and 8 at WAS 33: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep right to Antonio Williams for 30 yards. EPA 2.39 Q3, 2:51, 1 st and 10 at WAS 40: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep right to Treylon Burks for 53 yards. Penalty on Quinyon Mitchell: Illegal Contact, 5 yards (declined). EPA 4.0 Q4, 2:18, 1 st and 10 at PHI 37: Rachaad White left tackle for 33 yards. EPA 3.16 Q4, 8:30, 2 nd and 8 at WAS 33: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep right to Antonio Williams for 30 yards. EPA 2.39 Q1, 0:33, 4 th and 4 at PHI 38: Drew Stevens 56 yard field goal. EPA 2.28 Q1, 15:00: Jake Elliott kicks off 59 yards, returned by Luke McCaffrey for 44 yards. EPA 2.26 Q4, 9:01, 4 th and 14 at WAS 23: Jake Elliott 41 yard field goal no good. EPA -2.93 Q3, 3:01, 3 rd and 4 at WAS 37: Tanner McKee sacked by Dorance Armstrong for 3 yards. Tanner McKee fumbles (forced by Dorance Armstrong), recovered by Charles Omenihu at WAS-40. EPA -3.88 Biggest Plays for Eagles Q1, 5:29, 1 st and 10 at WAS 26: Tanner McKee pass complete deep left to Saquon Barkley for 24 yards. Penalty on Rasul Douglas: Illegal Contact, 5 yards (declined). EPA 2.9 Q1, 12:14, 4 th and 11 at PHI 37: Drew Stevens 55 yard field goal no good. EPA -2.72 Q1, 5:37, 1 st and 20 at WAS 10: Jayden Daniels pass complete short middle to Chig Okonkwo for 11 yards. Chig Okonkwo fumbles (forced by Andrew Mukuba), recovered by Zack Baun at WAS-26. EPA -3.08 OFFENSE Jayden Daniels completed 16 of 29 attempts (55.2%, ADOT 9.7 yds) for 217 yds and 1 TD, with 1 dropped pass. He had a career-low 2 rushing attempts for 23 yds. Daniels took 2 sacks for 20 yds. According to PFF, he faced 10 pressures, his lowest figure in a complete game this season. Daniels’ effort was good for a 58.8 total QBR, which ranked 16 th among starting QBs in Week 8. He was penalized 5 yards for a false start in the 1 st quarter. Rachaad White led the Commanders’ rushing attack, with 11 attempts for 55 yds (5.0 Y/A), 1 TD, 2 first downs, and a long run of 33 yds. His effort was good for a 45.5% rushing success rate, a little below the 40 th percentile for RBs this season. White averaged just 1.5 yards before contact per attempt, which is in the bottom 10% for running backs this season. White caught 2 of 3 passing targets for 5 total yds. Austin Ekeler had 8 carries for 36 yds (4.5 Y/A) and 1 first down (37.5% success rate). Ekeler averaged 3.5 YBC/Att, which is above the 90 th percentile for RBs this season. He was not targeted as a receiver. Jeremy McNichols had 5 rushing attempts for 21 yds (4.2 Y/A) and 1 first down. He averaged 2.4 YBC/Att, right around league average for RBs this season. Despite the modest rushing average, he achieved an 80% rushing success rate. He caught his only passing target for 7 yds. title: Washington Commanders vs. Rams in Week 9: Inside the Matchup
summary: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates […]
full_text: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026. From John Portis: The 2-4-1 Washington Commanders head into Week 9 coming off their second win of the season and the first for Jayden Daniels as a starter since October of 2025. While the team showed improvement in their victory over the Eagles, plenty of questions remain around the team’s ability to repeat the performance against a tougher opponent. The Los Angeles Rams may fit the bill after recovering from a shaky start, squaring their record at 4-4 following a victory over the winless Chargers on Sunday. L.A.’s offseason additions of cornerback Trent McDuffie and EDGE Myles Garrett made the Rams a popular preseason pick to make the Super Bowl even before All-Pro defensive tackle Aaron Donald un-retired to re-join the team. Unfortunately for head coach Sean McVay and the Rams, things have not gone according to plan. After a rough opening-week loss in Melbourne, Australia, to the 49ers, the Rams moved Garrett to injured reserve; wide receiver Davante Adams subsequently ruptured his hamstring late last month. Los Angeles has missed both players this season, losing close matchups to the Broncos, Bills and Cardinals by four points or less . Even so, the Rams’ wins have been been against a modest lineup of opponents. The Giants, Eagles, Raiders and Chargers have a combined record of 10-19-1, with only the Giants above .500. The team did open Garrett’s 21-day practice window this week but his status for Sunday is uncertain, as is that of tight end Colby Parkinson. Cornerback Jaylen Watson was surprisingly ruled out for the season Wednesday with a shoulder injury while Trent McDuffie sat out with a back injury of his own. The Rams’ offensive line is a different animal than the one the Commanders faced last week and is rated as one of the best in the NFL, allowing the least pressures in the league so far this season. As Bill mentioned in his preview (which you can see below), McVay retained the services of Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua with the luxury of two talented running backs in Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. The two rushers combined for 192 rushing yards against the Raiders and another 129 versus the Chargers. It is no surprise, considering McVay’s presence, that the Rams have one of the top offenses in the NFL. What is surprising is their lack of explosiveness, especially in the passing game, as the Rams’ explosive play rate of 5.8% ranks 27th in the league. Despite missing Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson, McVay and offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase continue to run plenty of heavy 13 personnel ( 35% rate), throwing out of the formation frequently. The Rams have the second-best success rate on designed runs this season (48.3%). Yet they continue to not run the ball (37.7% designed run rate coming into today ranks 21st). pic.twitter.com/agGI0O2jJN — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) November 1, 2026 Commanders linebacker Sonny Styles should help match up against those looks, but Washington placed defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw on injured reserve on Wednesday. While the Commanders are hopeful they will get defensive tackle Johnny Newton back for Sunday’s game, expect Los Angeles to test Washington’s replacements inside early. If Charles Omenihu, Tim Settle and Shy Tuttle can hold up against the Rams’ offensive front, the defense should have a good chance of limiting their offense. Daronte Jones and the defensive secondary should also continue to focus on generating takeaways. Los Angeles has now given the ball away 12 times in 8 games . That works out to 1.5 turnovers per game, with most being charged to Matthew Stafford, who has thrown eight interceptions in eight contests. That’s as many as he gave up in a full 17-game season in 2025. The Rams have compiled a .500 record despite those turnovers with a defense that is also very good. In fact, Chris Shula’s defense is ranked in the Top 5, with cornerback Trent McDuffie and safety Quentin Lake playing at elite levels. Chris Shula's defense: 21 PPG allowed (12th) 301.1 YPG allowed (5th) -0.12 EPA/play (6th) 41.3% success rate allowed (8th) 6.23 yards per pass attempt (5th) 8 turnovers forced (17th) 11.1% missed tackles (9th) …. all without Myles Garrett. — Sosa Kremenjas (@QBsMVP) November 2, 2026 Is Trent McDuffie making a case as the BEST CB in football? – Lowest passer rating allowed: 34.7 – T-2nd in PFF coverage grade – ZERO touchdowns allowed Rams got an absolute steal this offseason… pic.twitter.com/s0OwzLYSCl — LAFB Network (@LAFBNetwork) October 30, 2026 Among safeties through Week 8, Quentin Lake ranks: 🔵1st in passes defended (8) 🔵1st in incompletions as primary defender (17) 🔵T-2nd in INTs (3) 🔵2nd in hurries (5) 🔵T-11th in tackles (50) (TruMedia) pic.twitter.com/jm4FQ0nipi — Los Angeles Rams PR (@TheLARamsPR) November 3, 2026 In a case of mirrored situations, the Commanders offense should test the interior of the Rams defense, as they’re missing defensive tackles Poona Ford and Kobie Turner. In their victories over the Rams, the Bills and Cardinals totaled 230 and 120 rushing yards, respectively. Obviously, a team with a top offense and defense doesn’t secure a 4-4 record without having some flaws. This holds true for McVay’s team, as they have 61 accepted penalties (24th) against them so far this season. For reference, the Commanders have 55 accepted penalties this year. Special teams have also been an Achilles’ heel for the Rams, and they have already changed kickers twice this season, swapping Harrison Mevis for Blake Grupe and then Grupe for Brandon McManus while adding second kicker Joshua Karty exclusively for kickoffs. Special teams coordinator Larry Izzo’s group has not stood out this season but did show up last week , and the Commanders’ special teams could give Washington an advantage on Sunday. Special Teams EPA through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/jkmVWblN8Z — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) November 3, 2026 Dan Quinn and the Washington Commanders will need to take advantage of every opportunity they can find to get ahead of Sean McVay and the Rams in what should be an interesting matchup in Landover. Betting Lines Point Spread : Rams -5.5 Game Total (Over/Under) : 47.5 points Opening odds for the Commanders have them as 5.5-point home underdogs against the Los Angeles Rams. The Over/Under opens at 47.5 in a game expected to be higher scoring than last week’s game against the Eagles. Original article from Bill-in-Bangkok published July 7 Week 9 Preview: LA Rams at Washington Commanders Date: November 8, 2026, 1:00 p.m. ET Location: Northwest Stadium in Landover Maryland The Rams are led by quarterback Matthew Stafford, who has had a career renaissance in Los Angeles. With the championship window possibly closing as Stafford reaches his 18 th season at age 38, the front office acquired edge rusher Myles Garrett through a trade and signed cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson to bolster the defense. With respect to the coaching staff, Sean McVay promoted Nate Scheelhaase to offensive coordinator to maintain playbook continuity after Mike LaFleur’s departure to the Cardinals. The team also hired former Commanders OC Kliff Kingsbury as assistant head coach, and Bubba Ventrone from Cleveland to lead the special teams unit. All in all, analysts see this as a winning combination. The Commanders will need to be at their best against a Rams team that will come to Landover in Week 9 fresh off of three west coast games against the Cardinals, Raiders and Chargers, ranked 29 th , 28 th , and 7 th , respectively, in ESPN’s 2026 Power Index .…

title: NFL Week 9 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, betting odds, fantasy tips
summary: Bills vs. Vikings? Drake Maye vs. Jordan Love? The NFL in Madrid? There are 14 more games in Week 9, and we have picks, predictions and more for all of them.
full_text:
Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season is here! Football is back in Madrid, this time featuring the Bengals and Falcons. Back in the States, Drake Maye and Jordan Love  will face off, Shedeur Sanders might start in place of Deshaun Watson ( concussion ), and the Raiders return to the Bay Area.

 We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder give us final score picks for every game.

 Let's get into the full Week 9 slate, which culminates with "Monday Night Football" matchup between the Bills and Vikings on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless otherwise noted, and all odds are via Draftkings.)

 
 Jump to a matchup: 
 CIN-ATL | DAL-IND | NYJ-KC 
 DET-MIA | CLE-NO | NYG-PHI 
 LAR-WSH | DEN-CAR | HOU-LAC 
 GB-NE | LV-SF | ARI-SEA 
 TB-CHI | BUF-MIN 

 Thursday: JAX-BAL 
 Bye: TEN , PIT 

 
 

 What ESPN Analytics says ... 
 

 

 
 

 Bengals (5-2) at Falcons (3-5)  in Madrid 
 9:30 a.m. ET | NFL Network | CIN -3 (52.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Bengals: The numbers say quarterback  Joe Burrow is in the midst of a career year. After he tallied six touchdowns (five passing, one rushing) last week, that's what Falcons DC Jeff Ulbrich believes, too. Said Ulbrich: "He's playing his best football that he's ever played in his career, in my opinion, right now." Burrow leads the NFL in passing TDs (20) and ranks fourth in passing yards (2,115). -- Ben Baby 

 What we're hearing on the Falcons:  Atlanta will need to disrupt Burrow to give itself the best chance to win. The Falcons have the personnel and scheme to do it, too -- Brandon Dorlus and Gervon Dexter Sr . rank first and second, respectively, in the NFL among DTs in pressure rate. They are the first teammates to be first and second in that category through eight weeks since 2018. -- Marc Raimondi 

 Stat to know: The Falcons' have 16 turnovers, second most in the NFL behind the Chargers (17). It's also Atlanta's most through eight games of season since 2003 (19). -- ESPN Research 

 

 Bold prediction:  Dorlus will record a sack. He has a 11.5% pressure rate when playing tackle, best in the NFL. -- Walder 

 Injuries: Bengals | Falcons 

 Fantasy nugget: The Bengals have averaged a league-high 36.3 points per game over their past three games, but running back  Chase Brown has scored 10 or more fantasy points just once during that stretch. He has still averaged 18.6 touches per game, and now he faces a Falcons defense that has allowed the fourth-most fantasy points per game to backs. See Week 9 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight:  Burrow is 15-7-1 against the spread/straight up in nonconference games and 22-10 ATS/straight up following a win since 2022. Atlanta can pressure QBs, but Burrow gets the ball out quickly enough to make that tough. If the rush doesn't get there, the Falcons allow almost a 75% completion percentage. With WRs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins , Cincinnati has the guys to turn those clean pockets into TD drives. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Bengals 30, Falcons 24 
 Moody's pick: Bengals 30, Falcons 27 
 Walder's pick: Falcons 23, Bengals 21 
 FPI prediction: CIN, 77.3% (by an average of 7.7 points)

 

 Matchup must-reads: Trio brought in to replace All-Pro DE has shined for Bengals ... Falcons' Pearce back from suspension, expected to play ... Bengals DE Howell out indefinitely after wrist surgery 

 
 

 Cowboys (3-5) at Colts (2-6) 
 1 p.m. ET | Fox | DAL -5.5 (51.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Cowboys: For at least the third time this season, the Cowboys are facing a must-win game. Last week's overtime loss was difficult to move on from given the poor defensive and offensive performances while playing at home. Now on the road and facing a team that has fired its general manager and could trade even more of its top players, Von Miller senses danger. "Those guys are fighting for their lives as well," he said. "They're trying to find their identity, too. And those teams are always scary whenever you play them because you really don't know what to expect." -- Todd Archer 

 What we're hearing on the Colts: The Colts have given up 33 or more points in four of their six losses this season, meaning Sunday's matchup with the high-scoring Cowboys has the potential to go awry. Indianapolis is coming off a 42-7 loss , and the Colts have shown very little defensive resistance this season. Of note will be the matchups between Colts CBs Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward and Dallas WRs CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . "Just a very, very talented group," coach Shane Steichen said of the Cowboys' playmakers. -- Stephen Holder 

 Stat to know: Colts QB Daniel Jones is the only QBR-qualified quarterback without a touchdown on a pass of at least 10 yards or more downfield this season. -- ESPN Research 

 Bold prediction: Colts RB Seth McGowan will score a touchdown. With Jonathan Taylor potentially on the trade block , I suspect Indianapolis might want to lighten his workload. That opens the door for a McGowan score. -- Walder 

 

 Injuries: Cowboys | Colts 

 Fantasy nugget: Cowboys RB Javonte Williams had 25 touches last week but finished with only 6.7 fantasy points. The workload hasn't been an issue. Williams has averaged 19.3 touches per game and has scored a touchdown in six of eight games. The Colts have allowed the sixth-most rushing yards per game, so Williams should bounce back in this matchup. See Week 9 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: Since 2024, Dak Prescott is 4-14 ATS as a favorite (7-11 straight up). Dallas keeps giving opponents chances to hang around, allowing more than 51% of third downs to be converted. Indianapolis has its own problems, but the Cowboys rarely force turnovers and struggle to end drives. Prescott has a favorable matchup, but asking this defense to protect a lead feels shaky. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 27 
 Moody's pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 24 
 Walder's pick: Cowboys 27, Colts 14 
 FPI prediction: DAL, 61.2% (by an average of 2.9 points)

 

 Matchup must-reads: Williams says Cowboys must 'execute,' over and over ... Colts' Steichen defends Taylor usage, says RB will keep role ...  Source: Colts, Adebawore agree to 2-year, $35M extension  ...  Forget about Cowboys' D, what happened to the GOTI offense? 

 
 

 Jets (2-6) at Chiefs (5-2) 
 1 p.m. ET | CBS | KC -10 (47.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Jets: New York is showing signs of life on offense, especially the past two weeks, but the Jets left a lot of points on the field because of poor efficiency in the red zone -- they're last with a 42% conversion percentage. They actually devoted more practice time this week to red zone play. "We just have to be better. And there is a sense of urgency," offensive coordinator Frank Reich said of the red zone woes. RB Breece Hall (quadriceps) is expected back after a five-game absence, but WR Garrett Wilson ( concussion ) could be out. -- Rich Cimini 

 What we're hearing on the Chiefs: Two words were expressed by defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo following the collapse last week : killer instinct. The Chiefs allowed the Broncos to score 15 points on two drives. Spagnuolo wants to see how his players perform if they have another lead. "That was on my objective for going into this game, if we are fortunate enough again to get in that situation," Spagnuolo said of building killer instinct. "... I asked everybody to ask themselves this question: Did you let up? Did we lose our edge? Did I call it differently? Hopefully, we will be presented with that…

title: NFL Week 9 arrivals: Trevor Lawrence doubles up on denim, Ethan Burke reps Ovechkin
summary: NFL stars continue to turn gameday arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
full_text:
November football doesn't come with one dress code.

 The Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens open Week 9 on Thursday night at M&T Bank Stadium, where possible showers could make a water-resistant jacket or a pair of sturdy boots part of the look.

 

 By Sunday, the South could see two takes on fall fashion. With sunshine and temperatures in the mid-60s in Charlotte, a varsity jacket or a knit polo would fit right in. In Miami Gardens, temperatures in the 80s leave room for breezy button-downs, relaxed trousers and shades.

 Out West, sunshine in Southern California and the Bay Area sets the stage for short sleeves and lighter fabrics. Seattle could call for a different approach, with possible showers in the forecast.

 The Northeast and Midwest offer more chances to break out fall staples. Temperatures in the 50s in Philadelphia and Foxborough are good territory for knitwear, and a cool Sunday night in Chicago gives players a reason to pull out a statement coat for the walk into Soldier Field.

 Here are the NFL's most fashionable arrivals from Week 9.

 

 Thursday night's fits 
 
Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence doubled up on dark denim for "Thursday Night Football," pairing a zip-front jacket with matching jeans and cream sneakers. Ravens rookie linebacker Ethan Burke , who was born in Annapolis, Maryland, and grew up in nearby Pasadena, showed some love to the Washington Capitals by layering a throwback Alex Ovechkin jersey featuring the Screaming Eagle logo over a black hoodie.

full_text:
While Week 8 meant the debut of two "Rivalries" jerseys, another alternate look returns to the field in Week 9, and a popular throwback comes back. 

 

 The Los Angeles Chargers are wearing their "Super Chargers" all-navy threads against the Houston Texans . Unveiled in 2025, the Chargers deemed the navy uniforms "a true modern throwback." It's a nod to threads worn in the 1990s and early 2000s, which coincided with a Super Bowl XXIX appearance and four AFC West titles. The navy jersey includes white modern numbers with an old-school outline and gold trim. The navy pants boast a bolt on the side, while a bolt also runs on the shoulders and helmet. "Super Chargers" is stitched in white on the neckline. 

 In a trend that's becoming more common around the league, the New York Giants and Philadelphia Eagles offer a matchup of throwback uniforms. The Eagles are rocking their "Kelly Green" threads, while it's a "Vintage White" look for the Giants. "Thursday Night Football" between the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks in Week 6 also brought a throwback threads matchup. Philadelphia brought back the iconic Kelly Green combination in 2023, while New York's look returned in 2025 after a one-year hiatus. 

 Alternates are still represented well throughout the week, though.

 The Baltimore Ravens are wearing their "Purple Rising" combination on "Thursday Night Football" against the Jacksonville Jaguars . Baltimore unveiled the look in the offseason as part of their wardrobe overhaul. It includes a new "Purple Rising" helmet, first introduced in 2024 with the alternate purple jersey. The primary logo appears on the metallic purple lid instead of the front-facing Ravens one. Different from the previous all-purple combination is a new "midnight purple" color, which is meant to emulate the iridescence of a raven's feather, and "Purple Rising" running on the inside collar.

 The New Orleans Saints are going gold against the Cleveland Browns . And it's another navy look for the Dallas Cowboys against the Indianapolis Colts , who are doing a rare home white out.

title: Regrading 2025 NFL deadline trades: How Gardner, Williams deals look right now
summary: How do the Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams blockbuster trades look one year later? What about the Jakobi Meyers, Rashid Shaheed and Jaelan Phillips deals?
full_text:
I'm a firm believer in evaluating trades the moment they happen. But we should check in on the results after they've played out, too. One year removed from a trade, how does it look in retrospect? Let's look back at the 2025 NFL trade deadline one year later. We're including blockbuster trades for Quinnen Williams and Sauce Gardner , along with other deals that sent players like Jaelan Phillips , Jakobi Meyers and Rashid Shaheed to playoff teams.

 In this exercise I'm grading trades like I always do, taking into account player quality, draft pick compensation, contract details and team time horizons. But in this case we have results of a year of play, too. These grades are descriptive of the past 12 months -- meaning they reflect the results of how they panned out -- along with my expectations for the remaining effects of the trade going forward.

 How should we feel about the Williams deal now? How about the Odafe Oweh for Alohi Gilman swap? Or the Shaheed deal, especially considering the Seahawks' Super Bowl LX victory ? Before this year's trade deadline hits on Nov. 10, let's finish up our evaluation of the last one.

 
 More trade deadline content: 
 Trade tracker | Trade grades 

 
 

 
 Jump to a 2025 regrade: 
 Gardner/Mitchell | Williams/Smith 
 Meyers  | Oweh/Gilman | Phillips 
 Shaheed | White | Campbell/Newsome 

 
 

 

 CB Gardner to the Colts for WR Mitchell, more 
 Colts got: CB Sauce Gardner 
 Jets got: WR Adonai Mitchell , 2026 first-round pick, 2027 first-round pick

 Original grade for Colts : D 
 New grade for Colts: F

 Original grade for Jets : A 
 New grade for Jets: A

 I had a sliver of empathy for the Colts when this trade was made given the situation they were in. At that moment, ESPN's Football Power Index gave Indianapolis an 11% chance to win the Super Bowl. Here's what I wrote, "Not only is this their best chance in years, but it's probably the best chance they will have for the next few years."

 I feel pretty good about that assessment 12 months later. But that didn't even come close to negating the obvious, instant takeaway from this trade when it was made: It was an ill-advised and reckless overpay. It's fine for NFL teams to push their chips in while contending. But there must be a price limit to every transaction, and the Colts blew past what was reasonable. It looks even worse now, because everything that has happened since has been a disaster for Indianapolis.

 Gardner suffered a calf injury in his third game with the Colts, which cost him all but one game the rest of the season. One week later, quarterback Daniel Jones suffered a season-ending Achilles injury . The Colts won only one game after trading for Gardner, plummeting from 7-2 to 8-9 and finishing the season out of the playoffs.

 

 With Gardner and Jones both healthy in 2026, there was still a chance for the trade to have some value. But neither has played great. Jones ranks 29th out of 30 qualifying quarterbacks in QBR while Gardner has allowed 1.1 yards per coverage snap this season -- average for an outside cornerback. Gardner also has plus-8.5 EPA allowed on targets (worse than average). While I believe some of Gardner's numbers are a result of contested catch variance and that he's playing better than his 1.1 number suggests, the results have not been great.

 Ultimately, the Colts lost their first-round pick last year (which the Jets turned into tight end Kenyon Sadiq ) and now don't have a first-round pick in 2027 -- right as they begin a rebuild. It's extremely unideal, especially since the Colts would have the No. 4 overall pick if the season ended today. That pick could go even higher, as Indianapolis fired GM Chris Ballard on Oct. 19 and has already traded multiple veteran players preceding this year's deadline.

 

 One part of this trade I haven't mentioned thus far is Mitchell, but he shouldn't be overlooked. This deal would have been an A for the Jets without him, but he's no throw-in. Mitchell had always shown an ability to get open, but that hadn't resulted in serious production. That might be in progress this season. Though he missed time with a finger injury , Mitchell has put up an extraordinary 2.6 yards per route run when he has been on the field. The Jets look like they also got a starting-caliber wide receiver out of this trade, making it even better.

 For the Jets, this move in conjunction with the Quinnen Williams trade has given New York the draft capital it needs to put together a talented young core and have a shot at a top quarterback in the 2027 draft. It has been a long, painful road for the Jets, but their willingness to deal their stars at last year's deadline has set them up for future success.

 

 

 DT Williams to the Cowboys for DT Smith, more 
 Cowboys got: DT Quinnen Williams 
 Jets got: DT Mazi Smith , 2026 second-round pick, 2027 first-round pick

 Original grade for Cowboys : F 
 New grade for Cowboys: D

 Original grade for Jets : A 
 New grade for Jets: A

 At the time of this trade, I was completely dumbfounded at Dallas' decision to make this deal. Prior to dealing for Williams, FPI gave the Cowboys a 7% chance to reach the playoffs, which is precisely when a team should not deal away future first-round picks for veterans.

 Part of my criticism was that Williams could play well in 2025 and that it wouldn't matter because of the hole the Cowboys had dug themselves. That's precisely what happened -- from Week 11 on, Williams ranked second and ninth in pass rush win rate and run stop win rate at defensive tackle, respectively. Those are incredible rankings! But they were not enough to get Dallas to the playoffs, as the Cowboys finished the season 7-9-1.

 This season, Williams still ranks in the top 10 in run stop win rate for interior defenders but his pass rush win rate has fallen to average (though he does have five sacks). And the Dallas defense? It's still bad, ranking 31st in EPA allowed per play.

 So my belief then is my belief now: Williams is a great player, but the Cowboys gave up far too much for him, especially considering where they were in the standings at the time of the deal. At the time of the original grade, I'm not sure we knew that the Cowboys were surrendering the better of their two 2027 first-round picks -- theirs and the Packers' -- which only furthered the downside for the Cowboys (and upside for the Jets).

 There were ripple effects, too. With a surplus at defensive tackle, the team traded Osa Odighizuwa ( for not enough !) to the 49ers in March, keeping Williams and Kenny Clark -- who came over in the Micah Parsons trade . The Cowboys also extended Williams with a lucrative three-year, $105.9 million extension in August.

 

 

 As for the Jets? This was a home run then and a home run now. The team wasn't going anywhere in 2025, and it was able to gain a ton of surplus value via draft capital, which is helping build a group of talented young players. The Jets were the biggest winners of last year's trade deadline, and it set them up for success in 2027 and beyond. It doesn't even matter that Smith didn't stick in New York .

 

 

 WR Meyers to the Jaguars 
 Jaguars got: WR Jakobi Meyers 
 Raiders got: 2026 fourth-round pick, 2026 sixth-round pick

 Original grade for Jaguars : C+ 
 New grade for Jaguars: B+

 Original grade for Raiders : A- 
 New grade for Raiders: B+

 This trade was made to help replace lost wide receiver production due to poor performance from Brian Thomas Jr . and a season-ending injury to Travis Hunter . Which is funny, because it turns out the perfect person to step up was already on Jacksonville's roster.  Parker Washington  emerged last season and has elevated his play even further in 2026 to where he is now the Jaguars' clear No. 1 wide receiver.

 Even though Washington has produced a superb 2.6 yards per route run since the trade for Meyers, Meyers has been a helpful player in his own right, recording 1.6 yards per route run since arriving in…

title: How the Jets trading stars Quinnen Williams and Sauce Gardner looks a year later
summary: Hours before the 2025 trade deadline, New York stockpiled first-round picks by sending its two stars to the Colts and Cowboys.
full_text:
In less time than it takes to play an NFL game, the New York Jets made two blockbuster trades ahead of the 4 p.m. ET deadline on Nov. 4, 2025, that would help alter the trajectory of three franchises.

 First, it was cornerback Sauce Gardner being traded to the Indianapolis Colts , first reported at 12:47 p.m. Then, it was defensive tackle Quinnen Williams  being  sent to the Dallas Cowboys at 2:05 p.m. The impact of the deals has already contributed to significant aftershocks.

 Since then, the combined record of the three teams is 14-35.

 The Colts' architect, general manager Chris Ballard, was fired  Oct. 19.

 

 Two coaches, the Jets' Aaron Glenn and the Colts' Shane Steichen, are fighting for their jobs, having gone 4-13 and 3-13, respectively.

 Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer, too, could be in trouble if his team doesn't challenge in a watered-down NFC East.

 A quick refresher:

 For the 25-year-old Gardner, a top young cornerback, the Jets received first-round picks in 2026 and 2027, along with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell -- widely perceived as a "throw-in" player, but New York insisted that he be included in the package.

 For Williams, one of the league's best defensive tackles, the Jets landed a 2026 second-round pick, a 2027 first-round pick and defensive tackle Mazi Smith , whom they cut in training camp. They have the rights to the better of the Cowboys' two first-round picks in 2027, as Dallas has its own selection and the Green Bay Packers ' pick from the Micah Parsons trade. The Jets insisted on that during negotiations.

 "I don't know if I would've traded two star defensive players in their prime," said a former NFC GM who is a current personnel analyst. "In hindsight, it worked out pretty well. The next guy will walk into a nice situation" -- meaning he assumes Glenn won't be back in 2027.

 The Jets, who accepted short-term pain for long-term gain, still are waiting to reap the full benefits of the trades. That will come in April, when they enter the draft with three first-round picks. With a glaring need at quarterback, they could have the ammo to target a specific player -- one of the main reasons for last year's trades.

 Coming into Week 9, ESPN Analytics projects them to have the fifth (their own), sixth (Colts) and 14th (Cowboys) selections. The Colts, who recently traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner for draft capital, are sinking like a horseshoe in a swimming pool, so that pick could be in the top three or four.

 "For the Jets, the Sauce Gardner trade might be one of the best of all time because of the draft compensation, and then you add in Mitchell, who can be a strong receiver," an AFC personnel scout said. "On the other hand, it has to be among the worst trades in Colts history because of the collapse."

 The Colts were in go-for-it mode when they acquired Gardner, thinking he was the missing piece. They've fallen on hard times, prompting them to part with two franchise cornerstones and replenish their draft cupboard.

 It's a traditional sell-off, considering Nelson, 30, and Buckner, 32, are past-their-prime players in the final year of their contracts. What the Jets did last year was bold because Gardner and Williams were only 24 and 27, respectively, with time on their contracts.

 It was unprecedented, too, as the Jets became the first team in the common-draft era (since 1967) to make multiple in-season trades to acquire a first-round pick.

 The Cowboys acquired Williams because they wanted a front-seven player to fill the Parsons void and improve their run defense. They're still struggling on defense, but they still have a 43% chance to make the playoffs, per ESPN Analytics.

 It's conceivable, even likely, that all three teams will miss the playoffs -- again.

 As Tuesday's trade deadline looms, Jets reporter Rich Cimini, Colts reporter Stephen Holder and Cowboys reporter Todd Archer look back at last year's blockbusters and how they affected their respective teams, and draft analyst Jordan Reid puts into context what the Jets could do with the draft capital that they acquired from the historic two hours.

 

 

 A surprising day for the Colts 
 Ballard for years showed an aversion to making aggressive moves. Outside of trading a first-round pick in 2020 for Buckner and a desperation trade for quarterback Carson Wentz in 2021, Ballard's tendency was to stock up on Day 2 and 3 draft selections to give him more shots at the team's draft board.

 So, it was particularly surprising when the Colts began searching for an impact defensive player before the 2025 trade deadline. But the Bengals were being stubborn with their terms on defensive end Trey Hendrickson . Other options also led nowhere.

 But the Jets, after significant sweetening, said yes on Gardner.

 It was always going to take a lot for a deal this audacious to pay off. And through no fault of Gardner's, it's difficult to say the Colts have gotten much return. First, Gardner has missed five of a possible 16 games since the trade because of calf injuries, including four games late last season when the Colts were fighting for a playoff spot. But a much bigger issue is the state of the Colts' franchise. The trade was put into place to help what was a 7-2 team make a postseason push.

 Now, Ballard is gone, and the Colts are, perhaps, the most calamitous team in the NFL. Their last game? A 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. It all makes for an awkward reality for Gardner.

 "It's definitely tough," Gardner said. "It's different than when I first got here. I'm a man of faith, so it's just one of those things where it's like, everything happens for a reason. God ain't going to put me in a certain position for no reason. We're going to overcome this thing."

 

 But the Colts will have to do that without the compensation they forked over to the Jets. The lack of a first-round pick in 2027 is especially painful given the likely roster rebuild that lies ahead. The fallout from the trade isn't the only reason the Colts are in a tough spot. But it certainly has made a bad situation much, much worse.

 Gardner recalls being elated after the trade, going from the struggling Jets to a team with -- at the time -- one of the best records in the NFL. Now, he's looking at having to endure a roster reboot, even if he's being a good sport about it all.

 "I embrace everything," he said. -- Holder 

 

 An impactful move for Cowboys 
 Williams was not pleased with his play in eight games with the Cowboys last season, despite being named to the Pro Bowl. The Cowboys, however, signed him to a three-year extension worth $105.9 million in August.

 Still, the Cowboys have struggled to stop the run and are not efficient in rushing the passer, but Williams' play has improved. His 11 tackles for loss rank second in the NFL and are the most among defensive tackles, and he leads the Cowboys in sacks (five).

 

 Yet, Williams wants more.

 "My standard is really high," Williams said. "I'm on the right trajectory, the right direction to play how I know I can play. Just setting the standard, not only for me, but for this defense in general, and the ability that we have as a unit, we can achieve those and we haven't achieved those yet, but we have the ability to achieve those."

 His voice is big in the locker room. He is one of the four captains and a member of the team's leadership council. His locker is next to  Dak Prescott 's, and Williams and the quarterback have had talks about getting the Cowboys to play more consistently.

 "Quinnen's been here for almost a year now. He kind of understands how we function, and so he's much more apt to speak his mind," Schottenheimer said. "When he talks, everybody kind of stops and listens." -- Archer 

 

 Jets still waiting on the results 
 Saying he wants to focus on the present, Glenn declined to reflect on the two trades, except to say Gardner and Williams are "great players and…

title: Forget about Cowboys' D, what happened to the GOTI offense?
summary: This summer, they talked about having the Greatest Offense There Is, but it's been worse than 2025.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- For all of the issues surrounding the Dallas Cowboys ' defense in 2026 -- and there are many -- there is a more perplexing reason why they are 3-5: a star-laden offense that returned every starter from a unit that was among the NFL's best in 2025.

 The points per game remain about the same (27.4 in 2026; 27.7 in 2025) and some areas are actually better this season (third-down rate, red zone offense), but the offense is putting up 50 less yards per game (391.9 to 342). The running game is off by 31 yards (125.6 to 94.1). The passing output has dipped from 266.3 yards per game to 247.9.

 Pass plays of 20 yards or more are down from 3.3 per game to 2.6. Runs of 10 yards or more are down from 2.7 per game to 1.8.

 In the first eight games last year, receiver  George Pickens had 43 catches for 685 yards and six touchdowns. In the first eight this year, he has 39 for 533 yards and two scores. Tight end Jake Ferguson had 51 receptions for 334 yards and six scores in the first eight games of 2025. He has 17 for 115 yards and three touchdowns this year, and he is now battling an ankle injury.

 

 On his way to 1,200 rushing yards in 2025, Javonte Williams had more than 75 rushing yards in five of his first eight games. He has two such games in the first eight this year, although he has matched the eight rushing touchdowns from that stretch in 2025.

 Quarterback  Dak Prescott had a completion percentage of 65.5% or better in six of the first eight games last season. This year, it's three of eight.

 During the summer, Prescott talked about an offense that would be GOTI, an acronym for Greatest Offense There Is . He was asked Thursday if the Cowboys have found an offensive identity. He paused for a few seconds.

 "Yeah, sure," he said. "I mean, is it one we're proud of? I don't know. We'll be better, I can promise you."

 Speaking on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Tuesday, owner and general manager Jerry Jones used the word "rebuild" when talking about the defense with first-time coordinator Christian Parker and a changeover in personnel through free agency and the draft.

 "We had a letdown there in the game Sunday," Jones told the team's flagship station in reference to last week's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals . "The plan is dependent upon that offense carrying us when we have weakness in the defense as we evolve going forward."

 The Cowboys have scored at least 30 points five times, but when they have been needed most -- at the end of the Baltimore Ravens loss in Rio de Janeiro in Week 3, in the fourth quarter and overtime against the Cardinals, for largely the entirety of the losses to the Green Bay Packers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers -- they have not had answers.

 "It's hard to say we're pressing, but yeah, when you've got the talent we've got, when you've got the expectation, the standards that we have for ourselves and you go three-and-out or you don't score a touchdown, yeah, that's frustrating and you've got to make sure that you don't allow that to continue to bleed," Prescott said. "Because then that bleeds into guys making [missed assignments] or not doing the details the right way because they want the big play rather than just sticking to it."

 

 Wide receiver CeeDee Lamb was even more succinct.

 "We stop ourselves," Lamb said. "That s--- is frustrating. It's annoying. I hate it. Then, ultimately, we end up losing."

 The Cowboys offense has become more stagnant than it was a year ago.

 At coach Brian Schottenheimer's introductory news conference, he said he is a big believer in cut splits, shifts and motions "to distort things." In 2025, the Cowboys ranked 11th in motion (66.5%) and 15th in motion at the snap (35%). This season, the Cowboys are 30th in motion (56.4%) and last in motion at the snap (24.8%), according to ESPN Research.

 "We certainly have them in," Schottenheimer said. "Without having the list in front of me, we believe in moving and shifting and motioning and things like that."

 Schottenheimer mentioned playing from behind as a reason why the motion numbers have dipped because they needed to play faster.

 The Cowboys were down two scores in the fourth quarter of three games:  New York Giants , Buccaneers and Packers. Against the Ravens, they faced an 11-point deficit in the third quarter but scored in less than two minutes. Against the Houston Texans , they trailed 16-6 at halftime and scored touchdowns on their first three drives of the second half.

 "And then sometimes, you do cloud the picture [with motions and shifts]," Schottenheimer said.

 The lack of big plays has been alarming, although Schottenheimer mentioned the Cowboys' ability to draw pass interference penalties. According to ESPN Research, the Cowboys are tied for second by drawing nine pass interference penalties, accounting for 139 yards, which is second most to Green Bay's 152.

 Getting Pickens more involved is a point Schottenheimer and offensive coordinator Klayton Adams acknowledge, but in four of the past five games, the receiver hasn't had a first-quarter catch. In the first half of three games, he has one or no catches.

 "I think a little bit of it [is] unlucky, a little bit of it [is] we got to design stuff that forces the issue to him," Adams said. "And then sometimes when we do, we got to make more happen with it than just an incompletion or a three- or four-yard gain. The goal is to score a touchdown regardless of who you're getting the ball to, but he's definitely somebody that we would love to have get the ball to and get going early. "

 

 Schottenheimer has said teams have played a lot of "shell coverage" to limit the explosive plays, but how does that explain the struggle to run the ball? The Cowboys are averaging 94.1 yards, 25th in the league.

 The Cowboys were without their best lineman, left guard Tyler Smith , for the first four weeks, but in three of the four games since his return, the Cowboys have averaged less than four yards per carry.

 "The biggest thing that's disappointing for us is the run game, especially with the dudes in our room," center Cooper Beebe said.

 The blitz has hurt the Cowboys, too. In three of the past four games (Tampa Bay, Green Bay and Arizona), the Cowboys have not had answers. Prescott was sacked a season-high four times by the Cardinals and was under duress against the Packers and Buccaneers.

 On the season, the Cowboys have two touchdowns against the blitz.

 "There's opportunity in it when people do it to us, and we haven't taken advantage of that," Adams said. "And that's kind of been my message to the team is, whether it's a passing down or a run down, if we can inflict pain, it's probably not coming back -- and we obviously just haven't done that consistently enough."

 Nine games remain to get it right, starting Sunday against the 2-6  Indianapolis Colts  ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ).

 "I don't really like continuing to talk about this week in week out as if I got it figured out, and then we go out there and do what we do," Lamb said. "So we just got to go out there and play ball."

title: Packers give Micah Parsons boost in return from ACL injury
summary: Green Bay hopes Parsons will be back before Thanksgiving as it remains in the playoff hunt.
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- In the back of their minds, those in the Green Bay Packers ' locker room knew Micah Parsons ' return at some point this season would matter only if they did one thing: Stay alive.

 Three weeks into the season, there was reason to think that wouldn't happen. The Packers were 1-2, and the return of their star pass rusher was still weeks, even months, away.

 Yet safety Xavier McKinney , one of the defensive captains, had one thought.

 "Get back into the mix," he said, "and let's get this thing going."

 By the time Parsons returned to the practice field  Wednesday, the Packers had done just that. At 5-3 heading into Sunday's game at the New England Patriots  ( 4:25 p.m. ET, Fox ), they're smack dab in the NFC playoff picture nearing the midway point of the season. While Parsons is expected to miss at least two more games with an eye on returning for the Thanksgiving Eve game at the Los Angeles Rams , the Packers believe they've given Parsons a reason to come back for something more than just individual pride after a devastating and complex knee injury .

 "We put ourselves in a solid situation," McKinney said. "It could be better, and we all know that. But it could be worse."

 

 Parsons didn't necessarily look at the season that way. He was coming back, eventually, regardless of the Packers' record when he was cleared to return. He was focused on the end of the season, not the beginning, especially after they began last season 9-3-1 before losing five straight after he blew out his knee in Week 15.

 "I don't really buy into records because you've seen teams that lose a lot of games, finish strong, or last year we started strong, finished terrible," Parsons said after his return to practice on Wednesday. "It doesn't really matter about how you start, it's about how you finish."

 That's exactly the conversation Parsons said he was having recently with rookie edge rusher Dani Dennis-Sutton , who, like Parsons, played at Penn State before coming to the NFL.

 "I said, 'It's November time. You've got to lock in,'" Parsons said.

 Dennis-Sutton asked, "What's November time?"

 "I said, 'I get it, you're at Penn State last year, you're getting ready to think about bowl game you're heading to,'" Parsons said. "But I said, 'November gets ready for December, and December tells us who we're going to be for playoffs. ... It's going to get harder, it's going to be more challenging, but we've got to be ready to step up.'

 "That's what I'm excited for. I came back for the greatest time of football, and that's November football and December football. Let the show begin."

 

 In some ways, the Packers' defense has overachieved without Parsons. Through Week 8, the Packers ranked in the top 10 in fewest yards allowed (10th), fewest passing yards allowed (eighth) and fewest points allowed (10th).

 They have allowed 20 or fewer points in five straight games, their longest single-season streak since 2022 and one short of their longest streak since they won the Super Bowl in the 2010 season.

 What's more, they have allowed 20 or fewer points and had multiple takeaways in five straight games, their longest streak since 1994. A sixth straight game like that would tie the longest single-season streak by any NFL team in the past 30 years. Their 15 takeaways rank tied for second and are one more than the Packers had all of last season.

 Now they will get an emotional boost from Parsons even before they get to see him in game action.

 "We know it'll be probably a couple weeks to get him back in the swing of things," quarterback Jordan Love said. "But just to have him back out there on the practice field, to know that he'll be coming back soon, is great."

 The pass rush, minus one of the NFL's best pass rushers, hasn't been bad, either. The Packers rank sixth in sacks (22) despite not having a single player ranked in the top 16 in that category ( Lukas Van Ness , with a team-high 4.5 sacks, is tied for 17th). They're second in quarterback pressures (117), according to ESPN Analytics, despite not having a single player in the top 15 in that category (Van Ness, with a team-high 22, is tied for 16th).

 Much of the credit for that has gone to first-year defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon, who has been described by Packers coach Matt LaFleur as a "savant."

 

 While Gannon has been lauded for his blitzes, it has been  about disguise and the anticipation of extra rushers more than the actual rate at which he has sent more than five after the quarterback. The Packers rank only 12th in the league in blitz rate (33%), according to ESPN Analytics.

 "Wins and losses are the only stat I'm worried about," Gannon said this week when asked whether he's surprised his pass rush has been so effective without Parsons. "But yeah, I think our guys have done a good job of taking the coaching and affecting the game in a positive way, executing the game plan as much as we can, and we got some guys winning at a pretty good rate of one-on-ones right now. It's about the players."

 Parsons admitted he will probably be on a snap count when he does return to game action, saying that playing 50 snaps per game is "just not realistic. My body's not there yet. I don't think my knee's built for that yet."

 But even that will make a difference.

 "It's going to be a different monster," McKinney said. "He provides a certain level intensity for our defense, a certain level of playmaking for our defense. He's a game-changer, he's a game-wrecker. When we get him back, it's going to be a lot better than what it is. But we've still got to put in the work. We can't think it's just going to happen."

title: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter's 2026 season: Snaps on offense, defense
summary: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver  Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. The Jaguars have followed through on that, making the 2025 No. 2 overall pick a starter on defense and mixing him in where designed on offense. 

 He has started every game at cornerback and has played at least four snaps on offense in all but one game (Week 4 at Cincinnati). He has made big plays on both sides of the ball and had the best game of his career in Week 6, when he clearly showed what kind of threat he can be. Head coach Liam Coen has been consistent in saying that Hunter's offensive usage is fluid.

 "You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches, then absolutely will."

 How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

 

 

 

 Week 9 at Baltimore Ravens 
 It was a quiet night for Hunter on defense -- five tackles on 44 snaps -- but a bad one on offense. Hunter played six snaps on offense and fumbled the only time he touched the ball. Hunter caught a receiver screen from Trevor Lawrence , and Ravens safety Malaki Starks knocked the ball loose 1 yard behind the line of scrimmage. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan recovered the ball at midfield, and the Ravens took over with 5:10 to play in the third quarter with the Jaguars ahead 20-3.

 The turnover didn't hurt the Jaguars, though, because the Ravens then turned the ball over on downs four plays later, with tight end Mark Andrews fumbling the snap on fourth-and-1. Hunter was officially credited with one catch for minus-1 yard.

 

 

 Week 8 vs. Indianapolis Colts 

 Coming off a Week 7 bye week, it was a relatively quiet day from Hunter -- in terms of stats, anyway. Hunter played 49 of the 60 total snaps on defense tallying four tackles. He played six snaps on offense with one rush for 5 yards and no catches on one target. A new wrinkle this week is that he played a season-high four snaps on special teams -- returning a punt for 1 yard and securing a fair catch on another.

 

 

 Week 6 vs. Houston Texans in London 
 Hunter had the best game of his career against the Texans at Wembley Stadium, catching four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown and also intercepting C.J. Stroud in the end zone. He's just the fourth player since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger with a receiving touchdown and interception in the same game and the first to do it since Philadelphia's Brian Dawkins in 2002. The touchdown and interception came on consecutive drives.

 Per NFL Next Gen Stats, Hunter had 34 coverage snaps and limited the Texans to two catches on five targets. However, he also was hit with a questionable pass interference penalty in the end zone against Nico Collins that gave the Texans the ball at the 1-yard line late in the first half. Despite that, this was the first time Hunter has made a significant impact on both sides of the ball -- 58 snaps on defense and 9 on offense (season high) -- in the same game in his 13 career games. 

 

 

 Week 5 vs. Philadelphia Eagles in London 
 Hunter played every defensive snap (59) for the second week in a row and had six tackles (second-most on the team) and a pass breakup. He was penalized for defensive pass interference that wiped out a third-and-17 incompletion in the second quarter. It gave the Eagles the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line and Philadelphia running back Will Shipley scored two plays later.

 On offense, Hunter played five snaps and touched the ball for the first time since Week 1, catching a 9-yard pass on second-and-7 from the Jaguars' 40-yard line. Parker Washington scored on a 51-yard catch-and-run on the next play.

 

 

 Week 4 at  Cincinnati Bengals 
 Hunter played every defensive snap (71) in a 22-17 win against the Bengals and had four tackles and two pass breakups. It's the first time in his career he's played every defensive snap and it was necessary because the Jaguars were down cornerbacks Montaric Brown (hamstring) and Christian Braswell (knee) because of injury.

 "He played his ass off today," head coach Liam Coen said.

 Hunter, however, called his play "decent" and was disappointed that his interception got erased by a roughing the passer penalty on defensive tackle Arik Armstead .

 "I like to criticize myself a lot harder," Hunter said. "My wife does, too. I still give up a catch today, so she's going to be on me about that when I get home."

 Hunter didn't play at all on offense, the first time in his career that has happened. Coen said he didn't want to risk him getting hurt on that side of the ball because that would leave them down three cornerbacks. Hunter said he wasn't mad at that decision.

 

 

 Week 3 vs. New England Patriots 
 In a 35-6 win against the Patriots, Hunter saw an increase in snaps with 42 on defense (70%) and a decrease on offense with four snaps (6.7% of all offensive snaps). He recorded four tackles and his first career interception, picking off New England quarterback Drake Maye in the back of the end zone late in the first half to preserve the Jaguars' 14-3 lead. Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hunter out-jumped Chism for the ball. Hunter didn't touch the ball on offense for the second consecutive game, leaving him with only two touches so far this season.

 
 

 Week 2 at Denver Broncos 
 Hunter played 43 total snaps in the loss against the Broncos: 35 on defense (59.3% of all defensive snaps), seven on offense (12.7% of all offensive snaps) and one on special teams. He had one pass breakup and four tackles, and he was penalized for pass interference on a Bo Nix sideline pass to receiver Courtland Sutton . The 22-yard penalty -- plus Coen's unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing the call -- gave the Broncos the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line. The Broncos scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown on the next play. Hunter was not targeted on offense.

 After Week 2, Coen explained that his cornerbacks are handling drives with a planned rotation -- which is why Hunter was in for only 59.3% of defensive plays.

 "We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now.

 "But yeah, it's a rotation. Pre-game, we have it all laid out. The players know it. They all know the rotation. It's been clearly laid out to them what the expectations and standards are."

 
 

 Week 1 vs. Cleveland Browns 
 Hunter started at cornerback and played 27 snaps on defense (55.1% of total defensive snaps) and four on offense (7.1% of total offensive snaps) against the Browns. On offense, he had one carry for 3 yards on a jet sweep and one catch for 8 yards on a screen pass. He has had at least one catch in every game in which he played (eight games) to this point. On defense, Hunter was targeted once on defense which resulted in a Deshaun Watson completed a 4-yard pass to KC Concepcion .

title: Dolphins coach Hafley brings familiarity with Lions
summary: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley saw plenty of the Lions' top-ranked offense while leading Packers defense.
full_text:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Jeff Hafley knows what to expect when it comes to facing the Detroit Lions .

 The Miami Dolphins coach spent two years preparing for Detroit as the Green Bay Packers' defensive coordinator; when asked about the challenges Detroit presents, he had to stop himself after a lengthy, detailed answer about stars such as Jared Goff , Jahmyr Gibbs , Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta .

 Ahead of their matchup with the Lions on Sunday (1 p.m., E.T., CBS), the Dolphins' gameplan is rooted in respect for the NFL's top-ranked offense.

 "I think they're built the right way and they're the No. 1 offense in the NFL for a reason," Hafley said. "It's coaching, it's players, it's developing. Give coach (Dan Campbell) credit and give them credit, he's done a great job."

 The Lions average 395 yards per game this season, while their 29 points per game ranks third in the league. Gibbs and St. Brown rank second and 10th in rushing and receiving yards, respectively, and Goff has thrown only one interception against 15 touchdowns.

 Similar to when the Dolphins faced the 49ers in Week 2, Hafley said Sunday's game presents an "exciting" challenge for the youngest defense in the NFL.

 "They could hit you from a variety of different angles, whether it's in the run game or the pass game," he said. "I view that as a challenge that we look forward to. I mean, anytime you get a chance to go up against the top offense in the league, you need to prepare and you need to rise up to the level that you're going to play against. And for a young group of guys, I think it's really exciting."

 

 The Lions rank third in the NFL in explosive plays -- rushes of at least 10 yards and completions of at least 20 yards. Miami hopes to limit such plays by controlling time of possession and keeping the Lions' offense off the field.

 Rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor is trending toward playing Sunday after missing last week's game with a concussion. He practiced fully twice by the end of the week.

 Proctor was missed in Week 8; the Dolphins entered the week averaging 3.09 yards before contact per rush attempt, the second-most in the NFL. In last week's loss to the Patriots, however, they averaged a season-low 1.74 yards before contact.

 Running back Ollie Gordon II said Proctor's presence will be felt.

 "It's one of those things that I feel like once you've been in so many weeks with certain people, it's just boom, you mesh," Gordon said. "You mesh different, so I feel like it's one of those things we'll get back to it. It'll be us, and we'll be back to being us."

 Sunday also presents an intriguing stage for the Dolphins' fledgling passing offense, which ranks 30th in yards per game this season. Detroit allows a league-high 276.6 passing yards per game, but Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis isn't ready to call Sunday an advantageous matchup.

 Detroit still sacks opposing quarterbacks at the eighth-highest rate in the NFL and ultimately, Willis said, the Lions' numbers against the pass haven't stopped them from accumulating five wins this season.

 "They have a couple ups and downs like everybody else in the league and they just so happen to be statistically where they're at," he said. "But they've won a lot of games. They've won more games than we have and when you put it like that, it makes you think about whether that stat is really true or not.

 "So I just try to focus on continuing to try to instill the game plan, make sure we're all on the same page and try to go out there and execute."

title: What 18 contenders should do at the NFL trade deadline: Who could get aggressive?
summary: Should the Giants keep adding? Could the Bills go all-in? Would the Steelers stay conservative? Here's how 18 teams at or above .500 should approach the deadline.
full_text:
Should your favorite team be going all-in at the NFL trade deadline , which hits at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday? Should it be realistic about its strengths and weaknesses and stay put over the next week? Or is the best plan something in between?

 Today, I'm going to answer those questions for the 18 teams that reached Week 9 at .500 or better. Given their roster and play this season, I believe that four teams should stand down at the deadline and avoid sacrificing serious draft capital for any moves. Nobody is going to turn down a steal of a deal if one is available, but those four franchises shouldn't be prioritizing major additions.

 
 Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' 

 
 But as for the rest, I've split the other 14 teams into several tiers, ranging from organizations that should be extremely active at the deadline to ones that should be very selective and careful about making the right move for a very particular sort of player. I'll lay out each team's needs and current situation.

 I'll also name two possible trade candidates for each team. One will be a luxury trade addition, where the team would be adding a starter or even a borderline star to the roster and paying accordingly for the privilege. The other is a bargain deal, where the team would instead be looking for a rotational player or depth for the back of its roster. (Teams are listed alphabetically within each tier.)

 

 
 Jump to: 
 BAL | BUF | CHI | CIN | CLE | DEN 
 DET | GB | JAX | KC | LV | LAR 
 MIN | NE | NYG | PIT | SF | SEA 

 
 

 Should be aggressively adding 
 Let's start with the teams that should be most aggressive in seeking out talent before the deadline and work our way down to the ones that should put their phone on airplane mode.

 

 Buffalo Bills  (6-1) 
 Positions of need: OL, LB, S

 Was Buffalo's 36-10 victory over the Ravens a sign that defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard was able to find the right mix of players and pressures during the bye week or a product of the Ravens being stuck playing Joe Fagnano at quarterback for most of the game? I'd lean more toward the latter than the former, but I also wouldn't be shocked if Leonhard's defense took a step forward after having a week to rest and reflect on what went wrong early in the season. Playing an early-season schedule that included the Lions, Patriots and Rams also didn't help matters for Buffalo, who will now get the Vikings, Jets and Dolphins over the next three weeks.

 

 That self-scouting might determine how aggressive general manager Brandon Beane wants to be at the deadline. The Bills believe in linebackers  Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard , but adding a cover linebacker to rotate in wouldn't hurt. The Bills also just cut C.J. Gardner-Johnson , who started six games for them earlier this season, so landing a safety who can hold up in coverage would be a helpful move.

 Luxury target: I loved the idea of the Bills going after guard  Quenton Nelson , which would have given them a difference-maker at their weakest spot up front, but that's no longer an option. Would the Cardinals ever be willing to trade safety  Budda Baker , who has made eight Pro Bowls and continues to make an impact as a disruptive force in center field and along the line of scrimmage in his age-30 season? Baker is due more than $8 million over the remainder of this season and $17.8 million in 2027, which is the final year of his existing deal.

 Bargain target: If the Chargers are unloading, the Bills might call about cornerback Elijah Molden , who is due $3.3 million over the remainder of the season. The Colts could also be interested in moving 28-year-old Cam Bynum , a move that would save Indy nearly $6 million in cash. Buffalo doesn't have a ton of cap space, but it could restructure  Greg Rousseau 's contract or ask the Cardinals or Colts to retain some money by sending a better pick as part of either deal.

 

 
 

 Detroit Lions  (5-2) 
 Positions of need: DL, LB, CB

 The Lions have seen their rivals in Chicago make a huge move in trading two first-round picks for Jeffery Simmons , and the Packers are also going to get Micah Parsons back from a torn ACL . Yes, the Lions have welcomed Brian Branch back into the lineup and will hope to get Kerby Joseph on the field in the weeks to come, but even with those two safeties in the lineup, the Lions have real questions about their defense.

 Those issues were sadly exacerbated by the neck injury suffered by star linebacker Jack Campbell in the win over the Vikings on Sunday. Campbell's health is more important than any football situation, and it seems callous to talk about replacing him in the lineup. But because Campbell is one of the better linebackers in the league, the Lions will have to adjust without one of their best players on the field.

 Detroit is fielding the league's fourth-best offense by points allowed per possession, so anything general manager Brad Holmes can do to help the defense would go a long way to getting the Lions to the top of the NFC North. The good news is virtually anything would be of use. A rotational edge rusher to work in with  DJ Wonnum  across from Aidan Hutchinson ? A cover linebacker to help fill in for Campbell? A cornerback -- or even two -- to push Roger McCreary , Rock Ya-Sin  and  Ennis Rakestraw Jr ., none of whom have looked like they are ready to start for a playoff team this season? The Lions don't want to mortgage their future, but finding the right trade would go a long way toward topping their rivals in the division.

 Luxury target: In my column suggesting trades a few weeks ago, I argued for the Lions to swoop in on  Khalil Mack and  Donte Jackson in a deal with the Chargers to address both edge and cornerback. That would cost Detroit nearly $8 million over the remainder of the season, a not insignificant amount for any team to take on in the middle of the season. The Lions could trade more draft capital to get the Chargers to pay that total down, but the picks should be more important to Holmes than the cash at the moment.

 Bargain target: Veteran cornerback Mike Hughes was with a very different version of this Lions team in 2022 before leaving for the Falcons in free agency. He has started most of his time there, but after A.J. Terrell Jr . returned from injured reserve, Hughes has been in a reserve role, including a season-low eight defensive snaps during last week's loss to the Buccaneers . He wouldn't be an obvious upgrade on any of the options in Detroit, but the 29-year-old has been a reliable low-end starter at corner for most of his time in Atlanta.

 

 

 
 

 Jacksonville Jaguars  (5-2) 
 Positions of need:  OT, DT, CB, S

 The Jaguars could be one of the few competitive teams to deal players at the deadline if they decide to move on from wide receiver  Brian Thomas Jr . But most of their calls should be about adding talent to the roster. A swing tackle would be helpful with Anton Harrison expected to miss the remainder of the season and Patrick Mekari  -- who can play either guard or tackle -- on injured reserve after undergoing back surgery before the season.

 General manager James Gladstone might also have to address the defense, which lost defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton and safety Eric Murray to season-ending injuries last week against the Colts . Cornerback might also be a concern, given that Travis Hunter 's offensive role has expanded, which could lead to some series off on defense.  Montaric Brown was having a rough season before suffering a hamstring injury, too. The Jags don't need to add a star on defense, but another solid contributor or two would be big as they enjoy a three-game lead atop the AFC South.

 Luxury target: Eagles defensive tackle Moro Ojomo could be set to follow Milton Williams ' path toward a big contract in free agency. Ojomo's path to the starting lineup in Philadelphia has been buried by the presence of Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis , both of whom are on long-term contracts for…
